profile.plan: Fiends that trigger when a card effect discards them, so the deck throws its own hand away on purpose and turns each discard into a search, a Special Summon or removal.

hooks.label: Discards your own hand
hooks.why: Grapha, Snoww, Sillva and the rest only work when a card effect discards them, so any outside card that makes you discard is an activator.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Dark World monster is a Fiend, so cards that search, revive or boost Fiends work on the whole deck.

profile.plan: Sends its own cards from the Deck to the GY; Tearlaments monsters sent there by a card effect Fusion Summon by shuffling materials from the hand, field and GY back into the Deck.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Scheiren, Havnis and Merrli Fusion Summon when a card effect sends them to the GY, so every outside card that mills is another way to start.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: The deck mills three to five cards at a time, so outside monsters with an effect when they are sent to the GY get used for free.

hooks.label: Aqua support
hooks.why: The Main Deck Tearlaments monsters are all Aqua, and their Fusions ask for Aqua materials.

profile.plan: Level 7 Psychics that summon themselves for free, stack into Rank 7 Xyz bosses, and win by banishing the opponent's cards face-down until they have no zones left.

hooks.label: Banishes opponent's cards face-down
hooks.why: Shangri-Ira locks another one of the opponent's Monster or Spell & Trap Zones every time a card they own is banished face-down, so anything that banishes face-down spreads the lock.

hooks.label: Effects when banished
hooks.why: Kashtiratheosis, Big Bang, Overlap and Akstra all trigger when banished, and Riseheart and Tearlaments Kashtira banish your own cards as cost, so outside cards with banished triggers come along for free.

hooks.label: Recovers banished cards
hooks.why: The archetype banishes its own cards constantly, and Birth, Preparations and Kashtiratheosis all want banished Kashtira cards back, so anything that recovers banished cards keeps the engine fueled.

hooks.label: Outside Level 7 monsters
hooks.why: Kashtira Birth Normal Summons Level 7 monsters without Tributes and the deck's Xyz bosses want 2+ Level 7 materials, so any self-summoning Level 7 monster is another body and another overlay.

hooks.label: Rank 7 Xyz support
hooks.why: Riseheart and Kashtiratheosis lock the Extra Deck to Xyz only and the bosses are Rank 7, so support aimed at Rank 7 Xyz Monsters fits the whole Extra Deck.

hooks.label: Psychic support
hooks.why: Nearly every Kashtira Main Deck monster is a Psychic, so generic Psychic searchers, revival and boosts reach the whole deck.

profile.plan: Wyrm Synchro deck that turns every card it banishes (mostly as costs) into advantage, Summons Tuner Tokens and Synchro Summons huge bosses, locked to Synchro-only while the Tokens are out.

hooks.label: Banishes your own GY cards
hooks.why: Chixiao, Taia, Assessment and Punishment all banish from your GY as cost or effect, and every banished card pumps Chengying, triggers Strife and revives Abyss Dragon Swordsoul.

hooks.label: Effect when banished
hooks.why: The deck banishes its own cards constantly, so any outside card with an effect that triggers when it is banished gets it for free.

hooks.label: Non-Tuner Wyrms
hooks.why: Chixiao and Qixing Longyuan require non-Tuner Wyrm materials, and Mo Ye, Longyuan and Taia pitch or banish Wyrm monsters as costs, so any outside Wyrm monster pulls double duty.

hooks.label: Wyrm support
hooks.why: Nearly every Swordsoul monster and its Synchro bosses are Wyrms, so generic Wyrm search, revival and protection hits the whole deck.

hooks.label: Synchro Summoning cards
hooks.why: The Tokens lock you into Special Summoning only Synchro Monsters from the Extra Deck, so outside cards that Synchro Summon are the only Extra Deck plays that still work.

profile.plan: Tribute Summons big Wyrms by Tributing its own Continuous Spells/Traps, and pays for everything by destroying its own cards, turning each loss into searches, draws and removal.

hooks.label: Rewards destroying your cards
hooks.why: Dragonic Diagram, Mariamne, Mariamne Paradox and Apocalypse all destroy your own cards in hand or on field as a cost or trigger, so any outside card that does the same is free ammunition.

hooks.label: Wants to be destroyed
hooks.why: The archetype destroys its own hand and field constantly, so outside monsters with an effect when they are destroyed by a card effect get it for free.

hooks.label: Easy Tribute Summon bosses
hooks.why: The whole deck is built around Tribute Summons, boosted by Dragonic Diagram and Dreiath's protection, so any outside boss that Tribute Summons itself fits right in.

hooks.label: Continuous Spell/Trap payoffs
hooks.why: True Dracos Tribute Continuous Spells/Traps instead of monsters and Master Peace banishes them from the GY as a cost, so outside cards built around Continuous Spells/Traps pull double duty as Tribute fodder and ammunition.

hooks.label: EARTH/WATER/FIRE/WIND Extra Deck bosses
hooks.why: Metaltron XII Special Summons a Fusion, Synchro or Xyz Monster that is EARTH, WATER, FIRE or WIND straight from the Extra Deck when an opponent destroys it, so those bosses are a payoff.

hooks.label: Wyrm support
hooks.why: Every True Draco and True King monster is a Wyrm, so generic Wyrm support works across the whole deck, and Mariamne even searches non-WIND Wyrms.

profile.plan: A hyper-Spell engine that keeps its Main Monster Zone empty, Link Summons its Ace monsters into the Extra Monster Zone, and gets stronger effects once 3+ Spells sit in its GY.

hooks.label: Fills the GY with Spells
hooks.why: Kagari, Shizuku and nearly every Sky Striker Spell upgrade their effect once you have 3 or more Spells in your GY, so outside cards that stock the GY with Spells are fuel.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Sky Striker Ace Link Monster and the Sage line are Machine monsters, so generic Machine search, revival and protection hits the whole board.

hooks.label: Generic Link Monsters
hooks.why: Azalea Temperance and S.P.E.C.T.R.A. must be Link Summoned using a Link Monster among the materials, so outside Link Monsters give freely available material.

hooks.label: Cards for an empty Main Monster Zone
hooks.why: The whole deck plays with no monsters in its Main Monster Zone to keep its Spells live, so outside cards that reward or work under that same condition come with a free payoff.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Beast-Warrior circus that Tributes its own Extra Deck monsters to fuel Tribute Summons, triggering 'if Tributed' effects and amping up Tribute Summoned monsters.

hooks.label: Monsters with Tribute triggers
hooks.why: Rehearsal, Malabarisme, Finale and the Tribute Summons themselves Tribute your monsters as a cost, so any outside monster with an effect 'if this card is Tributed' gets it for free.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon payoff monsters
hooks.why: Biancaviso's quick-effect Tribute Summon, Soiree Operations and New Face all reward Tribute Summoning, and Dristy, Fiends, Cappello and Finale only work while you control a Tribute Summoned monster.

hooks.label: Tribute fodder generators
hooks.why: Rehearsal, Malabarisme, Finale and the Ritual Summons all Tribute monsters from your hand or field as a cost, so the deck constantly needs bodies to give away.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Biancaviso and Soiree Operations Tribute Summon during the opponent's turn as Quick Effects, so extra Normal Summons let you Tribute Summon again after using one.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Clown Crew monster is a Beast-Warrior, so generic Beast-Warrior searchers and boosters reach the whole circus.

profile.plan: A beatdown deck of DARK Dragons (Level 7 'Red-Eyes Black Dragon' above all) that Fusion Summons, revives from the GY and burns the opponent, with a Zombie off-shoot built around Red-Eyes Zombie Dragon.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Return of the Red-Eyes, Meteor Black Comet Dragon and Red-Eyes Fusion all Special Summon or use Normal Monsters, so outside cards that revive or search Normal Monsters power the deck.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Nearly every Red-Eyes monster is a Dragon and Red-Eyes Darkness Metal Dragon revives Dragons from hand or GY, so generic Dragon searchers and revivers slot straight in.

hooks.label: Zombie Tuners
hooks.why: Red-Eyes Zombie Dragon Lord needs a Zombie Tuner and Red-Eyes Zombie Necro Dragon scales with Zombies in the GY, so Zombie Tuners unlock the Synchro line.

hooks.label: Equip Cards
hooks.why: Gearfried the Red-Eyes Iron Knight pops Equips for removal and Red-Eyes Slash Dragon turns Equip Cards into negations and revives Warriors equipped to it, so Equip Spells feed both.

hooks.label: Recovers banished Dragons
hooks.why: Red-Eyes Darkness Metal Dragon Summons itself by banishing a face-up Dragon you control and Darkness Metal, the Dragon of Dark Steel can revive banished monsters, so Dragons that come back from banishment keep the engine fueled.

profile.plan: LIGHT Machine beaters that flood the field, level into Rank 5/6 Xyz bosses, and Fusion Summon giant Machine Fusion monsters.

hooks.label: Banishes your own LIGHT Machines
hooks.why: Cyber Network banishes LIGHT Machines from the Deck and later Special Summons every banished one, and Cyberload Fusion uses your face-up banished cards as Fusion Material, so banishing your own Machines is fuel, not loss.

hooks.label: LIGHT Machine support
hooks.why: Every Cyber Dragon monster is a LIGHT Machine, and Cyber Emergency and Cyber Repair Plant search any LIGHT Machine, so generic support for the Type and Attribute hits the whole deck.

hooks.label: Level 5 Machine monsters
hooks.why: Cyber Dragon Nova needs 2 Level 5 Machine monsters, and Herz and Drei turn themselves and the rest of the archetype into Level 5, so any outside Level 5 Machine is ready Xyz material.

hooks.label: Level 6 LIGHT Machines
hooks.why: Cyber Dragon Infinity wants 3 Level 6 LIGHT Machines as material, and its attach effect can grow further from there.

hooks.label: Machine Fusion Monsters
hooks.why: Cyber Pharos Fusion Summons any Machine Fusion Monster from the Extra Deck, and Nova and Eternity Dragon revive one for free, so any outside Machine Fusion is a valid boss.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be discarded
hooks.why: Cyber Dragon Nachster discards 1 other monster as a cost to Special Summon itself, so outside monsters with an effect when discarded get it for free.

profile.plan: Flip monsters that trigger when sent to the GY by a card effect, Fusion Summoning them into El Shaddoll bosses that recycle Spell/Traps from the GY.

hooks.label: Sends your DARK monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Every Shaddoll main deck monster triggers when sent to the GY by a card effect (Beast draws, Squamata mills, Wendi Summons), so outside cards that send your own DARK monsters there are extra activators.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Shaddoll Fusion, Sinister Shadow Games and El Shaddoll Construct constantly send cards from hand, field and Deck to the GY, so outside monsters with an effect there get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Flip monster support
hooks.why: The deck is built on FLIP effects and Link-2 Shaddoll Construct requires 2 Flip monsters, so outside cards that Flip Summon or flip monsters face-down set off the archetype's effects again.

hooks.label: Fusion material payoff
hooks.why: Shaddoll Fusion, El Shaddoll Fusion and Nephe Shaddoll Fusion Fusion Summon every turn, so outside monsters with an effect when used as Fusion Material trigger on each Summon.

hooks.label: DARK monster support
hooks.why: Winda and Meshahrail require a DARK monster as Fusion Material and most main deck Shaddolls are DARK, so generic DARK support slots straight in.

profile.plan: A beatdown deck of Level 8 LIGHT Dragons built around Blue-Eyes White Dragon, using its Level 1 Tuners and its own cards' costs to put big Dragons on the field and Fusion, Synchro or Ritual Summon over them.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Nearly every monster in the deck is a Dragon, and Blue-Eyes Abyss, Jet and the Synchro payoffs all reward or summon Dragons, so generic Dragon support covers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends your Dragons to the GY
hooks.why: The White Stones trigger when they are sent to the GY and Sage, Master and Protector send your Effect Monsters to the GY as a cost, so any outside card that sends your Dragon cards to the GY is free fuel.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Sage with Eyes of Blue, Master with Eyes of Blue and Protector with Eyes of Blue all send your Effect Monsters to the GY as a cost to Summon a Blue-Eyes, so outside monsters with effects that trigger in the GY get used for free.

hooks.label: Level 8+ Dragons
hooks.why: Blue-Eyes Abyss Dragon searches any Level 8 or higher Dragon in your End Phase, so any big outside Dragon boss is live in this deck.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Blue-Eyes White Dragon is a Normal Monster and Dragon Spirit of White counts as one in the hand and GY, so cards that support Normal Monsters work on the deck's core cards.

hooks.label: Fusion Summons from the GY
hooks.why: Ultimate Fusion shuffles Blue-Eyes materials from the hand, field and GY into the Deck, so outside Fusion cards that can use GY materials keep the Fusion line going without needing a full field.

profile.plan: Classic Spellcaster control built around Dark Magician: it searches and revives Level 7 DARK Spellcasters, Fusions and Rituals them out, and turns every Spell/Trap activation into advantage.

hooks.label: DARK Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Dark Magic Expanded boosts and protects DARK Spellcasters, and Apprentice Illusion Magician powers up 'your other DARK Spellcaster monster', so the whole deck shares that type and attribute.

hooks.label: Spell Counter engines
hooks.why: Skilled Dark Magician accumulates Spell Counters on each Spell activation and cashes three in for a Dark Magician, so cards that hand out or feed off Spell Counters ride the deck's spell-slinging.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Apprentice Illusion Magician and Dark Magician Girl the Magician's Apprentice Special Summon themselves by discarding 1 card, so outside cards with an effect when they are discarded get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Illusion Magic and Magician's Rod Tribute a Spellcaster monster as a cost, and Magician of Black Chaos MAX Tributes any monster, so monsters with effects when Tributed get used for free.

hooks.label: Level 6+ Spellcaster GY bait
hooks.why: Magicians' Souls sends 1 Level 6 or higher Spellcaster from the Deck to the GY as its cost, so big Spellcasters with an effect in the GY are live even when milled.

hooks.label: Dragon fusion material
hooks.why: Dark Magician the Dragon Knight, Amulet Dragon and Dark Magician Girl the Dragon Knight each Fusion Summon with 'Dark Magician' plus 1 Dragon monster, so any Dragon is usable material.

profile.plan: Fiend Devils (and the DARK Dragon Synchro engines that carry their name) that pay Life Points, roll dice and turn their own monsters being sent to the Graveyard into advantage.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Almost every Archfiend, from Summoned Skull to Archfiend Emperor to Masterking Archfiend, is a Fiend, so generic Fiend searchers, revivers and boosters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Fiend Tuners
hooks.why: Bone Archfiend sends a Fiend Tuner from hand or Deck to tune Levels, Hot Red Dragon Archfiend Bane summons Tuners, and Red Nova Dragon and King Calamity need 2 Tuners as Synchro material.

hooks.label: Mills Fiend monsters
hooks.why: Archfiend's Ghastly Glitch, Bone Archfiend and Masterking Archfiend all send Fiend monsters from the Deck to the GY, feeding Heiress' search, Gilfer's equip and Masterking's die roll.

hooks.label: Makes you pay LP
hooks.why: The dice Archfiends like Skull Archfiend of Lightning and Shadowknight pay LP every Standby Phase, and Masterking Archfiend turns every LP payment into a mill or a die roll, so any outside card that costs LP fuels it.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Fiends
hooks.why: Pandemonium searches an Archfiend whenever one is destroyed by a card effect, and Nefarious Archfiend Eater revives itself by destroying your monster, so outside cards that blow up your Fiends pay you twice.

profile.plan: Warrior HEROes with a different Attribute each that Fusion Summon with Polymerization, Miracle Fusion and Neos Fusion, turning their Normal Monster bodies and everything sent to the GY or banished along the way into advantage.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Elemental HERO monster, including the big Fusions and Links, is a Warrior, so generic Warrior searchers, revives and boosters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Triggers when used as Fusion material
hooks.why: Liquid Soldier draws two cards when used as Fusion Material for a HERO and Shadow Mist searches when sent to the GY, so the deck is constantly feeding Fusion Summons and outside monsters that trigger on being sent there get it for free.

hooks.label: Triggers when banished
hooks.why: Miracle Fusion and Neos Fusion banish HERO monsters from the field and GY as material, and The Shining recovers banished HEROes, so outside cards that trigger on being banished or that recover banished monsters fit.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Avian, Burstinatrix, Sparkman, Clayman and Neos are all Normal Monsters (and Neos Alius counts as one), so cards that search, revive or protect Normal Monsters work on a large part of the deck.

hooks.label: Polymerization synergy
hooks.why: Blazeman searches Polymerization, Prisma copies a material by revealing a Fusion Monster, and Wonder Driver Sets 'Polymerization' and 'Fusion' Spells from the GY, so any outside card built around Polymerization or Fusion Summoning from the GY fits.

hooks.label: Banishes for Fusion Summoning
hooks.why: Miracle Fusion Fusion Summons by banishing materials from the field or GY, so outside cards that banish your own monsters from the GY feed both it and The Shining's ATK boost.

profile.plan: A loose family of draw-engine cards (the Pots of Greed) that trade future resources, cards in hand or your own Deck and Extra Deck for raw draws right now.

hooks.label: Punishes opponent draws
hooks.why: The Gift of Greed and Gift Card-style effects hand your opponent draws, so outside cards that trigger or punish each time the opponent draws turn those draws into damage or advantage.

hooks.label: Reacts to your draws
hooks.why: The deck's whole engine is drawing cards, and Shard of Greed counts every normal draw, so outside cards that gain counters or trigger each time you draw compound every draw spell.

hooks.label: Uses your face-down banished cards
hooks.why: Pot of Desires, Pot of Extravagance and Pot of Prosperity banish large chunks of your own Deck and Extra Deck face-down, so outside cards that shuffle or exploit banished cards give that cost a second life.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be Tributed
hooks.why: Dark Spirit Art - Greed Tributes a DARK monster as a cost to draw, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Flip Summon support
hooks.why: Pot of The Forbidden is a Level 9 Rock Flip monster with a powerful FLIP effect, so outside cards that flip it face-down again, protect it, or support Flip Summons reuse that effect.

profile.plan: Link Fiends that discard a card as a cost whenever they're Link Summoned to pop, spin or search, and get bonuses when co-linked.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Every Knightmare Link monster discards 1 card as its cost when Link Summoned, so outside cards with an effect in the hand or GY when they're discarded get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Level 9 monsters
hooks.why: Knightmare Incarnation Idlee protects Level 9 monsters from destruction and itself sits at Level 9, so outside Level 9 bosses pair naturally.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: All the Main Deck Knightmare Link monsters are Fiends, so cards that search, revive or boost Fiends serve the whole Link board.

hooks.label: Link Monsters with different names
hooks.why: The Link monsters require 2 or more monsters with different names as material, so any deck that spams differently-named Link or easily-Summoned monsters feeds them.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Knightmare Incarnation Idlee sends all Link Monsters on the field to the GY, and the deck's removal and shuffling effects send cards there too, so outside monsters with GY effects when sent profit.

profile.plan: Mixes LIGHT and DARK monsters and banishes one of each from the hand or GY to Summon its big beaters, then feeds banished cards back into Synchro plays and recovery.

hooks.label: Fills the GY with LIGHT/DARK
hooks.why: Chaos Sorcerer, Chaos Emperor Dragon and The Chaos Creator Summon themselves by banishing 1 LIGHT and 1 DARK monster from your GY, so anything that stocks the GY with them is fuel.

hooks.label: Banishes your own LIGHT/DARK
hooks.why: The deck constantly banishes its own monsters from the hand and GY as Summoning costs, and Chaos Zone gains a Chaos Counter for each monster banished.

hooks.label: Triggers when banished
hooks.why: Chaos Valkyria sends from Deck and Chaos Witch makes Tokens when they are banished from the hand or GY, so the deck banishes its own cards on purpose.

hooks.label: Recovers banished monsters
hooks.why: Chaos Space, Chaos Zone, Chaos Beast and The Chaos Creator all reuse your banished LIGHT and DARK monsters, so the banished zone is a second hand.

hooks.label: LIGHT Tuner monsters
hooks.why: Chaos Angel, Chaos Goddess, Chaos Archfiend and Chaos Beast all need a LIGHT Tuner plus DARK non-Tuners, and Chaos Angel even lets a LIGHT/DARK monster count as the Tuner.

profile.plan: DARK Warrior HEROs that feed their own Graveyard and Fusion Summons, turning discards, GY banishes and Tributes of their monsters into draws, revival and big Fusion bosses.

hooks.label: Discards DARK Warriors
hooks.why: Destiny Draw, Dangerous's cost and Dynatag, Blade Master and Dark Angel all want to be discarded from the hand, so any outside card that makes you discard feeds them.

hooks.label: Mills DARK Warriors
hooks.why: Dangerous sends a Destiny HERO from the hand or Deck to the GY and D Cubed sends one from the Deck, so outside cards that send your DARK Warrior monsters to the GY trigger their GY effects.

hooks.label: DARK HERO monsters
hooks.why: Fusion Destiny locks you into Special Summoning only DARK 'HERO' monsters for the rest of the turn, so outside DARK HERO monsters stay playable alongside it.

hooks.label: Tribute fodder tokens
hooks.why: Plasma and Dogma Special Summon themselves by Tributing 3 monsters, so outside cards that swarm Tokens or free bodies supply the Tributes.

hooks.label: Normal Spell payoffs
hooks.why: Diamond Dude excavates and later activates Normal Spells straight from the GY for free, so strong Normal Spells are pure value in this deck.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Destiny HERO monster is a DARK Warrior, so generic Warrior support reaches the whole deck.

profile.plan: DARK Dragon Link bosses that destroy your own cards as costs and pay out of a GY full of DARK Dragons and DARK Link Monsters.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be destroyed
hooks.why: Borrelshroud, Trisborrel, Borreload Liberator and Borreload Riot Dragon all destroy your own cards as part of their effects, so outside monsters with an effect when they are destroyed get it for free.

hooks.label: DARK Dragon support
hooks.why: Every Borrel monster is a DARK Dragon and Borreload Furious Dragon Fusion Summons with 2 DARK Dragon monsters, so generic DARK Dragon support works on the whole Extra Deck.

hooks.label: DARK Link Monsters
hooks.why: Borreload Savage equips a Link Monster from the GY, Execute Protocols banishes a DARK Link Monster from the GY and Borrelcode summons a Topologic, so the deck wants other DARK Link Monsters in the GY and Extra Deck.

hooks.label: Mills DARK Dragons
hooks.why: Triple Borrel Launch and Trisborrel pay out of a GY stocked with DARK Dragon monsters, so outside cards that send your own DARK Dragons from the Deck to the GY fuel them.

profile.plan: Fusion Summons Dragons around Fallen of Albaz using materials from the hand, field and GY, banishing LIGHT and DARK monsters along the way.

hooks.label: Banishes LIGHT or DARK monsters
hooks.why: Branded Regained draws whenever a LIGHT or DARK monster is banished, and Branded Befallen banishes one from the GY as its cost, so any outside card that banishes those fuels both.

hooks.label: Mills the Extra Deck
hooks.why: Branded in High Spirits and The Fallen & The Virtuous both want a Fusion Monster sent from the Extra Deck to the GY, so outside cards that do that set up their recoveries.

hooks.label: Easy LIGHT materials
hooks.why: Albion the Branded Dragon needs a LIGHT monster as Fusion Material alongside Fallen of Albaz, so outside LIGHT monsters that Summon themselves are free material.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Fallen of Albaz and the Bystials are all Dragons, and Branded in White demands a Dragon as Fusion Material, so generic Dragon support covers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed Dragons
hooks.why: Branded Beast Tributes a Dragon monster as its cost every turn, so a Dragon with an effect when it is Tributed gets it for free.

profile.plan: FIRE Cyberse monsters that fill the Graveyard, swarm with self-summoning Level 3s and 4s, and repeatedly Link Summon - often reusing the same Link Monster as material for stronger 'reincarnated' versions.

hooks.label: Self-summoning FIRE Effect Monsters
hooks.why: Heatleo, Pyro Phoenix and Raging Phoenix all need 2+ FIRE Effect Monsters as Link material, so outside FIRE Effect Monsters that Special Summon themselves keep the Link Summons coming.

hooks.label: Mills FIRE monsters
hooks.why: Gazelle Special Summons itself the moment a Salamangreat monster is sent to the GY, and the whole deck wants its monsters there, so outside cards that mill FIRE monsters from the Deck are pure fuel.

hooks.label: Cyberse support
hooks.why: Every Salamangreat monster is a Cyberse and Balelynx needs a Level 4 or lower Cyberse to make, so generic Cyberse searchers and revival work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be Link material
hooks.why: The deck Link Summons several times a turn, so outside monsters with an effect when they are used as Link material get that trigger for free, like Coyote and Fennec do.

profile.plan: Hand traps that discard themselves while you control no cards and draw a card every time the opponent Summons from a particular zone, so the deck rides on the opponent's turn and banks advantage.

hooks.label: Works with an empty field
hooks.why: Every Mulcharmy can only be used while you control no cards, so outside cards that activate or summon under the same condition never clash with it.

hooks.label: Triggers when you draw
hooks.why: Fuwalos, Purulia and Meowls draw repeatedly during the opponent's turn, so any outside card with an effect that fires when you draw converts each draw into extra value.

hooks.label: Forces opponent's Special Summons
hooks.why: Each Mulcharmy only pays off when the opponent actually Summons, so outside cards that make the opponent Special Summon from the hand or GY keep the draw engine running.

profile.plan: A Fiend deck that uses every Summoning method at once — Pendulum, Fusion, Synchro, Xyz and Link — while its Dark Contracts search and summon for it at the price of burning you every Standby Phase.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every D/D and D/D/D monster is a Fiend, and Dark Contract with the Swamp King can Fusion Summon any Fiend Fusion Monster, so generic Fiend support reaches the whole deck.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Necro Slime, Lamia and Vice Typhon all summon by banishing D/D cards from the GY, and Copernicus only sends D/D cards there from the Deck, so milling sets all of them up at once.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: Necro Slime and Vice Typhon banish D/D monsters from the GY as Fusion Material, so outside monsters that trigger when banished get used for free.

hooks.label: Takes damage for value
hooks.why: Orthros Special Summons itself from the hand when you take damage, Tell's effect only works if you took effect damage that turn, and Leonidas summons off it, so cards that make you take your own effect damage become fuel.

hooks.label: Continuous Spell payoffs
hooks.why: Every Dark Contract is a Continuous Spell or Trap and Cerberus returns any Continuous Spell from the GY to the hand, so outside Continuous cards are extra contracts that the deck can recycle.

hooks.label: Pendulum Monster partners
hooks.why: Gilgamesh places two D/D Pendulum Monsters from the Deck and Deus Machinex swaps Pendulum Monsters between zones and field, so outside Pendulum Monsters give the engine more scales to work with.

profile.plan: Swarm the field with self-Summoning DARK Winged Beasts, Normal Summon one to trigger Black Whirlwind's search, then layer the board with DARK Synchro bosses.

hooks.label: DARK Winged Beast support
hooks.why: Every Blackwing monster is a DARK Winged Beast and the Synchro bosses keep that typing, so generic support for that Type and Attribute works across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Synchro Summons DARK monsters
hooks.why: The deck's whole payoff is DARK Synchro Monsters like Armor Master and Onimaru, and Boreastorm explicitly requires a DARK Tuner, so outside cards that Synchro Summon with DARK materials slot straight in.

hooks.label: Gives extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Black Whirlwind searches every time a Blackwing is Normal Summoned and Nothung grants an extra Normal Summon, so any outside card granting additional Normal Summons doubles up on triggers.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck

profile.plan: DARK Dragons that Special Summon themselves by banishing LIGHT or DARK monsters from the Graveyards, punishing LIGHT/DARK decks while feeding a banished pile that Dis Pater turns into advantage.

hooks.label: Fills GYs with LIGHT/DARK
hooks.why: Every Bystial Special Summons itself by banishing a LIGHT or DARK monster from either GY, so any outside card that loads LIGHT or DARK monsters into a Graveyard is Summon fuel.

hooks.label: Rewards being banished

hooks.label: Branded Continuous backrow
hooks.why: The Bystial Lubellion places a 'Branded' Continuous Spell/Trap from the Deck face-up, so outside Branded Continuous cards are a free engine piece.

hooks.label: Level 6+ DARK Dragons
hooks.why: Lubellion must be Special Summoned by Tributing a Level 6 or higher DARK Dragon, and Alba Los wants Bystial Tributes, so big outside DARK Dragons are ideal Tribute fodder.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Every Bystial monster is a Dragon and Dis Pater needs non-Tuner Dragon Synchro material, so generic Dragon search and support works across the whole deck.

profile.plan: Winged Beasts that swarm as "Harpie Lady" copies, bounce cards back to the hand, and Xyz/Synchro their Level 4 WIND monsters into dragons.

hooks.label: WIND Winged Beast support
hooks.why: Every Harpie is a WIND Winged Beast, Hunting Ground boosts all Winged Beasts and Feather Storm just needs any WIND Winged Beast on the field.

hooks.label: Bounces your own WIND monster
hooks.why: Harpie Dancer returns a WIND monster to your hand to re-Normal Summon it, Harpist triggers off bouncing your Winged Beast, and Harpie Conductor punishes the opponent whenever a Harpie returns to your hand.

hooks.label: Level 4 WIND monster
hooks.why: Harpie's Pet Phantasmal Dragon needs exactly 3 Level 4 WIND monsters as Xyz Material, and the whole Main Deck Harpie core is Level 4 WIND.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Harpist, Perfumer and Oracle all trigger on being Normal Summoned, and Dancer's bounce effect only pays off with another Normal Summon available.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Hysteric Party and Harpie Channeler both discard cards as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when discarded get it for free.

profile.plan: Pendulum Magician scales that destroy their own Pendulum cards as cost and trigger off cards being destroyed, turning every destruction into searches, Special Summons and fusion of Supreme King Z-ARC.

hooks.label: Destroys your own cards
hooks.why: Chronograph, Astrograph and Acrobatic Magician Special Summon themselves when a card you control is destroyed, so outside cards that destroy your own cards set them off.

hooks.label: Wants to be destroyed

hooks.label: DARK Spellcaster support

hooks.label: Pendulum support
hooks.why: Duelist Alliance and Pendulum Call search Pendulum cards and the whole engine lives in the Pendulum Zones, so generic Pendulum cards and scale manipulation slot straight in.

hooks.label: Adds from face-up Extra Deck
hooks.why: Pendulum Paradox, Amazing Pendulum and Oafdragon recover face-up Pendulum Monsters from the Extra Deck, so outside cards that keep Extra Deck cards face-up or recycle them feed that loop.

hooks.label: Frees the Pendulum Zones
hooks.why: Amazing Pendulum only works with empty Pendulum Zones and Wavering Eyes blows them up for value, so outside cards that remove or recycle your own scales turn that into advantage.

profile.plan: A Link-climbing Cyberse deck that stacks small Link Monsters and uses in-hand coders as extra Link material, searching Cyberse monsters with Cynet Codec as it goes.

hooks.label: Cynet Spell/Trap support
hooks.why: Micro Coder adds any 'Cynet' Spell/Trap from the Deck when used as material, so every Cynet card outside the archetype is a search target.

hooks.label: Low-Link Cyberse monsters
hooks.why: Transcode Talker and Decode Talker Heatsoul Special Summon Link-3 or lower Cyberse monsters from the GY or Extra Deck, so any small Cyberse Link Monster is a free body or revival target.

hooks.label: Cyberse support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is Cyberse and Cynet Optimization locks you into Cyberse Extra Deck Summons, so generic Cyberse searchers, revival and boosters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Decode Talker, Powercode Talker and Decode Talker Integration Tribute monsters they point to as a cost, so outside monsters with effects when Tributed get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Rewards being banished from GY
hooks.why: Accesscode Talker and Protectcode Talker banish Link Monsters from your GY as costs, and Recoded Alive banishes your banished Code Talkers back, so Cyberse monsters with effects when banished recycle well.

profile.plan: A swarm of Level 1 defensive Fiends that clutter the field, Tribute themselves and each other for battle-phase tricks, and swarm further with Tokens and 300/200 bodies.

hooks.label: Tributes Level 1 monsters
hooks.why: Linkuriboh revives itself by Tributing a Level 1 monster from the field, so outside cards that Tribute your Level 1 monsters keep its loop going.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Multiply, Kuribandit, Kuribah/Kuribeh and Linkuriboh all Tribute your monsters as cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Level 1 monsters
hooks.why: Linkuriboh is a Link-1 needing any Level 1 material and the whole deck is Level 1 bodies, so any outside Level 1 monster is extra fodder and Link material.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Nearly every Kuriboh monster is a DARK Fiend, and Kuribeh Normal Summons a Fiend from the hand, so generic Fiend support covers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Dark Magician support
hooks.why: Magikuriboh and Kuriboh - Multiply! fetch and Summon Dark Magician or Dark Magician Girl, and Magikuriboh recycles itself when your Spellcasters are destroyed, so Dark Magician support cards finish the job.

hooks.label: Number Xyz Monsters
hooks.why: Astral Kuriboh copies the Rank of a Number Xyz Monster and locks the Extra Deck to Number Xyz, so Number Xyz bosses and their support are the deck's Extra Deck payoffs.

profile.plan: A family of Counter Traps that pay large chunks of Life Points to negate Summons, Spell/Trap activations and monster effects.

hooks.label: Counter Trap support
hooks.why: Every negation in the archetype is a Counter Trap, so outside cards that punish the opponent for Chains or reward you for resolving Counter Traps stack with the whole deck.

hooks.label: Life Point gain
hooks.why: Judgment, Strike, Warning, Accusation and Scolding all pay 1500 to half your LP as a cost, so outside cards that recover Life Points let you keep paying.

hooks.label: Draw engines
hooks.why: Solemn Wishes gives 500 LP for every card you draw, so outside cards that draw cards turn it into steady recovery.

hooks.label: Aesir protection partners
hooks.why: Solemn Authority targets an "Aesir" monster you control and protects it, so outside cards that help put Aesir monsters on the field complete it.

profile.plan: Big Level 5+ monsters with 2400/2800 ATK that Tribute Summon over their own squires for strong on-Summon removal, while locking themselves out of the Extra Deck.

hooks.label: Extra Tribute Summons
hooks.why: The whole deck wins by Tribute Summoning, and Eidos only gives one extra Tribute Summon per turn, so anything else that grants additional Normal or Tribute Summons adds another Monarch play.

hooks.label: Tribute fodder Tokens
hooks.why: Every Monarch needs monsters to Tribute, so outside cards that Summon Tokens give reusable Tribute fodder without using up hand cards.

hooks.label: Easy Tribute Summon monsters
hooks.why: Erebus, Ehther and the Mega Monarchs can be Tribute Summoned by Tributing 1 Tribute Summoned monster, so any outside monster that Tribute Summons itself cheaply chains into them and satisfies Return of the Monarchs' search.

hooks.label: Attribute changers
hooks.why: The Mega Monarchs only get their bonus effect when Tributed with a monster of their own Attribute, and The First Monarch counts as two Tributes for a matching Attribute, so cards that change Attributes line those bonuses up.

hooks.label: Reacts to being Tributed
hooks.why: The deck Tributes its own monsters every turn, so outside monsters with an effect that triggers when they are Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Tributes opponent's monsters
hooks.why: The Monarchs Stormforth shows the plan: using the opponent's monsters as Tribute fodder, so other outside cards that Tribute monsters your opponent controls give the same free Summons and removal in one.

profile.plan: LIGHT Dragon Xyz deck that stacks Level 8 monsters into Rank 8 Galaxy-Eyes Xyz bosses, detaching materials for removal and negation while banishing whatever gets in the way.

hooks.label: Equips for Xyz material
hooks.why: Full Armor Photon Dragon can detach Equip Cards equipped to it to destroy opponent's cards, turning any equip into ammunition.

hooks.label: Detached-material triggers
hooks.why: Afterglow Dragon summons or attaches Galaxy-Eyes Photon Dragon when detached, so the deck constantly detaches materials and outside cards with effects when detached get them for free.

hooks.label: Tributes big ATK monsters
hooks.why: Galaxy-Eyes Photon Dragon Summons itself by Tributing 2 monsters with 2000+ ATK and Hyper Galaxy Tributes one too, so outside cards that Tribute or reward Tribute Summoning large monsters fit.

hooks.label: Level 8 LIGHT monsters
hooks.why: The Rank 8 bosses need 2-3 Level 8 monsters as material and most of the deck's enablers only need a Photon or Galaxy monster on field, so any Level 8 LIGHT monster is Summonable material.

hooks.label: LIGHT monster support
hooks.why: Nearly every monster in the deck is LIGHT, and Cipher X Dragon protects your LIGHT monsters from targeting.

hooks.label: Rewards banishing monsters
hooks.why: Photon Dragon and Photon Stream banish cards as removal and Vanisher banishes monsters it destroys, so outside cards that punish or exploit banished monsters combo with it.

profile.plan: DARK Warrior ghosts that swarm Levels 2-4, banish their cards from the GY as cost, and climb the Ranks of DARK Xyz Monsters with Rank-Up-Magic.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: Fog Blade, Wing, Sword, Cloven Helm and the other Phantom Knights banish their own cards from the GY as a cost on nearly every effect, so outside monsters with an effect when they are banished get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Level 3 DARK extenders
hooks.why: Break Sword, Malevolent Scythe and the other Rank 3 Xyz need two Level 3 monsters, and all the Main Deck Phantom Knights are Level 3 DARK, so outside cards that Special Summon more Level 3 DARK monsters feed every Xyz.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic Spells
hooks.why: Malevolent Scythe searches Rank-Up-Magic Spells and Raider's Unbreakable Mind Sets them from Deck or GY, so any outside Rank-Up-Magic is a free reloadable ladder for the DARK Xyz deck.

hooks.label: Grants effects as Xyz Material
hooks.why: Ragged Gloves shows the deck's payoffs live on its Xyz Monsters: a monster used as material hands its effect to the DARK Xyz, so outside monsters that do the same stack onto Break Sword and Raider's Knight.

hooks.label: DARK support
hooks.why: Every Phantom Knights monster and every Xyz they climb into is DARK, and Rank-Up-Magic Force and Rusty Bardiche both spend DARK monsters as fuel, so generic DARK monster support covers the whole deck.

profile.plan: Mills its own Deck every turn to stack the Graveyard, then Special Summons Judgment Dragon for free and revives or Synchro-summons off the GY fuel.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Nearly every Lightsworn card sends cards from the top of the Deck to the GY, and Wulf, Felis, Lightsworn Judgment and Lightsworn Sabre all trigger when milled, so any outside miller is another engine.

hooks.label: Triggers when milled
hooks.why: Charge of the Light Brigade and every End Phase mill throw cards into the GY, so outside monsters with an effect when sent from the Deck to the GY get it for free like Wulf and Felis do.

hooks.label: Triggers when banished
hooks.why: The Twilightsworn monsters banish Lightsworn monsters from the hand or GY as a cost, and Punishment Dragon is Summoned off banished Lightsworn, so outside cards that trigger when banished are free value.

hooks.label: LIGHT support
hooks.why: Almost every Lightsworn monster is LIGHT, so generic LIGHT support covers the whole deck and their Synchro bosses like Michael.

hooks.label: Big LIGHT Dragons
hooks.why: Minerva, Lightsworn Maiden searches LIGHT Dragon-Type monsters by Level and Dragonling fetches any 3000/2600 Dragon, so outside LIGHT Dragon bosses slot straight into the search lines.

profile.plan: Rank 4 LIGHT Warrior Xyz monsters that dodge attacks by detaching materials, then Rank-Up and re-Xyz into bigger Utopias while ZW monsters equip to them for power.

hooks.label: Other Number Xyz monsters
hooks.why: Number S0: Utopic ZEXAL, Number 93: Utopia Kaiser and Utopic Draco Future are Summoned from multiple same-Rank 'Number' Xyz Monsters, so any Number Xyz you own is extra material for them.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic Spells
hooks.why: Number S0: Utopic ZEXAL and Number 99: Utopic Dragon can be Xyz Summoned by discarding a 'Rank-Up-Magic' Spell, so every Rank-Up-Magic is a free Summoning cost for the deck.

hooks.label: Rewards negated attacks
hooks.why: Number 39: Utopia and Utopia Roots detach to negate attacks every turn, so outside cards that trigger when an attack is negated (or themselves negate attacks) chain off the deck's signature move.

hooks.label: Attaches itself as Xyz material
hooks.why: Every Utopia effect spends materials by detaching, and Xyz Agent shows the deck wants free refills, so outside cards that attach themselves to your Xyz Monsters keep the negation engine running.

hooks.label: Triggers when material is detached
hooks.why: Utopia, Utopia Ray, Lightning and the whole ladder detach as a cost on nearly every activation, so outside cards with effects when an Xyz Material is detached fire for free.

hooks.label: LIGHT Warrior support
hooks.why: Nearly every Utopia monster is a LIGHT Warrior, so generic LIGHT and Warrior searchers and boosters work across the whole Extra Deck.

profile.plan: Gives the opponent an unstoppable giant by Tributing one of their monsters, then runs the game on Kaiju Counters and the biggest monsters on the field.

hooks.label: Destroys cards on the field
hooks.why: Kyoutou Waterfront places a Kaiju Counter every time a card is sent from the field to the GY, so any outside card that blows up cards fuels the counter economy that pays for every Kaiju effect.

hooks.label: Level 8 or higher support
hooks.why: Every big Kaiju is Level 7 or higher (mostly 8–10), so outside cards whose payoffs key off high-Level monsters apply to the whole deck.

hooks.label: Rank 8 Xyz engines
hooks.why: The Level 8 Kaiju (Gameciel, Dogoran, Gadarla, Mecha-Dogoran) sit in hand waiting for a Kaiju on the other side, and outside cards that Xyz Summon with Level 8 monsters turn them into a Rank 8 toolbox.

hooks.label: Punishes attacking monsters
hooks.why: Interrupted Kaiju Slumber forces both summoned Kaiju to attack if able and locks their battle positions, so outside cards that trigger when the opponent's monster attacks get free value.

hooks.label: Flips monsters face-down
hooks.why: Kaiju Capture Mission turns a Kaiju face-down Defense Position to bank counters, and Kaiju have no flip downside, so outside cards that also flip monsters face-down stack with that game plan.

profile.plan: Fuses Aleister the Invoker with one monster of each Attribute to make a toolbox of Invoked Fusion Monsters, banishing materials from the field and GY along the way.

hooks.label: Generic Fusion Summon support
hooks.why: Invocation and Magical Meltdown revolve around Fusion Summoning, so any outside card that Fusion Summons is another way to reach the Invoked toolbox, and Meltdown even protects the summon.

hooks.label: Extra Fusion Monsters
hooks.why: Invoked Augoeides, Magistus Omega, De Anima and Elysium all use Fusion or Extra Deck monsters as material, and Hyperinvoked Aeon needs Fusion Monsters with different Attributes.

hooks.label: Monsters that want banishing
hooks.why: Invocation banishes monsters from your field and GY as Fusion Material, and Omega Summon Special Summons banished monsters back, so outside monsters with an effect when they are banished get used for free.

hooks.label: Banished zone recovery
hooks.why: Invocation recovers Aleister from banishment and Omega Summon revives banished monsters, so outside cards that return or use your banished cards keep the engine looping.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Aleister and Aleister the Invoker of Madness are Spellcasters, and Magistus Omega can Special Summon a Level 4 Spellcaster from your Deck, so generic Spellcaster support has plenty of targets.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Fiend Fusion/Link engine that lives in the GY: it discards its own monsters, sends LIGHT Fiends from Deck to GY, and recycles them as Fusion materials while equipping its Link Monsters to bosses.

hooks.label: LIGHT Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Fiendsmith monster is a LIGHT Fiend and the Fusion and Link Summoning conditions demand LIGHT Fiend materials, so generic LIGHT Fiend support feeds every Summon in the deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Engraver discards itself, Fiendsmith's Tract and Rextremende discard as a cost, so outside cards with an effect when discarded get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Lacrima and Rextremende send LIGHT Fiend monsters from the Deck and Extra Deck to the GY, so outside monsters with an effect there get milled into value.

hooks.label: Level 7+ LIGHT Fiend bosses
hooks.why: Fiendsmith in Paradise wipes the field around one Level 7 or higher LIGHT Fiend you control, so any big outside LIGHT Fiend becomes an almost-unstoppable attacker.

hooks.label: Self-summoning LIGHT Fiends
hooks.why: Requiem and Sequence need a LIGHT Fiend monster as Link material and Sanct wants a body, so outside LIGHT Fiends that Special Summon themselves extend the plays.

profile.plan: Anti-Extra-Deck Spellcasters that dump Fusion, Synchro, Xyz and Link Monsters from the Extra Deck to the GY as fuel, punish opponents who rely on them, and Ritual Summon big LIGHT bosses.

hooks.label: Extra Deck monsters that want to be milled
hooks.why: Punishment, Maximus, Alba Zoa, Lawbringer, Dogmatikacism and Nation all send monsters from your own Extra Deck to the GY, so Extra Deck monsters with effects when sent there get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Banishes Fusion or Synchro from your GY
hooks.why: Dogmatika Maximus and Dogmatikamacabre banish Fusion/Synchro Monsters from your GY as a cost, and Dogmatika Genesis wants banished Extra Deck monsters to return, so outside cards that do the same thing double as cost payers and setup.

hooks.label: Discard fodder for Albaz
hooks.why: Fallen of Albaz discards 1 card as the cost for its Fusion Summon, so outside monsters with an effect when they are discarded turn that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: LIGHT Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Nearly every Dogmatika monster is a LIGHT Spellcaster, so generic LIGHT or Spellcaster searchers, revivals and boosts work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Ritual searchers
hooks.why: Dogmatikamatrix and Dogmatikaturgy reward Ritual Summoning White Knight, White Relic and Alba Zoa, so outside cards that search or support Ritual Monsters and Ritual Spells keep that engine running.

profile.plan: DARK Plants that glue Predator Counters onto the opponent's monsters to shrink them to Level 1 and then eat them as Tribute or Fusion material, Fusion Summoning big DARK Dragons.

hooks.label: DARK monster support
hooks.why: Every Predaplant monster and nearly every Fusion in the deck is DARK, and Dragostapelia, Chimerafflesia and Greedy Venom specifically require DARK materials.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Ophrys Scorpio sends a monster from your hand to the GY as a cost, and Byblisp and Sarraceniant trigger when they are sent there, so outside monsters that reward being discarded or sent get value for free.

hooks.label: Fusion and Polymerization Spells
hooks.why: Darlingtonia Cobra and Chimerafflesia search 'Fusion' or 'Polymerization' Spells, and Verte Anaconda copies one straight from the Deck.

hooks.label: DARK Fusion Monsters
hooks.why: Chlamydosundew, Predaprime Fusion and Predaplanet all Fusion Summon any DARK Fusion Monster, so outside DARK Fusions are extra bosses the deck can make.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Ambulomides Tributes your own monster as cost to Special Summon from the Deck, and Starving Venom Predapower tributes countered monsters to negate, so outside monsters that trigger when Tributed turn that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Plant support
hooks.why: Almost every Main Deck Predaplant is a Plant, so generic Plant searchers and revivers work across the deck.

profile.plan: Dragon maids that swap between small hand-cycling forms and big Dragon forms, returning to the hand over and over to Fusion Summon Dragon Fusion Monsters that protect them.

hooks.label: Bounces your own Dragons
hooks.why: House Dragonmaid destroys an opponent's monster whenever another face-up Dragon you control returns to your hand, so outside cards that bounce your own Dragons are removal.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Laundry Dragonmaid sends the top 3 cards of your Deck to the GY when Summoned, so outside milling cards both feed the GY and trigger Dragonmaid effects.

hooks.label: Rewards being milled
hooks.why: The deck repeatedly sends its own cards to the GY via Laundry, Parlor and Hospitality, so outside monsters with an effect when sent to the GY get it for free.

hooks.label: Big generic Dragons
hooks.why: Dragonmaid Changeover and House Dragonmaid use any Dragon as Fusion Material, and Sheou specifically requires a Level 5 or higher Dragon, so outside boss Dragons slot straight into the Fusion Summons.

hooks.label: Works while banished
hooks.why: Lady's Dragonmaid banishes its materials and summons Dragonmaids from the banishment, so outside cards that use themselves or your cards while banished keep those resources live.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Every Dragonmaid monster and Fusion is a Dragon and the Fusions ask for Dragon materials, so generic Dragon support covers the whole deck.

profile.plan: Cartoon monsters that swarm while 'Toon World' is on the field, pay Life Points to attack, and then attack the opponent directly while they control no Toons.

hooks.label: Token and body generators
hooks.why: Toon Summoned Skull, Manga Ryu-Ran and Blue-Eyes Toon Dragon must Tribute monsters to Summon themselves while 'Toon World' is up, and Toon Cannon Soldier Tributes anything for burn, so cheap bodies are always useful.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Toon Cannon Soldier Tributes monsters for 500 damage each and the big Toons Tribute monsters as their Summoning cost, so outside cards that trigger off being Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Direct-attack damage triggers
hooks.why: Every Toon attacks the opponent directly through Toon World, so outside monsters with effects that trigger when they inflict battle damage go off constantly, like Toon Masked Sorcerer's draw.

hooks.label: Banished card recovery
hooks.why: Toon Kingdom banishes cards from the top of your Deck face-down by the handful, so outside cards that recover or reuse banished cards turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Rewards being discarded
hooks.why: Toon Dark Magician discards a Toon card as its effect cost, so outside monsters that trigger when a card effect discards them from the hand are free ammunition.

profile.plan: A toolbox of Quick-Play Spells that temporarily negate or protect a single monster at instant speed, paying for the strongest one by sending your other cards to the GY.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Forbidden Droplet sends any other cards from your hand and field to the GY as its cost, so outside cards with an effect when a card effect sends them there get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Quick-Play Spell recycling
hooks.why: Every Forbidden card is a Quick-Play Spell spent on the opponent's turn, so anything that recovers or Sets Quick-Play Spells from the GY keeps the toolbox looping.

hooks.label: Battle damage calculation tricks
hooks.why: Forbidden Scripture negates all other effects during damage calculation and uses each monster's original ATK, so outside cards that trigger during damage calculation still fire while Stat-modifying effects are wiped out.

profile.plan: Machine beatsticks that shut off the opponent's backrow when they attack, winning through big Tribute Summons, Fusions and piercing battle damage.

hooks.label: Gadget monsters
hooks.why: Ancient Gear Reactor Dragon and Hydra attack again when Tribute Summoned using a Gadget, and Gadjiltron Dragon and Chimera gain bonus effects for each Gadget Tributed.

hooks.label: EARTH Machine support
hooks.why: Every Ancient Gear monster is an EARTH Machine, and Ancient Gear Ballista requires 2 EARTH Machines as Link Material, so generic support for that Type and Attribute hits the whole deck.

hooks.label: Rewards being destroyed
hooks.why: Ancient Gear Catapult and Ballista destroy your own face-up cards as a cost or setup, so outside cards with an effect when they are destroyed get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Self-Tribute Summoning bosses
hooks.why: Geartown cuts Tributes by one and Ancient Gear Castle substitutes itself with counters, so outside high-Level monsters that Tribute Summon themselves come down nearly free and feed Tribute-based payoffs.

hooks.label: Machines worth discarding
hooks.why: Ancient Gear Golem - Ultimate Pound discards 1 Machine monster to attack again, so outside Machine monsters with an effect when discarded turn that cost into advantage.

profile.plan: Fairy-and-Fiend Fusion deck that splices outside LIGHT and DARK monsters into Level 8+ Fusion Monsters, with payoffs whenever cards leave the Extra Deck or the Fusion leaves the field.

hooks.label: Sends from your Extra Deck
hooks.why: Guiding Quem and Despian Luluwalilith both trigger when a card leaves the Extra Deck, so any outside card that sends Extra Deck cards to the GY turns them on.

hooks.label: LIGHT or DARK Fusion material
hooks.why: Quaeritis and Masquerade the Blazing Dragon Fusion Summon with any LIGHT or DARK monster next to a Despia monster, so outside LIGHT/DARK monsters are ready material.

hooks.label: Rewards being Fusion material
hooks.why: Dramaturge and Ad Libitum revive themselves when used as Fusion Material, and the deck Fuses constantly, so outside monsters with effects on being used as material get them for free.

hooks.label: Level 8+ Fusion bosses
hooks.why: Despia Theater only Fusion Summons and recovers Level 8 or higher Fusion Monsters, and Ad Libitum can revive one from banished or GY, so any big outside Fusion is a valid payoff.

hooks.label: LIGHT Spellcaster with matching stats
hooks.why: Despian Luluwalilith Special Summons a LIGHT Spellcaster monster whose ATK equals its DEF straight from the hand or Deck, so such outside monsters are free bodies.

profile.plan: Flip Effect Spellcasters that steal opposing monsters of each Attribute, then upgrade into Familiar-Possessed forms and Link Charmers that revive monsters from the opponent's Graveyard, all powered by Attribute diversity.

hooks.label: Flip monster support
hooks.why: Every base Charmer is a Flip Effect Monster that steals a monster on Flip, so cards that flip your monsters face-up or protect them in face-down Defense Position keep the thefts coming.

hooks.label: Fills the opponent's GY
hooks.why: The Link Charmers Special Summon a monster of their Attribute from the opponent's Graveyard, so any outside card that puts the opponent's monsters there gives them targets.

hooks.label: Attribute diversity payoffs
hooks.why: Charmer Quartet in Bloom and Awakening of the Possessed gain ATK for each different Attribute on the field, so cards that change or add Attributes widen the gap.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is a Spellcaster and Unpossessed and Charmers of the Grand Circle summon or revive Spellcasters with 1500 DEF, so generic Spellcaster support covers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Triggers when discarded
hooks.why: The Channelers discard this card plus another monster of their Attribute as a cost to search, so outside monsters with an effect when they are discarded get it for free.

profile.plan: Reveal monsters in hand and gamble on random discards; each Danger! pays off when discarded by an effect, Special Summoning itself or blowing something up, so the deck turns hand-throwing into board advantage.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Every Danger! monster triggers when discarded by a card effect, so outside monsters with their own 'if this card is discarded' effect get set off for free by the deck's random discards.

hooks.label: Discard outlets
hooks.why: Nessie, Mothman and friends only get their reveal-and-discard rolling when other effects can dump cards from your hand, so any outside card that makes you discard is another activator for the whole hand.

hooks.label: DARK support
hooks.why: Every Danger! monster is DARK, so generic DARK searchers, revivers and boosts work across the whole deck.

profile.plan: Warriors that swarm the field by Special Summoning each other, build up Bushido Counters, and protect their leaders by destroying other Six Samurai instead — synchroing into Shi En to negate.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Six Samurai monster is a Warrior and Shi En requires Warrior Synchro materials, so generic Warrior searchers, revivers and boosts work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Warrior Tuners
hooks.why: Both Shi En synchros need a Warrior Tuner plus Six Samurai non-Tuners, and the deck's own Tuners are low-stat, so any outside Warrior Tuner is usable material.

hooks.label: Places Bushido Counters
hooks.why: Gateway of the Six, Six Samurai United, Shien's Dojo and Temple of the Six all spend Bushido Counters from the field, and Battle Shogun searches cards that place them, so any outside card that places Bushido Counters is fuel.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Mizuho and Hand of the Six Samurai Tribute another Six Samurai as a cost, and Shinai triggers when it is Tributed, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be destroyed
hooks.why: Shien, Zanji, Irou and the rest constantly destroy their own Six Samurai as a substitute, so outside monsters that trigger when destroyed by a card effect get that trigger repeatedly.

profile.plan: Warrior knights that pile Equip Spells onto themselves, milling Noble Arms and equipping FIRE Warriors from the Deck to fuel Synchro and Xyz bosses.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Isolde searches any Warrior and Durendal, Renaud and the Infernoble Knights all revive or equip Warrior monsters, so generic Warrior help works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: FIRE Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Infernoble Knight and the Infernoble Arms are FIRE Warriors, and Durendal, Joyeuse and Astolfo specifically summon or search FIRE Warriors.

hooks.label: Equip Spells with GY effects
hooks.why: Isolde and Ogier send Equip Spells from the Deck to the GY as fuel, so outside Equip Spells that do something when sent there get it for free.

hooks.label: Cards that equip things
hooks.why: Emperor Charles destroys a card every time an Equip Card becomes equipped to any monster, even during the Damage Step, so outside cards that equip repeatedly are removal engines.

hooks.label: LIGHT Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Gawayn Special Summons itself and Black Laundsallyn summons off a face-up LIGHT Normal Monster, so outside LIGHT Normal Monsters are free extenders.

hooks.label: Sends your Equip Spells
hooks.why: Charles the Great negates by sending an Equip Spell from hand or field to the GY as a cost, so any outside card that supplies or recycles Equip Spells keeps the negation live.

profile.plan: Tribute Summons the three Egyptian Gods with 3 Tributes apiece, flooding the field with Tokens and multi-Tribute slimes to pay for them, then cashes in with pay-LP and Tribute-triggered payoffs.

hooks.label: Tribute fodder generators
hooks.why: The Gods need 3 Tributes each and Soul Crossing lets you Tribute even opponent's monsters, so anything that fills your field with Tokens or bodies fuels the Summon.

hooks.label: Extra Tribute Summons
hooks.why: Ancient Chant grants an extra Tribute Summon, and the deck wants to stack several Gods in one turn, so more extra Normal Summons for high-Level monsters keep it going.

hooks.label: Reward being Tributed
hooks.why: Reactor Slime and the Gods Tribute your monsters as cost, so outside monsters that trigger when Tributed get that for free.

hooks.label: Level 10 WATER monsters
hooks.why: Egyptian God Slime is Summoned by Tributing 1 Level 10 Aqua with 0 ATK, and Fusion Summons with a Level 10 WATER material, so big WATER monsters fit.

hooks.label: Easy self-Tribute Summons
hooks.why: The deck's engine all revolvees around Tribute Summoning, so outside bosses that Tribute Summon themselves cheaply ride the same support like Soul Crossing and Ancient Chant.

hooks.label: Make yourself take damage
hooks.why: Guardian Slime Special Summons itself from hand when you take battle or effect damage, so outside cards that burn your own LP turn on that trigger.

profile.plan: A family of Trap Holes (and Dark Hole) that punish the opponent's Summons, attacks and monster effects with destruction, banishment and negation, plus a Dragon that feeds on mass destruction.

hooks.label: Destroys all monsters
hooks.why: Dark Hole Dragon Special Summons itself from the hand or GY whenever a card effect that does not target destroys a monster, so outside mass-removal like the deck's own Dark Hole sets it off.

hooks.label: Normal Traps worth discarding
hooks.why: Traptrix Holeutea activates by discarding 1 Normal Trap, so outside Normal Traps with Graveyard effects get used twice.

hooks.label: Banishes Traps from your GY
hooks.why: Treacherous Trap Hole only works while your GY has no Trap Cards, so outside cards that remove your Traps from the Graveyard keep it live.

hooks.label: Summons from the top of the Deck
hooks.why: Time Dimension Hole Special Summons whatever Normal-Summonable monster it excavates, so outside cards that stack or send monsters to the top of the Deck make it reliable.

profile.plan: A Plant/Dragon Synchro deck that recycles Rose Dragons as Synchro Material, banishes Plant monsters from its Graveyard as costs, and collapses the field with Black Rose Dragon.

hooks.label: Plant support
hooks.why: Nearly every card in the deck is or works on Plant monsters — Mark of the Rose, Thorn of Malice, Rose Lover, Twilight Rose Knight and Frozen Rose all care about Plants.

hooks.label: Plant Tuners
hooks.why: White Rose Dragon Special Summons itself from the hand if you control a Dragon or Plant Tuner, and Bird of Roses Summons two Plant Tuners from the Deck.

hooks.label: Synchro Summons your cards
hooks.why: Red Rose Dragon and White Rose Dragon trigger when sent to the GY as Synchro Material, so any outside card that Synchro Summons using your monsters sets them off.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished from the GY
hooks.why: Black Rose Dragon, Splendid Rose and Mark of the Rose all banish Plant monsters from your GY as a cost, so Plant monsters with an effect when banished get it for free.

hooks.label: Big Plant bosses
hooks.why: Rose Paladin searches any Level 7 or higher Plant monster from the Deck, so outside Plants of that size are one card away.

hooks.label: Destroys your Plants
hooks.why: Crossrose Dragon Summons a Rose Dragon from the GY when a monster you control is destroyed by a card effect, and Blue Rose Dragon and Revival Rose revive their targets when destroyed.

profile.plan: Banish Beast, Beast-Warrior and Winged Beast monsters from the GY to Link Summon big monsters, milling the Deck to load the GY and getting bonuses when its cards are sent there or banished.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Fraktall and Kitt send monsters from the Deck to the GY to load it, so any outside card that mills feeds their engine.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Shuraig, Ferrijit, Nervall, Kitt and Mouser all trigger when sent to the GY, so outside monsters of the right Types with GY triggers get used for free.

hooks.label: Special Summons banished monsters
hooks.why: Fraktall, Nervall and Kerass banish their GY monsters as a cost and Revolt brings banished monsters back, so outside cards that revive banished monsters keep the resources alive.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior and Winged Beast support
hooks.why: Every card in the deck is a Beast, Beast-Warrior or Winged Beast and locks you into those Types for Link Material, so generic support for them works across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Other Beast Link monsters
hooks.why: Fraktall, Nervall, Kerass and Hammer Summon any Beast, Beast-Warrior or Winged Beast Link Monster from the Extra Deck, so every such Link monster outside the archetype is a bonus boss.

profile.plan: A Rank 4 Xyz engine of DARK Winged Beasts that stacks its own monsters as materials and climbs the Ranks with Rank-Up-Magic Spells to reach giant Falcons with wipe, burn and lock effects.

hooks.label: Other Rank-Up-Magic Spells
hooks.why: Wise Strix, Tribute Lanius and Brave Strix all search or Set Rank-Up-Magic Spells generically, and Soul Shave Force / Skip Force can revive any Raidraptor Xyz they rank up, so the archetype's own searchers happily fetch outside Rank-Up-Magics.

hooks.label: Level 4 DARK Winged Beasts
hooks.why: Force Strix searches any Level 4 DARK Winged Beast and Wise Strix Special Summons one straight from the Deck, so outside monsters with that exact typing plug straight into the engine.

hooks.label: Winged Beast support
hooks.why: Every Raidraptor monster is a Winged Beast, Force Strix gains ATK for each Winged Beast you control, and Pain Lanius only allows Winged Beast Xyz Summons with it, so Type-wide support hits the whole deck.

hooks.label: Rewards while an Xyz material
hooks.why: Raider's Wing and Brave Strix hand extra effects to the Xyz Monster using them as material, so outside monsters that do something while attached as Xyz Material stack on top of the archetype's Falcons.

hooks.label: Effects when detached
hooks.why: Raidraptor Xyz Monsters constantly detach materials as a cost for their effects, so outside cards that trigger when detached from an Xyz Monster get it for free.

hooks.label: Feeds the GY with Xyz Monsters
hooks.why: Skip Force, Rise Rank-Up-Magic Raidraptor's Force and Final Fortress Falcon all re-use Raidraptor Xyz Monsters from the GY or banishment as material or revival targets, so outside cards that send or cycle Xyz Monsters through the GY keep those payoffs live.

profile.plan: DARK Dragons that blow themselves up on purpose: every Rokket self-destructs when targeted by a Link Monster's effect and then revives another Rokket from the Deck, chaining destruction into Link Summons.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Every Rokket Dragon plus Squib Draw and Tactical Exchanger wants to be destroyed on the field, so any outside card that destroys your own monster is another trigger for their End Phase revival.

hooks.label: Wants to be destroyed
hooks.why: The deck destroys its own board constantly (Rokket Tracer, Squib Draw, the Rokket Dragons' self-destructs), so outside monsters with an effect when they are destroyed get it for free.

hooks.label: DARK Dragon support
hooks.why: Nearly every Rokket is a DARK Dragon and the deck locks itself into DARK Extra Deck Summons, so generic DARK Dragon search, revive and boost cards fit the whole deck.

hooks.label: Level 7 DARK Dragons
hooks.why: Rokket Loader searches any Level 7 DARK Dragon and Rokket Synchron revives Level 5+ DARK Dragons, so big outside DARK Dragons are free bodies.

hooks.label: Rewards Link Material
hooks.why: Noctovision Dragon draws when sent to the GY as Link Material and Rokket Coder substitutes DARK monsters from hand as Borrel material, so outside cards with effects when used as Link Material stack on the deck's Link Summons.

hooks.label: Makes DARK monsters live
hooks.why: Rokket Caliber Tributes itself to Special Summon a DARK Dragon or Machine from hand and Rokket Loader can turn a monster DARK, so big DARK Machines and hand-summoning DARK support plug straight in.

profile.plan: Fiend demons that destroy their own cards on purpose, chaining summons and Link Summons off every destruction, including using the opponent's monsters as Link material.

hooks.label: Destroys your own cards
hooks.why: Nearly every Unchained monster summons itself or a teammate when a card you control is destroyed by card effect (Aruha, Rakea, Sarama, the Set Spells/Traps), so outside cards that blow up your own Fiends or Set cards are activators.

hooks.label: Wants to be destroyed by card effect
hooks.why: The archetype's destruction is indiscriminate, so outside monsters with an effect when they are destroyed by a card effect get it for free while sitting alongside Unchained cards.

hooks.label: Triggers off any destruction
hooks.why: Unchained Abomination and Unchained Ogre Shara (from the GY) respond whenever ANY card on the field is destroyed by card effect, so outside cards whose destruction effect also removes the opponent's cards chain into free removal.

hooks.label: Set card destroyed rewards
hooks.why: Abomination's Prison, Escape and Wailing all Special Summon an Unchained monster from the Deck when the Set card is destroyed, so outside Spells/Traps with a payoff when their Set self is destroyed extend the engine.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Unchained monster is a Fiend and Sharvara, Shara and Yama Special Summon Fiends from the hand or GY, and the deck locks you into Fiends, so generic Fiend support fits the whole deck.

hooks.label: DARK Link monsters
hooks.why: Anguish, Rage and Disaster Link Summon a DARK Link Monster using the opponent's monster plus your card as material, so any outside DARK Link Monster is a valid boss to steal their monsters into.

profile.plan: Synchro deck built around Stardust Dragon and its upgraded forms, which Tribute themselves to negate destruction, Summons and activations, then return from the Graveyard; the small LIGHT Dragons and Tuners feed endless Synchro Summons.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Stardust Synchron and Stardust Wurm Tribute monsters as a cost, and Victim Sanctuary and Stardust Wish have extra payoffs whenever a monster is Tributed, so outside monsters that trigger on being Tributed get used for free.

hooks.label: Level 1 LIGHT Dragons
hooks.why: Stardust Wurm Special Summons Level 1 LIGHT Dragons from the hand and GY, and Arrive in Light stacks a Level 1 Dragon from the hand or Deck, so the deck is full of ways to deploy them.

hooks.label: Low-Level Tuners
hooks.why: Accel Synchro Stardust Dragon revives a Level 2 or lower Tuner and Arrive in Light Special Summons a Tuner from the hand after each Synchro Summon, so Tuners that summon themselves keep the chains going.

hooks.label: Dragon Synchro revival
hooks.why: Stardust Shimmer, Phantom and Chronicle Spark Dragon all reward controlling and reviving Dragon Synchro Monsters, so outside cards that bring back or boost Dragon Synchros slot straight in.

hooks.label: Level 8 Dragon boss support
hooks.why: Stardust Wurm and Stardust Mirage only need any Level 8 or higher Dragon Synchro Monster on the field, so big outside Dragon Synchro bosses other than Stardust also switch those effects on.

profile.plan: DARK Zombies that pay Life Points to search and swarm, steal opposing monsters straight out of the Graveyard, and rip cards from the opponent's Deck while draining them with battle damage.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: Every Vampire monster is a Zombie, and Vampire Takeover and Vampire Sucker lock or reward controlling Zombie monsters specifically.

hooks.label: Mills the opponent's Deck
hooks.why: Vampire Kingdom triggers whenever a card is sent from the opponent's Deck to the GY, and Vampire Lord, Duke and Grace force those sends themselves, so any outside mill feeds the engine.

hooks.label: Summons from the opponent's GY
hooks.why: Vampire Sucker draws a card whenever a Zombie is Special Summoned from either GY, and Voivode can Tribute 2 monsters to revive itself when your opponent's GY is Summoned from, so outside cards that revive from the GY chain these payoffs.

hooks.label: Easy Tribute Summons
hooks.why: Vampire Dragon searches when a Tribute Summoned monster leaves the field and Vampire's Domain grants extra Normal Summons, so outside monsters that Tribute Summon themselves cheaply fit right in.

hooks.label: Destroys monsters by battle
hooks.why: Fraulein, Scarlet Scourge, Grimson and Vampire Baby Special Summon monsters they destroy by battle, and Fraulein pumps a Zombie's ATK during damage calculation to guarantee the kill.

hooks.label: Level 5+ Zombie special summoner
hooks.why: Vampire Grace Special Summons itself from the GY whenever a Level 5+ Zombie is Special Summoned by a Zombie effect, so outside Zombie monsters that revive big Zombies trigger it for free.

profile.plan: A Spellcaster lockdown deck built around the Necrovalley Field Spell, which seals both Graveyards while Gravekeeper's flip monsters, Tributes and searchers grind out advantage under that lock.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Nearly every Gravekeeper's monster is a DARK Spellcaster, from Spy to Visionary, so generic Spellcaster searchers, boosters and revival hit the whole deck.

hooks.label: Flip Summon support
hooks.why: Spy, Guard and Ambusher are Flip Effect monsters you want turned face-up or Summoned face-down, so cards that flip monsters or reward Flip Summons power the deck's core engine.

hooks.label: Easy Tribute Summon bosses
hooks.why: Oracle, Visionary and Chief all pay off Tribute Summons, so big outside monsters that Tribute Summon themselves cheaply slot straight into that payoff.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Descendant and Cannonholder Tribute your face-up Gravekeeper's monsters as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Field Spell protection
hooks.why: The whole deck switches on with Necrovalley on the field, and Shaman already stops opponents destroying Field Spells, so cards that protect or search your own Field Spell keep the lock alive.

hooks.label: Battle damage finishers
hooks.why: Spear Soldier inflicts piercing damage and Vassal turns its battle damage into effect damage, so cards that boost battle damage or punish it synergise with the beatdown plan.

profile.plan: Ritual Summons huge Fairy negators (Herald of Perfection and Ultimateness) that fuel their omni-negates by sending Fairy monsters from the hand to the GY, recycling that fuel over and over.

hooks.label: Recycles Fairy monsters to hand
hooks.why: Perfection, Ultimateness and Mirage Lights all send Fairies from your hand to the GY as a negate cost, so anything that reloads Fairies into your hand keeps the negates live.

hooks.label: Fairies that trigger in the GY
hooks.why: The deck sends Fairies from the hand to the GY several times per turn as negate costs, so outside Fairies with an effect when sent there pay off for free.

hooks.label: Ritual Spells that Tribute Fairies
hooks.why: Oracle of the Herald and Dawn of the Herald Tribute monsters from hand or field for the Ritual Summon, and Arc Light searches any Ritual Spell, so generic Ritual support that Tributes your Fairies slots straight in.

hooks.label: Low-Level Fairies
hooks.why: Diviner of the Herald Special Summons a Level 2 or lower Fairy from hand or Deck when Tributed, so any small Fairy with a useful effect comes along for free.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is a LIGHT Fairy and the negates need Fairy fuel, so generic Fairy searchers, revival and boosters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sanctuary in the Sky cards
hooks.why: Zeradias searches The Sanctuary in the Sky and depends on it staying on the field, so outside cards built around that Field Spell pair naturally.

profile.plan: DARK Reptiles that Tribute themselves and each other as costs, triggering searches and self-revival each time, and cap out with Level 8 Ritual bosses Summoned by Tributing Reptiles.

hooks.label: Tributes your Reptiles
hooks.why: Every Mitsurugi monster has an 'If this card is Tributed' trigger, so any outside card that Tributes your Reptiles as a cost or effect is free advantage.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: The deck Tributes from hand, field and Deck many times per turn (Prayers, Magatama, Ritual, Mikoto redirect), so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Summons Reptile tribute fodder
