hooks.why: Mitsurugi Ritual and Magatama Tribute Reptiles totaling Level 8, so outside cards that Special Summon or Token-summon Reptiles keep the Rituals flowing.

hooks.label: Tributes opponent's monsters
hooks.why: Wousu Summons itself by Tributing an opponent's monster and Sacred Boundary makes the opponent Tribute one, so cards that remove threats by Tribute fit the theme and dodge destruction protection.

hooks.label: Reptile support
hooks.why: Every Mitsurugi monster is a Reptile and the Ritual Spells only accept Reptile materials, so generic Reptile search, revival and protection works across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Reptile Ritual support
hooks.why: The Ritual Spells Summon 'any Reptile Ritual Monster', so outside Reptile Ritual Monsters and generic Ritual support for them are directly usable here.

profile.plan: EARTH Machine trains that swarm Level 10 bodies and stack them into Rank 10/11 Xyz cannons, turning detached materials into burn and destruction.

hooks.label: Level 10 EARTH Machines
hooks.why: The deck constantly Special Summons Level 10 EARTH Machines to stack into Rank 10 Xyz Summons, so any outside card of that shape is free material.

hooks.label: Rank 10 Machine Xyz bosses
hooks.why: Juggernaut Liebe can be Xyz Summoned on top of any Rank 10 Machine Xyz Monster, so other archetypes' Rank 10 Machine Xyz bosses become upgrade steps.

hooks.label: Detaches Xyz materials
hooks.why: Heavy Freight Train Derricrane destroys a card when detached to activate an Xyz effect, and Barrage Blast converts detached materials into removal, so any outside Xyz monster with a detach-cost effect triggers payoffs.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Nearly every card in the deck is a Machine, and multiple cards like Snow Plow Hustle Rustle and Night Train Blue Traveler lock you into Machine Summons, so generic Machine support works on everything.

hooks.label: Bonus effects as Xyz material
hooks.why: Express Train Trolley Olley shows the deck overlays Level 4 Machines into Xyz Monsters, so outside monsters that grant effects when used as Xyz Material stack onto the cannons.

hooks.label: Sends your own field cards
hooks.why: Super Express Bullet Train requires sending 2 other cards you control to the GY to attack, and Exceptional Schedule and Anger Knuckle send cards you control as costs, so outside cards that send your field cards feed those costs.

profile.plan: Spellcasters and Dragons that Fusion Summon using monsters from the hand and field, and pay off each material by setting a Dracotail Spell/Trap from the Deck.

hooks.label: Fusion Summons from the hand
hooks.why: Faimena, Mululu, Rahu and Ketu all Fusion Summon using monsters from your hand or field, so outside cards that Fusion Summon by the same route extend the deck's core play.

hooks.label: Rewards being Fusion material
hooks.why: Arthalion, Gulamel and Shaulas require a monster in the hand as Fusion material, so any outside monster that triggers when it is sent to the GY or used as Fusion material gets its effect for free.

hooks.label: Sends two monsters at once
hooks.why: Arthalion, Gulamel and Shaulas revive themselves from the GY whenever 2 or more monsters are sent to the GY at the same time, so any outside card that sends multiple of your monsters there is a free revival trigger.

hooks.label: Dragon or Spellcaster Fusions
hooks.why: Faimena and Ketu can Fusion Summon any Dragon or Spellcaster Fusion Monster from the Extra Deck, not just Dracotail ones, so outside bosses of those kinds are live payoffs.

hooks.label: Fusion Monster protection
hooks.why: The deck commits to Fusion Monsters only (Mululu and Rahu lock the Extra Deck to Fusions) and Gulamel's removal depends on you controlling one, so outside cards that support or protect Fusion Monsters fit the deck's whole board.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Faimena, Lukias and Phryxul are Spellcasters and Urgula recycles Spellcaster Dracotails specifically, so generic Spellcaster support reaches the deck's search and Fusion engine.

profile.plan: A hand-trap deck that Summons Tuners from the hand to negate your opponent's activations, then constantly banishes and returns its own Psychic monsters, Synchro Summoning PSY-Framelords along the way.

hooks.label: Banishes your Psychics
hooks.why: PSY-Framelord Lambda searches whenever a face-up Psychic you control is banished face-up, and PSY-Frame Accelerator and Overload banish your own PSY-Frames as routine plays.

hooks.label: Triggers when banished
hooks.why: The deck banishes its own monsters every turn — End Phase banishing from the Framegears, Accelerator and Omega — so any outside monster with an effect when it is banished gets it for free.

hooks.label: Recovers banished cards
hooks.why: PSY-Framelord Omega returns banished cards to the GY and the deck's monsters keep leaving play face-up, so cards that fetch banished cards back keep the engine fueled.

hooks.label: Psychic support
hooks.why: Every PSY-Frame card is a Psychic monster, so generic Psychic search, revival and boost cards work on the whole deck.

profile.plan: Wyrm spirits that self-Summon when you control no Effect Monsters and spend themselves from hand or GY to protect your face-up non-Effect Monsters, winning through Normal Monsters and Wyrm Links and Synchros.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Nearly every Tenyi effect keys off controlling a face-up non-Effect Monster, so any outside card that Summons or supports Normal Monsters turns the whole deck on.

hooks.label: Wyrm support
hooks.why: Every Tenyi monster, Link and Synchro is a Wyrm, and Ashuna locks you into Wyrms, so generic Wyrm support covers the entire deck.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Heavenly Dragon Circle and Tenyinfinity Tribute a Wyrm monster as a cost, so outside Wyrms with an effect when Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be milled
hooks.why: Vessel for the Dragon Cycle sends a Wyrm from the Deck to the GY, so outside Wyrms with an effect when sent to the GY are free value.

hooks.label: Wyrm Synchro bosses
hooks.why: Suruya's payoff and Draco Berserker's materials want Wyrm Synchro Monsters, so outside Wyrm Synchros are the best Extra Deck targets.

hooks.label: Field Spell payoffs
hooks.why: Mula Adhara adds any Field Spell from the Deck when Synchro Summoned, so strong standalone Field Spells are effectively searchable.

profile.plan: WATER control monsters that lock the opponent's Summons, Spells and attacks while swarming Tuners to Synchro Summon dragons like Trishula, paying costs by discarding, Tributing and banishing their own cards.

hooks.label: WATER monster support
hooks.why: Revealer, Hexa Spirit and the Ice Barrier trap lock you into WATER monsters, and the Synchros demand WATER materials, so generic WATER support works on nearly every card in the deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Brionac, Gungnir, Geomancer and Revealer all pay by discarding cards, so outside monsters with an effect when discarded turn that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Hexa Spirit and Strategist send Ice Barrier monsters from hand or Deck to the GY, and the Ice Barrier trap sends any Level 5+ WATER monster from the Deck, so outside WATER monsters with graveyard effects get there for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Winds Over the Ice Barrier Tributes your Ice Barrier monsters and Mirror Mage Tributes any other Effect Monster, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed make that cost free.

hooks.label: WATER Synchro support
hooks.why: The deck's bosses are WATER Synchro Monsters, and Mirror Mage locks you into Summoning nothing but them, so outside cards that search, Summon or protect WATER Synchros fit perfectly.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck of Level 7 Dragons that sets Scales, Pendulum Summons big monsters, cashes in its own Pendulum cards by destroying them for searches and extra Summons, and mixes Fusion, Synchro, Xyz, Ritual and Link bosses around them.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Almost every Odd-Eyes monster is a Dragon, and the Fusions and Odd-Eyes Advent specifically call for Dragon monsters, so generic Dragon support reaches the whole deck.

hooks.label: Dragon Ritual Monsters
hooks.why: Odd-Eyes Advent can Ritual Summon any Dragon Ritual Monster from the hand or GY, and Pendulumgraph Dragon searches the Ritual Spell for it.

hooks.label: Destroys your Pendulum cards
hooks.why: Sky Iris, Odd-Eyes Override Dragon and Supreme King Dragon Odd-Eyes all pay off destroying your own Pendulum cards, so outside cards that destroy your cards become search and draw enablers.

hooks.label: Pendulum monsters that trigger when destroyed
hooks.why: Butler, Valet, Arcray and the Four Heavenly Dragons all convert being destroyed into a Pendulum Zone placement or recovery, so destruction-happy outside cards give them value for free.

hooks.label: Shuffles Extra Deck Pendulums back
hooks.why: Odd-Eyes Vortex Dragon's negation costs shuffling a face-up Pendulum Monster from your Extra Deck into the Deck, so any card that recycles face-up Extra Deck Pendulums feeds the negate.

profile.plan: Level 1 Spellcaster Ritual and Fusion monsters that steal the opponent's monsters as Equip Spells and turn their ATK against them.

hooks.label: Sends itself to the GY
hooks.why: Golden-Eyes Idol and Faceless Magician trigger when sent to the GY or banished by a card effect, and Relinquished Fusion banishes materials from the GY, so outside monsters with effects that send or banish your own cards get them going for free.

hooks.label: Fusion Summons from the GY
hooks.why: Relinquished Fusion summons by banishing materials from the hand, field and GY, so any outside card that Fusion Summons using GY material fits the deck's game plan.

hooks.label: Banished as Fusion material
hooks.why: Relinquished Fusion banishes its materials, so outside cards that have an effect when they are banished, or when used as Fusion material, are paid off by the deck's own summoning.

hooks.label: Level 1 monsters
hooks.why: Relinquished Anima needs a Level 1 non-Token monster as Link material, Black Illusion Ritual Tributes a Level 1+ monster, and the deck is built around Level 1 bodies, so outside cards that summon or supply Level 1 monsters are extra fuel.

hooks.label: Equip Card support
hooks.why: The archetype wins by holding the opponent's monsters as Equip Spells on its own monsters, so outside cards that move, exploit or count Equip Cards get steady work.

hooks.label: DARK Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Eyes Restrict card is a DARK Spellcaster, so generic support for that Type and Attribute works across the whole deck.

profile.plan: Banish-centric Warriors and Machines that banish their own cards and the opponent's, then come back or retrieve them from the banished zone for value.

hooks.label: Banishes your own cards
hooks.why: Scout Plane, Survivor, Patrol Plane, Destroyer and D.D. Post all trigger or fuel up when your cards get banished, so outside cards that banish from your own hand, field or GY are activators.

hooks.label: Triggers while banished
hooks.why: The deck banishes its own cards constantly, so outside cards with an effect when they are banished get their trigger for free.

hooks.label: Banishes instead of GY
hooks.why: D.D. Dynamite and D.D. Post pay off for cards in the banished zone, so cards that banish everything instead of sending it to the Graveyard grow the payoff.

hooks.label: DARK support
hooks.why: Over half the deck is DARK, and Dark Dimension Soldier Special Summons banished DARK monsters specifically, so generic DARK support has plenty of targets.

hooks.label: Scales with banished cards
hooks.why: D.D. Post boosts ATK for each of your banished cards and Assault Carrier wants exactly 3 banished, so outside cards whose payoff counts banished cards stack with the deck's own counters.

profile.plan: DARK Machine Link monsters that banish themselves from the GY as costs to Special Summon and recycle each other, culminating in Link bosses and the Rank 8 Dingirsu, while locking you into DARK monsters.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Orcustrated Return, Orcustrated Babel, Galatea-I and Orcustrated Einsatz all send cards from your hand or Deck to the GY as costs, so outside monsters with GY effects when sent get there for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: Orcustrated Einsatz and Orcustrated Core banish your cards from hand, field or GY as costs, so outside monsters with effects that trigger when banished get triggered on purpose.

hooks.label: DARK Machine support
hooks.why: Every Orcust monster is a DARK Machine and Orcust Crescendo even locks you into DARK Machine Special Summons, so generic DARK Machine support works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Recovers banished Machines
hooks.why: Galatea, Longirsu and Orcustrion all shuffle your banished Machine monsters back into the Deck, and Dingirsu attaches them as material, so cards that retrieve banished monsters give the deck more fuel and reuse.

hooks.label: DARK Machine Link Monsters
hooks.why: Galatea and Longirsu need an Orcust plus Effect Monsters as Link material, and Dingirsu can be Xyz Summoned using an Orcust Link Monster, so other DARK Machine Links slot into the engine and share the DARK locks.

hooks.label: Level 8 DARK monsters
hooks.why: Dingirsu, the Orcust of the Evening Star wants 2 Level 8 monsters on board, and the deck's DARK-only Special Summon locks mean Level 8 DARK monsters are the best bodies to stack for it.

profile.plan: A Fiend trap-deck that floods the field with Normal Traps, triggers off every Normal Trap activation and every monster removed by a Normal Trap effect, and Sets more traps from the Deck as the combo goes.

hooks.label: Normal Traps with removal
hooks.why: Arianna, Ariane, Lovely and Welcome all pay off when a monster leaves the field by your Normal Trap effect, and Lady/Farewelcome/Set-Up fetch or Set non-Labrynth Normal Traps from the Deck.

hooks.label: Normal Traps it can Set
hooks.why: Labrynth Set-Up Sets non-Labrynth Normal Traps straight from the Deck and Lovely Sets any Normal Trap from the GY, so every Normal Trap in the database is live.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Labrynth monster is a Fiend, the Welcome traps Special Summon Fiends, and the field spell summons a Fiend off any outside Normal Trap, so generic Fiend support works on everything here.

hooks.label: Level 8 Fiend bosses
hooks.why: Big Welcome Labrynth's GY effect only targets an opponent's card if you control a Level 8 or higher Fiend monster, so outside bosses of that shape upgrade the deck's removal.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Stovie Torbie and Chandraglier discard a card as a cost to Set Labrynth cards, and Labrynth cards themselves send from the hand to activate, so outside monsters with an effect when discarded get used for free.

profile.plan: Destroys its own FIRE monsters on purpose — by hand, field or Deck — because every Fire King has a bonus effect when it is blown up, then revives and Xyz Summons Level/Rank 8 FIRE bosses.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Ulcanix, Kirin and Sanctuary all pay for effects by destroying a FIRE monster in your hand or field, so any outside card that destroys your own monster triggers Garunix, Barong and Yaksha for free.

hooks.label: Bonus when destroyed
hooks.why: The deck destroys its own monsters several times a turn, so outside monsters with an effect when they are destroyed get triggered for free alongside the Fire Kings.

hooks.label: FIRE Beast-type support
hooks.why: Onslaught, Echelon, Ulcanix and Arvata all specifically fetch or summon FIRE Beast, Beast-Warrior or Winged Beast monsters, so support for those Types hits the whole deck.

hooks.label: Rank 8 FIRE Xyz bosses
hooks.why: The Fire Kings are all Level 8 and Sanctuary Xyz Summons a FIRE Xyz Monster with them during the opponent's turn, so more FIRE Xyz monsters give the deck extra bosses.

hooks.label: Fiend Tuners
hooks.why: Cursed Fire King Doom Burst Special Summons itself from hand whenever you control a Fiend Tuner, so any Fiend Tuner turns it into a free body.

profile.plan: Discard and banish its own LIGHT and DARK Thunder monsters to search, then Fusion Summon big Thunder bosses and pay costs by banishing more Thunder monsters from the GY.

hooks.label: Banishes your Thunder monsters
hooks.why: Dragondark, Dragonroar, Dragonhawk and Dragonmatrix all trigger when banished, so any outside card that banishes your Thunder monsters sets them off.

hooks.label: Recovers banished Thunder monsters
hooks.why: Thunder Dragon Fusion uses face-up banished materials, Dragonhawk and Dragonroar reuse banished Thunder Dragons, and Duo puts banished cards back in the Deck, so the deck wants ways to get banished Thunder monsters back.

hooks.label: Discards Thunder monsters
hooks.why: Every Thunder Dragon main Deck monster's engine effect is discarding itself, so outside cards that discard Thunder monsters from your hand trigger and extend that.

hooks.label: Thunder support
hooks.why: Colossus, Titan, Thunderstormech and Fusion all demand Thunder monsters as materials, and Discharge and Hundred Thunders lock you into Thunder, so generic Thunder support fits the whole deck.

hooks.label: Banishes LIGHT and DARK from GY
hooks.why: Thunder Dragonduo Special Summons itself by banishing 1 LIGHT and 1 DARK monster from your GY, so outside cards that banish those Attributes as a cost or effect fuel it while feeding the banish triggers.

profile.plan: A WIND Machine engine that swarms the field with Speedroid Tuners and Levels 3–4 monsters, then converts them into Synchro and Fusion bosses, banishing its own cards from the GY as costs along the way.

hooks.label: WIND monster support
hooks.why: Taketomborg Special Summons itself off any WIND monster and locks you into WIND Summons, and Horse Stilts sends WIND monsters from the Deck, so the whole engine runs on WIND.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Barbaroid and Pair Cycroid Fusion Summon using Machine monsters, and Mixeroid Tributes Machines and banishes them from the GY, so generic Machine help hits nearly everything in the deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished from the GY
hooks.why: Den-Den Daiko Duke, Tri-Eyed Dice and Speed Recovery all banish the deck's own cards from the Graveyard as costs, so outside monsters with an effect when banished trigger for free.

hooks.label: Gets value when Tributed
hooks.why: Mixeroid and Taketomborg Tribute the deck's monsters as costs, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get used for free.

hooks.label: Mills WIND monsters
hooks.why: Horse Stilts sends any WIND monster from the Deck to the GY, feeding Speed Recovery and Den-Den Daiko Duke, so outside WIND monsters with Graveyard effects pair with it.

hooks.label: Gains effects in the GY
hooks.why: Den-Den Daiko Duke revives Speedroid Tuners from the GY and Speed Recovery recycles them, so the deck keeps mining its Graveyard for more Summons.

profile.plan: A deck-out control deck of Quick-Play Spells that Special Summons Fusion monsters from the Extra Deck while banishing the opponent's Deck card by card, dodging its own Battle Phase skips.

hooks.label: Banishes the opponent's Deck
hooks.why: Every Runick Quick-Play and Freki banish cards off the top of the opponent's Deck as the win condition, so outside cards that banish from the opponent's Deck accelerate the deck-out.

hooks.label: More Quick-Play Spells
hooks.why: Runick Allure banishes the top card of the opponent's Deck every time any Quick-Play Spell activates, so every outside Quick-Play Spell is extra damage, and Runick Fountain's recycle-and-draw rewards playing more of them.

hooks.label: Punishes banished cards
hooks.why: The deck banishes the opponent's cards in large numbers every turn, so outside cards that react when a card is banished or use the opponent's banished cards get constant triggers.

hooks.label: Fairy LIGHT Fusions
hooks.why: Hugin and Munin are LIGHT Fairy Fusion Monsters that spend themselves from the field, so generic LIGHT or Fairy support covers the deck's Main Names while they defend the backrow.

profile.plan: Warrior Ritual bosses that summon by banishing or sending LIGHT and DARK monsters to the GY, then banish the opponent's cards away while huge 3000 ATK soldiers attack twice.

hooks.label: Banishes your own GY
hooks.why: Beginning Knight and Evening Twilight Knight search when they are banished from the GY, and Envoy of Chaos, Super Soldier Ritual and both Envoys banish LIGHT and DARK monsters from the GY as a cost or Summoning requirement.

hooks.label: Sends LIGHT and DARK to the GY
hooks.why: Super Soldier Synthesis sends 1 LIGHT and 1 DARK monster from the hand and Deck to the GY as its Ritual cost, so any outside card that dumps them feeds the Ritual and the Spell Counter count on Gateway to Chaos.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck, from the Level 4 Knights to the Level 8 Soldiers, is a Warrior, so generic Warrior searchers and boosters reach the whole deck.

hooks.label: Normal Monster ritual material
hooks.why: Legendary Swordsman shuffles every card the opponent controls into the Deck when Ritual Summoned using a Normal Monster, and Black Luster Ritual Tributes any monsters totaling Level 8.

hooks.label: Ritual Spell recovery
hooks.why: The whole engine runs on Ritual Spells, with Gateway, Beginning Knight and Legendary Swordsman all spending effects to fetch one.

hooks.label: Spell Counter cards
hooks.why: Super Soldier Shield can Set itself from the GY by removing a Spell Counter from anywhere on your field, and Gateway to Chaos only stores counters on itself, so outside cards that carry their own Spell Counters make the Shield live.

profile.plan: Cyberse monsters that banish themselves as a cost and pay LP to Special Summon back from banishment, chaining Link Monsters and banishing the opponent's resources.

hooks.label: Banishes your own Cyberse
hooks.why: Chessy Cat, Dormouse, March Hare and Maliss in the Mirror all banish Maliss cards from the hand, Deck or GY as a cost, so any outside card that banishes your own DARK Cyberse monsters is both an activator and a way to dodge the archetype's names.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: Every Maliss monster and Maliss in the Mirror triggers when banished, and the deck banishes from hand, Deck, field and GY constantly, so outside DARK Cyberse monsters with an effect when banished get used for free.

hooks.label: Recovers banished cards
hooks.why: March Hare and Hearts Crypter shuffle or return banished Maliss cards, so the deck wants tools that recycle its banished resources back into circulation.

hooks.label: Generic Link Monsters
hooks.why: White Rabbit and friends lock you out of the Extra Deck except Link Monsters for the rest of the turn, so the only outside bosses that fit are Link Monsters.

hooks.label: Cyberse support
hooks.why: Every Maliss monster is a DARK Cyberse and Red Ransom banishes Cyberse monsters from the Deck, so generic Cyberse search and support hits the whole deck.

profile.plan: A Warrior/Machine Synchro deck whose Tuners revive Level 2 or lower monsters from the Graveyard and fire effects off when cards are used as Synchro Material, culminating in big Warrior Synchro bosses like Junk Warrior.

hooks.label: Synchro Material GY triggers
hooks.why: Jet Synchron and Junk Converter trigger when sent to the GY as Synchro Material, so the deck constantly Synchro Summons using monsters that want to be there.

hooks.label: Tuners that want to be Tributed
hooks.why: Starlight Junktion Tributes a Tuner to Summon a Synchron from the Deck, and Junk Signal Tributes any monster, so Tuners with effects when Tributed get used for free.

hooks.label: Level 2 or lower Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Junk Synchron and Starjunk Synchron revive Level 2 or lower monsters with effects negated, and Junk Warrior and Junk Warrior Extreme gain ATK and mass-revive them, so vanilla low-Level bodies are pure upside.

hooks.label: Synchro Monster support
hooks.why: Junk Dragonlet, Junk Mail and Junk Connector all pay off when you control or Summon Synchro Monsters, so outside cards built around Synchro Monsters compound it.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Jet Synchron, Junkuriboh, Junk Giant and Junk Dragonlet are Machines, and Machine Assembly Line gives them attack and revival, so generic Machine support covers half the deck.

profile.plan: LIGHT Spellcaster Tuners that pay for their effects by sending Spell/Traps to the GY, turning self-mill into Synchro chains and recurring their spells from the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Astellar Special Summons itself whenever a Spell/Trap is sent to your GY to activate a monster's effect, so outside Spell/Traps with a trigger there get used for free as cost.

hooks.label: Fuels Spell/Trap costs
hooks.why: Elzette, Astellar, Rciela, Rucia and Diabell all send a Spell/Trap from your hand or field to the GY as a cost, so outside cards that discard or send your own Spell/Traps keep those costs flowing.

hooks.label: Illusion or Spellcaster Synchros
hooks.why: Silvera and Rciela grant every Illusion and Spellcaster Synchro Monster you control 500 ATK plus piercing or destruction protection, so any outside Synchro boss of those Types slots straight in.

hooks.label: LIGHT Spellcaster Tuners
hooks.why: Astellar Special Summons any LIGHT Spellcaster Tuner from the Deck, and Elzette returns from the GY when one is Special Summoned on the opponent's turn, so off-theme ones still trigger the deck.

hooks.label: Reacts to being Tributed
hooks.why: Scourge of the White Forest Tributes a Synchro Monster as a cost, so outside Synchro monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck White Forest monster is a LIGHT Spellcaster, and Tales and Rciela reward controlling or searching Spellcasters.

profile.plan: Fiend Tuners that swarm the field to Synchro Summon Red Dragon Archfiend and other DARK Dragon Synchro bosses, then cash in their GY effects.

hooks.label: Red Dragon Archfiend support
hooks.why: Vision Resonator searches any Spell/Trap that mentions Red Dragon Archfiend, and Soul Resonator protects your cards while you control that monster, so any outside card naming it slots straight in.

hooks.label: Level 4 or lower Fiends
hooks.why: Soul Resonator and Resonator Command add any Level 4 or lower Fiend from the Deck, so outside Fiends of that Level are extra copies of the search.

hooks.label: DARK Dragon Synchro bosses
hooks.why: Crimson Resonator and Red Rising Dragon lock the Extra Deck to DARK Dragon Synchro Monsters, so other archetypes' bosses of exactly that shape are the payoff.

hooks.label: Rewards being Synchro material
hooks.why: Synkron and Vision Resonator trigger when sent to the GY, and Resonant Destruction destroys a card each time a Resonator is used as Synchro Material, so outside monsters with effects when used as material get value for free.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Resonator monster is a Fiend, so generic Fiend search, revive and boost cards work across the whole deck.

profile.plan: Machine Tuners that Synchro Summon on the opponent's turn, destroying their own face-up cards and banishing from the GY to pay costs.

hooks.label: Low-Level Tuner monsters
hooks.why: Halqifibrax Link Summons with any 2 monsters including a Tuner, then pulls a Level 3 or lower Tuner straight from the Deck, so any small Tuner is a starter.

hooks.label: Wants to be destroyed
hooks.why: Smiger, Thystvern, Rosenix, Prasiortle, Sulfefnir and Sulfador all destroy a card you control as cost or payoff, so outside cards with an effect when destroyed get it for free.

hooks.label: Triggers when banished
hooks.why: Citree banishes its Synchro materials and Impact revives banished monsters, so outside cards with an effect when they are banished get triggered or recycled by the deck.

hooks.label: Tuner Synchro Monsters
hooks.why: Halqifibrax Prism Special Summons a Tuner from the Extra Deck, and Quandax and Phoenix require a Tuner Synchro Monster as material, so outside Tuner Synchros slot right in.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Smiger, Thystvern, Rosenix and Prasiortle lock your Extra Deck summons into Machine Synchro Monsters, and every Crystron is a Machine, so generic Machine support covers the whole deck.

profile.plan: Cyberse deck that swarms with small @Ignister monsters of every Attribute, then converts them into Link, Fusion, Synchro, Xyz and Ritual bosses, especially 2300 ATK Cyberse and the Link-6 Arrival.

hooks.label: Cyberse support
hooks.why: Every @Ignister monster is a Cyberse and many effects like Dark Templar and A.I.Land only let you Summon Cyberse monsters afterwards, so generic Cyberse support works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Link Monster toolbox
hooks.why: The deck constantly Link Summons and its payoffs care about Link Monsters you control or revive (Allied Code Talker negates by Tributing one, Dark Templar revives monsters in its zones), so outside Link Monsters that fit those zones are free bosses.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Hiyari and Kurikurinku Tribute your Cyberse and @Ignister monsters as a cost, and A.I.Q Tributes a Link Monster every Standby Phase, so outside cards with an effect when Tributed get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be used as material
hooks.why: Doyon, Bururu and Linkslayer all get bonus effects when your cards are sent to the GY as material for a Cyberse Extra Deck Summon, so outside monsters with effects when used as material synergize.

hooks.label: DARK Cyberse monsters
hooks.why: Backup @Ignister searches any DARK Cyberse monster and Wizard @Ignister revives one from the GY, so outside DARK Cyberse monsters are extra copies of the deck's core combo pieces.

hooks.label: Different-Attribute monsters
hooks.why: The Arrival Cyberse @Ignister needs 3+ monsters with different Attributes and Dark Templar needs 3 monsters with different names, so outside monsters covering Attributes the small @Ignisters lack widen your Link options.

profile.plan: A posse of Level 5 cops that swarm the field for free, stack into Rank 5 (and Rank 9) Xyz monsters, and grow stronger or punish the opponent whenever a monster effect is activated from the hand or GY.

hooks.label: Level 5 self-summoners
hooks.why: Every K9 Xyz needs 2 Level 5 monsters and the deck's own ones Special Summon themselves, so any outside Level 5 monster that can put itself on the field is instant Xyz material.

hooks.label: Rank 5 Xyz bosses
hooks.why: Hound, Jacks and Ripper are generic Rank 5 plays ('2 Level 5 monsters'), and Release Restraint can even target any Rank 5 Xyz you control, so other archetypes' Rank 5 bosses slot straight in.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic stacking
hooks.why: Forced Release and Release Restraint Xyz Summon a new K9 monster on top of one you control while transferring materials, so Rank-Up-Magic style cards that stack a higher Rank Xyz over your board extend the same line.

hooks.label: Xyz material payoff monsters
hooks.why: Lupis and Jacks hand their effects to any Xyz Monster that has them as material, so outside Xyz monsters that care about having or attaching extra material get more out of the K9 engine.

profile.plan: DARK Fairies that pay Life Points to copy their own Spells/Traps from the Graveyard, Tribute Summon their biggest angels, and Fusion Summon Level 6+ DARK Fairies.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Darklord except Marie is a Fairy, Superbia and Condemned Darklord revive or summon Fairy monsters, and The First Darklord protects all Fairy monsters you control.

hooks.label: Sends DARK Fairies to the GY
hooks.why: Ukoback, Asmodeus and Morningstar send cards from the Deck to the GY, and Gulgolet, Capricious Darklord and Djehuty all trigger when sent there, so anything that sends your DARK Fairies to the GY is value.

hooks.label: Big DARK Fairy monsters
hooks.why: Darklord Dance and Darklord Uprising Fusion Summon using DARK Fairy materials, and both Fusions want Level 6+ DARK Fairies, so outside monsters that fit that profile are extra bosses and material.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon payoff
hooks.why: Morningstar and Desire want Tribute Summons and Condemned Darklord lets you Tribute Summon by banishing from the GY, so outside monsters that Tribute Summon themselves cheaply or reward Tribute Summons fit right in.

hooks.label: Forbidden Quick-Play Spells
hooks.why: Gulgolet and Djehuty search 'Forbidden' Quick-Play Spells directly from the Deck or GY, so those cards are part of this deck's engine.

profile.plan: Anti-Special-Summon Insect hand monsters that jump out when the opponent Summons, clogging their field and punishing Extra Deck plays.

hooks.label: Insect support
hooks.why: Every "C" monster is an Insect, and Super Armored Robot Armed Black Iron "C" needs Insect monsters in the GY, so generic Insect support covers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Mills Insects to the GY
hooks.why: Super Armored Robot Armed Black Iron "C" summons itself by equipping 3 same-named Insect monsters from your GY, so outside cards that send Insect monsters from the Deck to the GY stock that up.

hooks.label: Reacts to being banished
hooks.why: Retaliating "C" banishes any card that would be sent to the GY, so outside cards with an effect when they are banished trigger for free while it is face-up.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Shiny Black "C" Squader is a Normal Monster, so outside cards that search or protect Normal Monsters work on it.

profile.plan: Monsters locked behind their own named Equip Spells, plus Eatos who arrives when your Graveyard is empty and Chimera who wants Fusion Spells — a slow Equip-based control deck.

hooks.label: Searches Equip Spells
hooks.why: Guardian Tryce, Baou, Elma, Ceal, Kay'est and Grarl cannot be Summoned at all unless their matching Equip Spell is already face-up, so finding the right Equip is the deck's bottleneck.

hooks.label: Re-equips from the Graveyard
hooks.why: Guardian Elma already pulls Equip Spells back from the GY onto itself, and Ceal and Eatos feed on sending equips to the GY, so equips that come back or cards that re-equip them are value.

hooks.label: Fusion Summons with a Spell
hooks.why: Guardian Chimera must be Fusion Summoned using materials from hand and field and only triggers its draw-and-destroy payoff when the Fusion Summon comes from a Spell Card or effect, so any outside Fusion Spell works.

hooks.label: Banishes your own Graveyard
hooks.why: Guardian Eatos Special Summons itself from hand only while you have no monsters in your Graveyard, so outside cards that banish your own GY monsters keep her live and reload the condition.

hooks.label: Level 7-8 Dragon bosses
hooks.why: Guardian of Felgrand equips a Level 7 or 8 Dragon from hand or GY for ATK and later Tributes itself to Special Summon it, so big Dragons from any archetype become free bodies.

hooks.label: LIGHT monster support
hooks.why: Guardian of Order Special Summons itself when you control 2 or more LIGHT monsters, and Guardian of Felgrand, Trust Guardian and the Skull Guardians are all LIGHT.

profile.plan: High-level LIGHT Psychics that Special Summon themselves from the hand into columns already stacked with 2+ cards, then control the board by column position and recycle their banished monsters.

hooks.label: Gifts the opponent a monster
hooks.why: Mekk-Knights like Blue Sky and Purple Nightfall Special Summon themselves only when 2 or more cards share a column, and opponent's cards in your column count, so cards that plant a monster on the opponent's field set that up single-handedly.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Mekk-Knight Spectrum Supreme sends 1 other card you control in its column to the GY as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when a card effect sends them to the GY get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Psychic support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Mekk-Knight is a Psychic monster, so generic Psychic searchers, revivers and boosters work across the whole archetype.

hooks.label: LIGHT support
hooks.why: Almost every Mekk-Knight monster is LIGHT, so Attribute support for LIGHT monsters covers the deck's bosses and its revival targets.

hooks.label: Big Level 5+ bosses
hooks.why: World Legacy's Secret Special Summons any Level 5 or higher monster from your GY and World Legacy Whispers gives a Level 5 or higher monster 1000 ATK/DEF, so any high-Level outside boss that reaches the GY is a free body and a buff target.

profile.plan: LIGHT Fairy monsters that hide Set in the Spell & Trap Zone as Spells and Special Summon themselves when destroyed on the opponent's turn, then Xyz Summon into Rank 5 bosses.

hooks.label: Destroys your own backrow
hooks.why: Artifact monsters Set in the Spell & Trap Zone only come alive when destroyed, so any outside card that destroys your own Set Spell/Traps is another activator, like Beagalltach and Ignition already do.

hooks.label: Wants to be destroyed by the opponent
hooks.why: Sanctum, Ignition and Unleashed all have bonus effects when destroyed by an opponent's card, and the deck happily leaves backrow in harm's way.

hooks.label: Level 5 LIGHT monsters
hooks.why: Every main deck Artifact is Level 5 LIGHT, Durendal needs 2 Level 5s, and Unleashed reveals a Level 5 LIGHT monster from the hand to draw.

hooks.label: Rank 5 Xyz support
hooks.why: Durendal and the deck's Xyz Summons via Unleashed are all Rank 5, so outside cards built around Rank 5 Xyz Monsters fit on top.

profile.plan: Level 4 Insect and Plant girls that search and deploy each other, then convert 'Hole' Normal Traps into free removal and advantage while feeding Sera's summons and Rank 4 Xyz plays.

hooks.label: Normal Trap payoffs
hooks.why: Sera summons a Traptrix whenever a Normal Trap is activated and Nepenthes rewards it too, so any outside card that triggers off a Normal Trap activation is a free extra reward.

hooks.label: Plant support
hooks.why: Half the archetype including Sera, Pudica and Pinguicula are Plant monsters, and Cularia and Atypus demand Insect/Plant materials, so generic Plant support works across the deck.

hooks.label: Insect support
hooks.why: Myrmeleo, Mantis, Arachnocampa, Atrax and Allomerus are Insects, and Cularia and Atypus ask for Insect/Plant Link materials, so generic Insect support fits.

hooks.label: Traps that live in the GY
hooks.why: Vesiculo sends a Set Trap you control to the GY as its Summoning cost, so outside Trap cards with an effect when they are sent to the GY get used for free.

hooks.label: When Tributed monsters
hooks.why: Genlisea Tributes itself to Set Hole Traps and Traptrip Garden Tributes your monsters as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get triggered for free.

profile.plan: Wins by holding all five Forbidden One pieces in the hand (or dumping them into the Graveyard for Exodius and Necross), so the deck draws hard and cycles pieces between hand, Deck and Graveyard.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Exodius wins when five different Forbidden One cards are in the Graveyard and sends them there itself, so any outside card that sends cards from your Deck to the Graveyard stacks the alternate win condition faster.

hooks.label: Recovers cards from your Graveyard
hooks.why: The hand win needs all five pieces in hand, and pieces end up in the Graveyard from Exodius and Obliterate!!!, so outside cards that add cards from the Graveyard to the hand rescue them.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: The arms and legs are all Level 1 DARK Normal Monsters and Exodius gains 1000 ATK per Normal Monster in your Graveyard, so cards that mill, revive or search Normal Monsters feed the deck twice.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Forbidden One piece and boss is a DARK Spellcaster, so generic Spellcaster search and support hits the entire deck.

profile.plan: Beast-Warrior Fusion deck that spams Fusion Summons with Polymerization and Lunalight Fusion, turning every Lunalight monster sent to the GY or banished into more summons and searches.

hooks.label: Sends your DARK Beast-Warriors to the GY
hooks.why: Kaleido Chick, Emerald Bird, Yellow Marten, Silver Hound, Scarlet Tiger and Crimson Fox all trigger when sent to the GY by a card effect, so any outside card that sends your monsters there is free value.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: The deck constantly sends its own monsters from hand, field and Deck to the GY as costs and effects, so outside monsters with a trigger there get used for free.

hooks.label: Banishes from the GY
hooks.why: Wolf Fusion Summons by banishing materials from the GY, Masquerade lets Fusion Summons banish GY monsters as material, and Sabre Dancer gains 200 ATK for every banished or GY Beast-Warrior, so the deck banishes its GY constantly.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when banished
hooks.why: Kaleido Chick locks the opponent out of the Battle Phase when banished, and the deck banishes its own GY monsters as Fusion material, so outside monsters that pay off when banished fit the same engine.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Lunalight monster and every Fusion is a Beast-Warrior, and Sabre Dancer counts all Beast-Warriors in both GYs for ATK, so generic Beast-Warrior support works across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Fusion Monsters with piercing
hooks.why: Wolf gives all your Lunalight monsters piercing against Defense Position monsters, and Panther Dancer and Leo Dancer attack every opponent monster repeatedly, so big Fusion bosses with piercing or multi-attacks end games faster.

profile.plan: A Spellcaster engine that chains 'Spellbook' Spells to search more of them, fueling the GY and banished zone for payoffs like Spellbook of Fate and Judgment's big Special Summon.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is a Spellcaster and cards like Spellbook of Power, Fate, Wisdom and Star Hall only work while you control one.

hooks.label: Level 5+ LIGHT or DARK Spellcasters
hooks.why: Temperance and Justice of Prophecy Special Summon or search exactly these from the Deck, and Reaper of Prophecy summons the DARK ones.

hooks.label: Level 7 Spellcaster Xyz material
hooks.why: Hierophant of Prophecy needs 2 Level 7 Spellcasters, so any outside Level 7 Spellcaster is a direct material.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Spellbook of Knowledge sends a Spellcaster you control to the GY as a cost to draw 2, so monsters with an effect when sent there get it for free.

hooks.label: Spell Counter cards
hooks.why: Spellbook Star Hall grows and searches off Spell Counters, and the deck activates Spells constantly, so other Spellcaster support built on Spell Counters stacks with it.

profile.plan: Warriors that swap out at the end of every Battle Phase: each Gladiator Beast battles, shuffles itself back into the Deck, and tags in a fresh one whose Special Summon effect fires.

hooks.label: Discard triggers
hooks.why: Heraklinos negates Spells and Traps by discarding 1 card as a cost, so outside cards with an effect when they are discarded get used for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be shuffled into the Deck
hooks.why: Every Gladiator Beast constantly shuffles itself and its allies from the hand, field and GY back into the Deck, so outside monsters that trigger when shuffled in get that for free.

hooks.label: Extra or direct attacks
hooks.why: The tag-out only happens if the monster attacked or was attacked, so outside cards that grant additional attacks or let monsters attack directly guarantee the Battle Phase triggers.

hooks.label: Special Summons from the Deck
hooks.why: Colosseum gains a Counter each time a monster is Special Summoned from the Deck and powers up the whole team, so outside cards that Summon straight from the Deck grow it fast.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior support
hooks.why: Laquari, Darius, Attorix, Heraklinos and Tamer Editor are all Beast-Warriors, so generic Beast-Warrior support hits the deck's core attackers and its boss.

hooks.label: Battle Phase protection
hooks.why: Nerokius and Dragases shut off the opponent's answers during the Damage Step, and the whole deck lives inside the Battle Phase, so outside cards that restrict the opponent's effects during battle stack with that lock.

profile.plan: WATER Aqua frogs that live in the Graveyard—Treeborn Frog revives itself every turn for free Tribute fodder while the deck swarms Level 2 monsters into Toadally Awesome and Tributes Frogs for value.

hooks.label: Level 2 Aqua Xyz material
hooks.why: Toadally Awesome needs 2 Level 2 Aqua monsters as Xyz Material, so any outside Level 2 Aqua monster is another body for it.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon bosses
hooks.why: Treeborn Frog Special Summons itself from the GY every Standby Phase, giving a free Tribute every turn, and Des Frog rewards Tribute Summoning with a swarm effect.

hooks.label: Effects when Tributed
hooks.why: Substitoad and Tradetoad Tribute monsters as a cost to summon Frogs from the Deck and GY, so outside cards that trigger when they are Tributed get used for free.

hooks.label: Aqua monsters that want the GY
hooks.why: Toadally Awesome's negation sends an Aqua monster from your hand or field to the Graveyard as a cost, and Swap Frog mills Level 2 or lower WATER Aquas from the Deck, so Aquas with GY triggers turn those costs into value.

hooks.label: Mills WATER Aquas
hooks.why: Swap Frog sends a Level 2 or lower WATER Aqua from the Deck to the GY on Summon, setting up Ronintoadin, Toadally Awesome and Dupe Frog recoveries.

hooks.label: Aqua and WATER support
hooks.why: Every Frog is a WATER Aqua, and Toadally Awesome's recovery and negation both care about WATER and Aqua cards, so generic support for either works deck-wide.

profile.plan: A trap-based control deck whose Dominus Traps negate Summons and searches straight from the hand, at the price of locking off monster effects by Attribute for the rest of the Duel, with Rosepamela fetching them and shielding its Set cards.

hooks.label: Fills your GY with Traps
hooks.why: Impulse and Purge only destroy the negated card if you have a Trap in your GY, and Spark and Spiral punish you for not having one, so outside cards that put Traps in the GY power up all four.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Rosepamela's search makes you discard 1 card as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are discarded turn that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Sets more face-down Traps
hooks.why: Rosepamela's continuous effect makes your face-down Spell/Trap cards indestructible by card effects, so outside cards that Set extra Traps sit safely under that protection.

hooks.label: LIGHT Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Rosepamela is a LIGHT Spellcaster, so generic support for that Type and Attribute works on the archetype's only monster.

profile.plan: A Warrior beatdown deck built around Tribute Summoned Level 7 Gaia knights fusing with Level 5 Dragons into Gaia the Dragon Champion, with piercing battle damage and Tribute triggers as payoff.

hooks.label: Tributes your Gaia knights
hooks.why: Arisen Gaia and Charging Gaia both have effects that trigger when they are Tributed, so outside cards that Tribute your monsters as a cost turn them into searches or Summons.

hooks.label: Level 5 Dragons
hooks.why: Catapult Turtle and Gaia the Magical Knight Special Summon Level 5 Dragons from hand, Deck and GY, Galloping Gaia searches them, and they are the Fusion material for Gaia the Dragon Champion.

hooks.label: Switches monsters to Defense
hooks.why: The whole deck's payoff is piercing damage through Spiral Spear Strike and Gaia Dragon, the Thunder Charger, so outside cards that put opposing monsters into Defense Position feed it, and Soldier Gaia switches on Summon itself.

hooks.label: Tuners
hooks.why: Gaia Knight, the Force of Earth is a generic Level 6 Synchro and Gaia Drake, the Universal Force is built on a non-Effect Synchro Monster, so Tuners give the deck Extra Deck access.

hooks.label: Big Warrior bosses
hooks.why: Soldier Gaia Tributes itself to search any Level 7 or higher Warrior, and Gaia the Fierce Knight Origin counts as two Tributes for a Warrior Tribute Summon, so outside Warrior bosses slot straight in.

hooks.label: Ritual Summon support
hooks.why: Arisen Gaia banishes itself from the GY as material for a Black Luster Soldier Ritual Summon, so outside cards that Ritual Summon using the GY complete that line.

profile.plan: WIND Dragons that equip themselves to Winged Beast warriors and hop off as Tuners to Synchro Summon, using Dragon Ravine to discard and mill the pieces into the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Sends Dragons from Deck to GY
hooks.why: Dux, Vajrayana, Barcha and Militum all equip Dragunity monsters from the GY, so any outside card that sends a Dragon from the Deck to the GY fuels the equip engine like Dragon Ravine and Tribus do.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Dragon Ravine, Senatus and Gae Dearg all discard your own cards as a cost, so outside WIND monsters with an effect when they are discarded get used for free.

hooks.label: WIND support
hooks.why: Every Dragunity monster, Tuner and non-Tuner alike, is WIND, so cards that search, revive or boost WIND monsters work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Dragon Synchro bosses
hooks.why: Remus, Whirlwind and Senatus lock your Extra Deck to Dragon monsters, so outside Dragon Synchro monsters are the payoff bosses the deck can still Summon.

hooks.label: WIND Winged Beast non-Tuners
hooks.why: Gae Dearg searches and Gae Bulg banishes WING Winged Beasts, and the Synchro Knights require non-Tuner Winged Beast material, so outside WIND Winged Beast monsters are both searchable and usable as Synchro material.

profile.plan: Warrior ninjas that hide face-down in Defense Position, Flip Summon for removal, and Tribute each other to cheat out Ninjitsu Art transforms and big bosses.

hooks.label: Flip Effect monsters
hooks.why: Armed Ninja, White Ninja, Crimson Ninja and the face-down summoners like Mitsu and Kagero reward keeping monsters face-down, so outside Flip monsters with removal or utility effects slot straight in.

hooks.label: Flips monsters face-down
hooks.why: Jioh destroys a card every time a monster is flipped face-up and Green Ninja re-sets monsters, so outside cards that turn monsters face-down or flip them keep those triggers firing.

hooks.label: Reacts to being Tributed
hooks.why: Ninjitsu Art of Transformation, Duplication and Shadow Sealing all Tribute a Ninja monster as a cost, so an outside card with an effect when it is Tributed gets triggered for free.

hooks.label: Beast, Winged Beast or Insect targets
hooks.why: Ninjitsu Art of Transformation Tributes a Ninja to Special Summon a Beast, Winged Beast or Insect from the Deck up to 3 Levels above it, so strong high-Level monsters of those Types are the payoff.

hooks.label: Dragon, Dinosaur or Sea Serpent targets
hooks.why: Ninjitsu Art of Super-Transformation sends both monsters to the GY to Special Summon a Dragon, Dinosaur or Sea Serpent of the combined Level from the Deck, so big bosses of those Types are the prize.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Most Ninja monsters including Hanzo, Sasuke and the Armor Ninja Xyz bosses are Warriors, and Blade Armor Ninja needs two Level 4 Warriors as material.

profile.plan: Crystal Beasts dodge destruction by turning into Continuous Spells in the Spell & Trap Zone, then spend those cards as fuel to Summon Rainbow Dragon and the other Ultimate Crystal bosses.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Every Crystal Beast places itself in the Spell & Trap Zone instead of the GY when destroyed in a Monster Zone, and Crystal Conclave and Crystal Pair trigger on it too, so destroying your own monsters is pure gain.

hooks.label: Sends your Continuous Spells to the GY
hooks.why: Crystal Abundance, Crystal Raigeki, Rainbow Path and Rainbow Ruins all pay by sending Crystal Beast cards from the Spell & Trap Zone to the GY, so outside Continuous Spells and Traps with an effect when sent there get that cost for free.

hooks.label: Places monsters as Continuous Spells
hooks.why: Sapphire Pegasus and Crystal Blessing fill the Spell & Trap Zone with Crystal Beasts, and Ruby Carbuncle and Crystal Promise Summon from there, so outside cards that place monsters into the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells add ammo.

hooks.label: Rewards being banished from the GY
hooks.why: Rainbow Dragon, Rainbow Overdragon and Advanced Dark banish or send Crystal Beasts from the GY as costs, so outside cards with an effect when they are banished get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Pendulum monsters for the Scales
hooks.why: Crystal Keeper sets Scale 2 and Crystal Master sets Scale 5, which together Pendulum Summon the Level 3 and 4 Crystal Beasts straight from hand.

profile.plan: LIGHT monsters that swarm the field with Level 4 bodies, stack Levels with Photon Satellite, and cash everything in for Rank 4 Xyz and Level 8 Galaxy-Eyes bosses, often locking you to LIGHT Summons while doing it.

hooks.label: Self-summoning LIGHT Level 4s
hooks.why: Photon Sanctuary and Photon Delta Wing lock the turn's Summons to LIGHT monsters, so extenders that Special Summon themselves and are themselves LIGHT Level 4 keep the Rank 4 Xyz engine rolling inside the lock.

hooks.label: LIGHT support
hooks.why: Photon Sanctuary, Photon Delta Wing and Galaxy Trance all restrict Summoning to LIGHT monsters, and every Photon monster is LIGHT, so generic LIGHT support slots straight in.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon LIGHT bosses
hooks.why: Photon Emperor grants an extra Normal Summon of a LIGHT monster after he arrives, so big LIGHT monsters with their own easy Tribute Summon use that free Summon.

hooks.label: Discards big LIGHT monsters
hooks.why: Photon Emperor Special Summons himself when sent to the GY from anywhere except the field, so outside cards that discard or send LIGHT Level 8 monsters from the hand turn Emperor into a free body.

hooks.label: LIGHT Dragon support
hooks.why: Twin Photon Lizard and Photon Wyvern are LIGHT Dragons and Photon Current only triggers for a LIGHT Dragon being attacked, so outside cards that support LIGHT Dragon monsters have extra targets here.

profile.plan: A Tuner toolbox that Synchro Summons constantly, with each Synchron triggering when it is used as material and tuners that Synchro Summon during the opponent's turn.

hooks.label: Triggers as Synchro Material
hooks.why: Fleur, Nitro, Hyper, Bri, Changer and Necro Synchron all fire when sent to the GY as Synchro Material, so any outside monster that triggers the same way joins the toolbox for free.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Nearly every Synchron is a Machine, so generic Machine searchers, revival and boosts hit the whole deck.

hooks.label: Revives from your GY
hooks.why: Satellite Synchron Special Summons itself whenever a monster is Special Summoned from your GY, so outside cards that revive give it a free body.

hooks.label: Synchro Summons again
hooks.why: Synchronized Realm burns for every Synchro Summon and the deck's tuners Synchro Summon on the opponent's turn, so outside cards that Synchro Summon as a Quick Effect or more than once a turn stack payoffs.

profile.plan: Psychic and Wyrm monsters that Special Summon themselves by sending Virtual World cards from Deck to GY, then climb into Level/Rank 3-and-up Synchro and Xyz bosses that feed on the Graveyard and banished zones.

hooks.label: Level 3 monsters
hooks.why: Lulu, Kirin and Toutou lock you into Special Summoning Level/Rank 3 or higher for the turn, and the Rank 3 Xyz (Longlong, Jaja) need Level 3 material, so other Level 3 monsters slot straight in.

hooks.label: Psychic and Wyrm support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Virtual World monster is a Psychic or Wyrm, and Longlong and Jiujiu specifically want monsters sharing Type and Attribute in the GY.

hooks.label: Works while banished
hooks.why: Toutou and Nyannyan banish themselves when they leave the field, and the Gate cards banish themselves from the GY as costs, so outside cards with an effect when banished get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Discards for value
hooks.why: Toutou and Xuanwu make you discard or send cards from your hand as costs, so outside Psychic/Wyrm monsters that trigger when discarded get that for free.

hooks.label: Banishes from your own GY
hooks.why: The Gates banish Virtual World cards from the GY as costs and Shenshen recycles banished monsters back to the GY, so outside cards that banish your own GY cards as a cost keep the banished zone stocked and reusable.

profile.plan: A package of Quick-Play and Normal Spells that flips monsters face-down and face-up, so the deck turns any Flip monster into an instant trigger and messes with the opponent's board while reviving Zombies.

hooks.label: Flip effect monsters
hooks.why: Book of Taiyou flips a face-down monster face-up immediately, so any outside Flip monster's effect triggers the turn it is Set.

hooks.label: Wants to be flipped face-up
hooks.why: Book of Moon, Eclipse and Lunar Eclipse flip your own monsters face-down, so an outside monster with an effect that fires when it is flipped face-up can re-trigger at will.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: Book of Life Special Summons a Zombie from the GY and banishes an opposing monster, so outside cards that search, revive or feed Zombies make it live.

hooks.label: Punishes opponent draws
hooks.why: Book of Eclipse makes the opponent draw a card for each monster flipped face-up in the End Phase, so outside cards that trigger on or punish the opponent drawing convert that drawback into damage or disruption.

hooks.label: Face-down monster payoffs
hooks.why: Book of Moon and Eclipse fill both fields with face-down Defense Position monsters, so outside cards that reward or exploit face-down monsters, like ones that flip them face-up or destroy them, get extra value.

profile.plan: Fusion Summons Gem-Knight Fusions out of its own Deck and hand, mixing Normal Monster gems with one outside monster of the right Type, while turning anything sent to the GY into more material.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Garnet, Lapis, Sapphire, Crystal and Tourmaline are all Normal Monsters, and Lazuli, Obsidian, Alexandrite, Emerald and Gem-Elephant all care about Normal Monsters in the hand, GY or field.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Nepyrim, Lazuli and Obsidian all trigger when sent from the hand or Deck to the GY by a card effect, so any outside card that mills feeds the engine.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Lady Lapis Lazuli, Crystal Rose, Prismaura and Brilliant Fusion constantly send cards from the hand, Deck and Extra Deck to the GY as costs, so outside monsters with effects there get triggered for free.

hooks.label: LIGHT Fusion material
hooks.why: Seraphinite only needs 1 Gem-Knight plus 1 LIGHT monster, so any LIGHT monster is a live Fusion material for Brilliant Fusion or Gem-Knight Fusion.

hooks.label: Fusion Summon support
hooks.why: The deck Fusion Summons every turn with Brilliant Fusion, Gem-Knight Fusion, Dispersion and Absorb Fusion, so outside cards that Fusion Summon or reward Fusion Monsters stack with the engine.

profile.plan: Level 3 DARK Fiends that Special Summon themselves while you control no Spells/Traps and trigger when a card effect sends them to the Graveyard, made into Rank 3 Xyz and Link plays that mill their own Deck.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Dante, Beatrice and Cherubini send cards from your own Deck to the Graveyard as their core effects, so any outside card that mills joins the engine.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: The deck constantly sends cards from the hand, field and Deck to the Graveyard, so outside monsters with an effect when they are sent there go off for free.

hooks.label: Level 3 DARK Fiends
hooks.why: Scarm searches any Level 3 DARK Fiend and Libic Special Summons one from the hand, so outside monsters with that exact typing slot straight into the deck.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Burning Abyss monster and Malacoda are Fiends, so generic Fiend search, revival and boost cards work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends your cards to the GY
hooks.why: The Malebranches only trigger when sent to the Graveyard by a card effect, so outside cards that send your own cards there set off Cir, Graff, Farfa and the rest.

profile.plan: Level 4 Pyro and Thunder engines that swarm the field and stack materials onto Rank 4 Xyz bosses, paying costs by sending cards from the hand and field to the GY and by detaching Xyz materials.

hooks.label: Level 4 self-summoning monsters
hooks.why: Every Ryzeal effect locks you into Rank 4 Xyz Summons for the turn, so any outside monster that Special Summons itself and is Level 4 is another body for the Xyz Summon.

hooks.label: Attaches Xyz material
hooks.why: Ryzeal Duo Drive, Detonator and Plugin all attach extra cards as material, and Detonator's protection and Duo Drive's stats scale with material count, so outside cards that stack more material on a Rank 4 Xyz Monster compound the payoff.

hooks.label: Detaches as a cost
hooks.why: Star Ryzeal Special Summons itself by detaching a material and Detonator pays for its disruption the same way, so outside cards that detach materials freely reload the engine.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Ice Ryzeal, Node Ryzeal and Palm Ryzeal all send cards from the hand, field or Deck to the GY as costs, so outside Level 4 monsters with an effect when sent there get triggered for free.

hooks.label: LIGHT Pyro monsters
hooks.why: Sword Ryzeal searches any LIGHT Pyro monster from the Deck, so outside cards of that exact combination are directly fetchable.

hooks.label: FIRE Thunder monsters
hooks.why: Ext Ryzeal searches any FIRE Thunder monster from the Deck, so outside cards of that exact combination are directly fetchable.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck of Dragons that lives in the scales: it Pendulum Summons Level 7s, recycles destroyed Odd-Eyes cards out of the Extra Deck, and stacks Rank 7 Xyz Pendulum bosses that jump between the Monster Zone and Pendulum Zone.

hooks.label: Destroys your own cards
hooks.why: Odd-Eyes Arc Pendulum Dragon, Mirage Dragon and Persona Dragon all trigger when your Odd-Eyes cards are destroyed by battle or card effect, so any outside card that destroys your own field is an activator.

hooks.label: Places monsters as Continuous Spells
hooks.why: Snake-Eyes Doomed Dragon Special Summons itself by sending 2 face-up Monster Cards from your Spell & Trap Zone to the GY, and Vengeance Dragon turns monsters into Continuous Spells, so cards that park monsters in the backrow feed both.

hooks.label: Recovers Pendulum Monsters
hooks.why: Revolution Dragon, Phantasma Dragon and Rebellion Dragon all want Dragon Pendulum Monsters from the Deck, Extra Deck or GY, so outside cards that fetch Pendulum Monsters keep the engine going.

hooks.label: Level 7 Dragons
hooks.why: Rebellion Dragon and Raging Dragon Xyz Summon using 2 Level 7 Dragon monsters, so outside Level 7 Dragons — especially ones easy to Pendulum Summon — are bodies the deck's whole Rank 7 engine already works with.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Every monster in the archetype is a Dragon, and Revolution Dragon locks your Pendulum Summons to Dragons, so generic Dragon support covers the whole deck.

profile.plan: Spellcaster Pendulum deck that stacks Spell Counters on its field every time a Spell resolves, then spends them to Special Summon bosses and swing the board.

hooks.label: Spell Counter cards
hooks.why: Citadel and the Pendulum monsters place a counter every time a Spell resolves and Citadel pays costs for any counter-removing effect, so outside cards that place or spend Spell Counters slot straight in.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is a Spellcaster and Selene, Lab and Regulus all summon or reveal Spellcasters specifically, so generic Spellcaster support works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Level 7+ Spellcaster bosses
hooks.why: Endymion's Lab Special Summons a Level 7 or higher Spellcaster from the hand or Deck for six counters, so any big Spellcaster from another archetype is a free payoff.

hooks.label: Pendulum support
hooks.why: The deck plays Pendulum Scales of 2 and 8 and its monsters return to the Scale when destroyed, so cards that set Scales or Pendulum Summon keep the engine going.

hooks.label: Wants Spells discarded
hooks.why: Endymion, the Master Magician and Servant of Endymion both discard as a cost, so outside cards with an effect when they are discarded from the hand get it for free.

hooks.label: Continuous Spell support
hooks.why: Rogue of Endymion Sets a Continuous Spell directly from the Deck and the deck's own cards are Continuous Spells, so outside Continuous Spells with paying effects arrive set-up.

profile.plan: A Pendulum circus that sets two Performapal scales, Pendulum Summons swarms between them, destroys its own scales for value, and Fusion Summons Odd-Eyes-style bosses with the monsters it summons.

hooks.label: Destroys your own scales
hooks.why: Pendulum Sorcerer, Lizardraw and Gentrude all pay off when cards you control are destroyed, so outside cards that destroy your own Pendulum cards are free value.

hooks.label: Fills your Pendulum Zones
hooks.why: Gentrude and Five-Rainbow Magician replace destroyed scales from the Deck, so outside cards that place Pendulum Monsters in your Pendulum Zones keep the engine running.

hooks.label: Rewards being Pendulum Summoned
hooks.why: The whole deck lives on Pendulum Summons between its scales, so outside monsters with effects that trigger when Pendulum Summoned fire for free.

hooks.label: Fusions using Pendulum materials
hooks.why: Trump Witch, Trump Girl, Splashmammoth and U Go Golem Fusion Summon using monsters you control, so Fusion Monsters that treat Pendulum Monsters as material slot straight in.

hooks.label: Magician Pendulum Monsters
hooks.why: Celestial Magician, Popperup and U Go Golem all Summon or search 'Magician' Pendulum Monsters, so any of them is a direct partner from outside the archetype.

hooks.label: Continuous Spell payoffs
hooks.why: Sky Magician gains ATK whenever you activate a Spell and bounces a Continuous Spell to replay a 'Magician' one, so Continuous Spells with reusable activations suit it.

profile.plan: Summons the three Level 10 Sacred Beasts by dumping Continuous Spells, Traps and Fiends into the Graveyard, then keeps drawing off Fallen Paradise while they dominate the field.

hooks.label: Sends your Traps to the GY
hooks.why: Uria gains 1000 ATK for each Continuous Trap in your GY and Hyper Blaze sends Traps from your hand or Deck there, so any outside card that sends Traps to the GY feeds the boss.

hooks.label: Places Continuous Spells/Traps
hooks.why: Hamon and Uria are Summoned by sending 3 face-up Continuous Spells or Traps you control to the GY, so outside cards that put those cards on the field from the Deck build the Tribute for free.

hooks.label: Level 10 Tribute Summon bosses
hooks.why: Opening of the Spirit Gates and Awakening of the Sacred Beasts recover a Continuous card whenever you control a Level 10 monster, and Fallen Paradise protects them while drawing, so any outside Level 10 Tribute Summon monster turns the recovery on.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be Tributed
hooks.why: Raviel Tributes 3 Fiends to Summon itself and both it and Shimmering Scraper Tribute monsters as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed give free value.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Dark Beckoning Beast grants an extra Normal Summon of a Fiend and Opening of the Spirit Gates revives Fiends with 0 ATK/DEF, so generic Fiend support works on the archetype's whole engine.

profile.plan: Level 1 Machine Ritual deck that Special Summons itself by Tributing Drytron or Ritual Monsters, then Ritual Summons giant Machine bosses using ATK instead of Levels.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: Alpha Thuban, Zeta Aldhibah, Gamma Eltanin, Delta Altais and Beta Rastaban all Tribute a Drytron or Ritual Monster from hand or field as a cost, so outside monsters that get an effect when Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Drytron monster is a Machine, and Meteonis Drytron and Meteoroa Drytron Tribute Machine monsters from hand or field by their ATK as Ritual material.

hooks.label: Any Ritual Monster
hooks.why: Meteonis Drytron can Ritual Summon any Ritual Monster from hand or GY, the Drytrons Tribute Ritual Monsters as cost, and DA Draconids Special Summons a 4000 ATK Ritual Monster from hand or Deck.

hooks.label: Cannot be Normal Summoned
hooks.why: Every Drytron enabler locks you into only Special Summoning monsters that cannot be Normal Summoned/Set for the rest of the turn, so the only outside monsters playable that turn are ones with that text.

profile.plan: Level 1 LIGHT Beasts that flood the field by self-Summoning once you control a Link-1 monster, then turn themselves into Level 2 Synchro Tuners that Synchro Summon on the opponent's turn.

hooks.label: Link-1 Monsters
hooks.why: Cupsy, Cooky and Lollipo Special Summon themselves whenever you control a Link-1 monster, and the Yummy Way Synchros treat a Link-1 monster you control as a Level 1 Tuner, so any outside Link-1 monster is a free starter and Synchro enabler.

hooks.label: LIGHT Beast support
hooks.why: Every Yummy Main Deck monster is a LIGHT Beast, and Yummy★Snatchy is Link Summoned using a Level 4 or lower LIGHT Beast, so generic LIGHT Beast searchers and support power the whole deck.

hooks.label: Level 2 Synchro Monsters
hooks.why: The small Yummies self-Summon if you control a Level 2 Synchro Monster, and Marshmao upgrades its effect when Summoned by a Synchro Monster's effect, so outside Level 2 Synchro Monsters keep the engine going.

hooks.label: LIGHT Beast Synchro Monsters
hooks.why: Yummyusment★Acroquey destroys a card whenever you Synchro Summon a LIGHT Beast Synchro Monster and Yummy★Redemption draws off the same trigger, so any outside LIGHT Beast Synchro boss gives both payoffs.

profile.plan: Quick-Effect monsters that reveal FIRE, EARTH and DARK monsters in the hand to pay for their effects, constantly bouncing each other back to hand and re-summoning during either player's turn.

hooks.label: Loves being bounced to hand
hooks.why: Heavy Borger and Caesar Valius return your monsters to the hand as the cost to Summon themselves, so outside monsters with an effect when they go back to the hand get it for free.

hooks.label: Works from hand by revealing
hooks.why: The whole deck pays for its effects by revealing monsters in the hand, so outside monsters whose own effects activate in the hand by revealing themselves fit right in.

hooks.label: Column-based cards
hooks.why: Razen and Pantera destroy every card in their column and Trinity Burst bounces everything in the summoned monsters' columns, so outside cards that place or punish cards in columns stack with that.

profile.plan: Fusion Monsters built around Fallen of Albaz that fuse using materials from the field, GY and face-up banished cards, and pay their costs by sending cards from the Extra Deck to the GY.

hooks.label: Sends your Extra Deck to the GY
hooks.why: Dogmatikalamity must send an Extra Deck card to the GY to attack and counts Fusion Monsters in your GY, so outside cards that send your own Extra Deck cards to the GY are both ammo and payoff.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent from the Extra Deck
hooks.why: Mirrorjade and Dogmatikalamity send Extra Deck cards to the GY as costs every turn, so outside Fusion/Extra Deck monsters with an effect when sent to the GY get it for free.

hooks.label: Fusion Summons from the GY
hooks.why: Lubellion Fusion Summons by shuffling materials from the field, GY and face-up banished cards, and locks you into Fusion Monsters, so outside Fusion Summoning that uses GY materials keeps the engine going.

hooks.label: Fusion Monster enablers
hooks.why: Every Fusion in the deck needs a DARK, LIGHT or Effect Monster as the non-Albaz material, so outside DARK or LIGHT Fusion Monsters that mention Fusion materials the deck already runs fit as Extra Deck bosses.

profile.plan: Spellcasters that equip Fusion, Synchro, Xyz and Link monsters from the Extra Deck onto their bodies as Equip Spells, turning every Magistus into a carrier of a bigger monster's powers.

hooks.label: Level 4 Spellcasters
hooks.why: Artemis Links off any Level 4 or lower Spellcaster, Ninaruru and Rilliona Wardrobe are Xyz made of two Level 4 Spellcasters, and Zoroa, Trismagistus and Zoroa the Conflagrant all Summon Level 4 Spellcasters from the hand or GY.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Nearly every Magistus monster is a Spellcaster and the Fusion and Xyz monsters demand Spellcaster materials, so generic Spellcaster support hits the whole deck.

hooks.label: Extra Deck monsters that equip
hooks.why: Magistus Theurgy can equip any non-Magistus Fusion, Synchro, Xyz or Link Monster to your monster, so Extra Deck monsters with an effect while equipped come along for free.

hooks.label: Adds Spellcasters to hand
hooks.why: Crowley Special Summons itself whenever it is added to your hand except by drawing, and Spenta searches Magistus, so outside cards that recover or search Spellcasters keep the engine moving.

hooks.label: Fusion Summons from hand and field
hooks.why: Crowley and Magistus Invocation Fusion Summon using monsters from your hand or field including a Spellcaster, so more Fusion Summoning effects mean more chances to bring out Aiwass and Verethragna.

profile.plan: Fairy LIGHT monsters that win by stacking 200-damage pings onto everything the opponent does — drawing cards, activating effects, being banished — while Link-climbing into big Trickstars.

hooks.label: Inflicts effect damage
hooks.why: Narkissus Special Summons itself whenever the opponent takes effect damage, and Noble Angel and Drumatis destroy a card or zero a monster's ATK each time effect damage is inflicted, so any outside burn card is a trigger.

hooks.label: Makes the opponent draw
hooks.why: Lycoris inflicts 200 damage for every card added to the opponent's hand and Bloom makes them draw, so outside cards that gift the opponent draws become burn.

hooks.label: Banishes from opponent's GY
hooks.why: Rhodode inflicts 200 damage for each card banished from the opponent's GY, so outside cards that remove their GY become a damage engine.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Foxglove Witch needs 2+ Fairy monsters and every Trickstar is a Fairy, so generic Fairy support covers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent from hand to GY
hooks.why: Crimson Heart and Rhodode discard Trickstar cards as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when sent from the hand to the GY, like Mandrake, get triggered for free.

profile.plan: A swarm of Level/Rank/Link 2 Thunders that copy each other onto the field, lock the game into nothing but 2s, and turn every Xyz detach and Tribute into negation and removal.

hooks.label: Level 2 self-Summoners
hooks.why: Blue, Red, Carrot, Jet and Pixies all Special Summon themselves for free once you control any Level 2 monster, so outside Level 2 monsters that do the same snowball from turn one.
phrases: you can Special Summon this card

hooks.label: Rank 2 Xyz bosses
hooks.why: Gigantic Spright Special Summons any Level 2 monster from the Deck by detaching material, and Double Cross attaches monsters to a Rank 2 monster you control, so strong Rank 2 Xyz monsters are the payoff.

hooks.label: Level 2 GY effects
hooks.why: Sprind sends a Level 2 monster from the Deck to the GY and Elf Special Summons Level 2 monsters from the GY, so outside Level 2 monsters with Graveyard effects are used twice.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Spright Red and Spright Carrot Tribute another Level/Rank/Link 2 monster as the cost for their negations, so outside cards with an effect when they are Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Thunder support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Spright is a Thunder, so generic Thunder searchers, revival and boosts work across the whole archetype.

profile.plan: LIGHT Machine Union monsters that combine by banishing themselves from the field and GY into Fusion bosses, which then pay discards for removal and revive the banished parts.

hooks.label: Banishes your LIGHT Machines
hooks.why: ABC-Dragon Buster is Summoned by banishing A/B/C you control or in your GY, and revives banished LIGHT Machine Unions, so any outside card that banishes your own LIGHT Machines feeds the strategy.

hooks.label: Sends your Unions from field to GY
hooks.why: A-Assault Core, B-Buster Drake and C-Crush Wyvern all trigger when sent from the field to the GY, so outside cards that send your own monsters there turn into free Union searches and Summons.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: ABC-Dragon Buster, A-to-Z-Dragon Buster Cannon and XYZ Hyper Cannon all pay with discarding 1 card, so outside monsters with an effect when discarded get their cost refunded.

hooks.label: Union monsters
hooks.why: A, B and C search and Summon more Union monsters, and Union Driver equips Level 4 or lower Unions straight from the Deck, so any outside Union monster is live material.

hooks.label: LIGHT Machine support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is a LIGHT Machine and the Unions can only equip to LIGHT Machines, so generic LIGHT or Machine support works deck-wide.

hooks.label: Recovers banished monsters
hooks.why: ABC-Dragon Buster and XYZ Combine both Special Summon your banished monsters, so outside cards that recover or Summon from the banished zone keep the combo looping.

profile.plan: Illusion Fusion monsters that cheat themselves out by sending Sinful Spoils cards to the GY, mixing Illusion, LIGHT Spellcaster and Fiend materials into big Fusion and Synchro bosses.

hooks.label: Illusion monster support
hooks.why: Every Azamina monster and Fusion material is an Illusion, and Moa Regina revives Illusion monsters from the GY, so generic Illusion support works across the whole deck.

hooks.label: LIGHT Spellcaster material
hooks.why: Ilia Silvia and Mu Rcielago each require a LIGHT Spellcaster monster as Fusion material, so any outside LIGHT Spellcaster is live material.

hooks.label: High-Level Fiend material
hooks.why: Moa Regina needs a Level 6 or higher Fiend and Sol Erysichthon needs any Fiend as Fusion material, so big Fiends are direct food for the Fusion Summons.

hooks.label: Sends your Illusions to the GY
hooks.why: Queen Azamina Special Summons herself from hand or field when an activated effect sends her to the GY or banishes her, and Elzette searches when sent to the GY as material, so outside cards that send or banish your monsters by effect pay you twice.

hooks.label: Synchro Summons with your monsters
hooks.why: Elzette searches a Sinful Spoils card when used as Synchro Material, so outside cards that Synchro Summon using your hand or field monsters turn her into a free search.

hooks.label: Fiend, Illusion or Spellcaster Extra Deck bosses
