hooks.why: Vidolium Special Summons itself by returning 1 Fusion, 1 Synchro and 1 Xyz you control or in your GY to the Extra Deck, and Jupiter wants 3 Level 10 monsters as Xyz material, so generic big Fusion/Synchro/Xyz monsters are bodies that pay these costs.

hooks.label: Equip Spell engines
hooks.why: Jupiter can be Xyz Summoned using a monster you control equipped with 3 or more Equip Cards, and on Summon it re-equips any number of Equip Spells from your GY to itself.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY from the Extra Deck
hooks.why: Portal - Terminus sends a monster from your Deck or face-up Extra Deck to the GY as its activation, so outside Extra Deck monsters with an effect in the GY turn that cost into advantage.

profile.plan: Fuses Rocks with high-Level monsters by banishing materials straight from the GYs, then attacks repeatedly with piercing, self-replacing beaters.

hooks.label: Mills your own Rocks
hooks.why: Fossil Fusion banishes its materials from the GY, and Miracle Rupture already sends Level 4 or lower Rocks there, so any outside card that sends Rock monsters from the Deck to the GY is another Fusion enabler.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Weathering Soldier searches Fossil Fusion when sent to the GY by a card effect, so outside Rock monsters with their own GY triggers come along for free.

hooks.label: Mills the opponent's Deck
hooks.why: Skullgios and Skullgar fuse using Level 4+ monsters in the opponent's GY, so outside cards that send opponent's cards to the GY load their side of the Fusion with material.

hooks.label: Rock support
hooks.why: Every Fossil monster and Fusion material requirement is Rock, so generic Rock searchers, boosters and revival work across the whole deck.

profile.plan: LIGHT Fairies built around The Sanctuary in the Sky and Counter Traps, whose Parshath monsters pierce Defense Position monsters and draw or search off the battle damage they inflict.

hooks.label: Counter Trap payoff
hooks.why: Sacred Arch-Airknight Parshath Special Summons itself whenever you activate a Counter Trap or negate a Spell/Trap or monster effect, and it searches Parshath cards or Counter Traps off battle damage, so any outside Counter Trap that negates is an activator and a payoff.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Parshath monster is a Fairy, Knightlord's Summon and Arch's revival banish or summon Fairy monsters, and Sanctum boosts and stacks Fairies back on top of the Deck.

hooks.label: Sanctuary in the Sky synergies
hooks.why: Knightlord searches any card that specifically lists The Sanctuary in the Sky, and Nova Summoner and Neo-Parshath get stronger effects while it is on the field.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: Sacred Arch-Airknight Parshath banishes 2 Fairy monsters from hand, field and GY as a cost, and Knightlord banishes a Fairy from the GY to summon a bigger one from the hand, so outside Fairies with effects when banished get it for free.

hooks.label: Piercing enablers
hooks.why: Every Parshath monster inflicts piercing battle damage and then draws or searches off the damage inflicted, so outside cards that put opposing monsters in Defense Position or grant more attacks multiply the payoff.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Rebirth of Parshath and Celestial Knightlord Parshath both discard a card as a cost, so outside cards with effects when discarded turn those costs into advantage.

profile.plan: Pyro monsters that stack their Graveyard and then punish the opponent with effect damage, banishing their own FIRE monsters to fuel big bosses like Volcanic Emperor.

hooks.label: Sends Pyro monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Scattershot and Rimfire trigger when sent to the GY by any effect, and Fire Ejection sends a Pyro monster from the Deck, so outside cards that send Pyro monsters there are free activators.

hooks.label: Banishes Pyro monsters from your GY
hooks.why: Volcanic Emperor Special Summons by banishing 3 Pyro monsters from your field and/or GY, and Volcanic Inferno banishes a Pyro monster from the GY as a cost, so cards that banish your own Pyro monsters feed both.

hooks.label: Reacting to being banished
hooks.why: Emperor, Rimfire and Inferno banish your own Pyro monsters as cost or Summoning material, so outside monsters with effects when banished get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Effect damage enablers
hooks.why: The whole deck wins through effect damage — Slicer, Hammerer, Emperor, Scattershot and Volcanic Emission all burn — so outside cards that inflict damage or trigger on damage inflicted stack with them.

hooks.label: Pyro and FIRE support
hooks.why: Every Volcanic monster is a Pyro FIRE monster and Fire Ejection, Emperor and Inferno all specifically use Pyro monsters, so generic Pyro and FIRE support hits the whole deck.

profile.plan: Machine racers whose ATK and effects scale with their Level, pumping Levels with Field Spells and Quick-Play Spells, then Synchro Summoning into Level-riding bosses and negation.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every F.A. monster is a Machine and F.A. Shining Star GT requires 2 Machine monsters as Link material, so generic Machine searchers and revival work across the deck.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: The deck runs three different F.A. Field Spells and F.A. Auto Navigator only fetches F.A. ones, so outside cards that add or activate Field Spells from the Deck keep the engines running.

hooks.label: Machine Tuners
hooks.why: F.A. Dawn Dragster and F.A. Motorhome Transport are Synchro Summons from 1 Tuner plus non-Tuners, and Auto Navigator is the deck's only in-archetype Tuner, so extra Machine Tuners are Synchro fuel.

hooks.label: Level-raising cards
hooks.why: F.A. monsters gain 300 ATK per Level and unlock effects at Level 7+, so any outside card that raises a monster's Level strengthens the whole field, not just F.A. cards.

hooks.label: Self-banishing GY spells
hooks.why: F.A. Pit Stop, Test Run and Overheat all activate by banishing themselves from the GY, and F.A. Winners banishes your own cards as a cost, so the deck likes cards that banish themselves from the GY.

profile.plan: A Flip Effect deck of LIGHT Reptile 'Worms' that Sets itself face-down, flips for value, and Mills the opponent's Deck while Tribute Summoning big Worms one over another.

hooks.label: Flip Effect monsters
hooks.why: Nearly every Worm is a Flip Effect Monster and Worm Erokin and Worm Falco flip them back face-down to reuse, so any outside Flip Effect monster is another card the deck can Set, defend and flip for value.

hooks.label: Flips monsters face-down
hooks.why: Worm Erokin, Worm Falco, Worm Rakuyeh and Medusa Worm all cycle Worms back into face-down Defense Position, so outside cards that Set or flip your monsters face-down keep the engine looping.

hooks.label: Mills the opponent's Deck
hooks.why: Needle Worm, Warm Worm, Shield Worm and Aztekipede all send cards off the opponent's Deck, so a deck-out win wants more cards doing the same thing.

hooks.label: Reptile support
hooks.why: The core Worms are all Reptiles and Worm Cartaros, Worm King and Worm Queen only fetch or Tribute Reptiles, so generic Reptile searchers and revivers work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Rewards Setting cards
hooks.why: Worm Illidan gains a Worm Counter each time you Set a card and Worm Gulse gains one each time a monster is flipped face-up, so outside cards that Set cards from your hand or Deck feed both.

profile.plan: Cute Fairy toys that Fusion Summon Frightfur stitched-together monsters with Polymerization, rewarding every Fluffal used as Fusion Material with a follow-up effect.

hooks.label: Fusion Summoning Spells
hooks.why: Fluffal Dog, Owl and Cat search and recycle Polymerization, and Owl can pay 500 LP to Fusion Summon, so any outside Spell that Fusion Summons is another copy of the engine.

hooks.label: Reward when Fusion Material
hooks.why: Penguin, Cat, Dolphin, Rabbit and Octopus all trigger when sent to the GY as Fusion Material, so outside monsters with such an effect get it for free in the Fusion Summons.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Fluffal is a Fairy, so generic Fairy searchers, revivers and boosters cover the whole archetype.

hooks.label: Fusion Monster support
hooks.why: The deck's payoffs are Fusion Monsters, so outside cards that protect, revive or summon Fusions from the Extra Deck or GY fit it.

profile.plan: Warriors, Machines and other bruisers that equip monsters from the GY to themselves, gaining each other's effects and a pile of Equip Cards while doing it.

hooks.label: Sends your monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Every Therion Special Summons itself by equipping a Therion monster or a same-Type monster from your GY, so anything that loads your GY with monsters is fuel for Regulus, Borea, Ain and the rest.

hooks.label: Union self-equippers
hooks.why: Therion monsters pass their effects to whatever monster they are equipped to and 'Duke' Yul protects while you control an Equip Card, so monsters that equip themselves from anywhere add to the engine.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: 'King' Regulus and Therion Irregular are both Machines, and Regulus can equip any Machine from the GY, so generic Machine searchers and revivers work directly.

hooks.label: Rewards when sent to the GY
hooks.why: Therion Charge, Regulus' negate and Discolosseum all send your cards to the GY as cost or replacement, so outside monsters with an effect there get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Equip Card payoffs
hooks.why: 'Duke' Yul's protection and the shared 700 ATK boost only care that Equip Cards exist, so outside cards that reward you for controlling them stack with the archetype.

profile.plan: Psychic pilots banish themselves from the hand or field to Special Summon bigger Machine ships, and the ships float into the next pilot when destroyed, so the deck chains upward from small to huge while feeding on its own banished and destroyed cards.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Dark Destroyer, Sliprider and Kozmojo destroy cards you control, and every Kozmo ship triggers when destroyed by a card effect, so outside cards that blow up your own monsters chain the lineup upward.

hooks.label: Recovers banished cards
hooks.why: Kozmotown, Strawman and Scaredy Lion all recycle Kozmo monsters that banished themselves as Summon fodder, so outside cards that Summon or return cards from banishment turn the spent pilots back into resources.

hooks.label: Psychic support
hooks.why: The Psychic pilots (Farmgirl, Tincan, Soartroopers, the Wickedwitch line) are the deck's engine, and Soartroopers and Lightsword specifically ask for Psychic monsters.

hooks.label: Banishes monsters as cost
hooks.why: Dark Planet must be Summoned by banishing monsters from the hand, and the ships banish Kozmo monsters from the Graveyard as negation costs, so outside cards that banish your own monsters fuel the same stockpile the archetype feeds on.

profile.plan: A Dark Magician engine that reveals and adds Spellcaster support, then overlays it with gimmick payoffs: face-down cards for King of Yamimado, die rolls for Pazoo, and LP gain triggers for Sorcerer of Sebek.

hooks.label: Dark Magician support cards
hooks.why: Dark Magical Circle adds any Spell/Trap that mentions Dark Magician and Dark Magical Curtain searches one, so outside support written for Dark Magician slots straight into the engine.

hooks.label: DARK Spellcaster monsters
hooks.why: Dark Magical Curtain Special Summons any DARK Spellcaster from hand or Deck, so outside DARK Spellcasters are extra bodies the card can fetch.

hooks.label: Level 7+ Spellcaster bosses
hooks.why: Dark Paladin - Wave-Motion fuses Dark Magician with any Level 7 or higher monster, so big outside Spellcasters are ideal fusion material that also stay on-theme.

hooks.label: Yami Field Spells
hooks.why: King of Yamimado Special Summons itself from hand when Yami or face-down cards are on the field, so the Yami Field Spells are direct activators.

hooks.label: Cards that Set face-down
hooks.why: King of Yamimado gets protection and its self-Summon from face-down cards on the field, so outside cards that Set Spells/Traps from the Deck keep it online.

hooks.label: Die roll cards
hooks.why: Armor Wizard Pazoo's negate only works while you control a card with an effect that requires a die roll, so any die roll card gives the whole deck a free negation.

profile.plan: Pendulum Fiends that fill both Pendulum Zones, Tribute each other for value, and Set 'Abyss Script' Spells whose destruction by the opponent pays off big.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Abyss Actor monster is a Fiend, and Abyss Actor - Super Producer needs a Fiend as Link material.

hooks.label: Pendulum support cards
hooks.why: The whole deck lives in the Pendulum Zones and face-up Extra Deck, so outside cards that move, recover or Summon Pendulum Monsters slot straight in.

hooks.label: Wants to be destroyed by your effect
hooks.why: Abyss Actor - Super Producer destroys any face-up card you control as a cost, so outside cards with an effect when they are destroyed get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Triggers when discarded
hooks.why: Abyss Actor - Liberty Dramatist discards 1 card as a cost to jump to the opponent's field, so outside cards with an effect when they are discarded are free value.

hooks.label: Special Summons from Extra Deck
hooks.why: Curtain Raiser and Wild Hope pull face-up Abyss Actors out of the Extra Deck, and the deck constantly stacks monsters there, so outside cards that Summon from the Extra Deck extend it.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Ritual engine built around Lo, who serves as the entire Tribute for any LIGHT Warrior or Dragon Ritual Monster, searched and recycled by Continuous Spells/Traps that flood the board with big Dragon Ritual bosses like Saffira.

hooks.label: LIGHT Warrior/Dragon Rituals
hooks.why: Lo can be used as the entire Tribute and Prayers/Saffira/Blessing can Ritual Summon any LIGHT Warrior or Dragon Ritual Monster, so every such monster outside the archetype is a valid boss for the deck.

hooks.label: Ritual Summon support
hooks.why: Lo counts as the whole Tribute for any card effect that Ritual Summons using monsters, so outside cards that Ritual Summon from outside the deck add extra ways to put down the LIGHT bosses.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Saffira, Divine Dragon draws 2 then discards 1 and Saffira, Dragon Queen discards herself as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when discarded get used for free.

hooks.label: LIGHT Dragon support
hooks.why: Saffira, Sauravis and the Ritual bosses are all LIGHT Dragons, so cards that search, revive or boost LIGHT Dragons work across the deck.

profile.plan: Low-Level Machines that flip between Attack and Defense Position to change their effects on a dime, swarming the field for Synchro Summons while farming Morph Counters and equips.

hooks.label: Machine-Type support
hooks.why: Nearly every Morphtronic is a Machine, so generic Machine searchers, revivers and boosters work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Battle position changers
hooks.why: Morphtronic Map places a Morph Counter every time any monster's battle position changes and Morphtronic Cord destroys a Spell/Trap on each change, so outside cards that flip monsters power the whole engine.

hooks.label: Equip Card providers
hooks.why: Morphtronic Videon gains 800 ATK/DEF per Equip Card, Vacuumen throws equips for burn, and Earfon can be equipped to Synchro Monsters, so cards that equip to your monsters are ammunition.

hooks.label: Rewards when Tributed
hooks.why: Slingen and Datatron Tribute Morphtronic monsters as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Rewards when banished
hooks.why: Smartfon, Scannen, Remoten and Impact Return all banish your own Morphtronics as a cost or Summon condition, so outside cards with an effect when they are banished trigger on cue.

profile.plan: Level 2 WATER Beasts and Fish that replace themselves when destroyed by battle or sent to the Graveyard, flooding the field with small bodies for Xyz Summons.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Nimble Angler Special Summons two more Nimbles when it is sent from the hand or Deck to the Graveyard, so anything that mills your own cards sets it off for free.

hooks.label: Destroys your own field
hooks.why: Nimble Manta triggers when it is sent from the field to the Graveyard by a card effect, so outside cards that destroy or send away your own monsters turn it into more bodies.

hooks.label: Level 2 Xyz engine
hooks.why: Every Nimble is a Level 2 that Special Summons more Level 2s, so the deck floods the field with material for Rank 2 Xyz Monsters.

hooks.label: Beast support
hooks.why: Beaver, Momonga, Mega Hamster and Musasabi are all Beasts, so generic Beast searchers and boosters cover most of the deck.

hooks.label: Flip and face-down support
hooks.why: Mega Hamster and Momonga fill your field with monsters in face-down Defense Position, so outside cards that reward or protect face-down and Flip monsters get extra value.

profile.plan: Fiend pirates that equip their own monsters to their Extra Deck ships, with each ship's Attribute chosen to match whatever the opponent controls.

hooks.label: Opponent Attribute manipulation
hooks.why: Whitebeard, Redbeard and Blackbeard summon Plunder ships matching an Attribute your opponent controls or has in their GY, so outside cards that change or declare Attributes on the opponent's monsters let you summon any ship you want.

hooks.label: Level 4 self-summoning extenders
hooks.why: The whole Main Deck crew is Level 4 and Moerk is a Rank 4 Xyz over two of them, so outside Level 4 monsters that Special Summon themselves fill the board without diluting the crew.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Plunder Patroll monster, Main Deck and Extra Deck, is a Fiend, and Brann even boosts all other Fiends, so generic Fiend support hits the whole crew.

hooks.label: Union monsters
hooks.why: Blackbeard and Emblem of the Plunder Patroll equip any Effect Monster you control to a Plunder ship, so Union monsters that can become Equip Cards themselves are free extra equipment for those effects.

hooks.label: Extra Equip Cards
hooks.why: Parrrty draws one card for each Equip Card you control and Moerk, Brann and Lys only get their Quick Effects while equipped, so outside Equip Spells that survive on the field are pure value.

profile.plan: A Synchro-Summoning toolkit deck built around Level 7/8 Dragon Synchro Monsters and 'Crimson Dragon', reviving Tuners and Synchro Monsters from the GY and stacking Signal Counters for more revivals.

hooks.label: Level 7/8 Dragon Synchro bosses
hooks.why: Revolution Synchron, Synchro Rumble and Synchro Overtop are all built around Level 7 or 8 Dragon Synchro Monsters, so any such monster is a supported boss.

hooks.label: Revives Tuners from the GY
hooks.why: Synchro World with 7 Signal Counters and Synchro Rumble both Special Summon Tuners from the GY, and every Synchro Summon needs a Tuner on the field.

hooks.label: Revives Synchro Monsters
hooks.why: Synchro World with 10 Signal Counters, Synchro Rumble and Synchro Overtop all bring Synchro Monsters back from the GY, so outside cards that do the same extend the deck's recovery.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Synchro Fellowship's search ends with discarding 1 card, so an outside monster with a discard trigger or GY effect comes along for free.

profile.plan: Tribute Summons big WIND Winged Beasts cheaply while keeping the opponent's Spell & Trap Zones empty, letting its small birds revive themselves for free.

hooks.label: Winged Beast support
hooks.why: Every Simorgh monster is a Winged Beast and the deck's searchers, revival and Tributes all key off Winged Beast monsters.

hooks.label: WIND Attribute support
hooks.why: Almost every Simorgh is WIND (the DARK ones count as WIND on the field), and Elborz and Ancestry only reward WIND monsters, so generic WIND cards cover the whole deck.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon support
hooks.why: The deck's bosses — Lord of the Storm, Ancestry, Divinity, and Simorgh of Darkness's revival — all want Tribute Summons, and Elborz and Ancestry already shave Tributes off, so anything else that eases Tribute Summoning stacks with them.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be Tributed
hooks.why: Simorgh of Darkness and Lord of the Storm Tribute a WIND Winged Beast as a Quick Effect cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Fills the GY with DARK and WIND
hooks.why: Dark Simorgh Special Summons itself by banishing 1 DARK and 1 WIND monster from the GY or hand, so outside cards that mill or load the GY with those monsters power it up.

hooks.label: Locks the opponent's backrow
hooks.why: The small Simorghs revive themselves from the GY only while the opponent's Spell & Trap Zones are empty, and Dark Simorgh already blocks Sets, so outside cards that stop or punish Setting keep that lock on.

profile.plan: A handful of Equip Spells that do nothing on their own but turn the equipped monster's direct attacks into draws, mass destruction and skipped phases.

hooks.label: Direct attack enablers
hooks.why: Cursed Bamboo Sword grants a direct attack and Original Bamboo Sword and Soul Devouring Bamboo Sword pay off only when battle damage is inflicted by a direct attack, so anything that lets a monster attack directly is fuel.

hooks.label: Punishes direct-attack damage
hooks.why: Original Bamboo Sword wipes the field when the equipped monster deals battle damage by a direct attack, so outside cards that also trigger on that damage stack with it.

hooks.label: Equips Spells from the Deck
hooks.why: Original Bamboo Sword can equip another Bamboo Sword Equip Spell from the Deck, and Golden Bamboo Sword draws 2 while an Equip Spell is on the field, so cards that fetch or equip Equip Spells keep the payoffs live.

hooks.label: Skips opponent's phases
hooks.why: Burning Bamboo Sword skips the opponent's Main Phase 1 whenever you activate a Bamboo Sword card, so outside cards that lock out phases stack into a full lock.

profile.plan: A Ritual-focused deck that destroys its own Nephthys cards by card effect to trigger Standby-Phase rebirth effects, Ritual Summoning its Level 8 phoenixes with Rebirth of Nephthys.

hooks.label: Destroys your own cards
hooks.why: Every Nephthys effect key — Disciple, Defender, Devotee, Conductor, Cerulean Phoenix — waits for the card to be destroyed by a card effect, so any outside card that destroys your hand or field cards is an activator.

hooks.label: Wants to be destroyed
hooks.why: The archetype destroys its own cards as cost and by effect constantly (Disciple, Defender, Matriarch, Chronicler, Last Hope), so outside monsters with an effect when destroyed by a card effect get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster bosses
hooks.why: Nephthys, the Sacred Flame gains its best effects per Ritual Monster used as Link material, and Rebirth of Nephthys can Tribute any monsters, so outside Level 2 and Level 8 Ritual Monsters slot straight in.

hooks.label: Level 8 Winged Beasts
hooks.why: Nephthys, the Sacred Preserver searches any Level 8 Winged Beast, so outside Level 8 Winged Beast monsters are one-card follow-ups.

hooks.label: Reacts to being Tributed
hooks.why: Hand of Nephthys and Rebirth of Nephthys Tribute your monsters as Summoning material, so outside monsters that trigger when Tributed earn their effect for free.

hooks.label: Banishes DARK monsters from GY
hooks.why: Dark Nephthys banishes 2 DARK monsters from your GY to Special Summon itself, so outside cards that banish your own DARK monsters from the GY feed that cost.

profile.plan: LIGHT Beast-Warrior Level 4s that send their hand and Deck to the GY, fuel GY-banishing Bujingi effects, and stack themselves into Rank 4 Xyz bosses.

hooks.label: Banishes from your own GY
hooks.why: Quilin, Centipede, Hare, Boar and Fox all banish themselves from the GY as a cost, Hirume banishes a Bujin from the GY to Summon itself, and Amaterasu and Bujincarnation recover banished monsters, so any outside card that banishes cards from your GY as a cost or effect feeds the cycle.

hooks.label: Sends your hand to the GY
hooks.why: Yamato, Tsukuyomi, Mikazuchi and Mahitotsu all pay off when Bujin cards are sent from the hand to the GY, so outside cards that do the same to your hand are free fuel.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Kagutsuchi mills five on Summon and Mahitotsu sends from Deck to GY, so outside cards that mill put Bujingi beasts into the GY where their effects live.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: The deck constantly sends its own cards from hand and Deck to the GY, so outside monsters with an effect that triggers when they are sent to the GY by a card effect get used for free.

hooks.label: Level 4 LIGHT monsters
hooks.why: Every Bujin is a Level 4 LIGHT monster and Tsukuyomi needs two Level 4 LIGHT monsters as material, so any outside Level 4 LIGHT monster is Xyz fuel for the whole Rank 4 ladder.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior support
hooks.why: All the Main Deck Bujin bosses and the Bujingi tricks key off Beast-Warrior-Type monsters you control, so generic Beast-Warrior search and support hits the whole deck.

profile.plan: Warriors that Link Summon over and over, searching a new Gouki card every time one of their monsters leaves the field for the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Gouki monster is a Warrior and Powerload Ogre only asks for 2+ Warrior monsters as Link material, so generic Warrior support works across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends your monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Suprex, Headbatt and every other Gouki search a card when sent from the field to the GY, so outside cards that send or destroy your own monsters turn each one into a draw.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Twistcobra, Blade Ogre and Powerload Ogre all Tribute your monsters as costs, so outside monsters that trigger when Tributed get that cost for free.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summon users
hooks.why: Gouki Thunder Ogre grants an additional Normal Summon to its zones, so outside monsters with effects that trigger when Normal Summoned get a free extra activation.

hooks.label: Fusion material monsters
hooks.why: Gouki The Tyrant Ogre is Fusion Summoned from a Gouki Link Monster plus any Warrior, Dinosaur or Cyberse monster, so strong outside monsters of those Types are its other half.

profile.plan: A swarm of Level 4 EARTH Warriors that stack Levels and swarm the field to make Rank 4 Xyz Monsters, with Dodododo Warrior rewarding you for detaching it as material.

hooks.label: Rank 4 Xyz bosses
hooks.why: Dodododo Warrior locks you into Xyz Monsters for the turn, and the deck floods the field with Level 4s, so Rank 4 Xyz Monsters are the payoff.

hooks.label: Detaches Xyz material
hooks.why: Dodododo Warrior searches a Zubaba monster when detached from an Xyz Monster to pay for its effect, so outside cards that detach as a cost trigger it for free.

hooks.label: Utopia monsters
hooks.why: Onomatopia places a counter that boosts all your monsters each time a Utopia monster is Special Summoned to your field, so any Utopia or its supports feed it.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Nearly every Dododo monster is a Warrior, so generic Warrior searchers, revival and boosts reach the whole deck.

hooks.label: Level manipulation
hooks.why: Dododo Driver only tweaks Levels of monsters Special Summoned by Dododo effects, so outside cards that freely change Levels help hit the exact Rank for Xyz Summons.

profile.plan: Beast-Warrior warlords that out-tempo the opponent by bouncing, destroying and stealing their cards while feeding their own effects by sending cards from hand, field and Continuous Spells/Traps to the GY.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Ancient Warriors monster is a Beast-Warrior, and Double Dragon Lords Links using 2 Beast-Warrior monsters, so generic Beast-Warrior support hits the whole deck.

hooks.label: Continuous Spells that trigger in the GY
hooks.why: Zhou Gong, Lu Jing, Jia Wen and Zhuge Kong all send a face-up Continuous Spell/Trap you control to the GY as a cost, so outside Continuous Spells/Traps with an effect when sent to the GY get it for free.

hooks.label: Triggers off destruction
hooks.why: Zhang Yuan, Cao De and Jia Wen all follow up when a card the opponent controls is destroyed, so outside removal sets off a chain of follow-ups.

hooks.label: Attribute changers
hooks.why: Borrowing of Arrows and Sun-Liu Alliance only pay off when your Ancient Warriors have 2 or more different Attributes, so cards that change a monster's Attribute turn them on.

hooks.label: Bounces opponent's cards
hooks.why: Double Dragon Lords and Sun Mou return opponent's face-up cards to the hand, which also helps Lu Feng give itself away as the highest-ATK monster, so more bounce compounds the plan.

profile.plan: Fairy Pendulum musicians that set one odd and one even Pendulum Scale, swarm through Pendulum Summons, and recycle their monsters between the hand, field, and face-up Extra Deck.

hooks.label: Generic Pendulum monsters
hooks.why: GranSolfachord Musecia is Link Summoned from any 2 Pendulum Monsters, and the scales only care about odd and even values, so outside Pendulum Monsters slot straight into the engine.

hooks.label: Pendulum support cards
hooks.why: The whole deck lives on Pendulum Scales and face-up Extra Deck Pendulums, so outside cards that search, place or scale Pendulum Monsters work on it directly.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Solfachord and GranSolfachord monster is a Fairy, so generic Fairy searchers and boosts apply to the entire deck.

hooks.label: Puts Pendulums in Extra Deck
hooks.why: FaSolfachord Fancia, Solfachord Elegance and Musecia all want Pendulum Monsters sent to the face-up Extra Deck for later recycling, so outside cards that do that feed the payoffs of Harmonia, Symphony and Scale.

hooks.label: Extra Pendulum Summons
hooks.why: Solfachord Happiness grants an extra Pendulum Summon only once per turn, and Cutia, Dreamia and Fancia protect those Summons, so more outside cards granting additional Pendulum Summons extend the deck's swarming.

profile.plan: Little Level 3 Beasts park themselves in Defense Position around a big Link-3 boss that forces every monster into Defense, feeding payoffs that count Defense Position monsters and letting them attack from Defense with piercing.

hooks.label: Defense Position enablers
hooks.why: Reichheart draws, Reichphobia destroys and Alternative burns only once 3 or more Defense Position monsters are on the field, so outside cards that put monsters into Defense Position turn every payoff on.

hooks.label: Level 3 Beast support
hooks.why: Astra, Acro and Belone are all Level 3 EARTH Beasts and Tri-Heart recycles a Level 3 from the GY, so generic Level 3 Beast cards line up with the whole core.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior Link support
hooks.why: Light-Heart and Tri-Heart are Beast-Warrior Link Monsters, so outside cards that search or revive Beast-Warriors hit the deck's bosses.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Twinsaw and Alternative Tribute Scareclaw monsters as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get that trigger for free.

hooks.label: Banished from the GY
hooks.why: Arrival, Twinsaw and Decline all banish the archetype's cards from the GY as costs, so outside cards that trigger when they are banished from the GY get used on their own.

profile.plan: Rock Normal Monsters that combine: Alpha, Beta and Gamma Tribute into Valkyrion or banish into Berserkion, and the pair Fusion Summons into Imperion Magnum, with Epsilon and Magnet Induction flooding the field.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Alpha, Beta and Gamma are Normal Monsters, so any card that searches, revives or protects Normal Monsters works on the deck's core bodies.

hooks.label: Rock support
hooks.why: Every Magnet Warrior and Magna Warrior monster is a Rock, so generic Rock support covers the whole deck including Imperion Magnum.

hooks.label: Sends Rocks from Deck to GY
hooks.why: Epsilon sends a Level 4 or lower Magnet Warrior from the Deck to the GY, and Berserkion revives its materials from the GY, so milling your own Rock monsters feeds both.

hooks.label: Triggers when banished
hooks.why: Berserkion banishes your Magnet Warriors from hand, GY and field as its Summoning cost, so outside cards with an effect when they are banished get used for free.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: Valkyrion Tributes Alpha, Beta and Gamma from hand and/or field to Summon itself, so outside cards that do something when Tributed get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Fusion Summons using GY materials
hooks.why: Imperion Magnum must be Fusion Summoned using Valkyrion and Berserkion, and both are hard to keep on field, so Fusion cards that use materials from the hand, Deck or GY make it reachable.

profile.plan: DARK Fiends whose effects only switch on once your hand is completely empty, so the deck throws its hand away, fills the GY, and Special Summons from it while running on zero cards.

hooks.label: Discards your own hand
hooks.why: Infernity Sage, Wave-Motion Inferno and Infernity Inferno all empty the hand fast, and every Infernity effect needs that, so outside cards that make you discard your own cards speed up the payoff and load the GY for Necromancer, Launcher and ZERO-MAX.

hooks.label: Rewards empty hand
hooks.why: Nearly every Infernity card reads 'if you have no cards in your hand', so outside cards that also get stronger or trigger with no cards in hand are pulling in the same direction.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: The archetype is almost entirely DARK Fiends and Doom Slinger Special Summons Fiends from the hand, so generic Fiend search, revival and support hits the whole deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished from GY
hooks.why: Paranoia, General, Conjurer, Pawn and Queen all banish Infernity cards from the GY as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are banished from the GY get triggered for free.

hooks.label: DARK Attribute support
hooks.why: Infernity Paranoia Tributes a DARK monster as its cost and Queen banishes DARK monsters from the GY, so any outside card that supports DARK monsters has extra uses here.

profile.plan: Reptiles that live in the Graveyard, reviving themselves by Tributing your monsters and milling Reptiles of both Attributes to keep bodies and fodder flowing.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Nauya, Nunu, Water Lily, Serpent Strike and Daybreak all send Reptile monsters from your Deck to the GY, so any outside card that mills your own Deck feeds them.

hooks.label: Reptile support
hooks.why: Every Ogdoadic monster is a Reptile and Nunu locks you into Special Summoning Reptiles, so generic Reptile support covers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Keurse, Aron, Aleirtt, Amunessia and Ogdoabyss revive themselves by Tributing your monsters, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed get their cost paid for free.

hooks.label: Sends opponent's cards to GY
hooks.why: Aron and Amunessia trigger when the opponent's cards hit the GY, and Hollow and Flogos want monsters in the opponent's GY to steal, so outside cards that send the opponent's cards there fuel both.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to GY
hooks.why: Zohah and Flogos send cards from your hand to the GY and Serpent Strike sends monsters from your hand or field, so outside monsters with an effect when sent to the GY are free value.

profile.plan: A WIND Psychic/Winged Beast recursion engine that floats off battle and GY sends, chaining Special Summons from the Deck into Synchro and Xyz bosses while shuffling Gusto monsters from the GY back into the Deck for value.

hooks.label: Sends WIND monsters from hand to GY
hooks.why: Gusto Griffin Special Summons a Gusto from the Deck when it is sent from the hand to the GY, so any outside card that sends or discards your WIND monsters is a free Summon.

hooks.label: Sends your field to the GY
hooks.why: Gulldo, Falco and Vedir all Special Summon a Gusto from the Deck when they are sent from the field to the GY, so outside cards that send your own WIND monsters off the field pay you twice.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Gusto Squirro Special Summons a Level 5+ Gusto from the Deck when destroyed by a card effect, so outside cards that destroy your WIND monsters as a cost or effect turn into big Summons.

hooks.label: WIND support
hooks.why: Every Gusto monster and Extra Deck boss is WIND, and Pilica, Codor and Thunbolt all Special Summon WIND monsters, so generic WIND support hits the whole deck.

hooks.label: WIND Psychic recruiters
hooks.why: Codor and Thunbolt fetch any WIND Psychic with 1500 or less DEF, and Pilica revives WIND Tuners, so outside WIND Psychic monsters with low DEF slot straight into the recursion loops.

hooks.label: Battle-float payoffs
hooks.why: Gusto Egul, Winda and Thunbolt all trigger when destroyed by battle, and Sphreez reflects your battle damage to the opponent, so cards that make opponents attack or punish them for attacking fit the deck's plan.

profile.plan: Level 1 LIGHT Tuner support that converts itself into a Blue-Eyes monster from the hand or GY, while the archetype's Spells search out the Tuners and the Blue-Eyes cards that go with them.

hooks.label: Level 1 LIGHT Tuners
hooks.why: Wishes for Eyes of Blue searches any Level 1 LIGHT Tuner plus a Blue-Eyes Spell/Trap, so any such Tuner is a direct target.

hooks.label: Named Blue-Eyes White Dragon cards
hooks.why: Wishes for Eyes of Blue searches any Spell/Trap that specifically mentions "Blue-Eyes White Dragon" in its text.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Spirit with Eyes of Blue locks you into Special Summoning only Dragons, so only Dragon-restricted support is safe in this deck.

hooks.label: Reacts to being Tributed
hooks.why: Spirit with Eyes of Blue Tributes itself as its Summoning cost, so an outside card that triggers when it is Tributed gets a free activation.

hooks.label: Wants to be bounced
hooks.why: Vision with Eyes of Blue returns your own face-up monster to the hand as a cost-like setup, so monsters with an effect when returned to the hand pair with it.

profile.plan: A Link-spam deck of Insects, Plants and Reptiles that Special Summons by sending, banishing and recycling its own monsters, then revives its Link Monsters from the GY by putting materials back on the bottom of the Deck.

hooks.label: Banish-triggered monsters
hooks.why: Evil Seed banishes from the hand as a cost, Mantis Monk and Selene Snapper banish from the GY, and Wicked Butterfly only draws when it is banished, so any outside monster that acts when it is banished gets triggered for free.

hooks.label: Sends your own Deck to GY
hooks.why: Evil Seed's self-Summon sends an Insect, Plant or Reptile from the hand to the GY and Bloom searches into a discard, so milling cards of those Types from your own Deck feeds the deck's costs and triggers.

hooks.label: Discard-triggered cards
hooks.why: Ragnaraika Bloom searches a monster and then makes you discard 1 card, so any outside card with an effect when it is discarded turns that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Type-changing effects
hooks.why: Wicked Butterfly draws one card per different Monster Type among your Insects, Plants and Reptiles and Hunting Dance destroys one target per different Type on your Links, so outside cards that add or change monster Types raise those counts.

hooks.label: Insect, Plant and Reptile support
hooks.why: Every Ragnaraika card only summons or uses Insect, Plant or Reptile monsters and their effects only touch those Types, so generic support for those three Types works on the whole deck.

profile.plan: Fiend gunmen that fire Spells/Traps straight from the hand on either player's turn, and whose monsters trigger whenever a Spell/Trap is activated in their column.

hooks.label: LIGHT Fiend monsters
hooks.why: Mastermind Caspar's Link Summon requires a LIGHT Fiend monster, and every Main Deck Musketeer is one, so outside LIGHT Fiends supply material and share the Type/Attribute.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Magical Musket monster is a LIGHT Fiend, so generic Fiend searchers, revivers and boosts cover the whole deck.

hooks.label: Rewards Spell/Trap activations
hooks.why: The Musketeers trigger off Spell/Trap Cards being activated in their column and Zakiel draws once per activation, so outside cards that gain effects each time a Spell/Trap is activated compound the payoff.

hooks.label: Banishes the Graveyards
hooks.why: Magical Musket - Dancing Needle banishes up to 3 cards in the GYs, so outside cards that banish GY cards stack with it to shut down graveyard decks.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck that mixes Dracoslayer and Dracoverlord Pendulum Monsters, destroys its own Pendulum Zones on purpose to search, and Tributes them to Summon its big bosses.

hooks.label: Other Pendulum Scales
hooks.why: The Pendulum Effects of Luster Pendulum, Majesty Pegasus, Wind Unicorn Parallel and Dinomight Powerload all only work with a card in the other Pendulum Zone, so any outside Pendulum Monster with a usable Scale fills the gap.

hooks.label: Destroys your Pendulum Zone
hooks.why: Luster Pendulum's effect destroys the card in your other Pendulum Zone to search a copy of it, and Master Pendulum and Wind Unicorn Parallel destroy cards in Pendulum Zones too, so outside cards that destroy your own Pendulum Zone cards become searches.

hooks.label: Tributes your Pendulums
hooks.why: Dinomight Powerload adds a card from your Extra Deck when it is Tributed, and Master Peace is Summoned by Tributing a Dracoslayer, so outside cards that Tribute your monsters fuel both.

hooks.label: Wants to be destroyed
hooks.why: Ignis Phoenix Special Summons a Dracoslayer from the Deck and makes it a Tuner when it is destroyed, so outside Pendulum Monsters that trigger when destroyed by a card effect get set off by the deck's own destruction effects.

hooks.label: Level 4 Pendulum monsters
hooks.why: Majester Paladin is Xyz Summoned from 2 Level 4 Pendulum Monsters and Ignister Prominence needs non-Tuner Pendulum materials, so any outside Level 4 Pendulum Monster is direct material.

hooks.label: Field Spell payoffs
hooks.why: Majesty Pegasus adds any Field Spell from your Deck to your hand when Special or Pendulum Summoned, so Field Spells that pay off when you control them come with a free search attached.

profile.plan: Insect Flip monsters that hide face-down, punish the opponent for removing them by swarming two more from the Deck, and swarm to Link 2 bosses that buff and protect them.

hooks.label: Flips your own monsters face-up
hooks.why: The deck's power sits in FLIP effects like Receptor's search and Axon's Spell/Trap removal, and outside cards that flip your face-down monsters face-up trigger them without waiting a turn.

hooks.label: Link Monsters
hooks.why: Krawlers want to sit in zones a Link Monster points to, Crusadia Krawler searches there, and Neurogos and Synaphysis need 2 Insect or EARTH Link material, so generic Link Monsters are both engine and payoff.

hooks.label: Insect support
hooks.why: Every Krawler is an Insect and the Link bosses use Insect materials, so cards that search, revive or strengthen Insects work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Low-Level Insect monsters
hooks.why: World Legacy in Shadow Special Summons any Level 2 or lower Insect from the hand each turn, so other small Insects with useful effects come down for free alongside the Krawlers.

hooks.label: EARTH support
hooks.why: Synaphysis asks for 2 EARTH monsters as Link material and all Krawlers are EARTH, so cards that search or revive EARTH monsters feed both.

profile.plan: Rock Ritual Monsters that Ritual Summon each other straight from the hand, Deck and GY by Tributing monsters whose total Levels add up, paying nothing but the monsters on board.

hooks.label: Any Ritual Monster
hooks.why: Ophiel and Hagith Ritual Summon ANY Ritual Monster from the hand, and Bethor, Phaleg and Portal count and recycle Ritual Monsters in the GY, so every generic Ritual boss is a valid target.

hooks.label: Ritual Summon support
hooks.why: The deck's monsters Summon themselves but still rely on generic Ritual Summoning cards for speed, recovery and searching of both the monsters and their Levels.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Every Megalith Ritual Summon Tributes monsters from the hand or field whose total Levels add up, so outside cards with effects that trigger when they are Tributed get their payoff for free.

hooks.label: Level 4 EARTH fodder
hooks.why: Level 4 monsters on the field are the raw material for the Level-8 Megaliths and can be doubled by Megalith Promotion to reach Level 12 Notrah Plura, and EARTH support covers the whole archetype.

hooks.label: Rock support
hooks.why: Every Megalith monster is a Rock, so cards that search, revive or strengthen Rock monsters work across the entire archetype.

profile.plan: Fiends that wear the 'Evil Eye of Selene' Equip Spell for destruction and negation effects, paying Life Points each time to grow their attacker while Links and Familiars swarm around it.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Evil Eye monster is a Fiend, and Evil Eye Reemergence locks you into Special Summoning Fiends only, so generic Fiend support covers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Spells/Traps
hooks.why: Evil Eye Domain - Pareidolia and Evil Eye Repose both trigger when they are destroyed by card effect, recovering cards from the GY or banished zone, so any outside card that pops your own backrow is a plus.

hooks.label: Pays Life Points
hooks.why: Selene drains 500 LP every activation and its GY effect pays 1000, while Gorgoneio gives a bigger boost the lower your LP are, so the deck actively wants cards that spend LP.

hooks.label: Rewards lower Life Points
hooks.why: Evil Eye of Gorgoneio gives the equipped monster ATK equal to the LP deficit, so outside cards with payoffs while your LP are lower than your opponent's stack with it.

profile.plan: A machine-toy swarm deck that stacks Levels on the fly to Xyz Summon, and whose monsters' 'once while face-up' effects reset every time they get flipped face-down.

hooks.label: Flips your monsters face-down
hooks.why: Wind-Up Magician, Rat, Bat, Warrior and the rest are all 'only once while this card is face-up', and Zenmaister and Legendary Wind-Up Key already flip them face-down to reset that - any outside card that does the same reuses their effects.

hooks.label: Machine-Type support
hooks.why: Every Wind-Up Extra Deck monster - Zenmaines, Zenmaity, Zenmaioh, Zenmaister, Zenmaintenance - is a Machine, so cards that search, protect or boost Machines hit the whole Extra Deck.

hooks.label: Level 3 self-summoners
hooks.why: Zenmaines and Carrier Zenmaity are Rank 3 and need two Level 3 monsters, which the deck only has a few of (Rat, Rabbit, Dog, Hunter), so outside Level 3 monsters that Special Summon themselves are ready Xyz material.

hooks.label: Level manipulation
hooks.why: Shark, Warrior, Dog and Weights & Zenmaisures constantly shift Levels to line up Rank 3 to 5 Xyz Summons, so outside cards that change Levels extend that flexibility to any monster.

profile.plan: Tributes a Synchro Monster with Assault Mode Activate to swap it for a bigger, harder-to-Summon '/Assault Mode' boss that revives the Synchro when destroyed.

hooks.label: Synchro Monsters
hooks.why: Assault Mode Activate, Assault Mode Zero and Assault Reboot Tribute a Synchro Monster you control as the cost to bring out the /Assault Mode bosses, so the deck lives and dies on having Synchro Monsters to Tribute.

hooks.label: Tuner monsters
hooks.why: Psi-Reflector and Arcane Apprentice are Tuners, and every Summon route ends in Synchro Summoning the boss the deck will Tribute, so Tuners to pair with them are always wanted.

hooks.label: Revives your Synchro Monster
hooks.why: The base Synchro Monsters pile up in your GY after being Tributed, and the /Assault Mode bosses Summon them back from there when destroyed, so recovery that targets Synchro Monsters keeps the engine going.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Assault Mode Activate, Assault Mode Zero, Assault Reboot and Assault Overload Tribute your Synchro and /Assault Mode monsters as a cost, so outside monsters with effects when Tributed get those costs for free.

hooks.label: Extra Synchro Summon help
hooks.why: Arcane Apprentice only searches when used as Synchro material and the whole deck is built around getting a Synchro Monster on board fast, so cards that Synchro Summon using material from the hand, GY or opponent's field speed that up.

profile.plan: Corrupt copies of famous dragons that summon themselves by banishing the original, but die unless a face-up Field Spell is kept on the field.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Every Malefic monster destroys itself without a face-up Field Spell, and only Malefic Territory fetches one, so outside cards that search or protect Field Spells keep the whole deck alive.

hooks.label: DARK Dragon support
hooks.why: Nearly every Malefic monster is a DARK Dragon, so generic DARK or Dragon support works across the deck.

hooks.label: Synchro Monster recursion
hooks.why: Malefic Paradox Dragon Special Summons a Synchro Monster from either player's Graveyard, so outside Synchro Monsters with strong effects or self-recursion fill that slot.

hooks.label: Banished Level 8 Synchro revival
hooks.why: Malefic Paradigm Dragon returns a banished Level 8 Synchro Monster to the Extra Deck and Special Summons it, so outside cards that banish or recycle Level 8 Synchro Monsters feed that payoff.

hooks.label: When your monster is destroyed
hooks.why: Malefic Truth Dragon and Malefic Tune both trigger off a Malefic monster being destroyed by battle or card effect, so the deck tolerates and rewards outside cards that destroy your own monsters.

profile.plan: Spellcasters whose ATK grows with a Level that rises every turn, banishing their own Spellcasters to trigger effects, manipulate Levels and Synchro Summon.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Fortune Lady monster is a Spellcaster and Fortune Lady Every's Synchro Summon needs non-Tuner Spellcasters, so generic Spellcaster support works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Raises monster Levels
hooks.why: Every Fortune Lady's ATK is its Level x 200-400 and Fortune Lady Earth burns for 400 whenever its Level increases, so outside cards that raise Levels are direct damage and power.

hooks.label: Banishes cards from the GY
hooks.why: Fortune Vision grants protection whenever a card is banished by card effect, and Fortune Lady Every banishes Spellcasters from the GY to revive itself, so GY banishing cards pay off twice.

hooks.label: Recovers banished monsters
hooks.why: Fortune Lady Rewind Special Summons the deck's banished monsters and Fortune's Future draws 2 off one, so outside cards that return banished monsters keep that banished pile usable.

hooks.label: Spellcaster Synchro monsters
hooks.why: Fortune Lady Calling locks you to Synchro Monsters for the rest of the turn and Every asks for non-Tuner Spellcaster materials, so Spellcaster Synchro Monsters from other archetypes are the only Extra Deck options it allows.

profile.plan: Spams Level 4 Warrior monsters to stack up Rank 4 Warrior Xyz bosses (above all Rhongomyniad), fighting with piercing battle damage and ATK doublers, and pays its own LP down to 500 for power effects.

hooks.label: Makes Rank 4 Xyz
hooks.why: Every Champion, including Rhongomyniad and Kusanagi, is a Rank 4 Warrior Xyz built from Level 4 Warriors, so outside cards that Xyz Summon with Level 4s extend the boss lineup.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck, main and Extra, is a Warrior, so generic Warrior searchers, revivers and boosters work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Makes you discard Warriors
hooks.why: Thousand Blades' Special Summon-from-Deck effect costs discarding 1 'Heroic' card, so any outside card that makes you discard feeds it and fills the GY for Heroic Call and Magnum Excalibur.

hooks.label: Damages yourself
hooks.why: Thousand Blades revives itself when you take damage, and Claivesolish pays LP down to 500, so outside cards that inflict damage to you or cost LP are free value here.

hooks.label: Gains effect when detached
hooks.why: The Champions constantly detach materials for their effects, so an outside card that triggers when it is detached from an Xyz Monster as material gets used for free.

profile.plan: Machine Tuners and searchers that build Attribute-flexible Synchro monsters, triggering most of their effects off Normal Summons and deck-thinning searches.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Undine, Power Planner, Turbo, Neutron, Crusher, Magma and more only trigger when Normal Summoned, so any outside card granting additional Normal Summons multiplies the deck's triggers.

hooks.label: WATER monsters that want to be milled
hooks.why: Genex Undine sends 1 WATER monster from the Deck to the GY as its cost, so outside WATER monsters with an effect in the GY get it for free.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Nearly every Genex monster, including all its Tuners and Synchros, is a Machine, so generic Machine-Type support works across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be bounced
hooks.why: Genex Ally Birdman returns 1 face-up monster you control to the hand as its Special Summon cost, so outside monsters that trigger or recur when returned to the hand get value from it.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: Genex Worker Tributes itself and Genex Army and Genex Solar want Genex monsters Tributed, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed fit the deck's Tribute lines.

profile.plan: Machine Synchro deck that constantly flips its own monsters between Attack and Defense Position, triggering draws, banishes and buffs off every position change.

hooks.label: Changes battle positions
hooks.why: Bureido draws, Bureibu banishes, Anatomy gains counters and Trick House destroys off any battle position change of a Karakuri, so outside cards that flip monsters are free triggers.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Karakuri monster is a Machine, and Burei, Bureido and Bureibu all require Machine non-Tuner materials.

hooks.label: EARTH Machine Synchro bosses
hooks.why: Kunamzan locks you to Special Summoning only EARTH Machine monsters from the Extra Deck for the rest of the turn, so other big EARTH Machine Synchro monsters stay playable.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Ninishi grants an extra Normal Summon of a Karakuri each turn, so the deck wants more ways to Normal Summon repeatedly and keep its Tuners flowing.

hooks.label: Defense Position payoffs
hooks.why: Bureibu protects all your Defense Position monsters from battle destruction and Nanashick draws per Defense Position Karakuri, so cards that Set or Summon your monsters in Defense Position gain value.

profile.plan: LIGHT Fairy maidens that swarm from the hand and deck, stack and banish the opponent's cards, and roll over them with boosted attacks and an extra Battle Phase.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Valkyrie monster is a Fairy and Goddess Skuld's Oracle locks you to Summoning Fairies, so generic Fairy searchers and support fit the whole deck.

hooks.label: Banishes opponent's cards
hooks.why: Valkyrie Dritte and Funfte gain ATK for each of the opponent's banished monsters and Valkyrie Erda banishes their cards instead of sending them to the GY, so anything that banishes the opponent's resources feeds the payoffs.

hooks.label: Continuous Spell engine
hooks.why: The deck's core spells, Goddess Skuld's Oracle, Verdande's Guidance and Urd's Verdict, are all Continuous Spells that search each other, and Zweite recycles a Continuous Spell from the GY after battling.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent from the Deck
hooks.why: Valkyrie Funfte sends any 1 Spell/Trap from your Deck to the GY once per turn, so outside cards with an effect when sent from the Deck to the GY are triggered for free.

hooks.label: Union monsters
hooks.why: Valkyrie Chariot and Fortune Chariot are Union monsters that equip to your Fairies, and Pegasus Wing just needs any Union monster in the GY to let the Valkyries attack directly.

profile.plan: A swarm of small FIRE monsters (many of them Tuners with 200 DEF) that wins battles, banishes the opponent's Graveyard piece by piece, and Synchro Summons into big Pyro bosses.

hooks.label: FIRE attribute support
hooks.why: Every Flamvell monster is FIRE and cards like Firedog, Counter and Lady all search, banish or send FIRE monsters specifically, so generic FIRE support works across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Pyro non-Tuners
hooks.why: Ancient Flamvell Deity needs a FIRE Tuner plus non-Tuner Pyro-Type monsters, and Flamvell Fiend's burn counts Pyro monsters in your GY, so outside Pyro monsters are both Synchro fodder and damage.

hooks.label: Banishes the opponent's GY
hooks.why: Neo Flamvell Lady, Garuda, Shaman and Ancient Flamvell Deity all banish cards from the opponent's Graveyard, and Origin and Sabre get stronger the fewer cards sit there, so more GY-banishing outside cards compounds the lock.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Neo Flamvell Lady sends 1 FIRE monster from your hand to the GY as a cost and Flamvell Baby sends itself from the hand, so an outside FIRE monster with an effect when it hits the GY gets that cost for free.

hooks.label: Extra battle-phase damage
hooks.why: The deck's payoff cards all trigger on battle results — Uruquizas pierces and grows, Grunika and Fiend burn on battle damage — so outside cards that force battles or add damage in the Battle Phase multiply it.

profile.plan: Rank 4 FIRE Warrior Xyz brawlers that stack materials on their Boxers, detach them for protection and punches, and punish anything that happens during the Battle Phase.

hooks.label: Level 4 FIRE Warriors
hooks.why: Battlin' Boxer King Dempsey searches and sends any Level 4 or lower FIRE Warrior, and most of the deck's Rank 4s want exactly those bodies as material.

hooks.label: Sends your monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Glassjaw and Uppercutter trigger when sent to the GY by a card effect, so outside cards that mill or send your FIRE Warriors turn into free searches and revives.

hooks.label: Feeds Xyz materials
hooks.why: Lead Yoke spends materials to avoid destruction and Shadow detaches to Summon itself, so outside cards that attach more materials to your Xyz monsters keep the engine alive.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic spells
hooks.why: Comet Cestus and General Kaiser are Rank 5 upgrades that only pay off when summoned over Star Cestus and Nova Kaiser, so Rank-Up-Magics are the natural way up.

hooks.label: Counter Traps
hooks.why: Uppercutter searches and Sets any 'Counter' Counter Trap from the Deck or GY, and Jolt Counter wants more Counter Traps that fire during the Battle Phase.

profile.plan: Level 1 Flip monsters that hand themselves to the opponent face-down, then punish the opponent for flipping or holding them, backed by Rank 1 Xyz bosses.

hooks.label: Turns monsters face-down
hooks.why: Mimighoul Dungeon, Mimighoul Master and Giant Mimighoul all pay off while the opponent controls a face-down monster, so outside cards that flip the opponent's monsters face-down feed the whole engine.

hooks.label: Generic Flip monsters
hooks.why: Mimighoul Maker reveals and Special Summons any two Flip monsters with different names to the opponent's field, so strong outside Flip monsters are extra ammunition.

hooks.label: Level 1 self-summoners
hooks.why: Giant Mimighoul only needs 2 Level 1 monsters as material, so any outside Level 1 that Special Summons itself is free Xyz material.

hooks.label: Rank 1 Xyz payoffs
hooks.why: The deck makes Rank 1 Xyz Summons with its Level 1 monsters, so outside Rank 1 Xyz monsters with removal or disruption ride on the same materials.

profile.plan: Low-level Spellcaster girls that dodge attacks, redirect them and summon bigger Spellcasters from the hand or Deck, turning every attack on them into a free summon.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Chocolate Magician Girl and Kiwi Magician Girl discard Spellcaster monsters as costs, so outside monsters with an effect when they are discarded get used for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Lemon Magician Girl Tributes a Magician Girl as the cost to search any Spellcaster, so outside monsters that trigger when Tributed are free value.

hooks.label: Big Spellcaster bosses
hooks.why: Lemon, Apple and Chocolate Magician Girl Special Summon Spellcasters from the hand or Graveyard when attacked, so any Level 5 or lower Spellcaster is a live target for them.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Magician Girl is a Spellcaster and they search, summon and buff Spellcasters (Kiwi protects all Spellcasters you control), so generic Spellcaster support works across the deck.

hooks.label: Continuous Spell payoffs
hooks.why: Performapal Sky Magician Girl Special Summons itself from the hand for free while you control a Continuous Spell, so any Continuous Spell is an enabler.

hooks.label: LIGHT Spellcaster GY enablers
hooks.why: Performapal Sky Magician Girl sends a Level 4 or lower LIGHT Spellcaster from the Deck to the Graveyard, so outside LIGHT Spellcasters that want to be sent there get milled for free.

profile.plan: LIGHT Fairies that toss a coin when Summoned and get a good or bad effect off the result, aiming to fix the flip with Light Barrier and push out huge Level 10 bosses.

hooks.label: Coin toss cards
hooks.why: The Sun Special Summons itself whenever a coin-tossing card is on the field, and its Heads effect Sets a coin-toss Spell from the Deck while Chaos Ruler's Tails searches any coin-tossing card.

hooks.label: Sends your monsters to the GY
hooks.why: The World skips turns by sending 2 monsters you control to the GY, and the EX Rulers need exactly 3 monsters sent there to Summon, so anything that does it as part of its effect is free fuel.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: The World, the EX Rulers and Chaos Ruler's Fusion Summon all send your own monsters to the GY, so outside monsters that trigger there get their effect for free as Summoning fodder.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Temperance, the Fiend and the Hierophant all discard themselves from the hand as costs, so outside monsters with an effect when discarded turn into value.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Arcana Force monster is a LIGHT Fairy, so generic Fairy searchers, revival and boosts cover the whole deck including the Level 10 bosses.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Most Arcana Force monsters only get their coin effect when Summoned, so extra Normal Summons let multiple coin effects go off in one turn.

profile.plan: Stacks overlapping Rank 4 and 5 Xyz Monsters on top of each other, detaching materials for protective and disruptive effects, with Utopia Rising and Numbers Eveil turning every Xyz Summon into more bodies.

hooks.label: Level 4 monster spawners
hooks.why: Shark Drake, Utopia, Silent Honor ARK and Utopia Rising all Xyz Summon from Level 4 monsters, so anything that floods the field with Level 4s is fuel for the whole ladder.

hooks.label: Xyz material movers
hooks.why: Utopia Rising transfers its own materials to revived Numbers and Buzzking steals cards from the opponent's GY as material, so outside cards that attach or attach themselves as Xyz material keep the detach costs paid.

hooks.label: Rewards being detached
hooks.why: The deck detaches materials constantly as cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are detached as Xyz material get it for free.

hooks.label: Triggers on Xyz Summoning
hooks.why: Utopia Rising Special Summons itself from the GY whenever you Xyz Summon, and Numbers Eveil summons the whole stack at once, so outside cards that trigger off an Xyz Summon go off for free.

hooks.label: Same Rank Xyz makers
hooks.why: Number F0: Utopic Future Zexal needs two Xyz Monsters with the same Rank as material, so any outside engine that makes two of the same Rank feeds it directly.

hooks.label: WATER monster support
hooks.why: Spider Shark Xyz Summons with Level 5 WATER monsters and the Shark Drakes are all WATER, so cards that supply or support WATER monsters fit the water wing of the deck.

profile.plan: Low-ATK LIGHT Thunders that attack directly and trigger search, disruption or removal each time they deal battle damage, leaning on Thunders staying alive to rack up pings.

hooks.label: Thunder LIGHT support
hooks.why: Nearly every Watt monster is a LIGHT Thunder, and Wattcube, Wattjustment, Wattcannon and Wattcine all key off Thunder monsters, so generic LIGHT Thunder support works across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Direct attack monsters
hooks.why: Every Watt payoff - Wattcobra's search, Wattgiraffe's lock, Wattpheasant's banish, Wattberyx's discard - only fires on battle damage from a direct attack, so outside monsters that can already attack directly fit right in.

hooks.label: Grants extra attacks
hooks.why: Each attack is another direct-attack trigger and Wattcobra, Wattgiraffe and friends have low ATK but reusable effects, so cards that grant additional attacks multiply the payoff.

hooks.label: Battle damage triggers
hooks.why: The whole deck is built around inflicting battle damage, and Wattcine already converts it to Life Points, so outside cards with an effect when battle damage is inflicted get triggered every single turn.

hooks.label: Small LIGHT monsters
hooks.why: Wattsychic Fighting Porter Special Summons up to 2 Level 3 or lower LIGHT monsters from the hand and rewards matching Type or Level, so outside Level 3 or lower LIGHT monsters are free bodies and combos.

hooks.label: Attack boost and piercing
hooks.why: Watt monsters have tiny ATK and only deal meaningful damage through direct attacks, and Wattpheasant's banish and Wattuna's Summons scale off landing that damage, so ATK boosts and piercing make every ping count.

profile.plan: Ancient-artifact monsters that shift their own Levels around to stack two same-Level monsters and Xyz Summon a Rank 3 to 6 'Number', mostly Rocks and Machines of EARTH and LIGHT.

hooks.label: Rock support
hooks.why: The majority of the Main Deck Chronomalies are Rock monsters (Crystal Skull, Moai, Tula Guardian, Cabrera Trebuchet and more), so generic Rock searchers, revivers and boosts hit most of the deck.

hooks.label: Summons Level 5 monsters
hooks.why: The key bosses Machu Mech and Vimana need 2 Level 5 monsters, and the deck plays many Level 5s that only Special Summon themselves, so outside cards that put Level 5 monsters on the field complete the Rank 5 Xyz.

hooks.label: Effects when Tributed
hooks.why: Cabrera Trebuchet and Chateau Huyuk Tribute Chronomaly monsters as a cost and Magella Globe Tributes itself, so outside monsters that trigger when Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Effects when banished
hooks.why: Chronomaly Technology and City Babylon banish Chronomaly monsters from the GY and Colossal Head banishes itself, so outside cards with effects that trigger when banished from the GY turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Number and Xyz support
hooks.why: The deck's Extra Deck is all Xyz Numbers (Atlandis equips a Number from the GY, Tuspa Rocket grants its effect to a Number), so cards that support Xyz Monsters or specifically Number monsters pay off everywhere.

hooks.label: Level-changing help
hooks.why: Golden Jet and Sol Monolith shift Chronomaly Levels to line up Xyz materials, so outside cards that alter Levels extend that trick to any monster on the field.

profile.plan: DARK Reptiles that turn the opponent's monsters to 0 ATK, then search off, destroy, steal or Synchro over the weakened bodies.

hooks.label: Drops opponent ATK to 0
hooks.why: Echidna searches one Reptile per 0 ATK monster, Hydra destroys them all and draws, and Vaskii Tribute Summons off two of them, so any outside card that zeroes opponent ATK feeds every payoff.

hooks.label: Exploits 0 ATK monsters
hooks.why: Scylla revives monsters it destroys at 0 ATK and Viper takes control of 0 ATK monsters, so outside cards that bounce, steal or otherwise interact with 0 ATK bodies keep the pressure on.

hooks.label: Reptile support
hooks.why: Every Reptilianne monster is a Reptile and Echidna, Melusine and Gardna all search or summon Reptiles generically, so any Reptile-typed support card slots straight in.

hooks.label: Reptile Tuners
hooks.why: Melusine wants a Reptile Tuner plus non-Tuners and Coatl can count as a non-Tuner itself, so extra Reptile Tuners from outside give the deck more Synchro routes.

profile.plan: Light and dark doubles that swap between two Field Spells, Tributing their own monsters mid-Battle Phase to summon the counterpart and keep the right Field Spell active.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: The whole deck Tributes its own monsters as a Quick Effect to summon their counterparts, so outside monsters that trigger when Tributed get activated for free every turn.

hooks.label: Fusion Summon enablers
hooks.why: Dream Mirror of Chaos Fusions using monsters you control, your hand or banished GY monsters, so any extra Fusion Summon effect converts the deck's swappable bodies into Oneiros.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Every monster's Quick Effect only works while Dream Mirror of Joy or Terror is in a Field Zone, so cards that fetch or activate Field Spells keep the engine running.

hooks.label: Banished card recovery
hooks.why: Joy and Terror banish themselves each End Phase and Dream Mirror Fantasy and Recap recycle them, so cards that recover or shuffle banished cards smooth the cycle.

hooks.label: Attributes matter
hooks.why: The Fusions need two Dream Mirror monsters with different Attributes and swap LIGHT/DARK forms, so monsters that change Attributes keep material requirements flexible.

profile.plan: Chemistry Dinosaurs (Hydrogen, Oxygen, Deuterium) that combine into Water Dragon by Tributing or shuffling them with 'Bonding' Spells, clearing the field of FIRE and Pyro monsters.

hooks.label: Level 7 or lower Dragon Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Carboneddon banishes itself from the GY to Special Summon a Level 7 or lower Dragon Normal Monster straight from the hand or Deck, so any such monster is a free boss.

hooks.label: Dinosaur support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Bonding monster is a Dinosaur, so generic Dinosaur searchers, revival and boosters serve the whole deck.

hooks.label: WATER monster support
hooks.why: Hydrogeddon, Duoterion, Water Dragon and Water Dragon Cluster are all WATER, so cards that search, revive or protect WATER monsters reach most of the deck.

hooks.label: Effect when Tributed
hooks.why: Bonding - H2O and D2O Tribute two Dinosaur materials as a cost, so outside monsters that trigger when they are Tributed get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Rock Fusion Monsters
hooks.why: Magnet Bonding Fusion Summons any Rock Fusion Monster by shuffling Rock monsters from hand, field, GY and banishment into the Deck, so any Rock Fusion is an extra deck option.

hooks.label: Extra attacks
hooks.why: Hydrogeddon only copies itself when it destroys an opponent's monster by battle, so outside cards that let monsters attack again multiply its Summon trigger.

profile.plan: Pendulum Spellcasters that bank a Spell Counter every time any Spell Card resolves, then spend those counters to negate, banish, bounce and summon.

hooks.label: Spell Counter cards
hooks.why: Every monster effect pays by removing Spell Counters from your field, so outside cards that make or carry Spell Counters fuel and extend the deck.

hooks.label: Spellcasters
hooks.why: The whole deck is Spellcaster, so generic Spellcaster search, revive and boost cards reach every one of them.

hooks.label: Pendulum monsters
hooks.why: Their Pendulum Effects destroy themselves to summon or recycle face-up Pendulum Monsters from the Extra Deck, and all share Scale 4, so other Pendulum cards both fill the other Scale and recycle.

hooks.label: Spell activation triggers
hooks.why: Jackal King and Master Cerberus gain 2 Spell Counters per activated Spell, so outside cards with their own effect when a Spell Card is activated get triggered alongside them.

hooks.label: Destroyed own Pendulums
hooks.why: Their Pendulum Effects destroy themselves as a cost, so outside Pendulum monsters with an effect when destroyed get it for free.

profile.plan: A control deck that banishes its own monsters as a resource: each small Nemeses Special Summons itself by recycling a banished monster, and the bosses banish monsters with different Attributes out of the GY and field to wipe Attributes off the board.

hooks.label: Banishes your own monsters
hooks.why: Flag, Corridor, Keystone and Umbrella all Special Summon themselves by targeting one of your banished monsters, so any outside card that banishes your monsters from your GY or field is free ammunition.

hooks.label: Returns itself when banished
hooks.why: The deck constantly banishes its own monsters, so outside monsters with an effect that recovers or triggers while banished get used for free and can even be shuffled back for the Nemeses Summons.

hooks.label: Banishes everything
hooks.why: Macro-style outside cards that banish cards instead of sending them to the GY keep the banished zone stocked so every Nemeses monster can Special Summon itself on demand.

profile.plan: Fish that banish themselves and each other, coming back the following Standby Phase and Synchro Summoning on the opponent's turn, scaling with the number of banished cards.

hooks.label: Banishes your Fish
hooks.why: Ixeep and Psiics trigger, Snopios and Zep recover, when a Fish monster is banished, so any outside card that banishes your Fish is an activator.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: The deck banishes its own monsters constantly as cost and effect, so outside monsters that do something when banished get used for free.

hooks.label: Fish support
hooks.why: Every Ghoti card names Fish monsters and all its Synchros require Fish or Fish Tuner materials, so generic Fish searchers, revivers and boosters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Fish Synchro bosses
hooks.why: Ghoti Cosmos Special Summons any Fish Synchro Monster once eight Fish are banished, and the Tuners Synchro Summon Fish Synchros on the opponent's turn, so other archetypes' Fish Synchros are free bosses.

hooks.label: Mass banish payoffs
hooks.why: Ghoti of the Deep Beyond's ATK is 500 x the number of banished monsters and Ghoti Fury boosts by 100 per banished card, so cards that banish many cards at once supercharge them.

profile.plan: LIGHT Thunder batteries that swarm the field to fuel big Tribute Summons and GY-based revival, multiplying each other's summons.

hooks.label: Thunder monster support
hooks.why: Every Batteryman monster and their boss Voltech Dragon is a Thunder, so generic Thunder search, revival and boost cards hit the whole deck.

hooks.label: Summons Thunder monsters
hooks.why: Batteryman Solar makes a Token every time any Thunder monster is Normal or Special Summoned while it's on the field, so outside cards that Summon Thunders generate free bodies.

hooks.label: Revives from the Graveyard
hooks.why: Battery Charger, Portable Battery Pack and Quick Charger all recycle Batterymen from the GY, and Industrial Strength banishes Thunders from there as a cost, so the deck lives out of its GY.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Batteryman Fuel Cell Tributes a Batteryman every turn to bounce an opponent's card, so outside monsters that trigger off being Tributed get that cost for free.

hooks.label: Easy Tribute Summon bosses
hooks.why: Super-Electromagnetic Voltech Dragon is a Level 5 that wants a Tribute Summon and rewards it with extra effects, so other Thunder monsters that Tribute Summon themselves extend the deck's core plan.

profile.plan: Machine Synchro Dragons built around Equip Spells: they search and load Equip Spells from the Deck, protect themselves by sending equips to the GY, and Ultimaya Tzolkin turns every Set Spell/Trap into a free Synchro Summon.

hooks.label: Equip Spell cards
hooks.why: Power Tool Dragon reveals and adds Equip Spells, Mecha Dragon draws when one is equipped to it, and Braver Dragon equips them straight from the Deck and GY, so any outside Equip Spell is a payoff.

hooks.label: Cards that Set Spells/Traps
hooks.why: Ultimaya Tzolkin Special Summons a Synchro Monster from the Extra Deck every time a Spell/Trap is Set on your field, so outside cards that Set cards from the Deck or GY keep that engine running.

hooks.label: Equip-moving support
hooks.why: Braver Dragon sends its Equip Spells to the GY as a cost and Power Break returns Equip Cards from the field and GY to the Deck for burn, so outside cards that move Equip Spells around recycle the deck's fuel.

hooks.label: Level 7 or 8 Dragon Synchros
hooks.why: Ultimaya Tzolkin and Duel Link Dragon both Special Summon or copy a Level 7 or 8 Dragon Synchro Monster from the Extra Deck, so any outside one is an instant boss.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Power Tool Dragon, Braver Dragon and Mecha Dragon are all EARTH Machine Synchro Monsters, so generic Machine search and boost cards fit the whole core.

hooks.label: Same-Level Level 5+ pairs
hooks.why: Ultimaya Tzolkin is Summoned by sending 2 same-Level Level 5+ monsters (1 Tuner, 1 non-Tuner) to the GY, so outside cards that summon or search such pairs enable it.

profile.plan: Summons the three Sacred Beasts and fuses them into a 5000 ATK Lord by dumping cards into the GY, turning every discard and send into Tribute fodder and burn damage.

hooks.label: Level 10 nomi monsters
hooks.why: Phantasmal Summoning Beast Special Summons a Level 10 Pyro, Thunder or Fiend monster with ATK equal to DEF from the hand, Sacred Beasts Released searches Level 10 monsters that cannot be Normal Summoned/Set, and The Chaotic Phantasmal Sacred Beasts fuses using them.

hooks.label: Wants to be thrown away
hooks.why: Sacred Beasts Released and the Sacred Beasts' reveal-search effects discard cards as a cost, and Fallen Paradise of the Sacred Beasts sends 3 cards from the hand or field to the GY to Summon, so outside cards that trigger off being discarded or sent there are used for free.

hooks.label: Sends opponent monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Calamity of the Sacred Beasts - Hamon inflicts 1000 damage every time a monster is sent to your opponent's GY, so any outside removal that kills their monsters doubles as burn.

hooks.label: Fills your GY with Traps
hooks.why: Inferno of the Sacred Beasts - Uria gains 1000 ATK/DEF for each Trap in the GYs, and Fallen Paradise of the Sacred Beasts can send 3 cards of the same type there at once, so outside cards that dump your own Traps power him up.

profile.plan: Plants that excavate the top of their own Deck and send Plant monsters to the GY, where every card has a bonus effect when excavated and dumped there.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
