hooks.why: Nearly every Sylvan has an effect that triggers when it is excavated from the Deck and sent to the GY, so any outside card that mills or excavates your Deck is an activator.

hooks.label: Sends your Plants to the GY
hooks.why: Mount Sylvania, Orea and Princessprite send Plant monsters from the hand or field to the GY as costs, and Sagequoia Special Summons itself when a Sylvan is sent there, so outside cards that dump your monsters for value fit.

hooks.label: Flips your monsters face-up
hooks.why: Komushroomo's full excavation effect only happens when it is flipped face-up, so outside cards that Flip Summon or flip your monsters help set it off.

hooks.label: Stacks your Deck top
hooks.why: Charity, Hermitree and Orea arrange the top of the Deck before excavating, so outside cards that look at or stack the top of your Deck make the excavations reliable.

hooks.label: Plant support
hooks.why: Every Sylvan monster is a Plant and Dancepione, Princessprite and the Xyz bosses want Plant or generic Level/Rank material, so generic Plant support works on the whole deck.

profile.plan: Warriors that gamble their whole Deck away, drawing and revealing cards to Special Summon themselves and each other, then cash the randomness in for big Synchro bosses.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Peony, Clover, Maple, Pine with Crane, Zebra Grass with Moon, Paulownia with Phoenix and Willow with Calligrapher all Tribute a Flower Cardian monster as their Summoning cost, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Cherry Blossom with Curtain discards itself from the hand as a cost during the Damage Step, so outside monsters that trigger when a card effect discards them are free value.

hooks.label: Make opponent draw
hooks.why: Lightshower inflicts 1500 damage every time the opponent draws for their normal draw, and Moonflowerviewing also punishes their deck, so forcing the opponent to draw is burn.

hooks.label: Lock monsters in Defense
hooks.why: Boardefly gives every Flower Cardian attacker piercing, so outside cards that switch the opponent's monsters into Defense Position turn that into direct damage.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Flower Cardian monster in the Main and Extra Deck is a Warrior, so generic Warrior searching and revival works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Synchro Summon enablers
hooks.why: Lightflare needs a Tuner plus four non-Tuners, and Moonflowerviewing, Peony and Willow with Calligrapher can treat all materials as Level 2, so outside cards that flood the field with monsters for Synchro Material fit perfectly.

profile.plan: Pendulum Flip Machines that sit face-down like traps, flip themselves up as Quick Effect responses to whatever the opponent does, and feed on every face-up flip to stack E.C. Counters on the scales.

hooks.label: Flips your own monsters face-up
hooks.why: Every Enneacraft Pendulum Effect places an E.C. Counter each time a monster is flipped face-up, so outside cards that flip your monsters face-up add counters.

hooks.label: Sets your own monsters face-down
hooks.why: Enneacraft monsters re-arm their Quick Effect responses by going back face-down, so cards that change your monsters to face-down Defense Position keep the engine cycling.

hooks.label: Flip effect monsters
hooks.why: Each Enneacraft monster can reveal itself to Special Summon any monster from the hand in face-down Defense Position, so an outside Flip monster arrives set and ready to cash in its FLIP effect.

hooks.label: Puts opponent monsters face-down
hooks.why: Atori.MAR changes every opponent monster to face-down Defense Position and locks them there, so outside cards that set the opponent's monsters make that flip-and-lock stick while dodging their effects.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Enneacraft monster is a Machine, so cards that search, revive or power up Machines cover the whole deck.

hooks.label: Recovers Pendulum monsters
hooks.why: Enneacraft monsters go to the face-up Extra Deck when they leave the field, and Enneacraft Release only gets one back per turn, so outside cards that recover Pendulum monsters from the Extra Deck keep the flip monsters coming.

profile.plan: EARTH Rock warriors that stack the Graveyard with Level 4 Magnet Warriors, then banish or Tribute their way into Valkyrion and each other.

hooks.label: EARTH Rock support
hooks.why: Every Magnet monster is a Level 4 or lower EARTH Rock, and Magnetic Field and Sigma Minus both care only about EARTH Rocks, not names.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Delta and Sigma Minus send Magnet Warriors from the Deck to the GY, so any outside card that sends your own Rocks there feeds Delta's banish-summon and Magnet Conversion.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Alpha, Beta, Gamma and Omega Plus all Tribute themselves as a cost, so an outside monster with an effect when it is Tributed gets that for free on the same field.

hooks.label: Rock destroyed on purpose
hooks.why: Omega Plus destroys another Rock in your hand or field to Summon itself, so an outside Rock with a trigger when it is destroyed by a card effect turns that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Recovers banished monsters
hooks.why: Delta banishes three Magnet Warriors from the GY and Magnet Conversion banishes itself to revive a banished one, so outside cards that return banished Level 4 or lower Rocks keep those resources alive.

hooks.label: Fuses using Rocks
hooks.why: Sigma Minus Fusion Summons using Rock monsters from the hand or field, including itself from the hand, so outside Fusion cards that use EARTH or Rock materials pair with it.

profile.plan: Pendulum Machines that Tribute Summon their big monsters for free removal and swings, re-using Pendulum monsters as Tribute fodder over and over.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Qliphort Carrier and Helix trigger when Tributed, and the deck's Tribute Summons constantly feed them monsters as fodder.

hooks.label: Extra Tribute Summons
hooks.why: Qliphort Monolith draws a card for each monster Tributed for a Tribute Summon, so cards that grant additional Tribute Summons or Normal Summons multiply the payoff.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Qliphort Genius requires 2 Machine monsters as Link material and searches a Level 5 or higher Machine, and every Qli monster is a Machine.

hooks.label: Pendulum recovery
hooks.why: Qli monsters are Pendulums that end up face-up in the Extra Deck after being Tributed or destroyed, and Qlimate Change only recovers them once per turn.

hooks.label: Boosts Tribute Summoned monsters
hooks.why: Qliphort Shell and other Qlis gain their best effects only when Tribute Summoned, so outside cards that strengthen or protect Tribute Summoned monsters stack on the payoff.

profile.plan: Rank-Up engine for the 101-107 Number Xyz Monsters: it searches Rank-Up-Magic Spells, tributes and banishes its own Xyz Monsters to re-Summon them, and attaches old Numbers to the new ones as material.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic Quick-Play Spells
hooks.why: Seventh Ascension and Seventh Force both search Rank-Up-Magic Quick-Play Spells, and Ascension can copy one from the hand, so any of them is a payload.

hooks.label: Barian's Spell/Trap
hooks.why: Seventh Ascension and Seventh Force search 'Barian's' Spell/Traps as extra copies of the archetype's own support.

hooks.label: Xyz Monsters that like being Tributed
hooks.why: Rebirth of the Seventh Emperors Tributes all your Xyz Monsters as a cost, so Xyz Monsters with an effect when Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Xyz Monsters that like being banished
hooks.why: Reincarnation of the Seventh Emperors banishes your battling Xyz Monster with its materials, and Rebirth brings back banished Xyz Monsters, so Xyz Monsters with an effect when banished fit.

profile.plan: A Masked HERO build: FIRE and DARK Warriors search "Mask Change" and "Polymerization", then Mask Change swaps HEROes on the field into Level 6-8 Fusion monsters, with Dark Law turning everything the opponent sends to the GY into banishment and Legacy of a HERO refilling the hand from dead Fusions.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Dark Law, Furnace, Dusk Crow and Atomic are all Warriors, so generic Warrior searchers, revives and boosts work across the deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Masked HERO Furnace's search ends with 'discard 1 card' as a cost, so any outside card with an effect when a card effect discards it gets that trigger for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished from the GY
hooks.why: Masked HERO Dusk Crow banishes a monster from your GY as its Special Summon cost, and Atomic summons from banishment, so outside monsters that trigger when banished get value.

hooks.label: Sends Fusion Monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Legacy of a HERO draws 3 by returning 2 Fusion Monsters from your GY to the Extra Deck, so outside cards that dump Fusion Monsters from the Extra Deck keep it live.

hooks.label: Sends opponent's cards to the GY
hooks.why: Dark Law banishes any card that would go to the opponent's GY instead, so outside cards that send the opponent's cards there become permanent banish removal.

hooks.label: Polymerization support
hooks.why: Masked HERO Furnace searches 'Mask Change' or 'Polymerization', and the deck's Fusion Summons can go through Polymerization, so cards built around it extend the plays.

profile.plan: Summons huge WIND Dragon Synchro bosses on top of a Stardust Dragon core, using Level 1 Tuners and Stardust-named Synchros as material.

hooks.label: Level 8 Dragon Synchro boss
hooks.why: Converging Wills Dragon and Majestic Mirage only care about controlling a Level 8+ Dragon Synchro Monster or 'Stardust Dragon', so any outside monster that is one powers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Summons Level 1 Dragons
hooks.why: Converging Wills Dragon Special Summons a Level 1 Dragon monster from your Deck when you control a Level 8+ Dragon Synchro, so outside Level 1 Dragons are free material or bodies.

hooks.label: Synchro Summons Dragons
hooks.why: The Majestic Synchros need a Dragon Synchro Monster as material, so outside cards that Synchro Summon Dragons supply the required material.

hooks.label: Sends your Stardust Synchro away
hooks.why: Majestic Mirage triggers when a face-up Stardust Dragon or Stardust Synchro leaves your field by your card effect or as a cost, so outside cards that send or tribute your own monsters enable it.

hooks.label: Dragon Synchro support
hooks.why: Every Synchro in the deck is a WIND Dragon Synchro Monster, so cards that support or revive Dragon Synchro Monsters work on all of them.

profile.plan: A WATER/Machine Xyz deck that equips its Xyz Monsters to each other as Equip Spells, stacks Ranks by transferring materials, and detaches materials to search, draw and set.

hooks.label: WATER Xyz monsters
hooks.why: Reincarnation Unveiling Mail only Xyz Summons WATER Xyz Monsters and Armored Shark sends WATER Xyz Monsters from the Extra Deck to the GY, so any outside WATER Xyz boss is fuel and a target.

hooks.label: Detach payoff cards
hooks.why: Xyz Force, Xyz Lay, Unbreakable Xyz Barrier and the equips all detach materials as cost, so outside cards with an effect when they are detached get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Level changers
hooks.why: Xyz Align and Xyz Entrust change Levels to match the deck's Ranks (3 and 5), so outside cards that change Levels help stack Rank 3 and Rank 5 Xyz Summons.

hooks.label: Utopia support
hooks.why: Endless Bond and Unbreakable Xyz Barrier specifically reward LIGHT 'Utopia' and 'Utopic' Xyz Monsters, so Utopia-cluster cards slot straight in.

hooks.label: Attaches Xyz material
hooks.why: Xyz Poseidon Splash and Xyz Force want an Xyz Monster that has an Xyz Monster as material, and Bento attaches monsters from the opponent's GY, so outside cards that attach cards as Xyz material build that stack.

hooks.label: Fish GY revival targets
hooks.why: Armored Shark Special Summons Fish monsters from the GY whose Level matches a sent WATER Xyz Monster's Rank, so outside Level 3 or 5 Fish monsters are revivable bodies.

profile.plan: EARTH and Illusion monsters that sit in the backrow as Continuous Spells and hop out by paying LP or revealing Millennium Ankh, aiming to gather the Forbidden One pieces and Summon Exodia Incarnate.

hooks.label: Forbidden One pieces
hooks.why: Millennium Ankh needs to show 5 'Forbidden One' Monster Cards to Summon The Unstoppable Exodia Incarnate, so any card that is one of those pieces is part of the win condition.

hooks.label: Level 5+ Illusion or Spellcaster bosses
hooks.why: Maiden of the Millennium Moon locks your opponent out of targeting Level 5 or higher Illusion and Spellcaster monsters you control, so outside bosses of those kinds get free protection.

hooks.label: Triggers when you gain LP
hooks.why: Fiend Reflection of the Millennium gains LP whenever the opponent activates anything, so outside cards that reward or trigger off LP gain fire for free.

hooks.label: Monsters that become Continuous Spells
hooks.why: The whole deck works by placing its monsters in the Spell & Trap Zone as face-up Continuous Spells, so outside monsters that do the same add bodies the engine can still use.

profile.plan: A WATER Fish Synchro deck whose monsters become Tuners when Special Summoned from the GY, reviving into Synchro plays and re-summoning its White Aura Synchros from the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Fish monster support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck, including all its Synchros and Tokens, is a Fish, so generic Fish searchers, revivers and boosts hit the whole deck.

hooks.label: WATER monster support
hooks.why: The Synchros require WATER Tuners and WATER non-Tuners and banish WATER monsters from the GY to revive themselves, so cards that Special Summon or send WATER monsters feed every layer.

hooks.label: Revives from the Graveyard
hooks.why: White Stingray, White Sardine, White Sunfish and White Moray treat themselves as Tuners when Special Summoned from the GY, so any outside card that Special Summons a monster from your GY creates an extra Tuner.

hooks.label: Discards your WATER monsters
hooks.why: White Stingray Summons itself by discarding 1 WATER monster and Arbitration of White discards a Fish as a cost, so outside cards that discard your own WATER monsters are activators.

hooks.label: Wants to be destroyed
hooks.why: The White Aura Synchros Special Summon themselves from the GY when destroyed by an opponent's card, and White Circle Reef and Arbitration of White pay off your Fish being destroyed or sent to the GY, so outside monsters with those triggers come along for free.

hooks.label: Level 2 Normal Monster support
hooks.why: White Dolphin is a Level 2 Fish Normal Monster the deck can search and revive with its own cards, so outside support for low-Level Normal Monsters is extra material for the Synchros.

profile.plan: Machine Pendulum beatdown: Deskbots stack 500 ATK/DEF boosts on top of each other, swarm with Pendulum Summons, and use the Level 1 Tuner 001 to make Level 10 Synchros like Deskbot Jet.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Deskbot is a Machine, 002 boosts all Machines you control and 001 gains ATK per Machine, so generic Machine support hits the whole deck.

hooks.label: Mass Machine swarming
hooks.why: Deskbot 001 Special Summons itself from the GY when 2+ Machine monsters are Special Summoned at once, so cards that Summon multiple Machines revive it for free.

hooks.label: Level 10 Machine Synchros
hooks.why: Deskbot 001 is a Tuner and the deck routinely has Level 9 and other high-Level Machines on board, so outside Level 10 Machine Synchro Monsters use the same materials as Deskbot Jet.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Spells
hooks.why: Deskbot 005 and 006 in the Pendulum Zone trigger when destroyed, Summoning or searching a Deskbot, so outside cards that destroy your own Spell/Trap Cards set off both.

hooks.label: Pendulum support
hooks.why: Four Deskbots are Pendulum Monsters with Scale 1 and Scale 10, so generic Pendulum support cards that manage scales and Pendulum cards work with the engine.

profile.plan: Rank 4 and 6 Xyz negation bosses made from Dinosaur monsters, rewarded for material support that keeps their detach-costed negates online.

hooks.label: Level 4 Dinosaurs
hooks.why: Dolkka and Laggia need 2 Level 4 Dinosaur monsters as material, so any outside card that swarms or Special Summons them enables the Rank 4 plays.

hooks.label: Level 6 Dinosaurs
hooks.why: Solda requires 2 Level 6 Dinosaur monsters, so outside cards that summon high-Level Dinosaurs reach it.

hooks.label: Dinosaur support
hooks.why: All three Evolzars are made of Dinosaur materials, so generic Dinosaur Type support powers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Reattaches Xyz material
hooks.why: Every Evolzar effect is paid for by detaching material, so outside cards that attach more material keep their negates alive.

hooks.label: Xyz rebound on destruction
hooks.why: Dolkka and Laggia destroy the monsters they negate, and Solda destroys Special Summoned monsters, so outside cards that trigger or punish destruction by battle or effect stack with the removal.

profile.plan: A WIND Spellcaster Synchro engine that Special Summons itself from an empty field, locks you into WIND monsters, and wins by making big WIND Synchros that burn the opponent and pop cards whenever they take damage.

hooks.label: WIND monster support
hooks.why: Ice Bell, Glass Bell and Chimes lock your Special Summons to WIND monsters, so every WIND monster in the deck is fair game.

hooks.label: Burn damage to the opponent
hooks.why: Diamond Bell destroys a card every time the opponent takes battle or effect damage, so outside cards that inflict even a little damage become removal.

hooks.label: WIND Synchro Monsters
hooks.why: Snow Bell and Freeze Bell hand their destruction protection to any WIND Synchro Monster made with them, and the deck's bosses are all WIND Synchros.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Windwitch monster is a Spellcaster, so generic Spellcaster searchers and support hit the whole archetype.

profile.plan: Ritual Summons the giant Demise and Ruin by Tributing monsters that meet an exact Level total, then pays Life Points to wipe the field or attacks twice.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is a Ritual Monster, and Demise Supreme King and Ruin Supreme Queen only get their free effects when all Tributed materials were Ritual Monsters, so outside Ritual Monsters and cards that support them fit perfectly.

hooks.label: Reacts to being Tributed
hooks.why: Turning of the World Tributes Ritual Monsters from your hand as its cost, so outside Ritual Monsters with effects when they are Tributed or sent to the GY get their trigger for free.

hooks.label: Changes Levels
hooks.why: End of the World demands Tribute materials whose total Levels exactly equal the Ritual Monster's Level, so outside cards that raise or lower Levels make the numbers line up.

hooks.label: Ritual Spell searchers
hooks.why: The deck's Ritual Spells recycle each other from the GY but cannot fetch more from the Deck, so outside cards that add Ritual Spells to the hand keep the engine going.

hooks.label: Punishes Life Point payment
hooks.why: Demise pays 2000 LP to nuke the field, so outside cards that reward paying or recovering Life Points synergyse with the deck's repeated cost.

profile.plan: WATER Fish, Sea Serpent and Aqua monsters that feed off each other being sent to the GY, Xyz Summoning Rank 7 bosses and 'Number' monsters off their own bodies.

hooks.why: Every monster in the archetype is WIND and both Field Spells key off WIND monsters, so generic WIND-Attribute support covers the whole deck.

hooks.why: Divine Wind and Shrine of Mist Valley Special Summon Level 4 or lower and Level 3 or lower WIND monsters straight from the Deck, so outside WIND monsters at Level 3 or 4 with on-summon effects are the best targets.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck that searches and places Pendulum Monsters to set scales, Pendulum Summons multiple monsters of different Levels, and recycles face-up Pendulum Monsters from the Extra Deck, with a Level 7+ Fusion boss that Tributes for damage.

hooks.label: Pendulum Monster searchers
hooks.why: Pendulum Treasure, PenduLuMoon and Beyond the Pendulum all add Pendulum Monsters from the Deck, so outside cards that search Pendulum Monsters give the deck more consistency.

hooks.label: Extra Deck Pendulum recovery
hooks.why: Exceed the Pendulum and PenduLuMoon add face-up Pendulum Monsters from the Extra Deck to the hand, so outside cards that do the same recycle your Pendulum Summons.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: Master Spirit Tech Force - Pendulum Ruler Tributes a monster to destroy a card, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Pendulum Summon triggers
hooks.why: Beyond the Pendulum triggers when two monsters with different Levels are Pendulum Summoned, and Extra Pendulum grants an extra Pendulum Summon, so outside cards that trigger on Pendulum Summon fit the same timing.

profile.plan: Pendulum Dragons that lock both players out of the Extra Deck, searching and effects while they're on the field, but demand a monster Tribute every Standby Phase to keep the scales alive.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: Every Amorphage scale must Tribute 1 monster each Standby Phase or destroy itself, so a steady supply of Tokens keeps the floodgates up without spending hand cards.

hooks.label: Reacts to being Tributed
hooks.why: Amorphous Persona draws and Amorphage Infection searches when a monster is Tributed, so outside monsters with their own effect on being Tributed turn the upkeep cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon bosses
hooks.why: All Amorphage monsters lock both players out of Special Summoning from the Extra Deck, so the deck's own win condition is Tribute Summoning big main-deck monsters it can feed with the same Tribute fodder.

hooks.label: Pendulum Monster searchers
hooks.why: The whole deck runs on Pendulum Scales and Amorphage Lysis refills them from the Deck, so outside cards that fetch Pendulum Monsters keep the right scales in place.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Every Amorphage monster is a Dragon, so generic Dragon searchers, revival and boosts work across the whole deck.

profile.plan: A Pyro deck built around the Field Spell Obsidim, which lets its monsters Special Summon themselves while it's up, Fusion Summons big DARK Pyro monsters, and turns opposing monsters into Pyros so its destruction effects can hit them.

hooks.label: Pyro support
hooks.why: Every Ashened monster is a Pyro, Embers needs 2 Pyro monsters as Fusion material, and Extinguishing locks you into Pyro Extra Deck Summons, so generic Pyro support runs through the whole deck.

hooks.label: Field Spell engine
hooks.why: Priestess, King, Hero, Shaman and Spearhead only Special Summon themselves while Obsidim is in the Field Zone, and Embers recovers a Field Spell from the GY, so cards that search, place or recycle Field Spells keep the deck's ignition on.

hooks.label: Removes your own Field Spell
hooks.why: Obsidim Special Summons an Ashened monster from the Deck when it is destroyed or banished from the Field Zone, so outside cards that remove your own Field Spell set that off as removal plus a Summon.

hooks.label: Fusion Summons with Pyros
hooks.why: Embers needs 2 Pyro monsters as material, and Extinguishing and Ashened to Endlessness Fusion Summon Pyro Fusions using monsters from hand, field or the opponent's field, so more Pyro Fusion tools add extra bodies.

hooks.label: DARK Pyros that live in the GY
hooks.why: Extinguishing sends DARK Pyro monsters from the Deck to the GY, Inferno revives a Level 8+ DARK Pyro from the GY, and Shaman shuffles your Pyros back from the GY, so DARK Pyro monsters with effects in or from the GY fuel every line.

hooks.label: Punishes opponent's Pyros
hooks.why: Obsidim and Ashened to Endlessness turn opposing monsters into Pyro on your turn, and Hero destroys a Pyro on the field while Embers blows up opposing Pyros it battles, so outside cards that destroy or debuff Pyro monsters get surprise reach.

profile.plan: WATER Fish swarm that stacks Level 3–5 monsters into WATER and Number Xyz Monsters, paying for every effect by detaching Xyz Material.

hooks.label: WATER Xyz Monsters
hooks.why: Hydrojet Shark and Crystal Shark only work while a WATER Xyz Monster is on the field, and Crystal Shark locks your Extra Deck to Xyz Monsters, so any WATER Xyz boss fits straight in.

hooks.label: Number support
hooks.why: The deck's boss is Number 32: Shark Drake, and Crystal Shark is built to be material for a Number monster, so outside Number Xyz Monsters and their support slot in.

hooks.label: Wants to be Xyz material
hooks.why: Drake Shark and Veiss Shark grant extra effects to a Shark Drake Xyz Monster that has them as material, so outside monsters with payoffs when used as Xyz material come along.

hooks.label: Restocks Xyz Material
hooks.why: Shark Fortress, Shark Caesar and Veiss Shark's bonus effect all pay by detaching materials, so outside cards that attach cards to your Xyz Monsters keep them fuelled.

hooks.label: Summons Fish and company
hooks.why: Shark Stickers Special Summons itself whenever a Fish, Sea Serpent or Aqua monster hits your field, so outside cards that Special Summon those Types trigger it for free.

hooks.label: WATER Fish support
hooks.why: Nearly every Shark is a WATER Fish, Veiss Shark locks you to WATER Special Summons and Crystal Shark targets a WATER monster, so generic Fish and WATER support covers the deck.

profile.plan: Weak DARK Warriors whose effects all trigger when they inflict battle damage, so the deck swarms them with Mustering and tries to connect attacks.

hooks.label: Gives piercing damage
hooks.why: Every Dark Scorpion effect needs the monster to inflict battle damage, so outside cards that grant piercing let their attacks through monsters still count.

hooks.label: Enables direct attacks
hooks.why: Dark Scorpion Combination lets the whole team attack directly, and every effect needs battle damage, so outside cards that let a monster attack directly are extra activators.

hooks.label: Grants extra attacks
hooks.why: Each Dark Scorpion triggers once per hit, so cards that give a monster additional attacks stack their effects in one turn.

hooks.label: Reacts to battle damage
hooks.why: The archetype's whole game plan is inflicting battle damage, so outside cards that trigger when battle damage is inflicted fire on cue.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: All Dark Scorpion monsters are Warriors, so cards that search, revive or boost Warriors cover the team.

hooks.label: Swarms low-Level DARK Warriors
hooks.why: Mustering of the Dark Scorpions Special Summons them from the hand and Combination wants five bodies on the field, so outside cards that swarm low-Level DARK Warriors fill the board.

profile.plan: A ragtag Beast lineup built around Fusion Summoning Master of Oz and Koalo-Koala, with Big Koala as the big Normal Monster body.

hooks.label: Fusion Summon enabler
hooks.why: Master of Oz and Koalo-Koala are Fusion Monsters with no in-archetype Fusion Spell, so outside cards that Fusion Summon using materials from the hand, field or Deck make the Fusions reachable.

hooks.label: Fusion material substitute
hooks.why: Master of Oz and Koalo-Koala require specific named materials, so a monster that can substitute for any Fusion Material completes them with one copy of the named card.

hooks.label: Beast-Type support
hooks.why: Every Koala monster is a Beast, so cards that search, revive or boost Beasts work across the whole archetype.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Big Koala is a Level 7 Normal Monster, so cards that search or empower Normal Monsters find and strengthen the deck's main Fusion material.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent from hand
hooks.why: Koalo-Koala's destroy effect sends 1 Beast-Type monster from your hand to the Graveyard as a cost, so outside Beasts that trigger when sent to the GY get that cost for free.

profile.plan: LIGHT Warriors that grow stronger each turn, negate the opponent's Spell Cards and level up into bigger Silent Swordsman forms, with Silent Swordsman Zero scaling its ATK off its rising Level.

hooks.label: Special Summons Warriors
hooks.why: Silent Swordsman can only be Special Summoned by Tributing 1 Warrior-Type monster, so outside cards that quickly put Warriors on the field feed it.

hooks.label: Raises Levels
hooks.why: Silent Swordsman Zero gains 500 ATK for every Level above 4 that it reaches, so any outside card that raises its Level directly pumps it.

hooks.label: Enables direct attacks
hooks.why: Silent Swordsman LV5 levels up into LV7 only after inflicting battle damage with a direct attack, so outside cards that let your monsters attack directly finish the job.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Silent Swordsman monster is a Warrior, so generic Warrior searchers, revivals and boosts work across the whole deck.

profile.plan: A loose 'Change' spell family: Mask Change swaps a HERO for a Masked HERO, DoomZ Change destroys DoomZ cards for value, and Galaxy-Eyes Photon Change Dragon tags into Galaxy-Eyes Photon Dragon.

hooks.label: HERO monsters
hooks.why: Mask Change sends a HERO monster you control to the GY to Summon a Masked HERO of the same Attribute, so any outside HERO monster is usable change-material.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Spells
hooks.why: DoomZ Change gets its recovery and Special Summon only when a card effect destroys it, so outside cards that destroy your own Spell/Traps trigger it for free.

hooks.label: Big attackers to Tribute
hooks.why: Galaxy-Eyes Photon Change Dragon Summons itself by Tributing 2 face-up monsters with 2000 or more ATK, so outside monsters with 2000+ ATK that are easy to get on the field are Tribute fuel.

hooks.label: Galaxy-Eyes support
hooks.why: Galaxy-Eyes Photon Change Dragon is a Galaxy-Eyes LIGHT Dragon that Summons Galaxy-Eyes Photon Dragon, so outside Galaxy-Eyes cards stack with the same payoff.

profile.plan: Level 7-10 monsters with 2500 ATK and DEF that Special Summon themselves for free once any 2500-stat monster is on the field, fuel their big Illusion bosses by banishing 2500-stat monsters, and keep recycling their cards from the GY and banishment.

hooks.label: 2500 ATK and DEF monsters
hooks.why: Every small Regenesis Special Summons itself once any monster with 2500 original ATK or DEF is on the field, and the Regenesis Spell can search any such monster outright, so outside monsters with those stats are free extenders the deck wants.

hooks.label: Banish your own GY monsters
hooks.why: Regenesis Overlord is Summoned by banishing 2 monsters with 2500 ATK or DEF from the GY and its removal scales with banished 2500-stat monsters, so outside cards that banish your monsters from the GY feed both its Summon and its effect.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: The deck constantly banishes its own monsters with 2500 ATK or DEF (Regenesis Lord's Summon, Overlord's Summon, its Spell/Trap recovery), so outside monsters with an effect when they are banished get triggered for free.

profile.plan: A toolkit of generic Fusion Summoning Spells and Traps that turn whatever monsters you have on hand or field into Fusion Monsters, each with its own rider effect.

hooks.label: Fusion Summon spells
hooks.why: Every card here is a way to Fusion Summon from the hand or field, so any other outside card that Fusion Summons by effect is another copy of the plan.

hooks.label: Fusion Monster bosses
hooks.why: Lev Shaddoll Fusion and Surprise Fusion Tribute Fusion Monsters to cheat out more bodies, and Mementotlan Fusion needs Memento monsters as material, so any self-sufficient Fusion Monster is a target.

hooks.label: Fusion Monsters that like being Tributed
hooks.why: Lev Shaddoll Fusion and Surprise Fusion's GY effect both Tribute a Fusion Monster as a cost, so outside Fusion Monsters with an effect when Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: DARK monsters for Starving Venom
hooks.why: Starving Venom Fusion Dragon fuses using DARK monsters on either field and Quick-Effect fuses DARK Fusion Monsters, so a field of DARK monsters is raw material.

profile.plan: Level 3 DARK Fiends that Tribute monsters to keep setting Normal Traps from the Deck and GY, turning one-shot Traps into a repeatable resource loop.

hooks.label: Tribute fodder generators
hooks.why: Lilith Tributes a DARK monster and Malice Tributes 2 monsters as costs, so cards that flood your field with Tokens or easily Summon themselves keep those effects live.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Lilith and Malice Tribute monsters as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get it for free every turn.

hooks.label: Good Normal Traps
hooks.why: Lilith pulls Normal Traps from the Deck and Malice and Loris Set them from the GY, so any strong one-shot Normal Trap is the payoff the whole engine is built around.

hooks.label: Fast Trap activation
hooks.why: The deck Sets Normal Traps from the Deck and GY but normally cannot use them that turn, so cards that let a Trap be activated the turn it was Set unlock them immediately.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: All four Ladies are DARK Fiends and Alice searches Fiend monsters, so generic Fiend searchers, revival and boosters slot straight in.

profile.plan: LIGHT Spellcasters that grow as your opponent draws and your hand grows, negating Spells and climbing into Level 8 bosses Summoned by Tributing a Spellcaster or Warrior.

hooks.label: Opponent-draw punisher fodder
hooks.why: Silent Magician LV4 gains a Spell Counter, Silent Magician Zero gains Levels and the Silent Fighter draws a card every time the opponent draws, so outside cards that force the opponent to draw feed all three.

hooks.label: Tribute-fodder Spellcasters
hooks.why: Silent Magician must be Special Summoned by Tributing 1 Spellcaster and the Silent Fighter by Tributing a Level 7 or lower Spellcaster or Warrior, so outside monsters of those Types are Summoning material.

hooks.label: Spell Counter cards
hooks.why: Silent Magician LV4 places Spell Counters on itself when the opponent draws and needs 5 to become Silent Magician LV8, so outside cards built around Spell Counters share the resource.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Silent Magician monster is a LIGHT Spellcaster and the main Silent Magician only Summons by Tributing one, so generic Spellcaster support powers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Hand-size payoffs
hooks.why: Silent Magician and the Silent Fighter gain effects while you hold 6 or more cards and Silent Burning wants you to have the bigger hand, so outside cards that reward a large hand or draw you up fit.
phrases: 6 or more cards in your hand

profile.plan: WATER monsters that Special Summon themselves by Tributing a Level 7+ monster from the hand, then use that same Tribute-from-hand cost to power quick effects, Level 8 Tuners and Level-difference Synchro Summons.

hooks.label: Big monsters that Tribute themselves out
hooks.why: Every Ursarctic monster Tributes 1 other Level 7 or higher monster from the hand as its Special Summon cost, so any big monster that can Tribute Summon itself on the cheap is ideal Tribute fodder.

hooks.label: Rewards when Tributed from hand
hooks.why: The whole archetype pays for its Summons by Tributing Level 7+ monsters from the hand, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Level 8 Tuners
hooks.why: Septentrion and Grand Chariot must be Summoned by sending a Level 8 or higher Tuner and a non-Tuner Synchro Monster, so any Level 8+ Tuner is a usable Synchro material.

hooks.label: WATER support
hooks.why: Every Ursarctic monster is WATER, so cards that search, revive or boost WATER monsters work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Drytron support
hooks.why: Ursatron Alpha and Ultimate Flagship Ursatron are always treated as Drytron cards, so Drytron searchers and support find them.

profile.plan: Thunders that reveal themselves from the hand to destroy cards on the field, Special Summoning more Thunders from the hand each time and chaining searches onto every card that gets destroyed by a card effect.

hooks.label: Generic Thunder monsters
hooks.why: Every Blitzclique engine card Special Summons Thunder monsters from the hand as its payoff, so any strong Thunder monster from outside the archetype is a body this deck can deploy for free.

hooks.label: Triggers when destroyed
hooks.why: The archetype destroys cards constantly and its monsters search or recycle whenever any card is destroyed by a card effect, so outside cards with an effect when they themselves are destroyed get set off for free.

hooks.label: Destroys your Thunder monsters
hooks.why: Surge, Crackle, Grain and Emi each trigger off another card being destroyed by a card effect while on the field, so outside cards that destroy your own Thunder monsters set those searches off deliberately.

hooks.label: Wants to be bounced
hooks.why: Breakaway, Return Stroke and Whisker all return a Thunder monster you control to the hand as cost or effect, so outside monsters with a payoff when they are returned to or added to the hand get that for free.

hooks.label: Thunder support
hooks.why: Every Blitzclique monster is a Thunder, and Steppleader and Alternator search any Thunder monster, so cards that support the Type hit the whole deck.

profile.plan: Fuses, Rituals, Synchros and Xyzes DARK 'Magikey' monsters together with plain Normal Monsters, then matches its Extra Deck bosses' effects against the Attributes of monsters sitting in its own Graveyard.

hooks.label: Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Maftea can use Normal Monsters as Fusion material or Ritual Tribute from hand, field or Deck, and Vepartu and the Fusion/Synchro bosses all need a Normal Monster as material, so any outside Normal Monster is a body the deck can Summon and eat.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Clavkiys and the deck's material base are all Normal Monsters, and Magikey World and Vepartu only care about 'non-Token Normal Monsters', so outside cards that search, revive or protect Normal Monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Mills your own deck
hooks.why: Every boss monster checks Attributes of monsters in your GY, and Maftea can send a Normal Monster from the Deck to the GY as material, so outside cards that send your own cards from the Deck to the GY stock the GY with Attributes for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Maftea and Magikey Duo Ritual Summon by Tributing monsters from your hand or field, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get their trigger for free as the Ritual cost.

hooks.label: Wants to be Fusion material
hooks.why: Maftea Fusion Summons using monsters from your hand or field, and Magikey Fusion bosses need '1 Magikey monster + 1 Normal Monster', so outside cards with an effect when used as Fusion material pay off here.

profile.plan: LIGHT Wyrm monsters that banish themselves and each other, then come back or search during the next Standby Phase, so the deck lives in the banished zone.

hooks.label: Banishes your own Wyrms
hooks.why: Nephthys, Daedalus, Tyrant Dragon and Decoy Dragon all have effects when they are banished, so any outside card that banishes your Wyrm monsters sets them off for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: Ragnarok banishes the top 3 cards of your Deck, Ascension and Asymmetaphys banish from hand and Deck, so outside cards with an effect when they are banished get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Recovers from banished zone
hooks.why: The Metaphys monsters recycle themselves by shuffling banished cards back, so outside cards that fetch cards out of the banished zone keep the loop stocked.

hooks.label: Wyrm support
hooks.why: Every Metaphys monster is a Wyrm, so generic Wyrm searchers, revival and boosts work across the whole deck.

profile.plan: A grab-bag of three engines' hearts: Tearlaments cards that Fusion Summon from the GY when milled, a Kashtira Xyz that turns every banish into more material, and a Mannadium Synchro that grows with Tuners.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Kaleido-Heart and Heartbeat trigger when sent to the GY by a card effect, and Kaleido-Heart also shuffles a card whenever an Aqua monster hits your GY, so any outside card that mills is an activator.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Kaleido-Heart and Heartbeat both have effects when sent to the GY by a card effect, so outside cards that mill for free get extra value from cards with GY triggers.

hooks.label: Aqua support
hooks.why: Kaleido-Heart needs 2 Aqua materials and punishes the opponent whenever an Aqua monster is sent to your GY, so cards that search, summon or dump Aqua monsters feed both.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: Arise-Heart banishes every card instead of sending it to the GY, so outside cards with effects that trigger when banished get them for free.

hooks.label: Tuner monsters
hooks.why: Prime-Heart attacks once per Tuner used and Breakheart revives Tuners from the GY, so outside Tuners — above all LIGHT ones — are both material and ammo.

hooks.label: LIGHT monsters
hooks.why: Prime-Heart requires a LIGHT non-Tuner material and both Mannadium cards protect or revive LIGHT 1500 ATK/2100 DEF bodies, so LIGHT monsters that dump or revive themselves slot in.

profile.plan: Comeback racers that cheat themselves out for free whenever your LP are lower than your opponent's, then Synchro, Fusion, Xyz and Link Summon bosses that snap back to the Extra Deck every End Phase.

hooks.label: Makes you lose LP on demand
hooks.why: Every main deck Gold Pride monster Special Summons itself from hand only while your LP are lower than your opponent's, and Pin Baller and Star Leon upgrade their effects in that state, so any outside card that lets you pay or lose LP on purpose turns the whole deck on.

hooks.label: Also plays from behind
hooks.why: The deck's condition 'your LP are lower than your opponent's' is a payoff other cards are built around too, and those effects stack with Gold Pride's without conflicting.
phrases: LP are lower than your opponent's

hooks.label: Spams Level 3 monsters
hooks.why: Chariot Carrie needs exactly 2 Level 3 monsters as Xyz Material and Leon is only Level 3, so outside cards that flood the field with Level 3s give the deck an extra Rank 3 play.

profile.plan: WIND Spellcaster Pendulum monsters that search on every Summon, pay for their Spells and Traps by Tributing themselves, and sit behind untargetable, indestructible bodies.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Majespecter Cyclone, Storm, Tornado, Tempest, Wind and Majesty's Pegasus all Tribute a WIND Spellcaster as a cost, so an outside monster with an effect when it is Tributed turns that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Other WIND Spellcasters
hooks.why: Every Majespecter cost, Majesty's Pegasus' Summon and Majespecter Draco - Ryu's effect all demand a WIND Spellcaster, so any outside WIND Spellcaster monster is extra fuel and a valid Tribute.

hooks.label: Sets Pendulum Scales
hooks.why: The whole deck Pendulum Summons between its Scales 2 and 5, so outside cards that place Pendulum Monsters in the Pendulum Zone from the Deck keep the engine running.

hooks.label: Tributes your monsters
hooks.why: Majespecter Draco - Ryu Special Summons a WIND Spellcaster from the Deck whenever a monster is Tributed while it is on the field, so any outside card that Tributes your monsters triggers it for free.

profile.plan: A hybrid Machine/Cyberse Fusion-Ritual deck that swarms with self-Summoning 'Cyber' monsters, Fusion Summons Machine bosses like Cyber End Dragon, and layers Cyberse Ritual/Link payoffs on top.

hooks.label: Fusion Summons Machine monsters
hooks.why: Cyber Jormungardr and Cyber Dragon, the Luminous Mech Dragon both Fusion Summon Machine Fusion Monsters using your hand and field, so outside Fusion cards multiply their payoffs.

hooks.label: LIGHT Machine Fusion bosses
hooks.why: Cyber End Dragon, the Final Strike Dragon must be Fusion Summoned using 3 Machine monsters with 2100+ ATK and only rewards LIGHT materials, so other big LIGHT Machine Fusions give the deck more bosses.

hooks.label: Cyberse Ritual support
hooks.why: Cyberse Sage and Cyberse Code Magician are Ritual Monsters Summoned with Cynet Ritual, so any outside card that Ritual Summons or recovers them extends that line.

hooks.label: High-Link Cyberse Summons
hooks.why: Cyberse Desavewurm's negate only works while you control a Link-4 or higher Cyberse monster, so outside cards that Link Summon big Cyberse monsters turn on that disruption.

hooks.label: Doubles machine ATK
hooks.why: Cyber End Dragon, the Final Strike Dragon searches Limiter Removal on LIGHT-only Fusion and makes 3 attacks while its ATK is above original, so ATK-doubling cards are both its payoff and its win condition.

profile.plan: Continuous Traps that Summon themselves as monsters, so each card is both a body and a Trap while it sits in the Monster Zone.

hooks.label: Continuous Trap support
hooks.why: Apophis negates effects up to the number of other Continuous Traps you control, so outside cards that put or keep Continuous Traps on the field power its effect.

hooks.label: Sets Traps from the GY
hooks.why: Every Trap Monster in the GY is still a Trap, and Azurune sends Continuous Traps there from the Monster Zone, so outside cards that Set or recover Traps from the GY reuse them.

hooks.label: Extra Trap activations
hooks.why: The whole deck is Traps that need to be activated in the Main or opponent's turn, so outside cards that let you activate multiple Trap Cards or Trap effects in a turn let more of them come down at once.

profile.plan: A WIND Machine Synchro engine that recycles its Tuners from the hand, Deck and GY to Synchro Summon climbing bosses, often at Level 7 and beyond.

hooks.label: Level 7 WIND Synchro bosses
hooks.why: Hi-Speedroid Clear Wing Rider Tributes itself during the opponent's turn to Special Summon up to 2 Level 7 WIND Synchro Monsters from the Extra Deck, so any other Level 7 WIND Synchro Dragon is a free boss.

hooks.label: Synchro material payoffs
hooks.why: Speedroid Block-n-Roll only triggers when sent to the GY as Synchro Material, and Cork Shooter revives its materials, so outside cards with an effect when used as Synchro Material get free value in this deck.

hooks.label: WIND support
hooks.why: Nearly every card locks you into Special Summoning WIND monsters only, so generic WIND support runs through the whole deck without breaking the lock.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished from the GY
hooks.why: CarTurbo, Ultra Hound and Dupligate all banish cards from your GY as costs, so outside cards with an effect when they are banished get it for free.

hooks.label: Recycles banished WIND Synchros
hooks.why: Hexasaucer's Pendulum Effect only returns banished or GY WIND Synchro Monsters to the Extra Deck, and the deck repeatedly Synchro Summons, so cards that reuse its banished Synchro bosses pair well.

profile.plan: LIGHT Warrior support crew (ZS/ZW) that stack their Levels to Xyz Summon "Utopia" bosses, power them up with self-equipping weapons, and Rank them up with Rank-Up-Magic spells.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic Spells
hooks.why: ZS - Ascended Sage grants a search for a Rank-Up-Magic Normal Spell to the Utopia it becomes material for, and Zexal Construction searches Rank-Up-Magic spells, so every one is live.

hooks.label: Utopia Xyz bosses
hooks.why: ZS - Utopic Sage sacrifices itself to protect any LIGHT Utopia/Utopic Xyz Monster, and ZW weapons and Zexal Entrust revive or equip to Utopia monsters, so the deck is built around controlling them.

hooks.label: Level 4 LIGHT Warrior extenders
hooks.why: The ZS crew self-summons beside a Level 4 monster and ZS - Utopic Sage needs 2 Level 4 monsters as material, so more Level 4 LIGHT Warriors make the Rank 4 plays.

hooks.label: Rewards detaching materials
hooks.why: ZS - Utopic Sage and ZW - Dragonic Halberd detach materials as a cost, so outside cards that trigger when detached get free value.

hooks.label: Attach Xyz Monsters as material
hooks.why: Zexal Field attaches an Xyz Monster from your Extra Deck or GY as material whenever you Special Summon an Xyz Monster, so outside Xyz Monsters with effects that trigger while attached come along for free.

profile.plan: Cloud monsters that amass Fog Counters and spend them on removal, discards and Summons, while shrugging off battle destruction as long as they stay in face-up Attack Position.

hooks.label: WATER monster swarmer
hooks.why: Nimbusman Tribute Summons by Tributing any number of WATER monsters for Fog Counters, and Cloudian - Sheep Cloud leaves WATER Tokens behind, so any outside card that floods the field with WATER monsters is Tribute fodder.

hooks.label: WATER Fairy support
hooks.why: Nearly every Cloudian, including the Smoke Balls it Special Summons from anywhere, is a WATER Fairy, so generic Fairy and WATER support covers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Locks monsters in Attack Position
hooks.why: Every Cloudian destroys itself the moment it sits in face-up Defense Position, so outside cards that force or keep monsters in face-up Attack Position keep them alive.

hooks.label: Punishes attacking
hooks.why: Most Cloudians cannot be destroyed by battle and Ghost Fog cancels their battle damage, so the deck survives combat while cards that punish or redirect opponent attacks do free work.

profile.plan: A WIND Machine Synchro engine that spits out fast Synchro Monsters, banishes its Extra Deck Synchros as fuel and grinds the opponent down with double attacks, piercing and burn.

hooks.label: WIND Tuner suppliers
hooks.why: Kitedrake needs a WIND Machine Tuner and every Synchro here starts from Tuners, so outside cards that put WIND Tuners on the field or in the hand keep the engine going.

hooks.label: Banished from the GY payoff
hooks.why: Kendama banishes a Machine monster from the GY as a cost every turn, so outside Machines with an effect that triggers when banished get milled for free.

hooks.label: WIND Synchro support
hooks.why: Rubber Band Shooter bansishes WIND Synchro Monsters from the Extra Deck as a cost and summons lock you to Synchros, so outside cards that reward Synchro Summoning or support Synchro Monsters fit.

hooks.label: WIND attribute support
hooks.why: Every Hi-Speedroid monster is WIND and Hagoita's revival locks you to WIND monsters, so generic WIND support works across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Machine-Type support
hooks.why: All the archetype's monsters are Machines, so searchers, revival and boosts for Machine-Type cards hit the entire deck.

hooks.label: Battle damage amplifiers
hooks.why: Chanbara double-attacks, Kendama pierces and Puzzle doubles its ATK, so outside cards that extend battle damage reward the deck's all-out attacking style.

profile.plan: Level 10 Synchro bosses built from Nordic Tuners, which revive themselves at the End Phase whenever the opponent destroys them.

hooks.label: Special Summons Tuners
hooks.why: Each Aesir Synchro needs exactly 1 Nordic Tuner, so outside cards that put Tuners on the field directly feed every Summon in the deck.

hooks.label: Synchro Summon support
hooks.why: Odin, Thor and Loki are all Synchro Monsters that must be Synchro Summoned with a Tuner plus non-Tuners, so outside cards built around Synchro Summoning help make them.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: Nordic Relic Gungnir and each Aesir's revival banish your Nordic monsters as a cost, so outside monsters that act when banished get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Level 10 monsters
hooks.why: The Aesir bosses are Level 10 and effects like Megingjord and Draupnir boost whatever they target, so outside Level 10 monsters that Tribute Summon themselves are big generic partners.

profile.plan: A loose family of angel-named monsters: LIGHT Fairies that reward negation and Counter Traps, Plant 'Angel of Roses' self-summoners, and big Tribute Summoned angels.

hooks.label: Counter Traps
hooks.why: Harvest Angel of Wisdom recovers a Counter Trap from the GY when destroyed by battle, and Power Angel Valkyria searches a LIGHT Fairy whenever you negate an activation, so the deck wants generic Counter Traps to run.

hooks.label: Negation follow-up
hooks.why: Power Angel Valkyria searches a LIGHT Fairy each time you negate a Spell/Trap or monster effect, so any outside card that negates an activation doubles as a searcher.

hooks.label: Plant support
hooks.why: Fallen Angel of Roses and Queen Angel of Roses both use Plant monsters as cost or Tribute, and Angel Trumpeter is a Plant Tuner, so Plant searchers and swarmers feed them.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon payoff
hooks.why: Angel O7 only locks monster effects after a Tribute Summon, so big outside monsters that Tribute Summon themselves for one Tribute keep that lock while staying on curve.

profile.plan: EARTH Fairies that discard themselves plus another card to search, mill and revive EARTH monsters from the GY, building a full EARTH board under Vera's negation and ATK boosts.

hooks.label: Triggers off being discarded
hooks.why: Every Vernusylph monster's effect discards itself and another card as a cost, so outside cards with an effect when they are discarded get used for free.

hooks.label: EARTH support
hooks.why: The whole deck is EARTH, it locks you out of non-EARTH monster effects, and Vera and Full Bloom only pay off with 5 or more EARTH monsters, so generic EARTH support fits perfectly.

hooks.label: EARTH Fairy monsters
hooks.why: Misting Seedlings searches any EARTH Fairy monster, so non-archetype EARTH Fairies are direct targets.

hooks.label: Wants to be milled from Deck
hooks.why: Awakening Forests sends an EARTH monster straight from the Deck to the GY, so outside EARTH monsters with a Deck-to-GY trigger get used for free.

hooks.label: Revived EARTH monsters
hooks.why: Vernusylph in Full Bloom triggers whenever a Vernusylph is Special Summoned from the GY, and Corolla makes all EARTH monsters Vernusylphs, so any outside card that revives EARTH monsters sets off its bounce.

profile.plan: Machine Emperors that swarm onto the field the moment one of your monsters is destroyed by a card effect, then steal the opponent's Synchro Monsters as equip cards and grow huge off them.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Wisel, Granel, Skiel and the Synchro Absorption variant all Special Summon themselves from hand when a face-up monster you control is destroyed by a card effect, and Infinity Core summons an Emperor from hand or Deck when it is destroyed, so any self-destruction is free setup.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Meklord Army Deployer Obbligato and Meklord Astro the Eradicator lock you into Special Summoning Machine monsters only, so generic Machine support keeps everything working.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Meklord Emperor Wisel - Synchro Absorption sends a face-up Meklord you control to the Graveyard as a cost, and Meklord Astro Dragon Asterisk sends any number of them there, so an outside monster that triggers in the GY gets used for free.

hooks.label: Punishes Synchro Summons
hooks.why: Meklord Astro Dragon Asterisk inflicts 1000 damage each time a Synchro Monster is Special Summoned and the Emperors equip the opponent's Synchro Monsters, so outside cards that react to Synchro Summoning stack on the same play.

hooks.label: Fills your GY with Machines
hooks.why: Meklord Astro Dragon Triskelion Special Summons itself by banishing 3 Meklord monsters with different names from your Graveyard, so outside cards that send your own Machine monsters to the GY fuel its Summoning condition.

profile.plan: A deck of 1850 ATK Spellcasters that tell a story together: they name the opponent's monsters 'Prince of Fairies', then weave those monsters into Spellcaster Fusion Summons while negating anything the opponent tries to do.

hooks.label: 1850 ATK Spellcasters
hooks.why: Matchgiru Special Summons itself whenever any Spellcaster with 1850 ATK is on the field, Fairy Tail Tales reveals one for a second Normal Summon and shields you while you control one, so any outside 1850 Spellcaster is a full team member.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Fairy Tail monster is a Spellcaster, both Fusions ask for a Spellcaster material, and the deck locks you into Special Summoning Spellcasters, so generic Spellcaster support fits the whole engine.

hooks.label: Spellcaster Fusion Monsters
hooks.why: Tails of the Fairy Tails Fusion Summons any Spellcaster Fusion using hand, field and even the opponent's 'Prince of Fairies', so strong outside Spellcaster Fusions like Quintet Magician are the deck's win condition.

hooks.label: Level 4 Spellcasters for Wiccat
hooks.why: Fairy Tail - Wiccat is a Rank 4 Xyz needing two Level 4 Spellcasters, and Matchgiru plus the equip spell's Normal Summon keep supplying Level 4 bodies, so more self-summoning Level 4 Spellcasters stack the board.

profile.plan: Level 8 LIGHT and DARK Dragons that Special Summon themselves by banishing materials from the Extra Deck and Fusion Summon a boss that negates every activated effect.

hooks.label: Fusion Summons from hand or field
hooks.why: Both Evaporation and Sublimation Dragon Fusion Summon using monsters from your hand or field, so any outside card that Fusion Summons the same way extends the deck's main play.

hooks.label: Level 8 LIGHT or DARK Dragons
hooks.why: Dragonlord's Fusion asks for exactly 1 Level 8 LIGHT Dragon plus 1 Level 8 DARK Dragon, so any such monster outside the archetype is direct material.

hooks.label: Level 8 Dragon support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck monster here except Knight Armed Dragon is a Level 8 Dragon, and Dragon's Light and Darkness searches and boosts exactly that profile.

hooks.label: Banishes Dragons from the Extra Deck
hooks.why: Evaporation and Sublimation Dragon Summon themselves by banishing a Level 8 Dragon from your Extra Deck, so outside cards that banish your own Extra Deck cards set them up or interact with the banished material.

hooks.label: Reacts to being sent to the GY
hooks.why: Knight Armed Dragon copies the Attribute and Level of a banished Dragon and boosts a Dragon when sent to the GY, and Dragonlord revives a Dragon when destroyed, so the deck keeps getting value from its cards dying.

profile.plan: WIND monsters that chain Normal Summons, bounce the opponent's cards to the hand, and return to the hand themselves every End Phase, with Pendulum Summons of big Level 10s as backup.

hooks.label: WIND monster support
hooks.why: Every Yosenju monster is WIND, and Misak even gets its destroy effect against non-WIND monsters, so cards that search, revive or boost WIND monsters work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior support
hooks.why: All the core Level 4 Kamas and Sabu are Beast-Warriors, so generic Beast-Warrior support covers the deck's main monsters.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: The Kamas only chain off Normal Summons, so any outside card granting an additional Normal Summon lets you extend the Kama 1/2/3 chain like Kodam does.
phrases: in addition to your Normal Summon

hooks.label: Bounces opponent's cards
hooks.why: Mayosenju Hitot gains 500 ATK each time your effect returns a card to the hand, so any outside bounce effect feeds its boost while clearing the opponent's field.

hooks.label: Pendulum support
hooks.why: Daibak, Hitot and the Shinchus are Pendulum Monsters that the deck Places from the Deck, so outside cards that fetch or revive Pendulum Monsters or guard Pendulum Scales keep the Pendulum engine going.

profile.plan: A Synchro deck of EARTH Machines that keeps its Graveyard free of Spells and Traps, Pendulum Summons its pieces, and attacks with DEF while its big Synchros stand in Defense Position.

hooks.label: EARTH Machine support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Superheavy Samurai is an EARTH Machine, so generic cards that search, revive or protect EARTH Machines work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Wakaushi pays its cost by discarding 1 monster, so outside monsters with an effect when a card discards them get summoned for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Stealthy and Security Tribute themselves as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed turn that cost into a payoff.

hooks.label: Level modulation
hooks.why: Motorbike raises a Machine's Level by 2 to line up Synchro Summons, so outside cards that change Levels give the deck more ways to hit Level 8 and 12 Synchros.

hooks.label: Machine Pendulum monsters
hooks.why: Security searches a face-up Machine Pendulum Monster from the Extra Deck and Wakaushi fills Pendulum Zones, so other Machine Pendulum monsters have two extra ways to reach the field.

profile.plan: A Warrior toolbox built around Dark Grepher, who discards DARK monsters as a cost to send more DARK monsters from the Deck to the GY, setting up both Summon fodder and GY setup.

hooks.label: Level 5+ DARK/LIGHT bosses
hooks.why: Dark Grepher and Lightray Grepher Special Summon themselves for free by discarding a Level 5 or higher DARK or LIGHT monster, so big bosses of those Attributes in hand are Summon fuel.

hooks.label: Discards your own DARKs
hooks.why: Both Gephers' effects discard 1 DARK or LIGHT monster as a cost, so outside DARK or LIGHT monsters that trigger or float when discarded get their effect for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Dark Grepher sends 1 DARK monster from the Deck to the GY every turn, so DARK monsters with an effect when sent to the GY by a card effect get used for free.

hooks.label: Rewards banished LIGHTs
hooks.why: Lightray Grepher banishes LIGHT monsters from the Deck every turn, so outside cards that recover or trigger off banished LIGHT monsters turn that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Equip Spell support
hooks.why: Knight Day Grepher recovers an Equip Spell from the GY each turn, so Equip Spells — including Warrior equips — are the payoff cards to load back.

hooks.label: Gemini support
hooks.why: Knight Day Grepher is a Gemini monster that needs a second Normal Summon, so cards that grant extra Normal Summons or support Gemini monsters fit.

profile.plan: A Fusion deck that stitches Edge Imp and Fluffal parts into Frightfur Fusions, fusing from hand, field, GY and even by Tributing Fiends, and rewarding battle destruction.

hooks.label: Fusion Summon enablers
hooks.why: Frightfur Fusion, Frightfur Factory and Meister all Fusion Summon Frightfurs, so any outside card that Fusion Summons or fetches Fusion materials slots straight in.

hooks.label: Banishes Fusion spells from GY
hooks.why: Frightfur Factory Fusion Summons by banishing a 'Polymerization' or 'Fusion' Spell from the Graveyard, so outside cards that recycle or restock those spells fuel it.

hooks.label: Fiend tribute fodder
hooks.why: Frightfur Meister Tributes 2 or more Fiend monsters to Fusion Summon, and its Pendulum Effect Tributes small Fiends, so Fiends that do something when Tributed are free value.

hooks.label: Mills Fairies and Fiends
hooks.why: Nightmary gains 300 ATK for each Fairy and Fiend monster in your GY during your turn, so outside cards that send those Types to your Graveyard pump it.

hooks.label: Controls a Fairy
hooks.why: Toy Parade's Graveyard effect only works if you control a Fairy monster, so outside Fairies that are easy to keep on field turn it on.

hooks.label: Fusion Monster support
hooks.why: Frightfur Sanctuary makes all your Fusion Monsters count as Frightfurs, so generic outside cards that protect, revive or boost Fusion Monsters hit the whole deck.

profile.plan: A Continuous Spell engine that searches all its pieces, parks a redirect-tank marshmallow in front of the opponent, and counters their effects while treating itself as Dark Magician support.

hooks.label: Dark Magician monsters
hooks.why: Dark Magic Mirror Force inflicts 500 damage per destroyed monster only while you control Dark Magician, and the whole deck is built as Dark Magician-flavoured Spellcaster support.

hooks.label: Continuous Spell support
hooks.why: Every effect in the deck needs the Continuous Spell Shining Sarcophagus on the field, so outside cards that protect, recycle or reward Continuous Spells keep the engine alive.

hooks.label: Spells that want to be discarded
hooks.why: Shining Sarcophagus discards 1 Spell as its cost to send an opponent's revived monster to the GY, so outside Spell cards with effects when they hit the GY get that for free.

profile.plan: A Temple of the Kings deck that Sets Apophis Traps, searches through Set cards and Traps in the GY, and Fusion Summons big EARTH monsters while Anubis punishes anyone who destroys its backrow.

hooks.label: Sets Traps from the Deck
hooks.why: Treasures of the Kings searches only while you have 2 or more Set cards, and Anubis the Last Judge wants differently-named Traps around, so outside cards that Set Spell/Traps directly from the Deck fuel both.

hooks.label: Sends Traps to your GY
hooks.why: Anubis the Last Judge Special Summons itself with 3 differently-named Temple cards and/or Traps in the GY, and Treasures of the Kings searches off a Trap in the GY, so outside cards that send Traps to the GY set both up.

hooks.label: Destroys your own backrow
hooks.why: Anubis the Last Judge destroys an opponent's card whenever a Spell/Trap you control is destroyed by card effect, so outside cards that blow up your own Spell/Traps turn into removal.

hooks.label: EARTH Fusion Monsters
hooks.why: Defense of the Temple Fusion Summons 1 EARTH Fusion Monster using your hand and field, and can even steal the opponent's monsters as material when a Temple card is used, so any big EARTH Fusion fits the payoff.

hooks.label: Reptile support
hooks.why: The Apophis Traps the deck Sets become Reptile monsters on the field, so generic Reptile support and Reptile bosses work with them.

hooks.label: Floodgates to stack backrow
hooks.why: Verdict of Anubis needs you to control 3 or more other Spells/Traps and negates an opposing Spell/Trap, so Continuous Spells and Traps that sit on the field both feed the count and clog the opponent.

profile.plan: Level 10 Dragon, Dinosaur, Sea Serpent and Wyrm bosses that cheat themselves out by exploiting cards being destroyed, sent to the GY or banished, and pay their costs by shuffling their own Continuous Spells back into the Deck.

hooks.label: Mills your own cards
hooks.why: Kairo Ryu-Ge Emva Special Summons itself from the GY once 2 or more monsters have been sent from the hand or Deck to the GY, so any outside card that does that revives it for free.

hooks.label: Banishes monsters face-up
hooks.why: Genro Ryu-Ge Hakva summons itself back once 2 or more other monsters are banished face-up, so outside cards that banish monsters from your hand, field or Deck recharge it.

hooks.label: Destroys cards each turn
hooks.why: Kyoro Ryu-Ge Kaiva Special Summons itself from the hand once 2 or more cards have been destroyed this turn, so outside removal engines that destroy turn after turn keep it live.

hooks.label: Level 10 boss monsters
hooks.why: The Realm Continuous Spells grant their quick effects to any Level 10 or higher Dinosaur, Sea Serpent or Wyrm you control, so other archetypes' Level 10 bosses of those Types fit perfectly.

hooks.label: Scales and face-up Pendulum cards
hooks.why: Ryu-Ge Rising needs a Ryu-Ge Pendulum face-up and Sosei Mistva sits face-up in the Extra Deck, so outside cards that manipulate the face-up Extra Deck or Pendulum Zones interact with the deck's core loop.

profile.plan: EARTH Machine drones that swarm the field with each other, flip themselves face-down, stack Levels 3 and 4 into Rank 3/4 Xyz bosses, and cash spent bodies in from the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Level 4 EARTH Machines
hooks.why: Geargiauger searches any Level 4 EARTH Machine and Gear Gigant X is made from two Level 4 Machines, so the deck actively wants bodies of exactly that shape.

hooks.label: Revives Level 4 Machines
hooks.why: Gear Gigant X searches and Geargiano Special Summons any Level 4 Machine from the Graveyard, so outside cards that recur Level 4 Machines keep the Xyz engine running.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Geargia monster is an EARTH Machine and several effects lock you into Summoning Machines, so generic Machine search and support cards fit the whole deck.

hooks.label: Free Tribute fodder
hooks.why: Geargiano and Geargiarsenal Tribute themselves as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get their trigger for free.

hooks.label: Flip-effect monsters
hooks.why: Geargiarmor, Geargianchor and Geargiattacker set themselves face-down and trigger on being flipped, so the deck naturally plays the flip game and Geargiano Mk-II triggers on Flip Summons too.

hooks.label: Xyz material support
hooks.why: The deck's bosses are Rank 3 and Rank 4 Xyz Monsters that detach materials for their effects, so outside cards that attach or reward Xyz materials speed them up.

profile.plan: Cyberse and friends that Special Summon themselves by revealing a Ritual Monster, then Tribute their board and hand to Ritual Summon big Libromancer bosses.

hooks.label: Generic Ritual Monsters
hooks.why: Fire, Geek Boy, Agent and Magigirl all Special Summon themselves by revealing a Ritual Monster in your hand, so any outside Ritual Monster in hand is free summoning fuel and also something to actually Ritual Summon.

hooks.label: Ritual Summon support
hooks.why: First Appearance and Magigirl Tribute monsters from hand or field to Ritual Summon, and Origin Story destroys a Spell/Trap whenever any Ritual Monster is Ritual Summoned to your field, so outside cards that Ritual Summon or search Ritual Spells multiply the payoff.

hooks.label: Rewards for being Tributed
hooks.why: The deck Tributes monsters from the hand and field as Ritual Summon fodder, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get it triggered for free.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster search
hooks.why: Every small Libromancer needs a Ritual Monster revealed in hand to Special Summon itself, and none of them searches one from the Deck, so outside cards that add a Ritual Monster or Ritual Spell to the hand patch the deck's weak link.

profile.plan: LIGHT Machine and Fairy Synchro monsters that pile Equip Cards onto themselves and search more Vylon cards whenever an Equip Card is sent to the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Generic Equip Spells
hooks.why: Vylon Alpha equips any Equip Spell from the Graveyard to itself and Vylon Cube searches any Equip Spell from the Deck, so outside Equip Spells are never dead.

hooks.label: Sends your Equip Spells to the GY
hooks.why: Vylon Filament, Material, Segment and Component each search a Vylon Spell when sent to the Graveyard, and Omega and Epsilon pay by sending their Equip Cards away, so anything that removes your Equip Cards feeds the deck.

hooks.label: Equip Spell searchers
hooks.why: Vylon Cube and Vylon Delta add Equip Spells from the Deck to the hand, so the deck plays every Equip Spell as an archetype card and wants more ways to find them.

hooks.label: LIGHT Tuners
hooks.why: Vylon Epsilon, Sigma and Omega all require LIGHT Tuners (Omega needs two), so outside LIGHT Tuners are direct Synchro material.

hooks.label: LIGHT monster support
hooks.why: Every Vylon monster is LIGHT and Vylon Delta and Sigma demand LIGHT non-Tuner material, so generic LIGHT support covers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Union monsters
hooks.why: Vylon Tesseract and Pentachloro are Union monsters that live in the Spell & Trap Zone as Equip Cards, so other Unions and cards that exploit Union monsters fit the equip plan.

profile.plan: Spam Level 4 LIGHT monsters, stack them into Rank 4 and Rank 8/9 LIGHT Dragon Xyz bosses, and pile extra materials onto them for detach costs and protection.

hooks.label: Special Summons itself as Level 4 LIGHT
hooks.why: Galaxy War Drake and Galaxy Photon Dragon both trigger when a Level 4 LIGHT monster is Special Summoned to your field, so any self-summoning Level 4 LIGHT is free ammo.

hooks.label: LIGHT support
hooks.why: War Drake and Orbital 7 lock you into Special Summoning LIGHT monsters only, so generic LIGHT support works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Dragon Xyz bosses
hooks.why: Tachyon Primal attaches itself to an attacking Dragon Xyz Monster and Numeron Creation summons a Number Dragon Xyz, so big Dragon Xyz monsters from other archetypes slot straight in.

hooks.label: Feeds Xyz material
hooks.why: Tachyon Primal, Antimatter Dragon and Neo Photon Howling all pay off attached material and detach costs, so anything that attaches more cards to your Xyz Monsters keeps them loaded.

hooks.label: Banishes itself from the GY
hooks.why: Galaxy Journey Special Summons banished LIGHT or DARK monsters and revives your Xyz Monsters when they're banished, so outside cards that banish themselves from the GY as a cost come back for free.

hooks.label: Number Xyz monsters
hooks.why: Numbers Last Hope and Numeron Creation Xyz Summon or Special Summon Number monsters using your GY and field, so outside Number monsters give those spells targets.

profile.plan: LIGHT Warrior Xyz deck that floods the field with Level 4 tellarknights, stacks them into Rank 4 Xyz bosses like Delteros and Triverr, and ladders Ptolemaeus up into Rank 5 monsters like Constellar Diamond.

hooks.label: Rank 5 Xyz monsters
hooks.why: Tellarknight Ptolemaeus detaches 3 materials to Xyz Summon any non-Number Xyz Monster one Rank higher using itself, so every outside Rank 5 Xyz is a direct payoff.

hooks.label: Level 5 LIGHT monsters
hooks.why: Stellarknight Constellar Diamond needs 3 or more Level 5 LIGHT monsters, so outside monsters that are already Level 5 and LIGHT can be Xyzed straight into it.

hooks.label: Zefra cards
hooks.why: Stellarknight Zefraxciton's Pendulum lock and its destroy effect both accept Zefra cards, so any card that works with Zefra slots into the deck's Pendulum engine.

hooks.label: Xyz Material suppliers
hooks.why: Ptolemaeus pays 3 materials to ladder and 7 to skip a turn, so outside cards that attach themselves or other cards as Xyz Material keep it fueled.

profile.plan: A ragtag band of Alligator monsters, mostly Reptiles, whose few effects reward Tribute Summoning and attacking with Reptiles.

hooks.label: Reptile support
hooks.why: Lion Alligator and Spawn Alligator are Reptiles and Lion Alligator's piercing only works while you control another Reptile, so cards that search, revive or summon Reptiles power the whole deck.

hooks.label: Extra Tribute Summons
hooks.why: Spawn Alligator's End Phase revive only triggers on the turn it was Tribute Summoned by Tributing a Reptile, so cards that grant extra Normal Summons let you use it twice or set it up while keeping board presence.

hooks.label: Tribute-fodder Reptiles
hooks.why: Spawn Alligator needs to Tribute Summon by Tributing a Reptile-Type monster to get its revive, so outside cards that summon expendable Reptiles or Tokens supply the Tribute.

hooks.label: Piercing enablers
hooks.why: Lion Alligator already inflicts piercing battle damage when a Reptile attacks a Defense Position monster, so outside cards that force opponent monsters into Defense Position or grant more attacks multiply that payoff.

profile.plan: Small Psychic starters Tribute themselves and banish cards from the hand or field to summon a matching Level 8 Myutant, then Fusion Summon big monsters using banished and GY materials, turning the banish zone into a resource pool.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: M-05, ST-46, Mutant, Beast and Ultimus all banish cards from your hand, field, GY or Deck as costs, so outside cards with an effect when they are banished get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Fusion using GY materials
hooks.why: Myutant Cry Fusion Summons by shuffling materials from your field, GY and face-up banished cards into the Deck, so any outside Fusion card that uses GY or banished materials fits right in.

hooks.label: Fusion by banishing materials
hooks.why: Myutant Fusion summons by banishing materials from hand, field, Deck and GY, and the archetype's banished cards come back via Ultimus and the Level 8s, so Fusion cards that banish their materials feed the recovery loops.

hooks.label: Psychic support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Myutant monster and both Fusion bosses are Psychic, so generic Psychic searchers, revival and boosts work across the whole deck.

profile.plan: FIRE Warrior Fusions that equip Dragons to swordsmen for ATK and double attacks, Fusion Summoning by sending cards to the GY rather than with Polymerization.

hooks.label: Sends FIRE Warriors to the GY
hooks.why: Flame Swordsrealm Fusion Summons by sending a monster from your hand or face-up field to the GY, so any outside card that dumps a FIRE Warrior from hand or field is another Fusion enabler.

hooks.label: FIRE Warrior support
hooks.why: Every swordsman in the deck is a FIRE Warrior and Fighting Flame Sword can destroy a card whenever a FIRE Warrior you control declares an attack, so generic FIRE Warrior support works deck-wide.

hooks.label: FIRE Fusion Monster payoffs
hooks.why: Mirage Swordsman Special Summons itself whenever a face-up FIRE Fusion Monster is destroyed, so any outside FIRE Fusion boss extends the deck.

hooks.label: Equips to your monsters
hooks.why: Ultimate Flame Swordsman's destruction Quick Effect only works while equipped and the dragons attach themselves as Equip Spells, so outside Equip Spells are both protection and enablers.

hooks.label: Flips monsters face-down
hooks.why: Flame Swordsdance Tributes a face-down Defense Position monster from your field to Summon another swordsman, so cards that flip your monsters face-down feed that cost.

hooks.label: Fusion Summons from the GY
hooks.why: Salamandra Fusion and Flame Swordsrealm Fusion Summon from materials that are in the GY or sent there, so outside cards that Fusion Summon using GY materials keep the swordsmen coming.

profile.plan: A flip-based Rock deck that hides in face-down Defense Position, Flip Summons to sweep the opponent's monsters back to their hand or Deck, and punishes every bounce with discards from Criosphinx.

hooks.label: Flip Summon support
hooks.why: Guardian Sphinx and Pharaonic Guardian Sphinx win the game off their Flip Summons, so any outside card that flips them up or flips your monsters face-down keeps the engine going.

hooks.label: Bounces opponent's monsters
hooks.why: Guardian Sphinx returns all opposing monsters to the hand when Flip Summoned, and Criosphinx makes the owner of a bounced monster discard 1 card, so every extra bounce is removal plus a discard.

hooks.label: EARTH Rock support
hooks.why: Seven of the Sphinx monsters are EARTH Rocks, and Pharaonic Guardian Sphinx summons any Level 5 Rock straight from the Deck, so generic Rock and EARTH support covers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Level 5 Rock monsters
hooks.why: Pharaonic Guardian Sphinx Special Summons any Level 5 Rock monster from the hand or Deck in face-down Defense Position when destroyed, and Guardian Sphinx is one itself.

hooks.label: Defense Position battle damage
