hooks.why: Andro Sphinx and Sphinx Teleia burn for half the stats of Defense Position monsters they destroy by battle, so outside cards that force the opponent into face-down or Defense Position feed that damage.

profile.plan: A tiny band of EARTH Warriors built around Celtic Guard of Noble Arms, which can only attack with an empty hand but draws a card for each Celtic Guard you control whenever it deals battle damage.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Celtic Guardian is a Normal Monster, so outside cards that search, revive or boost Normal Monsters all work on it.

hooks.label: Empties your hand
hooks.why: Celtic Guard of Noble Arms cannot attack while you have cards in your hand, so outside cards whose cost or effect discards your own hand turn it on.

hooks.label: Piercing and extra attacks
hooks.why: Celtic Guard of Noble Arms draws a card for each Celtic Guard you control when it inflicts battle damage, so outside cards that give piercing or additional attacks multiply the draw payoff.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: All three Celtic Guard monsters are Warriors, so outside cards that search, revive or boost Warriors work on the whole deck.

profile.plan: EARTH Warrior bruisers that swarm Level 5s and an Level 8 king, powering up through Tributes and bouncing the opponent's monsters back to the hand.

hooks.label: Bounces opponent's monsters
hooks.why: Battleguard Echoes triggers every time a monster is returned from the field to the hand, and Battleguard Howling and Rage already bounce, so outside bounce cards stack extra Echoes uses.

hooks.label: Level 5 EARTH Warriors
hooks.why: Battleguard Echoes searches any Level 5 EARTH Warrior, not just Battleguards, so other Level 5 EARTH Warriors get fetched for free.

hooks.label: Level 8 Warrior bosses
hooks.why: Battleguard Cadet Tributes itself to Special Summon any Level 8 Warrior from the hand, so any big Level 8 Warrior is live in this deck.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Battleguard King Tributes any number of Warriors for extra attacks and Cadet Tributes itself, so outside Warriors with effects when Tributed pay off for free.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Battleguard monster is a Warrior and the King only Tributes Warriors, so generic Warrior search and revival support works on the whole deck.

profile.plan: A Fairy Synchro engine that stacks its own monsters into the Spell & Trap Zone as face-up Continuous Spells, then cashes them back into Extra Deck Summons while banishing the opponent's cards column by column.

hooks.label: Discard fodder spells
hooks.why: Angelechy Problem summons from the Extra Deck by discarding a Spell/Trap as a cost, so any outside Spell/Trap that wants to be discarded or set up from the GY afterwards comes for free.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Angelechy monster is a Fairy, so generic Fairy searchers, revival and boosters work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: LIGHT or DARK Synchros
hooks.why: Seneschal has each player Special Summon a Fairy Synchro Monster, and Strategy Score and Opposition lock your Extra Deck Summons to LIGHT or DARK Synchro Monsters, so any outside LIGHT/DARK Synchro — above all Fairy ones — slots straight in.

hooks.label: Tuner suppliers
hooks.why: All the deck's bosses are Synchro Monsters needing a Tuner plus non-Tuners, and Opening to e4 only summons Level 2 or 7 bodies, so outside cards that provide or summon Tuners keep the engine going.

hooks.label: Continuous Spell payoffs
hooks.why: The deck parks its monsters in the Spell & Trap Zone as face-up Continuous Spells and gains effects per Continuous Spell it controls, so outside cards that reward controlling Continuous Spells stack on top.

profile.plan: A Level-up Dragon line that crawls from LV4 to LV8 by destroying a monster in battle each turn, ending at a boss that negates every Spell.

hooks.label: Grants extra attacks
hooks.why: LV4 and LV6 only level up if they destroyed a monster by battle that turn, so cards letting your monster attack again guarantee the trigger.

hooks.label: Fire Dragon support
hooks.why: Every Horus monster is a FIRE Dragon, so generic FIRE Dragon search and revival works on the whole line.

profile.plan: Chaos Xyz monsters Summoned by Ranking Up a base Xyz monster with Rank-Up-Magic spells, stacking many same-Level materials and gaining bonus effects depending on what is attached.

hooks.label: Other Rank-Up-Magic spells
hooks.why: Barian's Force and Admiration of the Thousands only Rank Up into CXyz monsters, so any other Rank-Up-Magic gives the deck more ways to reach its Extra Deck.

hooks.label: Base Xyz Monsters
hooks.why: The Rank-Up-Magic spells and CXyz monsters all need an Xyz Monster on the field or in the GY as a starting point, so any outside Xyz monster is a Rank-Up target.

hooks.label: Xyz material fodder
hooks.why: Barian Hope gains 1000 ATK per material and Ultimatrainer only gets its draw effect with an Xyz Monster attached, so monsters that do something when used as material or detached get it for free.

hooks.label: Big self-summoning monsters
hooks.why: Fanatix Machinix and Skypalace Babylon need 3 or more Level 9-11 monsters as material, so high-Level monsters that Special Summon themselves supply them cheaply.

hooks.label: Attaches extra Xyz material
hooks.why: Every CXyz monster detaches materials for its effects and Barian Hope scales with attachments, so outside cards that attach cards as Xyz Material keep the engine running.

profile.plan: A crew of low-stat Machines that Special Summon themselves for free, link up into R.B. Link Monsters, and pay Life Points as ammo to destroy themselves alongside the opponent's cards, with every destroyed or returned R.B. monster paying you back in searches and re-Summons.

hooks.label: Life Point gain engine
hooks.why: Ga10 Cutter, Driller, Rocket, Lambda Cannon and Blade all pay Life Points as a cost, and Funk Dock and Next Phase hand Life Points back, so any outside card that gains Life Points is ammunition for the deck's costs.

hooks.label: Pays Life Points as cost
hooks.why: Funk Dock gains 500 LP every time an opponent's monster is destroyed and Next Phase refunds 2000, so the deck can afford outside cards that spend Life Points for big effects.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every R.B. monster is a Machine and the deck's Extra Deck locks repeatedly restrict you to Machine monsters with 1500 or less ATK, so generic Machine support covers the whole board and Extra Deck.

hooks.label: Reacts to being destroyed
hooks.why: Ga10 Cutter, Driller, Rocket, Pile Bunker and Lambda Cannon all destroy themselves as a cost, so outside Machine monsters with an effect when they are destroyed trigger for free every time.

hooks.label: Reacts when it leaves the field
hooks.why: Funk Dock Special Summons a fresh R.B. from the Deck whenever a face-up R.B. monster leaves the field by card effect, and Operation Test bounces the whole crew, so outside monsters with leave-field triggers chain into free Summons.

profile.plan: Warrior monsters that tag in and out by bouncing each other back to the hand, swarming the field through constant Special Summons and Normal Summons.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every U.A. monster is an EARTH Warrior, so generic Warrior searchers, revival and support hit the whole deck.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: U.A. Stadium searches a U.A. monster whenever one is Normal Summoned, and Hyper Stadium only grants one extra Normal Summon per turn, so more Normal Summon modifiers keep the searches flowing.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Perfect Ace discards 1 card as its negation cost, so outside monsters with effects when they are discarded get used for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be bounced
hooks.why: Midfielder, Libero Spiker and every U.A.'s self-Summoning condition constantly return your monsters to the hand, so outside cards that trigger or recycle when they are returned to the hand get value for free.

hooks.label: Equips to a Warrior
hooks.why: U.A. Powered Jersey equips only to a U.A. monster, and the deck's monsters keep changing places, so other Equip Spells that can re-equip or recycle themselves when their target leaves fit the swapping game.

profile.plan: A family of Fusion Summon Spells that pull materials from unusual places - the hand, field, Deck, GY and even the Extra Deck or banishment - often typed to LIGHT Warrior, Dragon, Machine or Normal Monster materials.

hooks.label: More Fusion Summons
hooks.why: Every card in the family is a Fusion Summon Spell, so any outside card that also Fusion Summons is another copy of the deck's core action.

hooks.label: Normal Monster materials
hooks.why: Fusion Draft adds a second material when the first is a Normal Monster and Primite Fusion requires one as material, so Normal Monsters are the family's preferred fuel.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Overload Future Fusion banishes materials from the GY and Fusion Armament revives materials from the GY, so sending monsters from the Deck to the GY stocks both.

hooks.label: Rewards Fusion Summons
hooks.why: The deck's whole turn ends in Fusion Summons, so outside cards that trigger or pay off when a Fusion Monster is Summoned fire for free.

profile.plan: Ritual monsters that chain up by Tributing the opponent's Attack Position monsters, turning every opponent monster into free Ritual material while keeping itself stocked through Recipe Ritual Spells.

hooks.label: Switches to Attack Position
hooks.why: Nouvelles can only Tribute Attack Position monsters, and Recipe Book forces face-up monsters into Attack Position, so outside cards that flip the opponent's monsters into Attack Position feed the ladder.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: The whole deck Tributes monsters as a cost and payoff, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Tributes opponent's monsters
hooks.why: Baelgrill, Balameuniere and the ladder Tribute the opponent's monsters as removal, and Recipe Book burns 850 LP each time a Ritual Monster Tributes, so outside cards that Tribute the opponent's monsters too keep that engine running.

hooks.label: Ritual support
hooks.why: Every Nouvelles monster is a Ritual Summoned by Recipe Ritual Spells, and the deck constantly Ritual Summons on the opponent's turn, so generic Ritual searchers and Ritual Summon enablers slot straight in.

hooks.label: Tribute fodder the opponent summons
hooks.why: Chef de Nouvelles punishes the opponent's Special Summons and the deck needs opposing Attack Position monsters on the field, so outside cards that Special Summon monsters to the opponent's side guarantee Tribute fodder.

profile.plan: A grab-bag of signature moves for other archetypes: destroy your own DARK monsters to search, destroy WATER monsters and opponents' cards, and revive big Dragons from the GY.

hooks.label: DARK monsters wanting destruction
hooks.why: Nightmare Pain destroys a DARK monster in your hand or face-up field as a cost to search, so outside DARK monsters with an effect when destroyed turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Fish, Sea Serpent and Aqua support
hooks.why: Virtue Stream destroys your Fish, Sea Serpent or Aqua monster alongside two opponent cards, and shields WATER monsters, so outside cards of those Types both fuel it and benefit.

hooks.label: Level 5+ Fiend Tribute fodder
hooks.why: Metalzoa X is Summoned by Tributing a Level 5 or higher Fiend, so any outside high-Level Fiend monster that summons itself easily feeds that.

hooks.label: Dragon Xyz in the GY
hooks.why: Tachyon Spiral of Destruction Special Summons a Dragon 'Number' monster from the GY, so outside Dragon Xyz monsters that land there are free bosses.

profile.plan: A Field Spell engine that Special Summons fairy-tale monsters straight from the Deck, pays rent by banishing 10 cards face-down every turn, and blows up anything that dares to attack it.

hooks.label: Searches Field Spells
hooks.why: The whole deck falls apart without Golden Castle of Stromberg in the Field Zone, and only Glife searches it, so generic Field Spell searchers are extra copies.

hooks.label: Recycles banished cards
hooks.why: The Castle banishes 10 cards from the top of the Deck face-down every single turn, so outside cards that shuffle or recover banished cards keep the Deck from running dry.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished face-down
hooks.why: The Castle's upkeep banishes 10 cards from the Deck face-down each turn, so outside monsters with effects that trigger when they are banished get activated for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Iron Cage sends a monster you control to the GY and later revives it, so outside monsters with effects that trigger when sent to the GY by a card effect get value on the way.

profile.plan: Pendulum monsters that jump from the Pendulum Zone into the Monster Zone and trigger every time one of your monsters moves to another Monster Zone, with Field Spells that weaponise the column layout.

hooks.label: Moves your monsters between zones
hooks.why: Shinonome, Saion, Voltage Viscount, Buster Baron, Arktos and Vaylantz Wave all pay off when a card in the Monster Zone moves to another Monster Zone, so any outside card that relocates your monsters is a trigger engine.

hooks.label: Extra Field Spell in the Field Zone
hooks.why: Konig Wissen and Shinra Bansho place a second card in the opponent's Field Zone and their column-stealing effects only work while there are 2 cards in the Field Zones, so any outside card that puts a Field Spell there completes them.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Genesis Grand Duke and Arktos Special Summon themselves from the face-down Extra Deck by Tributing your Level 5 or higher monsters, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Pendulum support
hooks.why: The whole deck is Pendulum Monsters that sit in Pendulum Scales and self-Summon, and Wakening and Wars place more of them from the Deck and Extra Deck, so outside cards that manage Pendulum cards or Extra Deck Pendulums fit.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: The FIRE half of the archetype - Buster Baron, Mad Marquess, Dominator Duke, Genesis Grand Duke - are all Machine monsters, so generic Machine support reaches them.

hooks.label: Summons monsters from your Spell & Trap Zone
hooks.why: Shinra Bansho and Mad Marquess Special Summon Monster Cards from your Spell & Trap Zone back to the Monster Zone, so outside cards that park monsters in the backrow as Continuous Spells give them ammunition.

profile.plan: Parasites that infect the opponent's Deck and field, turning their monsters into Insects, equipping onto monsters and sneaking big Insects into play.

hooks.label: Big Insect bosses
hooks.why: Parasite Paranoid Special Summons a Level 7 or higher Insect monster from your hand when its Equip Card goes to the GY, so any big Insect is a free Summon.

hooks.label: Insect support
hooks.why: Paracide and Parasite Paranoid turn monsters on both sides of the field into Insects, and most of the deck is Insect, so generic Insect support reaches everything.

hooks.label: Union monsters
hooks.why: The deck already equips its own monsters (Paranoid equips from the hand, Lunatite and Soltite are Unions), and only one Union can be equipped at a time, so more Union monsters add interchangeable protection bodies.

hooks.label: Fusion Monsters
hooks.why: Fusion Parasite substitutes for any one specifically listed Fusion Material and Fusion Summons using monsters you control, so any Fusion Monster with listed materials becomes Summonable.

hooks.label: Cards that benefit being equipped
hooks.why: Parasite Paranoid equips cards from the hand to monsters and Parasites convert to Equip Cards, so outside cards that gain effects while equipped to a monster stack onto the deck's equipping engine.

profile.plan: Level 1 DARK Spellcaster tricksters: Confit summons itself for free, Legion grants an extra Tribute Summon of a Spellcaster and retrieves Spellcaster Normal Monsters, and Lord swings for 1000 ATK per card in the Spell & Trap Zones.

hooks.label: Extra Tribute Summon enablers
hooks.why: Legion the Fiend Jester grants an additional Tribute Summon of a Spellcaster each turn, so cards that give more Normal Summons or set up Tribute fodder stack with it.

hooks.label: Big Spellcaster bosses
hooks.why: Legion's extra Tribute Summon only works on Spellcasters, so high-Level Spellcaster monsters with their own Tribute Summon or strong on-summon payoffs are the natural bosses.

hooks.label: Spellcaster Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Legion the Fiend Jester searches a Spellcaster Normal Monster from Deck or GY when it hits the GY, and the deck Tribute Summons them easily.

hooks.label: Fills Spell & Trap Zones
hooks.why: Jester Lord gains 1000 ATK for each card in the Spell & Trap Card Zones, so cards that place many Continuous Spells or Traps on the field turn it into a huge beater.

profile.plan: A control deck built entirely on Normal Monsters and 'Umi': Pacifis searches on each Normal Monster Summon, makes Tokens to protect itself, and the Equip Spells ride Normal Monsters into free dragons and burn.

hooks.label: Big Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Pacifis searches when you Normal or Special Summon exactly 1 Normal Monster and the Equip Spells only equip to Normal Monsters, so outside vanilla bodies with real ATK are the deck's engine.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: The Traps require all monsters you control to be Normal Monsters, and Pacifis locks you out of Effect Monsters, so generic Normal Monster searchers and revival are what the deck runs on.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Pacifis only triggers on Normal or Special Summoning exactly 1 Normal Monster, so cards granting additional Normal Summons give more searches.

hooks.label: Umi support
hooks.why: Pacifis is always treated as 'Umi' and the Traps activate from the hand when 'Umi' is on the field, so any card that cares about 'Umi' or gains from it is live here.

hooks.label: Equip Spell payoffs
hooks.why: Assault wins the Duel when the dragon carries three differently-named Phantasm Spiral Equips, so outside cards that search or recycle Equip Spells help stack them.

profile.plan: Low-Level WATER Aqua parasites that hijack the opponent's monsters: when a card effect or battle destroys them, they equip themselves to an opposing monster and take control of it, then Synchro into Graydle Dragon.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Eagle, Alligator and Cobra take over a monster when destroyed by battle or a Spell, Trap or monster effect, so any outside card that destroys your own WATER Aqua monsters is a self-activator.

hooks.label: Aqua Tuners
hooks.why: Graydle Dragon requires an Aqua-Type Tuner and destroys more cards the more WATER monsters are used as material, so outside Aqua/WATER Tuners and Synchro materials fit it.

hooks.label: Aqua support
hooks.why: Every Graydle monster is a WATER Aqua, and Graydle Slime Jr. locks you into WATER Special Summons, so generic Aqua support works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: WATER Synchro payoffs
hooks.why: Graydle Dragon counts the WATER monsters used for its Synchro Summon and revives a WATER monster from the GY when destroyed, so the deck wants more WATER Synchro bosses and revival targets.

profile.plan: A Volcanic engine of Continuous Spells that send Pyro monsters from the hand and Deck to the GY to destroy the opponent's monsters, plus a Quick-Play that powers up The Winged Dragon of Ra.

hooks.label: Pyro monsters that want the GY
hooks.why: Blaze Accelerator, Tri-Blaze Accelerator and Volcanic Blaze Accelerator all send Pyro monsters from the hand or Deck to the GY as a cost, so any Pyro with an effect there gets it for free.

hooks.label: Pyro support
hooks.why: Every monster the deck sends, summons and Tributes, including its Token, is Pyro/FIRE, so generic Pyro or FIRE support works on all of it.

hooks.label: Winged Dragon of Ra support
hooks.why: Blaze Cannon gives any Ra you control protection, a Tribute-based ATK boost and a mass send to the GY, so outside cards that fetch, summon or protect The Winged Dragon of Ra complete that plan.

profile.plan: Level 4 beasts that fill the Graveyard and stack Xyz materials to bring out Psychic Rank 4 'Number' Xyz Monsters.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Heraldic Beast Leo searches when sent to the Graveyard, so any outside card that sends monsters from the Deck to the GY turns into a free search.

hooks.label: Psychic Xyz support
hooks.why: The deck's bosses (Number 8, Number 18) are Psychic-Type Xyz Monsters and Augmented Heraldry only protects Psychic-Type Xyz Monsters, so generic support for them covers the whole endgame.

hooks.label: Attaches GY monsters as Xyz Material
hooks.why: Heraldic Beast Twin-Headed Eagle refuels empty Xyz Monsters from the Graveyard, and Patriarch pays by detaching, so outside cards that attach Graveyard monsters as Xyz Material keep the bosses loaded.

hooks.label: 'Number' Xyz Monsters
hooks.why: Gryphon, Stad Whale and Augmented Heraldry lock Extra Deck Summons to Xyz Summons using 'Heraldic Beast' or 'Number' material, so outside 'Number' Xyz Monsters are the only bosses the deck can still Summon under its own locks.

hooks.label: Revives your Xyz Monsters
hooks.why: Heraldic Beast Unicorn only revives Psychic-Type Xyz Monsters with its effects negated, so outside cards that Special Summon Xyz Monsters from the Graveyard recover the deck's bosses without that drawback.

profile.plan: Pendulum Warriors that sit in the Pendulum Zones, destroy each other on purpose to search FIRE Warriors, and use those destructions to fuel their bigger monsters' self-Summons and removal.

hooks.label: FIRE Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Igknight Pendulum effect searches a FIRE Warrior from Deck or GY when it destroys the Pendulum Zones, so any card that searches, revives or boosts FIRE Warriors slots straight in.

hooks.label: Other FIRE Warrior monsters
hooks.why: The Pendulum effects add any FIRE Warrior, not just Igknights, so outside FIRE Warrior monsters are payoffs the deck can search and Pendulum Summon.

hooks.label: Wants to be destroyed
hooks.why: The deck destroys its own cards constantly - Pendulum Zones via their effects, three cards for Champion and Lancer, up to three with Burst - so outside cards with an effect when they are destroyed get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Rewards your cards being destroyed
hooks.why: Igknights destroy three of their own cards at a time for Champion, Lancer and Burst, so outside cards that react to any of your cards being destroyed compound the payoff.

hooks.label: Pendulum recovery from Extra Deck
hooks.why: Their destroyed Pendulum Monsters pile up face-up in the Extra Deck and Igknight Burst only recovers Igknights, so outside cards that add face-up Pendulum Monsters back from the Extra Deck keep the engine fueled.

profile.plan: Fusion-summons giant DARK Fiends by banishing Uria, Hamon and Raviel from your hand, field and GY, then stacks Level 10 monsters into Trilojig which burns for half an enemy monster's ATK.

hooks.label: Banishes your own cards
hooks.why: Dimension Fusion Destruction and Armityle's Summon banish your Sacred Beast materials from your hand, field and GY, so outside cards that get value when banished come along for free.

hooks.label: Reacts to being banished
hooks.why: Both Summoning routes banish your Fiend monsters as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are banished trigger on their own.

hooks.label: Level 10 monsters
hooks.why: Trilojig needs exactly 3 Level 10 monsters as Fusion material, so any big outside Level 10 monster is usable material and a body in its own right.

hooks.label: Revives from your GY
hooks.why: Trilojig burns for half a monster's ATK every time another monster is Special Summoned from your GY, so revival effects become direct damage.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Chaos Phantom monster and the Sacred Beast materials are DARK Fiends, so generic Fiend search, revival and boosts cover the whole deck.

profile.plan: DARK Fiend Flip monsters that hide face-down, flip up for value, and swarm the field with face-down monsters to Summon and feed Tindangle Acute Cerberus.

hooks.label: Flip monsters
hooks.why: Tindangle Angel Special Summons any Flip monster from the hand or GY and Jhrelth takes a Flip monster from the Deck, so any outside Flip monster is an extender.

hooks.label: Flips your monsters face-up
hooks.why: The whole deck sits in face-down Defense Position waiting to be flipped, so outside cards that flip your monsters face-up trigger all their FLIP effects for free.

hooks.label: Summons face-down monsters
hooks.why: Tindangle Intruder Special Summons itself from the GY whenever a monster is Special Summoned to your field face-down, so any outside card that puts monsters face-down keeps that chain going.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every Tindangle monster is a Fiend, including the Link boss Acute Cerberus, so generic Fiend support works across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Flips opponent's monsters face-down
hooks.why: Tindangle Hound turns an opposing monster face-down to steal its ATK, and a board of face-down monsters pairs with cards that punish the opponent's flipped monsters

profile.plan: A Cyberse Link engine whose pieces trigger when used as Link material, stacking Link monsters that bounce cards, revive from the GY and attack repeatedly.

hooks.label: Link Summons with Cyberse
hooks.why: Firewall Defenser and Phantom trigger when sent to the GY as material for the Link Summon of a Cyberse monster, so any outside card that Link Summons using your Cyberse monsters sets them off.

hooks.label: Wants to be Link material
hooks.why: The deck constantly uses its Cyberse monsters as Link material, so outside Cyberse monsters with an effect when sent to the GY as Link material get it for free.

hooks.label: Cyberse support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is a Cyberse and the Link monsters demand Cyberse materials, so generic Cyberse support fits the whole engine.

hooks.label: Cyberse Tuner
hooks.why: Firewall Saber Dragon needs a Tuner and copies another Cyberse's Level, so outside Cyberse Tuners give it an easy Synchro Summon.

hooks.label: Revives from your GY
hooks.why: Firewall Singularity revives a Cyberse when a monster it points to is destroyed or sent to the GY, so outside cards that keep feeding Cyberse monsters to the GY and field keep it live.

profile.plan: A Beast-Type deck that Special Summons low-Level Beasts from the Deck and Graveyard, using them to destroy cards, search, and swarm while supporting Winged Beast, Insect, and Plant monsters.

hooks.label: EARTH Beast support
hooks.why: Every Mystical Beast of the Forest monster is an EARTH Beast, so support for that Type and Attribute works across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Triggers when discarded
hooks.why: Valerifawn discards a card as cost, and Carpiponica triggers when sent from hand to GY, so monsters that activate when discarded get value.

hooks.label: Beast that triggers when banished
hooks.why: Cerynemesia banishes a Beast monster from your hand or field to Special Summon an EARTH Beast from the Deck, so a Beast with a banished trigger turns that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Triggers when sent from Deck to GY
hooks.why: Kittytail sends a monster from your Deck to the GY, so any monster that activates when sent from the Deck to the GY gets its effect for free.

hooks.label: Sends Beast from Deck to GY
hooks.why: The deck relies on putting Beasts in the Graveyard for Valerifawn, Uniflora, and Carpiponica, so effects that send a Beast from the Deck to the GY set up those plays.

profile.plan: An EARTH Synchro-and-burn deck that chips away at the opponent with effect damage while milling their Deck with Iron Chain Dragon, Iron Chain Snake and Poison Chain.

hooks.label: Mills the opponent's Deck
hooks.why: Iron Chain Dragon, Iron Chain Snake and Poison Chain all win by sending the top of the opponent's Deck to the Graveyard, so outside cards that mill the opponent stack more of the same.

hooks.label: Punishes their Graveyard
hooks.why: The whole deck fills the opponent's Graveyard with their own cards, so outside cards that get rid of or exploit cards in their Graveyard turn that mill into real pressure.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Iron Chain Blaster sends an Iron Chain monster you control to the Graveyard as a cost, so outside monsters that trigger when sent there get it for free while feeding the burn.

hooks.label: Piercing damage
hooks.why: Iron Chain Dragon only mills when it inflicts Battle Damage, so outside cards that give piercing or direct attacks let the mill trigger far more often.

hooks.label: EARTH support
hooks.why: Every Iron Chain monster, including the Synchro, is EARTH, so generic EARTH support covers the whole deck.

profile.plan: Corporate researchers fuse GMX staff with Dinosaurs into big Dinosaur Fusion bosses, excavating their Deck over and over to Summon, fetch cards and punish every Summon the opponent makes.

hooks.label: Dinosaur support
hooks.why: Every GMX Fusion is a Dinosaur and cards like Selande and Selandea Special Summon Dinosaur monsters from hand, Deck and GY, so generic Dinosaur help works across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Fuses Dinosaur Fusion Monsters
hooks.why: GMX 55th Experiment Report already Fusion Summons any Dinosaur Fusion Monster, so more outside ways to Fusion Summon Dinosaurs keep the bosses coming.

hooks.label: Dinosaur Fusion bosses
hooks.why: The Fusions need 1 'GMX' monster plus 1 (or 2+) Dinosaur monster, so any outside Dinosaur Fusion Monster can be Summoned with the deck's own materials.

hooks.label: Rewards being excavated
hooks.why: Experiment #55, VELOX, COMPREX, Report and Suppression Squad excavate cards from your Deck nearly every turn, so monsters with an effect when excavated fire for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be shuffled into the Deck
hooks.why: Noma and the Fusions use materials by shuffling them from field, GY and banishment into the Deck, so monsters with an effect when shuffled back in get triggered.

hooks.label: Punishes opponent's Summons
hooks.why: VELOX and ALLOS gain LP every time the opponent Summons and COMPREX with 5 Dinosaur materials makes them lose 800, so outside cards that also trigger on the opponent's Summons stack further punishment.
phrases: your opponent Normal or Special Summons

profile.plan: Dark Plants that Fusion Summon DARK Fusion Dragons like Starving Venom, slapping Predator Counters on monsters to drop them to Level 1 and to pay for their own special Summoning and removal.

hooks.label: DARK Fusion bosses
hooks.why: Bufolicula Fusion Summons any DARK Fusion Monster from the Extra Deck, and the deck's payoffs want a Starving Venom Fusion Dragon, so any other DARK Fusion Monster is a valid target and alternative boss.

hooks.label: Places Predator Counters
hooks.why: Triantis and Longinephila lower counter monsters to Level 1 for Daredevil's counter-Tribute Summon, and Daredevil destroys a Spell/Trap per counter monster, so any outside card that places Predator Counters extends the engine.

hooks.label: Polymerization searchers
hooks.why: Lilizard and Longinephila fetch or Set Polymerization and the whole deck runs on Fusion Spells, so outside cards that search Fusion or Polymerization Spells keep the line going.

hooks.label: Plant support
hooks.why: Every Predaplant monster is a Plant and Predaprimitive locks you into Summoning Plant or Dragon monsters, so generic Plant support works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Fusion material substitutes
hooks.why: Bufolicula and Bal Teah Fusion Summon using monsters from your hand or field, so fusion substitute monsters and self-sending materials make those Summons easier.

hooks.label: Punishes opponent Summons
hooks.why: Predaprimitive and Bal Teah both trigger when a monster is Special Summoned to the opponent's field, so outside cards that bait or force opponent Special Summons turn those floating effects on.

profile.plan: WATER Machine Pendulum monsters that cover for each other from the Pendulum Zones (destruction substitution and effect negation) while their big attackers Tribute their little partners for extra attacks and disruption.

hooks.label: Pendulum Monster searchers
hooks.why: The deck lives and dies on having Dinomist monsters in its Pendulum Zones, and Dinomist Charge only searches one card per activation, so any outside card that finds Pendulum Monsters keeps the Scales up.

hooks.label: Places Pendulum Scales
hooks.why: Dinomist monsters all have Pendulum Effects that only work while they sit in the Pendulum Zone, so outside cards that set Scales directly from the Deck or Extra Deck turn on their protection and negation.

hooks.label: WATER Machine support
hooks.why: Every Dinomist monster is a WATER Machine, so any outside card that searches, revives or powers up WATER or Machine monsters works across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Spinos, Rex and Dinomist Howling all Tribute Dinomist monsters as a cost for extra attacks and bounce removal, so an outside monster that triggers when it is Tributed rides along for free.

hooks.label: Recycles Extra Deck Pendulums
hooks.why: Dinomist Charge only recovers Dinomist cards added to the Extra Deck face-up, so outside cards that shuffle or return your own face-up Pendulum Monsters from the Extra Deck back to hand or Deck keep the engine stocked.

profile.plan: Level 4 EARTH Rocks that swarm the field in Defense Position and stack into Rank 4 Xyz Monsters, with Goliath recovering spent Rocks from the GY.

hooks.label: Rank 4 Xyz Monsters
hooks.why: The deck floods the field with interchangeable Level 4 monsters and even gives bonus effects to Xyz Summons made from Gogogo material (Aristera & Dexia), so generic Rank 4s are its bosses.

hooks.label: Rock support
hooks.why: Almost every monster in the deck is a Level 4 EARTH Rock, so outside cards that search, revive or strengthen Rocks work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Revives EARTH Rocks from the GY
hooks.why: Giant and Ghost revive Gogogo monsters from the GY on Summon, and Goliath recycles Level 4 EARTH Rocks from the GY back to the hand, so the deck lives out of its Graveyard.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Gogogo Golem - Golden Form Summons itself by Tributing a Gogogo monster, so outside monsters with an effect that triggers when they are Tributed turn that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Attaches Xyz material
hooks.why: Goliath and Aristera & Dexia want Xyz Monsters loaded with material, so outside cards that attach more cards to your Xyz Monsters extend their effects.

profile.plan: Reptile 'Evoltiles' hatch Dinosaur 'Evolsaurs' from the Deck, then stack them into FIRE Dragon Xyz bosses; the deck Tributes its own Reptiles as costs and rewards Special Summoning FIRE Dinosaurs.

hooks.label: Tributes your Reptiles
hooks.why: Evo-Force and Evo-Instant Tribute a Reptile as their entire cost, and Evoltile Najasho triggers when Tributed, so outside cards whose cost is Tributing one of your Reptiles are free extensions.

hooks.label: Reptiles that want to be Tributed
hooks.why: The deck Tributes Evoltiles to Evo-Force and Evo-Instant constantly, so an outside Reptile with its own effect when Tributed turns that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Level 6 or lower FIRE Dinosaurs
hooks.why: Evolsaur Elias Special Summons a Level 6 or lower FIRE Dinosaur from the hand, so any outside monster matching that is an extra body the deck can deploy for free.

hooks.label: Reptile support
hooks.why: Every Evoltile is a Reptile, so generic Reptile search, revival and boost cards work across the whole hatch engine.

hooks.label: Graveyard Xyz material setup
hooks.why: Evo-Singularity turns an Evoltile and an Evolsaur already sitting in the Graveyard directly into an Evolzar Xyz Summon, so outside cards that load monsters into your own Graveyard power the deck's finisher.

profile.plan: Giant Machine battleships that survive battle by shedding counters, and when one is destroyed Boss Rush summons the next one out of the Deck.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Boss Rush Special Summons a replacement from the Deck during the End Phase when a B.E.S. monster is destroyed and sent to the Graveyard, so any outside card that destroys your own Machines reloads the ship.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every B.E.S. monster is a Machine, so searchers, revival and boosts for Machine-Type cards reach the whole fleet.

hooks.label: Places counters
hooks.why: Each B.E.S. only stays afloat while it has counters, so outside cards that add counters to your monsters patch a ship about to sink.

hooks.label: Bosses that dodge Tribute Summons
hooks.why: The B.E.S. ships are Level 5 to 11 and Boss Rush locks you out of Normal Summons entirely, so big Machines that Special Summon themselves by their own procedure slot straight in.

profile.plan: Level 8 bosses Special Summoned free from the hand once exactly 5 monsters of one Attribute sit in your GY, each unleashing a big effect on arrival.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: The Lords need exactly 5 monsters of one Attribute in the GY, so the deck is built to send its own monsters there fast, and any outside card that mills feeds them.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: The deck dumps monsters into the GY by design, so outside monsters with an effect when a card sends them to the GY come along for free.

hooks.label: Special Summons itself
hooks.why: The Lords are Summoned from the hand by their own condition, so the hand fills with big monsters that also summon themselves the same way.

profile.plan: A Rank 5 Xyz deck that floods the field with self-summoning DARK Fiends, then stacks them into "Number" and "Masquerade" Xyz Monsters and ranks them up.

hooks.label: Rank-Up-Magic Spells
hooks.why: V Umbral Horror's GY effect Special Summons a "Number" monster one Rank higher using your existing Xyz Monster as material, so Rank-Up-Magic Spells do the same job twice over.

hooks.label: Other Number Xyz Monsters
hooks.why: V Umbral Horror can Special Summon any "Number" monster from the Extra Deck, and Shining Umbral Horror counts as two materials for "Number" Xyz Summons needing three or more, so extra Number bosses are direct payoffs.

hooks.label: Changes Level to 5
hooks.why: Number C104: Umbral Horror Masquerade needs four Level 5 monsters, and Will o' the Wisp already copies levels, so outside cards that set your monsters' Levels to 5 make the big Xyz Summon possible.

hooks.label: Attach extra Xyz material
hooks.why: Masquerade's negate costs a detach and C104 upgrades by having the right material, so outside cards that attach extra material to your Xyz Monsters keep them fueled.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: All the Main Deck Umbral Horror monsters except the two Spellcasters are DARK Fiends, and Ghost can Summon any Level 4 or lower Fiend from the hand alongside itself, so generic Fiend help covers most of the deck.

profile.plan: LIGHT Aqua giants that flip the opponent's monsters face-down, then send their face-up cards to the Graveyard and stack two Level 10 monsters into a Rank 10 Xyz.

hooks.label: Flips opponent's monsters face-down
hooks.why: The deck's payoffs key off face-down monsters: Hound attacks directly while the opponent controls one, Embrace steals a face-down monster, and the bosses send the opponent's face-up cards to the GY, so any outside card that turns an opposing monster face-down feeds the plan.

hooks.label: Level 10 monsters
hooks.why: The Rank 10 boss needs 2 Level 10 monsters as material, and Demigod and Crystal God are the deck's own Level 10s, so any outside Level 10 monster is another Xyz body.

hooks.label: Rank 10 Xyz support
hooks.why: The deck's Extra Deck payoff is a Rank 10 Aqua Xyz that wants more material and protection for it, so cards built around Rank 10 Xyz Monsters fit.

hooks.label: Aqua support
hooks.why: Every Tistina monster is Aqua, and Returned of the Tistina can attach itself to any Aqua Xyz Monster as material, so generic Aqua support works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon payoffs
hooks.why: Tainted of the Tistina has its own Tribute Summon and becomes Level 10 when Normal Summoned, and Breath grants an extra Normal Summon of a big Aqua, so cards that reward Tribute Summoning fit the deck's alternate route.

profile.plan: Deep Sea is a WATER Synchro engine that mills its own Deck and pays Level 4 or lower WATER monsters as discard costs, turning every self-mill into a revive, search or Synchro play.

hooks.label: Discards WATER monsters
hooks.why: Minstrel, Repetiteur and Sentry all pay by discarding or sending Level 4 or lower WATER monsters, so any outside card that makes you discard WATER monsters is both cost fodder and an activator.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Every Deep Sea monster's Special Summoned effect sends the top cards of your Deck to the GY, so outside cards that mill fuel the follow-up recovery and revival effects.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent as WATER cost
hooks.why: The deck constantly sends cards from hand and Deck to the GY to activate WATER monsters' effects, so outside monsters with an effect when they are sent to the GY get triggered for free.

hooks.label: WATER monster support
hooks.why: The whole deck is WATER Sea Serpents and locks you into Special Summoning WATER monsters, so generic WATER searchers, revivers and boosters fit perfectly.

hooks.label: Big WATER boss targets
hooks.why: Repetiteur Special Summons a Level 5 or higher WATER monster from your GY when it leaves, so outside WATER bosses worth reviving are the payoff of the Synchro line.

profile.plan: Cyberse-styled enforcers that trap the opponent's monsters in their columns, paying for every effect by banishing their own cards from the hand, which also fuels GY effects that react to anything being banished.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: S-Force constantly banishes its own cards from the hand as a cost (Rappa Chiyomaru, Orrafist, Lapcewell, Nightcatcher), so an outside card with an effect when it is banished gets triggered for free.

hooks.label: Banishes your own cards
hooks.why: S-Force Origin and World Sorting both follow up whenever another card is banished, so an outside card that banishes your own cards sets off both for free.

hooks.label: Banished recovery
hooks.why: The deck's costs leave many S-Force monsters stranded in banishment, and only Pla-Tina and Specimen pull them back, so outside cards that recover banished monsters keep the deck stocked.

profile.plan: Self-discarding Dragons that fetch each other by discarding or banishing themselves plus a Dragon of matching Attribute, then stack Rank 7 Xyz Monsters on Level 7 Dragon materials.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Spectral and Nebulus discard a Dragon/LIGHT or Dragon/DARK monster as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are discarded get used for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished from the GY
hooks.why: The Dragon Rulers banish themselves and another Dragon from the GY as a cost to revive their Xyz bosses, so outside monsters that trigger when banished get used for free.

hooks.label: Level 7 Dragons
hooks.why: Chasma and Eclipse Xyz Summon using 2 Level 7 Dragon monsters, so any outside Level 7 Dragon is material.

hooks.label: Rank 7 Xyz Monsters
hooks.why: Disaster needs 2 Rank 7 monsters as material, so other Rank 7 Xyz Monsters stack onto it.

hooks.label: Dragon support
hooks.why: Every Dragon Ruler card is a Dragon and all their costs ask for Dragon monsters, so generic Dragon searchers, revivers and boosters work across the deck.

profile.plan: Warriors that turn Continuous Traps into monsters, banishing their own cards as costs and bouncing their Traps to reuse them, all centered on a Rank 4 Xyz boss.

hooks.label: Trap monsters
hooks.why: Home Stadium burns and negates whenever a Continuous Trap is Special Summoned to a Monster Zone, and Giantslaying rewards having one there, so any outside Continuous Trap that becomes a monster is another body plus a free trigger.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Lightning Tydeu's Summon cost is discarding 1 card, so outside cards with an effect when they are discarded get it triggered for free.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Argostars monster is a Warrior and Giantslaying grants an extra Normal Summon of a Warrior, so generic Warrior searchers and boosters reach the whole deck.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Level 4 Warriors
hooks.why: Arion needs 2 Level 4 monsters and only substitutes one of them with an Argostars, so outside Level 4 Warriors that Special Summon themselves complete the Rank 4.

hooks.label: Works while banished
hooks.why: Adra and Parthe banish themselves as costs and Eteo, Capane and Home Stadium all check for a banished Argostars, so outside cards with effects that work from banishment keep providing value there.

profile.plan: Ritual Summons WIND Winged Beast Peacocks that bounce the opponent's cards, alongside Spirit monsters that keep returning to the hand and trigger the deck's Continuous Spell and Trap every time one does.

hooks.label: Bounces your own monsters
hooks.why: Shinobird Power Spot and Shinobird Salvation both trigger when a face-up WIND monster you control returns to the hand, so anything that bounces your own monsters is extra search and removal.

hooks.label: Spirit monster support
hooks.why: The whole deck is Spirit monsters and Shinobaroness Shade Peacock searches any Spell/Trap that mentions them, so generic Spirit support slots straight in.

hooks.label: Ritual Summon support
hooks.why: Shinobird's Calling only summons the Peacocks, so outside Ritual Spells and preparators that can Ritual Summon them or search Ritual monsters widen the deck's options.

hooks.label: Banishes from your Graveyard
hooks.why: Shinobird's Calling banishes Spirit monsters from the GY as Ritual material, and Shinobaron Shade Peacock returns after being banished, so anything that banishes your GY cards feeds both.

hooks.label: Rewarded for being banished
hooks.why: Shinobaron and Shinobaroness Shade Peacock Special Summon themselves back the turn after they are banished, so a banish of your own monsters is pure advantage here.

profile.plan: Warriors of every Attribute that send each other from the hand or Deck to the GY as costs, growing stronger the more different Attributes pile up in the GY.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Palace of the Elemental Lords lets the sabers send monsters from the Deck to the GY instead of the hand, and its ATK boost counts different Attributes in the GY, so anything that sends your monsters from the Deck to the GY is free fuel and free diversity.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Main Deck Elementsaber is a Warrior, so cards that search, revive or boost Warriors work across the whole team.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Elemental Training Tributes a monster every turn to Special Summon from the Deck, so outside monsters with effects when they are Tributed turn that cost into profit.

hooks.label: Fills the GY with Attributes
hooks.why: Palace of the Elemental Lords gives 200 ATK/DEF per different Attribute in the GY and the sabers change their own Attributes there, so cards that change or add a monster's Attribute multiply the payoff.

hooks.label: Abuses face-down monsters
hooks.why: Molehu flips opponents' monsters face-down every turn with its Quick Effect, so cards that punish or exploit face-down Defense Position monsters compound it.

profile.plan: Level 4 LIGHT Fairies that Tribute themselves or each other to swarm huge Level 7 LIGHT Dragons from the hand, then bounce those Dragons back and forth to re-trigger their summoning effects.

hooks.label: Level 7 LIGHT Dragons
hooks.why: Almost every card in the deck summons, searches or returns a Level 7 LIGHT Dragon, so any outside boss monster of that exact kind slots straight in (e.g. as Balefire's and Ceremony's summon target).

hooks.label: Bounces your own monsters
hooks.why: Starry Knight Sky draws and Orbitael revives whenever a face-up Level 7 LIGHT Dragon you control returns to the hand, so outside cards that bounce your own monsters turn payoffs into engines.

hooks.label: Reacts to being Tributed
hooks.why: Astel and Orbitael Tribute a LIGHT monster you control as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: LIGHT Fairy support
hooks.why: The archetype's small monsters are all Level 4 LIGHT Fairies, Starring Knight revives exactly that combination, and Ceremony reveals a LIGHT Fairy from hand as a cost.

hooks.label: Level 4 Rank 4 makers
hooks.why: Starring Knight takes any two Level 4 monsters as Xyz Material and its fellow Knights are all Level 4, so generic Level 4 extenders feed it.

profile.plan: A wall of untargetable Plant Link Monsters that Special Summon Sunvine attackers from the Extra Deck every time you take damage, then heal it back.

hooks.label: Self-burn enablers
hooks.why: Dryas, Dryades and Dryanome each Special Summon a Sunvine and heal whenever you take battle or effect damage, so any outside card that inflicts damage on yourself is another summon trigger.

hooks.label: React to LP gain
hooks.why: The Sunavalon tree converts every instance of damage into a Life Point gain, so outside cards with an effect that triggers when you gain LP fire for free all game.

hooks.label: Plant Link Monsters
hooks.why: Melias, Dryades and Dryanome all need Plant monsters including a Plant Link Monster as Link material, and Bloom wants a Link-4 or higher Plant, so outside Plant Link monsters are both material and payoff.

hooks.label: Plant support
hooks.why: Every Sunavalon monster is a Plant, so generic Plant searchers, revive and protection work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Link monster GY recursion
hooks.why: Daphne returns Plant Link Monsters from your GY to the Extra Deck and Dryatrentiay recycles Link material into plays, so outside cards that recover Link monsters from the GY keep the engine running.

profile.plan: Level 8 DARK Dragons that pay half your LP to destroy and banish everything on the field, and grow 300 ATK for every card banished.

hooks.label: Banishes for cost
hooks.why: All three Gandoras gain 300 ATK for each banished card, so any outside card that banishes cards as a cost or effect is a permanent ATK boost.

hooks.label: Mentions Shining Sarcophagus
hooks.why: Gandora-G Special Summons a Level 7 or lower monster that mentions 'Shining Sarcophagus' straight from the Deck, so any such card is another body the deck can summon for free.

hooks.label: Fuels itself to the GY
hooks.why: Gigarays must be Special Summoned by sending 2 other monsters from your hand and/or field to the GY, so outside monsters that send themselves or others to the GY are free material.

hooks.label: Banishes your GY cards
hooks.why: Gandora destroys and then banishes cards on the field, so your own GY stays untouched for outside cards that use the GY as a cost — every banish also feeds their 300-ATK-per-banished-card bonus.

hooks.label: DARK Dragon support
hooks.why: Every Gandora is a DARK Dragon Level 8 with 0 ATK before boosts, so generic DARK Dragon searchers and revivers find and recycle them all.

profile.plan: Fiends that swarm the field with Level 4 bodies, Tribute Summon their Steelswarm bosses using each other as Tributes, and pay off with destructive Tribute Summon triggers.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Castor and Gatekeeper only add one extra Normal Summon each, and the deck needs lots of Tributes on the board for its Tribute Summons, so any outside card granting additional Normal Summons stacks with them.

hooks.label: Token fodder makers
hooks.why: Girastag and Longhorn can be Tribute Summoned with generic Tributes, so outside cards that Summon Tokens give the deck Tribute fodder without using up its Steelswarm bodies.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon payoff monsters
hooks.why: The deck is built entirely around Tribute Summoning, so outside monsters that say 'Tribute Summon this card' or trigger 'If this card is Tribute Summoned' fit the Tribute engine and get boosted alongside Girastag and Longhorn.

hooks.label: Rank 4 Xyz monsters
hooks.why: Most of the deck's monsters are Level 4 and Castor gives an extra Normal Summon, making two Level 4 monsters on the field routine, exactly what Steelswarm Roach and other 2-material Rank 4s need.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Nearly every Steelswarm monster is a DARK Fiend, so generic Fiend search, revival and boost cards work on the whole deck.

profile.plan: Plant Link monsters built from Normal Plant monsters, locking the Extra Deck into Plants and recurring Continuous Traps and Link Monsters from the graveyard.

hooks.label: Plant Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Every Sunvine Link 1 needs '1 Plant Normal Monster' as material, so any outside Plant Normal Monster (or Gemini, which counts as Normal in hand/field) is usable material.

hooks.label: Summon Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Sunvine Links are made from Plant Normal Monsters, and Sunvine Sowing only searches 'Sunseed' ones, so outside cards that Normal or Special Summon Normal Monsters extend the plays.

hooks.label: Plant monsters
hooks.why: Sowing and Shrine lock you into Special Summoning Plant monsters from the Extra Deck, so every payoff and boss monster in the deck is Plant and generic Plant support reaches everything.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Sunvine Cross Breed Tributes a Link Monster as its cost, so outside Link Monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Continuous Traps
hooks.why: Sunvine Shrine Sets a Continuous Trap directly from your GY each turn, so any Continuous Trap with a strong once-per-turn effect becomes repeatable value.

profile.plan: A line of high-DEF WATER Spellcaster wall monsters, mostly Normal Monsters, with a hand trap that protects Normal Monsters in battle and a LIGHT version that revives itself from banished LIGHT monsters.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Aqua Madoor and Neo Aqua Madoor are Normal Monsters, and Glacier Aqua Madoor only works when your Normal Monsters battle, so outside cards built around Normal Monsters strengthen the whole deck.

hooks.label: Draws off Normal Monsters
hooks.why: The deck's core is Normal Monsters, so outside cards that draw or search when you control or reveal Normal Monsters keep it moving.

hooks.label: Banishes your LIGHT monsters
hooks.why: Lightray Madoor Special Summons itself from the hand when 3 or more of your LIGHT monsters are banished, so outside cards that banish your own LIGHT monsters turn it on for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Glacier Aqua Madoor discards 1 card as a cost for both of its effects, so outside cards with an effect when they are discarded get used for free.

hooks.label: WATER Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Madoor monster is a WATER Spellcaster, so generic support for WATER monsters or Spellcasters covers the whole archetype.

profile.plan: Special Summons Level 5 'Awakening' monsters by sending a face-up Spellcaster and a Level 4 or lower EARTH/FIRE/WATER/WIND monster from the field to the GY, then benefits whenever those big monsters leave the field.

hooks.label: Spellcaster monsters
hooks.why: Every Awakening Summon and Possessed Partnerships needs a Spellcaster on the field (Partnerships specifically summons one with 1500 DEF), so any outside Spellcaster monster is Summon material.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: The Awakening monsters are Summoned by sending your face-up Spellcaster and Level 4 or lower monster to the GY by a card effect, so outside monsters with an effect when they are sent there trigger for free.

hooks.label: Sends your own field to GY
hooks.why: Rasenryu, Nefariouser and the other Awakenings search a 'Spiritual Art' or 'Possessed' card when sent from the field to the GY, so outside cards that send your monsters away keep the payoffs coming.

hooks.label: Flip monsters
hooks.why: Possessed Partnerships and Possessed Destiny place monsters in face-down Defense Position and flip them down, so Flip monsters that trigger when flipped get set off by the deck.

hooks.label: Banishes your GY
hooks.why: Spiritual Power Recovery Potion banishes Spellcasters and Spells from your GY as fuel, and Partnerships banishes itself there, so outside cards with effects while banished from the GY get used for free.

profile.plan: A Ritual Flip deck that Sets its own Flip monsters face-down, then flips them up on demand with Tarotrei and Tarotreith for repeated FLIP effects.

hooks.label: Flip monsters
hooks.why: Tarotreith, Coinorma and Tarotrei Special Summon Flip monsters from the hand, Deck and GY face-down, so any outside Flip monster is free extra value.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Prediction Ritual Tributes monsters from the hand or field to Summon, and Bibliomuse comes back when Tributed, so outside monsters with effects when Tributed get that cost for free.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster support
hooks.why: The deck's bosses are Tarotrei and Tarotreith, and Bibliomuse already protects Ritual Monsters you control, so cards that support Ritual Monsters patch onto them.

hooks.label: Forces monsters into Defense
hooks.why: Petalelf locks opponents' monsters into Defense Position and Astromorrigan destroys every Defense Position monster they control, so outside cards that shift the opponent's monsters into Defense set up the wipe.

profile.plan: Level 1-4 WATER Tuner Fish that revive themselves from the GY by discarding WATER cards, so the deck churns out WATER Synchro Monsters turn after turn.

hooks.label: Self-reviving discard fodder
hooks.why: Blaster and Archer revive themselves by discarding WATER monsters, so outside WATER monsters that trigger or reward being discarded get used for free.

hooks.label: Cards that discard WATER
hooks.why: Blaster, Archer and Harpooner all want a WATER card discarded or revealed from the hand, so outside cards that make you discard WATER keep them going.

hooks.label: WATER Synchro targets
hooks.why: Every Fishborg Tuner must be used for a WATER Synchro Monster, so outside WATER Synchro Monsters are the payoff.

hooks.label: Level 3 or lower WATER bodies
hooks.why: Blaster needs a Level 3 or lower WATER monster on the field to revive itself, so any easy WATER body in that range is an enabler.

hooks.label: WATER monster support
hooks.why: The whole deck is WATER Fish and locks Synchro Summons to WATER, so generic WATER search and support fits everything.

profile.plan: A Pendulum deck that stacks its Extra Deck with face-up Zefra Pendulum Monsters, then Pendulum Summons and pays off its Ritual, Fusion, Synchro and Xyz Summons through Oracle of Zefra and Zefraath.

hooks.label: Pendulum support
hooks.why: Zefraath lives in the Pendulum Zones, Zefra Path needs two Scales of 1 and 7, and Chosen of Zefra counts face-up Pendulum Monsters in the Extra Deck, so generic Pendulum support fuels the whole deck.

hooks.label: Extra Deck Summon payoffs
hooks.why: Oracle of Zefra gives a bonus effect whenever you Ritual, Fusion, Synchro or Xyz Summon using a Zefra monster, so outside cards that perform those Summons trigger it.

hooks.label: Reacts to being Tributed
hooks.why: Zefraath Tributes all monsters you control to Summon itself and Tributes 1 monster each turn to Summon a Zefra from the Deck, so monsters that trigger when Tributed get value for free.

hooks.label: Extra Deck monsters
hooks.why: Zefra Metaltron needs 2+ monsters Special Summoned from the Extra Deck as Link material and rewards monsters it points to that came from the Extra Deck, so big Extra Deck bosses are both fuel and payoff.
phrases: Special Summoned from the Extra Deck

profile.plan: Warrior monsters built around battle position changes and battle damage: Swallowtail and Morpho trigger when positions change or damage lands, and they stack into Photon Alexandra Queen, a Rank 4 that bounces the field.

hooks.label: Changes battle positions
hooks.why: Morpho Butterspy weakens an opponent monster by 1000 whenever an opponent monster's battle position changes, so outside cards that flip or shift positions turn it on for free.

hooks.label: Normal Summons Warriors
hooks.why: Blue Mountain Butterspy Special Summons itself from hand whenever you Normal Summon a Warrior, so outside cards providing extra Warrior Normal Summons or self-summoning Warriors extend the deck.

hooks.label: Makes battle damage
hooks.why: Swallowtail Butterspy lowers an opponent monster's ATK by the battle damage another of your monsters inflicts, so outside monsters that force attacks or push big battle damage feed it.

hooks.label: Level 4 Xyz enablers
hooks.why: Photon Alexandra Queen needs 2 Level 4 Butterspys, and the whole deck is Level 4, so outside Rank 4 Xyz monsters that accept any Level 4 materials give the deck other bosses.

hooks.label: Sends Moonlit Papillon
hooks.why: Moonlit Papillon summons a Butterspy from the Deck when sent from the field to the GY, so outside cards that tribute or send your own monsters recycle it.

profile.plan: Fuses its legendary guardians by banishing Sanga, Kazejin and Suijin from the hand, field and GY, then rebuilds its forces by Special Summoning the banished pieces back when the Fusions are broken.

hooks.label: Banishes your monsters from GY
hooks.why: Gate Guardians Combined and the smaller Fusions Summon themselves by banishing Sanga, Kazejin and Suijin from the hand, field and/or GY, so anything that moves your monsters into the banished pile feeds them.

hooks.label: Recovers banished monsters
hooks.why: The smaller Fusions Special Summon a banished Sanga, Kazejin or Suijin when they leave the field, so outside cards that bring banished monsters back keep the Summoning fuel circulating.

hooks.label: Warrior DARK support
hooks.why: Gate Guardian and Gate Guardians Combined are both DARK Warriors, so generic Warrior or DARK monster support covers the deck's bosses.

profile.plan: A Yubel hybrid engine that Tributes its own cards to put Yubel on the field, then Ritual Summons Relinquished by Tributing 2 monsters to steal the opponent's monster as an Equip, plus an Xyz Rank-up trick.

hooks.label: Yubel monsters
hooks.why: Samsara D Lotus Tributes itself to Special Summon a Yubel from the Deck, and its Quick Effect only works while you control a Yubel, so any Yubel card is the payoff.

hooks.label: Gets value when Tributed
hooks.why: Samsara D Lotus Tributes itself as a cost and Relinquished the Wicked Eye of Illusion Tributes 2 monsters to summon itself, so outside cards with effects when they are Tributed are free value.

hooks.label: Tribute fodder Tokens
hooks.why: Relinquished the Wicked Eye of Illusion needs 2 Tributes to Ritual Summon itself, so outside cards that make Tokens supply them without costing cards.

hooks.label: Triggers when banished as material
hooks.why: Sacrifice Level-Up banishes 2 materials from your Xyz Monster as its cost, so outside cards with an effect when banished get used for free.

hooks.label: Xyz climbing support
hooks.why: Sacrifice Level-Up needs an Xyz Monster on the field and summons a Rank-higher Xyz from the Extra Deck, so outside Xyz Monsters and cards that load them with materials fuel it.

profile.plan: A Machine Link deck that swarms Link-1 monsters, chains them together so co-linked appliances gain attacks and protection, then wins through battle-phase tricks like ATK-dropping, direct attacks and destruction after damage calculation.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Appliancer monster, Main Deck and Extra Deck, is a Machine, so generic Machine searchers, revivers and boosters work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Link Summon enablers
hooks.why: The deck's whole board is built by Link Summoning one Link-1 after another, and Electrilyrical World only searches when you Link Summon an Appliancer, so outside cards that make Link Summoning easier multiply the deck's plays.

hooks.label: Damage calculation tricks
hooks.why: Propelion, Celtopus, Breakerbuncle and Laundry Dragon all resolve during damage calculation, so outside cards that also act in that window stack with the deck's battle-phase effects.

hooks.label: Revives your Link Monsters
hooks.why: Kappa Scale, Reuse, Test and Conversion all recycle Appliancer Link Monsters from the GY, so any outside card that revives a Link Monster is another way to rebuild the board after a board wipe.

hooks.label: Monsters that reward pointing
hooks.why: Appliancer Test summons Link-1s specifically into zones a Link Monster points to, and co-linking drives every effect, so outside Link Monsters with effects in zones other monsters point to extend the deck's core mechanic.

profile.plan: EARTH Warrior brawlers that fight during the Battle Phase, growing stronger each time one of their monsters battles and rising again when the opponent's card effects knock them down.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: War Rock Gactos Special Summons itself from hand the moment an EARTH Warrior is Normal Summoned, so cards that grant additional Normal Summons give you extra chances to trigger it and to set up Level 5s like Orpis and Mammud.

hooks.label: EARTH Warrior monsters
hooks.why: Every trigger in the deck keys on 'your EARTH Warrior monster' battling or being Normal Summoned, and War Rock Mountain and Medium require all your monsters be Warriors, so any outside EARTH Warrior turns on Fortia's search, Orpis' mill and Mammud's removal for free.

hooks.label: Warrior Special Summon extenders
hooks.why: War Rock Medium locks you to Special Summoning only Warrior monsters for the rest of the turn after it fetches a War Rock Spell/Trap, so extenders that Special Summon Warriors keep the deck moving within that lock.

hooks.label: EARTH Warrior support
hooks.why: All fifteen War Rock cards revolve around EARTH Warriors, so generic cards that search, revive or power up EARTH Warrior monsters work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends your own cards to the GY
hooks.why: Gactos, Fortia and Wento Special Summon a Level 5 or higher War Rock from hand or Deck when sent from the Monster Zone to the GY by an opponent's card effect, so any outside card that knocks your own EARTH Warrior into the GY by effect is a free Summon trigger.

profile.plan: FIRE Warrior synchro knights that stack themselves as Equip Spells, using Level 1 Tuners and other Warriors to Synchro Summon and turning every equip into more material and removal.

hooks.label: Equips to Warriors
hooks.why: Turpin and Oliver revive from the GY by equipping to a Warrior you control, and Ricciardetto and Bradamante build around equipped monsters, so outside Equip Cards and equipping effects multiply every payoff.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: The whole deck is Warrior monsters and Ricciardetto locks you into Warrior Special Summons, so generic Warrior search, revive and boost cards keep it going.

hooks.label: Sends to the GY for materials
hooks.why: Ricciardetto can Special Summon any Level 4 or lower FIRE Warrior from the GY, so outside cards that fill the GY with FIRE Warriors give it targets.

hooks.label: FIRE Warrior Tuners
hooks.why: Synchro Summoning needs Tuners and Ricciardetto makes more from Level 4 or lower FIRE Warriors, so outside FIRE Warrior Tuners fit straight in.

hooks.label: Equipped monster payoffs
hooks.why: Turpin self-Summons off any monster equipped with an Equip Card and Oliver's attack trigger needs itself equipped, so outside cards that treat your monsters as equipped or equip from unexpected zones act as extenders.

profile.plan: Warrior LIGHT monsters that Fusion Summon by destroying their own Dual Avatar cards, turning each destruction into a bigger Fusion Monster and recovery.

hooks.label: Fusion Summon enablers
hooks.why: Dual Avatar Invitation Fusion Summons using monsters from hand or field, and the deck is locked into Fusion Monsters the turn it makes Tokens, so outside cards that Fusion Summon the same way add extra routes.

hooks.label: Floaters that trigger when destroyed
hooks.why: Yuhi, Defeating Evil and Ascendance all destroy your own Dual Avatar monsters on purpose, so an outside monster that gets an effect when destroyed by a card effect is used for free.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Dual Avatar monster, including all of its Fusion Monsters, is a Warrior, so generic Warrior searchers, revival and boosters work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Strong Warrior Fusions
hooks.why: Kon-Gyo and Mitsu-Jaku only get their Quick Effect negation and removal while you control 2 or more Fusion Monsters, so any outside Warrior Fusion helps switch those on.

hooks.label: Revives from the GY
hooks.why: Manifested A-Un's floating effect fills the GY with Yuhi and Kokoku, and Ascendance wants Dual Avatar monsters in the GY to recover, so cards that revive your Warriors recycle them.

profile.plan: A carnival of Machines and Psychics that equip their 'Attraction' Traps to monsters - usually the opponent's - to debuff or steal them, while summoning in response to Trap activations and the opponent's moves.

hooks.label: Equip Card support
hooks.why: Comica, Delia and Bufo all move 'Attraction' Traps between monsters and Family Faces lives on a monster being equipped, so outside cards that interact with Equip Cards keep the whole equip engine running.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Comica and Delia are the deck's Level 4 engines and both are LIGHT Machines, so generic Machine support covers the monsters that find and cycle the Attractions.

hooks.label: Psychic support
hooks.why: Both Arlekino bosses, the deck's main bodies and win condition, are DARK/LIGHT Psychics, so Psychic support protects and extends them.

profile.plan: A Rainbow Dragon build that cheats out the Level 12 Ultimate Crystal bosses, then turns its banished Crystal Beasts into a 7000-ATK board wipe engine, with backrow cards that trigger off Crystal Beasts being placed in the Spell & Trap Zone.

hooks.label: Places monsters in backrow
hooks.why: Crystal Miracle, Aegis, Boon and Brilliance all trigger when a Crystal Beast card is placed in your Spell & Trap Zone, so outside cards that put monsters there as Continuous Spells are free activators.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Crystal Aegis and Crystal Miracle destroy your own Crystal Beast cards as setup, and the archetype's monsters want to end up in the Spell & Trap Zone, so self-destruction is a benefit, not a cost.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: Ultimate Crystal Rainbow Dragon Overdrive banishes your monsters from the field and GY for its Summon and again when it Tributes itself, so outside monsters with effects while banished get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Feeds the banished pile
hooks.why: Overdrive gains 7000 ATK only while 7 or more differently named Crystal Beasts are banished, so outside cards that banish your monsters from the GY grow the pile it counts.

profile.plan: A swarm of Level 4 LIGHT Fairies that Special Summon each other from the hand, then overlay three or more of them into Rank 4 Xyz Monsters that draw and destroy.

hooks.label: Rank 4 Xyz Summons
hooks.why: Scepter and Scale grant bonus effects to Xyz Monsters Summoned using 3 or more monsters as materials, and Number 102 needs 3 Level 4 LIGHT monsters, so outside cards that Xyz Summon Rank 4 monsters stack extra triggers.

hooks.label: Level 4 LIGHT monsters
hooks.why: Number 102 requires 3 Level 4 LIGHT monsters as Xyz Material, and the rest of the deck only needs Level 4 bodies on the field, so any outside Level 4 LIGHT monster is straight material.

hooks.label: Spells that want to be discarded
hooks.why: Sage sends 1 Spell Card from the hand to the GY as its cost to Special Summon, so outside Spells with effects in the Graveyard are used for free.

hooks.label: Adds Xyz Material
hooks.why: Number 102 pays costs and protects itself by detaching Xyz Material, and Scepter's and Scale's bonus effects only work while material is attached, so outside cards that attach more material keep everything online.

hooks.label: Fairy support
hooks.why: Every Star Seraph monster is a Fairy, so generic Fairy searchers and boosters work across the whole deck.

profile.plan: Small monsters that swarm the field as Tribute fodder and give extra Normal Summons when Tributed, all to power out big Tribute Summons (the Monarch playstyle).

hooks.label: Monarch-style Tribute bosses
hooks.why: The Vassals' whole job is being Tributed away, so big Level 5+ monsters with strong Tribute Summon payoffs (Monarchs and the like) are the finishers this engine is built around.

hooks.label: Triggers when Tributed
hooks.why: Every Vassal pays off when Tributed for a Tribute Summon, so outside monsters with their own effects when Tributed stack extra value onto each Tribute.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Mithra grants an additional Tribute Summon when Tributed, and every extra Normal Summon is one more Tribute Summoned boss this deck can push out.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon payoff cards
hooks.why: The deck is locked out of Extra Deck Summons while Vassals set up, so it wins entirely through Tribute Summoning and cards that reward or enable Tribute Summons carry the strategy.

profile.plan: A gaggle of gambling cards built around rolling six-sided dice, rerolling bad results, punishing opponents' dice effects, and milling or banishing cards based on what the die says.

hooks.label: Die-rolling cards
hooks.why: Dice Re-Roll lets you reroll any die roll once per turn, so every outside card whose effect rolls a six-sided die becomes a controllable gamble.

hooks.label: Speedroid cards
hooks.why: Dice Roll Battle banishes a Speedroid monster from your GY and a Speedroid Tuner from your hand to Synchro Summon, and Speedroids themselves roll dice, so the whole Speedroid family slots in.

hooks.label: Wants to be milled
hooks.why: Dice It can send up to six cards from the top of your Deck to the GY, so outside monsters with an effect when a card effect sends them from the Deck to the GY get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Banishes from your GY
hooks.why: Dice It banishes cards from your GY equal to the die result on your turn, so cards with effects that trigger or work while banished pair with it.

profile.plan: A pile of Normal Monsters from the game's oldest sets — all vanilla, spanning every Type and Level — that lives or dies on generic Normal Monster support.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Every card in the archetype is a Normal Monster with no effect of its own, so outside cards that search, protect or power up Normal Monsters are the deck's engine.

hooks.label: Level 2 or lower vanillas
hooks.why: Abyss Flower, The Wandering Doomed, Pot the Trick and Tentacle Plant are Level 2 Normal Monsters, so recruiters and support aimed at low-Level vanillas find them.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon payoffs
hooks.why: Nine of the monsters are Level 5 and 6 vanillas that need two Tributes, so outside cards rewarding Tribute Summoning give them a reason to be played.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Beast/Plant/Fairy engine built around Synchro Summoning Ancient Fairy Dragon, keeping everything in Defense Position where the deck's monsters defend best and World of Spirits punishes attackers.

hooks.label: LIGHT Beast/Plant/Fairy monsters
hooks.why: Regulus Special Summons Level 4 or lower LIGHT Beast/Plant/Fairy monsters from the hand, and Ancient Fairy Life Dragon searches one when World of Spirits is up, so any such monster is free material.

hooks.label: High-Level LIGHT Dragon Synchros
hooks.why: World of Spirits only turns on its attack-punishing effects while you control a Level 7 or higher LIGHT Dragon Synchro Monster, and Ancient Fairy Dragon alone is not always enough.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Regulus the Fairy Beast shuffles a Field Spell from your GY to the bottom of the Deck to draw, so outside cards that fetch or recycle Field Spells keep World of Spirits coming.

hooks.label: Level manipulation
hooks.why: Spore the Fairy Seed raises its own Level by the number of monsters you control to reach Level 8 Synchro Summons, so outside cards that change Levels extend its tuning range.

profile.plan: Machine Pendulum musicians that spam the field through Pendulum Summons, face-down summons and Tuner-driven Synchro plays, scaling into their Field Spell and Rockks.

hooks.label: Machine WIND support
hooks.why: Every Symphonic Warrior monster is a WIND Machine, so generic support for that Type or Attribute hits the whole deck.

hooks.label: Pendulum support
hooks.why: Guitaar, DJJ, Miccs and Rockks all live in the Pendulum Zones, and Rockks and Miccs constantly need face-up Pendulum Monsters fetched back from the Extra Deck, so outside cards that manage Pendulum cards keep the engine going.

hooks.label: Flip monsters
hooks.why: DJJ Special Summons Symphonic Warriors from the Deck in face-down Defense Position, so outside Flip Effect Monsters summoned that way get their FLIP effects later, like Synthess does.

hooks.label: Easy Tribute Summon bosses
hooks.why: Miccs grants an extra Normal Summon after it hits the field and self-Summons by removing Symphonic Counters, so the deck can afford a big Tribute Summon on top of its swarming.

hooks.label: WIND Synchro bosses
hooks.why: Piaano, Basses, Drumss and Guitariss are all Tuners and Basses raises Levels by hand size, so the deck reaches Level 7 Synchro Summons like Rockks easily and any strong WIND Synchro monster fits the same slots.

profile.plan: A Level-climbing line of DARK Spellcasters that steal the opponent's monsters by equipping them to themselves, then sacrifice the equipped card when they would be destroyed in battle.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Chaos Allure Queen Summons itself from the hand by discarding another LIGHT or DARK monster, so outside monsters with an effect when they are discarded get it for free.

hooks.label: Discards your LIGHT/DARK monsters
hooks.why: Chaos Allure Queen needs another LIGHT or DARK monster discarded to Special Summon itself, so outside cards that make you discard keep feeding that cost and give follow-up plays.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Every Allure Queen monster is a Spellcaster and Golden Allure Queen Link Summons with 3 Spellcaster materials, so generic Spellcaster support fuels both the Main Deck and the Extra Deck.

hooks.label: Equips opponent's monsters
hooks.why: The whole deck's plan is taking the opponent's monsters and equipping them to itself as expendable shields, so outside cards that equip enemy monsters double down on that strategy.

profile.plan: LIGHT Machine Union monsters that equip to each other and banish themselves from field and GY to fuse into big LIGHT Machine Fusion bosses.

hooks.label: LIGHT Machine support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is a LIGHT Machine and their equipping and banishing effects only reach LIGHT Machines, so generic LIGHT or Machine support covers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Union monsters
