hooks.why: X-Cross Cannon equips appropriate LIGHT Machine Union monsters straight from the Deck, so outside Union monsters are extra bodies it can pull.

hooks.label: Level 8 LIGHT Machine Fusions
hooks.why: XYZ-Hyper Dragon Cannon banishes itself to summon the Fusion Materials listed on any Level 8 LIGHT Machine Fusion Monster, so those Fusion bosses are the deck's payoff targets.

hooks.label: Banish-fodder monsters
hooks.why: X-Cross Cannon and the Fusion Summon banish LIGHT Machines from field and GY as material, so outside monsters with an effect when banished get it for free.

hooks.label: Discards your own hand
hooks.why: XYZ-Hyper Dragon Cannon's Quick Effect destruction costs a discard, so outside cards that make you discard keep it fueled.

profile.plan: Colossal Level 10 DARK Fiends that can only be Tribute Summoned with 3 Tributes each, backed by Divine Evolution to make one unstoppable.

hooks.label: Tribute fodder swarms
hooks.why: Each Wicked God needs 3 Tributes and cannot be Special Summoned first, so outside cards that swarm your field with Tokens or cheap monsters are the fuel supply.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: You will Tribute three monsters every time you Summon a Wicked God, so outside monsters with effects that trigger when they are Tributed get used for free.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon payoffs
hooks.why: The Wicked Gods are pure Tribute Summons, so outside cards that search, draw or gain effects off a Tribute Summon reward the deck's own plan.

hooks.label: DARK Fiend support
hooks.why: All three Wicked Gods are DARK Fiends, so generic DARK or Fiend search and revival cards work on the whole archetype.

profile.plan: Trap and Spell 'Contact' cards cheat out HERO Fusion Monsters from the Extra Deck while ignoring their Summoning conditions, by recycling their materials from hand, field, GY and banishment back into the Deck.

hooks.label: Gets Neos on board
hooks.why: Instant Contact's summoned monster only keeps its effects and stays on the field while Elemental HERO Neos is on your field or in your GY, so any outside card that puts a Neos there is fuel.

hooks.label: HERO material makers
hooks.why: Favorite Contact summons HERO Fusions using materials from hand, field, GY and banishment, so outside cards that get HERO monsters into those zones or banish them on purpose widen what it can cheat out.

hooks.label: Dark Fusion support
hooks.why: Dark Contact searches Dark Fusion or Supreme King's Castle and Fusion Summons with Dark Fusion's name, so outside cards that work with Dark Fusion or Evil HEROes stack with it.

hooks.label: Shuffles cards into Deck
hooks.why: Favorite Contact and Dark Contact both place or shuffle their Fusion materials from the GY and banishment back into the Deck, so outside cards that return your cards there keep the materials reusable.

profile.plan: Rock monsters that cycle Triamid Field Spells in and out of the Field Zone, swapping them for new ones on the opponent's turn and triggering recycling effects whenever a Field Spell hits the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Rock-type support
hooks.why: Every Triamid monster is a Rock and Dancer, Fortress, Kingolem and Pulse all reward or support Rock-Type monsters.

hooks.label: Sends Field Spells from field
hooks.why: Each Triamid Field Spell has an effect when it is sent from the Field Zone to the Graveyard, so outside cards that swap out or replace your Field Spell trigger them for free.

hooks.label: Places Field Spells face-up
hooks.why: Triamid Loading searches a Triamid Spell/Trap whenever a Field Spell is placed face-up in the Field Zone, so anything that sets another Field Spell from the Deck is a free activator.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished from the GY
hooks.why: Triamid Pulse banishes two Rock monsters or Field Spells from your Graveyard as a cost, so outside cards with effects that trigger when banished get used for free.

hooks.label: Extra Rock Normal Summons
hooks.why: Triamid Hunter grants an additional Normal Summon of a Rock-Type monster while a Field Spell is up, and Triamid Cruiser draws and heals when a Triamid is Normal Summoned, so outside Rocks that want to be Tribute or Normal Summoned fit.

profile.plan: A Skull Servant deck that stuffs its GY with Zombies, grows the King of the Skull Servants off them, and mills its own Deck to fuel revival and searches.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Wightlord and Wight Reanimator send cards from the top or body of your Deck to the GY to load Skull Servants, so any outside card that mills your Deck feeds them.

hooks.label: Wants to be milled
hooks.why: The deck sends its own cards from the Deck to the GY several cards at a time, so outside monsters with an effect when sent from the Deck to the GY get it for free.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: Moissa Wight and Wight Reanimator lock you into Special Summoning Zombie monsters for the turn, so generic Zombie-type searchers, revival and extenders fit the whole deck.

hooks.label: Piercing damage support
hooks.why: Wight Reanimator gives your King of the Skull Servants piercing against Defense Position monsters, so outside cards that grant or reward piercing battle damage stack with it.

profile.plan: A Pendulum-Synchro hybrid of WIND Machines that swarms Tuners and Pendulum monsters, scales up to Synchro Summon Clear Wing dragons, and rides multi-attack Battle Phases.

hooks.label: WIND Machine support
hooks.why: Nearly every roid monster is a WIND Machine, and Hi-Speedroid Glider #2 literally requires a WIND Machine Tuner as material, so generic WIND Machine support covers the whole deck.

hooks.label: WIND Synchro bosses
hooks.why: Hi-Speedroid Glider #2 revives WIND non-Tuner Synchros, and Wing Synchron needs you to control two or more different Types of WIND Synchro Monsters, so any WIND Synchro Monster is both payoff and engine.

hooks.label: Extra attacks
hooks.why: Meteor Rush - Monochroid Special Summons itself after five or more attacks are declared and gains 1000 ATK per attack, so outside cards that grant additional attacks or attack all monsters turbocharge it.

hooks.label: Banishes your WIND monsters
hooks.why: Dominobutterfly retrieves banished WIND monsters and Glider #2 and Colonel Clackers banish themselves or Speedroid cards as costs, so outside cards that banish your WIND monsters feed that recycling.

hooks.label: Machines that want the GY
hooks.why: Einroid sends two Level 4 or lower Machine monsters from the Deck to the GY and Darumaknocker sends Speedroid cards there, so outside Machine monsters with effects when sent to the GY get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Discard outlets
hooks.why: Dominobutterfly and Dragonroid discard monsters as costs, so outside WIND monsters with effects that trigger when a card effect discards them turn those costs into advantage.

profile.plan: Level 12 Dinosaurs that destroy themselves and each other to cheat out their Fusion, Synchro, Xyz and Link bosses, each of which revives itself by shuffling a Normal Monster from the GY back into the Deck.

hooks.label: Destroys your own Dinosaurs
hooks.why: Meteorus Special Summons itself by destroying 2 other Dinosaur monsters in your hand and/or field, so any outside card that destroys your Dinosaurs sets that and the bosses' 'if destroyed' revives off.

hooks.label: Dinosaurs with destroyed triggers
hooks.why: All five bosses trigger when destroyed, and Meteorus destroys Dinosaurs in your hand and field, so outside Dinosaurs with their own 'if destroyed' effects come back for free.

hooks.label: Sends Normal Monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Every boss needs a Normal Monster in the GY to shuffle into the Deck and revive itself, so outside cards that mill or send Normal Monsters keep the loop alive.

hooks.label: Normal Dinosaur monsters
hooks.why: Gigantozowler Fuses 1 Dinosaur plus 1 Normal Monster, and the whole deck's revival costs Normal Monsters, so Normal Dinosaur monsters serve as both Fusion material and revival fuel.

hooks.label: Revives or summons Dinosaurs
hooks.why: Meteorus can only be Special Summoned by card effect, Exaraptor summons Dinosaurs from your hand and Drillygnathus summons banished Dinosaurs, so outside cards that Special Summon Dinosaur monsters extend every line.

hooks.label: Dinosaur support
hooks.why: Every Transcendosaurus monster is a Dinosaur, so generic Dinosaur searchers, revival and boosters work on the whole deck.

profile.plan: Untargetable Level 6 FIRE monsters that swarm the field, stack Xyz materials and Summon Rank 6 Hazy Flame Basiltrice with five materials.

hooks.label: FIRE Attribute support
hooks.why: Every Hazy monster is FIRE and Griffin requires your field and GY to be all FIRE, so generic FIRE support covers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Self-summoning Level 6 FIREs
hooks.why: Basiltrice needs 2 or more Level 6 FIRE monsters as Xyz Material, so outside FIRE monsters of that Level that Special Summon themselves build its materials for free.

hooks.label: Attaches Xyz material
hooks.why: Basiltrice gains protection per Xyz Material attached and reaches full immunity at five, and Hazy Pillar already shows the deck wants extra materials.

hooks.label: Mills your own Deck
hooks.why: Sphynx mills the top card and revives a FIRE monster off it, so outside cards that send your own cards to the GY keep that trigger live.

hooks.label: FIRE monsters that like being sent
hooks.why: Peryton, Mantikor and Hyppogrif all send or Tribute FIRE monsters from your hand and field as costs, so outside FIRE monsters with GY effects turn those costs into advantage.

profile.plan: A prank deck that floods both fields with low-Level Fiends called Dustons, which can't be Tributed or used as material, punish whoever destroys them, and stack up into Starduston for a total Summon lock.

hooks.label: Board wipes
hooks.why: House Duston and Diamond Duston Special Summon Dustons from the Deck when cards on the field are destroyed by battle or card effect, so any mass-destruction effect loads the board for free.

hooks.label: Sends your monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Starduston is Special Summoned by sending any number of Dustons you control to the Graveyard, so outside cards that send your own Level 1 Fiends there power up its ATK and DEF.

hooks.label: Level 1 monsters
hooks.why: Every Duston is a Level 1 Fiend with 0 ATK, so outside Level 1 monsters and Level 1 support cards slot straight in and survive the archetype's anti-Tribute, anti-material drawbacks.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: All Duston monsters and Starduston itself are Fiends, so generic Fiend revival, search and boost cards work across the whole deck.

profile.plan: A Rank 3 Xyz deck that Summons Level 3 Normal Monsters and uses them as material, then keeps recycling the cards attached to its Xyz Monsters as extra cards in hand.

hooks.label: Level 3 Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Exareptor, Gigadra, Zeptwing and Meltthrough all search, Summon or use Level 3 Normal Monsters as Xyz material, so any outside Normal Monster of exactly Level 3 is a body for the deck.

hooks.label: Attaches extra Xyz material
hooks.why: Meltdown, Meltthrough and Prima Materiactor reward every card attached to an Xyz Monster, so outside cards that attach material keep the detach-and-recover engine stocked.

hooks.label: Rewards when detached
hooks.why: Exagard, Gigaboros, Critical and Annulus detach Xyz material constantly, so outside monsters with an effect when they are detached get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: The deck Summons Level 3 Normal Monsters on purpose and Exagard even bounces a card when one is in the GY, so outside cards built around Normal Monsters have targets everywhere.

hooks.label: Rank 3 Xyz boosters
hooks.why: Exareptor Quick-Effect boosts a Rank 3 Xyz Monster and Exagard recovers materials for any Xyz, so outside Rank 3 Xyz Monsters stack onto the same engine.

profile.plan: Level 1-2 Plant seeds that revive Plant Normal Monsters and re-summon your Sunavalon/Sunvine Link Monsters by banishing themselves from the GY, all while locked into Plants.

hooks.label: Plant type support
hooks.why: Every Sunseed monster is a Plant and Sunseed Shadow locks you into Special Summoning Plants for the rest of the turn, so generic Plant support fits the whole deck.

hooks.label: Plant Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Sunseed Shadow Special Summons itself while you control a Plant Normal Monster and Sunseed Twin revives one from the GY, so any outside Plant Normal Monster is live material.

hooks.label: Mills Plant Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Sunseed Twin's revive only works if a Level 4 or lower Plant Normal Monster is already in the GY, so outside cards that send them there set it up.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: Sunseed Twin and Sunseed Shadow both banish themselves from your GY as a cost, so outside cards with an effect when they are banished get triggered for free.

profile.plan: A package of Spells and Traps that support three GY-based Fiend strategies at once: it fills the GY with Fiends, keeps your hand empty for Infernity, and recycles banished Infernoids.

hooks.label: Mills Fiends from the Deck
hooks.why: Void Apocalypse only sends one Fiend at a time, and Infernoids Special Summon themselves out of the GY, so outside cards that send Fiend monsters from the Deck to the GY feed the whole engine.

hooks.label: Discards your own hand
hooks.why: Void Cauldron destroys itself while you have cards in hand and Infernoids only survive with one, so outside cards that make you discard your own hand are activators.

hooks.label: Banishes your own GY cards
hooks.why: Void Breach and Void Reignition recycle banished Infernoids and count them for ATK, so outside cards that banish your own Fiend monsters from the GY set up the payoffs.

hooks.label: No-hand payoffs
hooks.why: Void Cauldron demands an empty hand and Contract with the Void summons Infernities, so outside cards that care about having no cards in hand fit the deck's whole game plan.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Every monster the archetype works with is a Fiend, so generic cards that search, revive or boost Fiends serve the whole deck.

profile.plan: LIGHT Insect swarming that flips its own monsters to Defense Position to trigger effects, then stacks them into a climbing ladder of Xyz monsters that shred the opponent's Defense Position monsters.

hooks.label: Changes your monsters' positions
hooks.why: Centibit and LEDybug Special Summon or search whenever they are flipped from Attack to Defense Position, and Corebage attaches a GY Insect when any monster changes position, so outside cards that flip your monsters into Defense give free triggers.

hooks.label: Level 3 LIGHT Insects
hooks.why: Centibit and LEDybug only summon or search Level 3 Insects and the base Xyz, Scaradiator, needs Level 3 LIGHT Insect materials, so outside monsters that are both fill every role.

hooks.label: Insect support
hooks.why: Every card in the deck is an Insect and each monster locks its Xyz use to Insect-Type Xyz Summons, so generic Insect searchers, revival and boosters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Rank 3-4 Insect Xyz
hooks.why: Corebage can be Xyz Summoned by detaching 2 materials from a Rank 3 or 4 Insect Xyz Monster, and Rhinosebus climbs off a Rank 5 or 6, so other Insect Xyz monsters are rungs on the ladder.

hooks.label: Forces opponents into Defense
hooks.why: Websolder's inherited effect zeroes DEF and forces Defense Position, Centibit attacks every Defense Position monster, Rhinosebus pierces and Corebage shuffles Defense Position monsters away, so outside cards that put the opponent's monsters in Defense fuel all of it.

profile.plan: Evolvolves FIRE Reptiles into FIRE Dinosaurs: Evoltiles Summon Evolsaurs, which then become Rank 6 Evolzar Xyz Monsters that negate with Reptile/Dinosaur materials.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Pholis Tributes a Reptile or Dinosaur you control as destruction substitution, so outside monsters with effects that trigger when Tributed get used for free.

hooks.label: Reptile or Dinosaur Level 6 Xyz material
hooks.why: Lars only needs to detach 1 material when all its materials are Reptile and/or Dinosaur, so Level 6 Reptiles and Dinosaurs are premium material for it.

hooks.label: FIRE monster support
hooks.why: Every Evol monster is FIRE, and Evolsaurs only get their effects when Special Summoned by a FIRE monster, so cards that support FIRE monsters work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Sends FIRE Reptile or Dinosaur to GY
hooks.why: Lios needs FIRE Reptile or Dinosaur monsters sent from the Deck to the GY for its Type-and-Level copy effect, so outside cards that do that set up its best plays.

profile.plan: EARTH Cyberse Links that swarm with Tokens and small bodies, then pay off co-linking and heavy EARTH Link bosses that force attacks onto themselves.

hooks.label: Discards your Cyberse monsters
hooks.why: Rock Hammer and Invalid Dolmen discard Cyberse monsters as a cost, and Pebble Dog searches when it is sent from the hand to the GY, so anything that sends your Cyberse cards there is fuel.

hooks.label: Cyberse monsters with hand-to-GY triggers
hooks.why: The deck constantly sends Cyberse monsters from the hand to the GY as costs, so outside Cyberse monsters that trigger there get it for free.

hooks.label: EARTH Link Monsters
hooks.why: Crystal Heart Special Summons EARTH Link Monsters from your GY to its zone and buffs them with counters, so any EARTH Link Monster is a reviveable win condition.

hooks.label: EARTH monster revival
hooks.why: Stubborn Menhir and Gravity Balance Special Summon EARTH monsters straight out of the GY, so the deck wants outside cards that load and exploit the EARTH GY.

hooks.label: EARTH and Cyberse support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is an EARTH Cyberse and Rock Hammer locks you into Cyberse Summons, so generic EARTH and Cyberse support works on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Co-link payoffs
hooks.why: Crystal Heart, Invalid Dolmen and Dolmen's effect-negation all switch on when monsters are co-linked, so outside cards that create or reward co-links multiply the payoff.

profile.plan: Traps and Spells that Set, flip and re-Summon "Ninja" monsters face-down, Tribute them to cheat out bigger Ninjas, and lean on Insect Ninjas with Hallucination Counters.

hooks.label: Ninja monsters
hooks.why: Every Ninjitsu Art card asks for a "Ninja" monster on the field or in the Deck, but this archetype itself provides none of them, so the monsters have to come from outside.

hooks.label: Flip monsters
hooks.why: Ninjitsu Art Notebook of Mystery, Iron Digger and Tenchi Kaimei all Special Summon or Set monsters in face-down Defense Position, so outside Flip monsters get their flip effects triggered for free.

hooks.label: Puts monsters face-down
hooks.why: Notebook of Mystery flips a face-up monster face-down and the deck hides its Ninjas in face-down Defense Position, so outside cards that do the same extend the disguise-and-flip game.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Ninjitsu Art of Dancing Leaves Tributes a Ninja or face-down monster as its activation cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Insect support
hooks.why: Mosquito Marching Special Summons Level 4 or lower Insect monsters and builds a board of Insects around Number 2: Ninja Shadow Mosquito, so cards that support Insects fit it.

profile.plan: A Psychic Xyz deck that stacks Level 4 monsters into Number 69: Heraldry Crest, copies the names and effects of enemy Xyz Monsters, and ranks up into bigger Heraldry Crests that shut those copies down.

hooks.label: Level 4 self-summoners
hooks.why: Number 69 needs 3 Level 4 monsters and its upgrades need 4 or 5, so outside monsters that Special Summon themselves from the hand are the cheapest way to stack materials.

hooks.label: Xyz monsters worth copying
hooks.why: Number 69 and Heraldry Crest of Horror copy the name, ATK and original effect of another face-up Xyz Monster, so any outside Xyz boss with a strong activated effect becomes a better payoff for the deck than for its own deck.

hooks.label: Extra Xyz Material
hooks.why: Crest of Horror and Dark Matter Demolition pay by detaching materials, and Number 69 starts with three, so outside cards that attach more material keep every effect live.

hooks.label: Psychic support
hooks.why: Every Heraldry monster is a Psychic Xyz Monster, and Flash of Heraldry only re-Sets itself while you control one, so generic Psychic-Type searchers and revivers keep the deck going.

profile.plan: Level 8 EARTH Beast-Warriors that cheat themselves out by mass-Tributing or banishing Materials, then swing for huge attacks; the deck is always hungry for Tribute fodder and banishable Machine monsters.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: Beast King Barbaros destroys everything when Tribute Summoned with 3 Tributes, and King Beast Barbaros Tributes monsters totaling Level 8+ to Special Summon itself, so Tokens are pure fuel for both.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Both Barbaros Summoning conditions Tribute your own monsters, so outside monsters that search or draw when Tributed pay you back for the cost.

hooks.label: Easy Tribute Summons
hooks.why: Beast King Barbaros's best play is a 3-Tribute Tribute Summon that wipes the opponent's field, so outside monsters that Tribute Summon themselves with fewer Tributes fit right in.

hooks.label: Beast-Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Barbaros monster is an EARTH Beast-Warrior, so generic Beast-Warrior searchers and boosters work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Banish-fodder Machines
hooks.why: Beast Machine King Barbaros Ür Special Summons itself by banishing a Machine and a Beast-Warrior, so Machine monsters you are happy to banish from the GY or field are free material.

profile.plan: Level 2 and Level 8 Gemini monsters that must be Normal Summoned twice to earn their effects, then Xyz Summon into Rank 8 bosses or recycle Geminis from the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Gemini monster support
hooks.why: Every Chemicritter monster is a Gemini, and Methydraco, Hydragon and Carbo Crab all only work with other Gemini monsters, so outside cards that treat or reward Geminis fit the whole deck.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Geminis must be Normal Summoned again to gain their effects, and Methydraco and Hydragon trigger on each Gemini Normal Summon, so cards granting additional Normal Summons speed everything up.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Unawakened Chemicritters are treated as Normal Monsters on the field and in the Graveyard, so outside cards that search or revive Normal Monsters reach them.

hooks.label: Revives from banishment
hooks.why: Dioxogre banishes Geminis from the Graveyard as a cost and Burnout banishes itself, so outside cards that Special Summon banished monsters recycle that fuel.

hooks.label: Level manipulation
hooks.why: Oxy Ox can make all your Geminis share one Level and the Level 2 Chemicritters need to reach Level 8 for Methydraco, so cards that change Levels help stack Xyz materials.

hooks.label: Monsters that trigger when banished
hooks.why: Dioxogre banishes a Gemini from the Graveyard as a cost every turn, so outside monsters with an effect when they are banished get it for free.

profile.plan: Live☆Twin Lil-la small monsters that special-summon themselves alongside Ki-sikil, negate answers by discarding, and burn the opponent every time something returns from the Graveyard.

hooks.label: Fiend support
hooks.why: Lil-la Sweet locks your Extra Deck to Fiend monsters while it is face-up, and the wider Live☆Twin / Evil★Twin bosses are all Fiends, so generic Fiend support hits the whole deck.

hooks.label: Revives Fiends from the GY
hooks.why: Lil-la Rap burns your opponent for 1000 every time you Special Summon from the GY, so outside cards that revive Fiend monsters set it off once per turn for free.

hooks.label: Banishes itself from the GY
hooks.why: Lil-la Treat pays for its ATK-drop effect by banishing itself from the GY, so outside cards that use themselves banished from the GY stack another payoff on the same cost.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Lil-la Sweet discards itself to negate an opposing response, so outside cards that get an effect when discarded make that cost hurt less.

profile.plan: A Rank 3 Rock Xyz deck that stacks Level 3 Rock-Type monsters and zeroes opposing monsters' ATK, then destroys anything sitting at 0 ATK.

hooks.label: Level 3 Rock monsters
hooks.why: Gorgonic Guardian needs exactly 2 Level 3 Rock-Type monsters as Xyz Material, so any other Level 3 Rock is another body for the Summon.

hooks.label: Rock-Type support
hooks.why: Every Gorgonic monster is a Rock, and Gargoyle and Cerberus only trigger off Rock-Type Summons, so generic Rock support hits the whole deck.

hooks.label: ATK reduction to zero
hooks.why: Gorgonic Guardian destroys any monster on the field with 0 ATK, so outside cards that drop a monster's ATK to 0 turn into removal.

hooks.label: Normal Summons extra Rocks
hooks.why: Gorgonic Gargoyle Special Summons itself when you Normal Summon a Rock, so cards granting extra Normal Summons trigger it for free.

hooks.label: Rewards being Xyz detached
hooks.why: Gorgonic Guardian detaches its Level 3 Rock materials as a cost every turn, so outside Level 3 Rocks that trigger when detached get that for free.

profile.plan: A Duel-long enchantment deck that locks monster hand effects out of the game in exchange for escalating privileges — double battle damage, extra attacks, free Tribute Summons of big monsters and free Spells — while banishing its Spells from the GY to grow its payoffs.

hooks.label: Free big bosses
hooks.why: Guilt-Gripping Morganite lets you Normal Summon Level 5 or higher monsters without Tributing, so any high-Level monster from outside the archetype becomes a free body.

hooks.label: Piercing damage
hooks.why: Succumbing-Song Morganite doubles battle damage and grants a second attack, so outside cards that force piercing or extra attacks turn each battle into a lethal one.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: Morgana the Witch of Eyes is the archetype's only monster, a DARK Spellcaster, so generic Spellcaster support runs the deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: Morgana's negate and both Spells' GY effects banish Morganite Spells from your GY as a cost, so outside Spells with an effect when banished get triggered for free.

profile.plan: A swarm of small WATER Aqua monsters backed by Continuous 'Aquarium' Spells that buff them in battle and revive an Aqua when an Aquarium leaves the field.

hooks.label: Sends your Continuous Spells away
hooks.why: All three Aquarium Spells revive an Aqua-Type monster from the Graveyard when sent from the field to the GY, so any outside card that removes your own Continuous Spell turns a passive buff into a revival effect.

hooks.label: Continuous Spell payoffs
hooks.why: The whole engine is Continuous Spells, so outside cards that reward you for controlling or using Continuous Spells get value from every Aquarium.

hooks.label: Aqua-type support
hooks.why: Every Aquaactress monster is an Aqua-Type WATER monster and the Aquarium Spells revive Aqua-Type monsters specifically, so generic Aqua or WATER support powers and recycles the whole deck.

profile.plan: A small family of Dragon bosses: Amorphactor Ritual Summoned to skip the opponent's Main Phase 1, Lector Pendulum as an anti-Pendulum wall, and Master Peace Tribute Summoned by Tributing monsters or your own Continuous Spells/Traps.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon support
hooks.why: Master Peace needs 3 Tributes to Normal Summon, so cards that grant extra Normal Summons, extra Tributes or make Tribute Summoning cheaper are enablers.

hooks.label: Tribute fodder Tokens
hooks.why: Master Peace is a Tribute Summon boss that can use any monsters as Tributes, so outside cards that fill the field with Tokens supply them cheaply.

hooks.label: Continuous Spells and Traps
hooks.why: Master Peace can Tribute Continuous Spells/Traps you control instead of monsters for its Tribute Summon, so durable Continuous backrow doubles as Summon fodder.

hooks.label: Wyrm support
hooks.why: Master Peace, the deck's main boss, is a Wyrm, so generic Wyrm searchers and support work with it.

hooks.label: Ritual Summon support
hooks.why: Amorphactor Pain is Ritual Summoned and searches another Dracoverlord when it leaves the field, so cards that help Ritual Summon a Level 8 keep that engine online.

profile.plan: The Ignister machine: Links Cyberse monsters of every Attribute together and pays off its signature 2300 ATK monsters, banishing its spells from the GY for extra effects.

hooks.label: Cyberse support
hooks.why: Every card in the deck searches, summons, protects or counts Cyberse monsters, so generic Cyberse support works across the whole engine.

hooks.label: 2300 ATK payoffs
hooks.why: You and A.I., A.I. Challenge You and A.I.'s Show all trigger off or revive monsters with 2300 original ATK, so outside cards that reference that number line up perfectly.

hooks.label: Banishes itself from the GY
hooks.why: FA.I.ghting Spirit and SA.I.dekick activate their follow-up effects by being banished from the GY, and SA.I.dekick revives banished Cyberse monsters, so cards that want to be banished stack with that plan.

hooks.label: Banishes your Cyberse
hooks.why: SA.I.dekick revives any banished Cyberse monster, so outside cards that banish your own Cyberse turn into free revival fodder.

hooks.label: Link Summons with Cyberse
hooks.why: The deck's payoff monsters are Link-3 or higher Ignister Links in the Extra Monster Zone, which A.I.'s Show requires, so outside cards that Link Summon off your Cyberse monsters extend that plan.

hooks.label: Attribute-changers
hooks.why: A.I. Meet You and A.I. Connect pick @Ignisters by Attribute and You and A.I. gives a different effect per Attribute, so cards that change or add Attributes unlock missing options.

profile.plan: Rank-Up-Magic Spells climb existing Xyz Monsters into higher-Rank bosses and reward attaching themselves as Xyz material.

hooks.label: Number Xyz bosses
hooks.why: Hyper Rank-Up-Magic Ultimate Force climbs into any Rank 10 or higher Number Xyz Monster, so those outside bosses are the payoff.

hooks.label: Attaches itself as Xyz material
hooks.why: Utopiforce, Zexal Force and Ultimate Force all attach themselves or reward being attached as Xyz material, so outside cards that become Xyz material fit the same plan.

hooks.label: Rank 4 Spellcaster Xyz
hooks.why: Rank-Up-Magic Magical Force needs a Rank 4 Spellcaster Xyz Monster in the GY to rank up, so those monsters are its starting material.

hooks.label: Revives your Xyz Monsters
hooks.why: Every Rank-Up-Magic here targets an Xyz Monster you control or in your GY, so outside cards that revive or Summon Xyz Monsters supply the base to rank up.

hooks.label: Utopia support
hooks.why: Utopiforce, Zexal Force and Ultimate Force all rank up Utopia and Utopic Xyz Monsters, so any outside card that supports them strengthens the climb.

profile.plan: Warriors built around attacking and Rank 6 Xyz Summons: the Level 6 Bounzers stack attacks, negate monster effects when detach, and Phantom Bounzer searches two more Bounzers when it dies.

hooks.label: Level 6 monsters
hooks.why: Photon Strike Bounzer needs exactly 2 Level 6 monsters as Xyz Material, and the deck's own bosses are Level 6, so any outside Level 6 body helps stack Rank 6s.

hooks.label: Cards you want discarded
hooks.why: Blade Bounzer's extra-attack effect discards 1 card as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are discarded get it for free.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Phantom Bounzer searches 2 Bounzer cards when it is destroyed on the field, so outside cards that destroy your own monsters turn it into a plus.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Bounzer monster is a Warrior, so generic Warrior searchers, revives and boosts reach the whole deck.

hooks.label: Extra attacks in Battle Phase
hooks.why: Blade Bounzer already attacks twice and Hammer Bounzer attacks while locking backrow, so outside cards that grant additional attacks or let monsters attack directly compound the deck's plan.

profile.plan: An X-Saber Synchro deck: EARTH Tuners like Bruno and Pellina swarm and Synchro Summon into big EARTH bosses like Commander Souza, who grows off banished monsters.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished
hooks.why: X-Saber Bruno banishes another EARTH monster from your hand, field or GY as its Special Summon cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are banished get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Grows off banished monsters
hooks.why: Commander Souza, Swordmaster gains 200 ATK for each banished monster, so outside cards that banish your own monsters from the GY make it stronger and feed Bruno's cost.

hooks.label: EARTH support
hooks.why: Bruno can only Synchro Summon using EARTH monsters and Souza needs EARTH non-Tuners, so the whole Extra Deck engine is locked to EARTH.

hooks.label: Synchro enablers
hooks.why: Pellina and Bruno want to Synchro Summon every turn, so outside Tuners and monsters that Special Summon themselves keep the EARTH Synchro engine going.

profile.plan: Traps that Tribute your face-up monsters to Special Summon armored Metal monsters from the hand, Deck or GY and equip themselves for protection, with Time Engine turning a destroyed Machine into a burn comeback.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Max Metalmorph and Flame Coating Metalmorph Tribute a face-up monster as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get it for free.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Time Engine's full destroy-and-burn payoff only applies to a Level 5 or higher Machine it revives, and the archetype's own bosses are Machines, so Machine support pulls the deck together.

hooks.label: Big Machine beaters
hooks.why: Time Engine Special Summons a destroyed monster back and inflicts damage equal to its original ATK, so the bigger the revived Machine, the bigger the burn.

hooks.label: Recovers Traps from the GY
hooks.why: Flame Coating Metalmorph checks for a Metalmorph Trap on your field or in your GY, so outside cards that Set or recover Traps from the GY keep that condition live.

profile.plan: Reptiles that Tribute themselves or other Reptiles to Special Summon big FIRE Dinosaurs from the Deck, then overlay them into Xyz bosses.

hooks.label: Level 6 or lower FIRE Dinosaurs
hooks.why: Megachirella and Casinerio Special Summon Level 6 or lower FIRE Dinosaurs straight from the Deck, so any outside card that IS one is a free payoff target.

hooks.label: Tributes your Reptiles
hooks.why: Megachirella needs a Reptile Tributed as its cost, so outside cards that Tribute your Reptile monsters double as activators.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: The deck Tributes Reptiles constantly, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed trigger for free.

hooks.label: Reptile support
hooks.why: Every Evoltile monster is a Reptile and Evo-Branch targets a face-up Reptile, so cards that search, revive or protect Reptiles work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Feeds Dragon Xyz Monsters
hooks.why: Megachirella attaches monsters from hand and GY to a Dragon Xyz Monster with no material, so outside cards that attach material to your Xyz Monsters keep the Evolzars loaded.

profile.plan: Upgrades Synchro monsters into bigger Level 7-12 /Assault Mode bosses via the Trap "Assault Mode Activate", which Tributes a Synchro Monster as the cost.

hooks.label: Synchro Monster engine
hooks.why: Every /Assault Mode is Summoned by Tributing a Synchro Monster, so the deck lives on outside Synchro Monsters it can Summon first.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Assault Mode Activate Tributes a Synchro Monster as its cost, so outside Synchro Monsters with an effect when they are Tributed get that trigger for free.

hooks.label: Dragon Synchro bosses
hooks.why: Three of the five /Assault Mode monsters upgrade Dragon Synchro Monsters (Stardust, Red Nova, Black Rose), so Dragon Synchro Monsters are the natural bosses to feed the Trap.

hooks.label: Fills the GY with Tuners
hooks.why: Red Nova Dragon/Assault Mode banishes opponent's cards up to the number of Tuners in your GY, so outside cards that send Tuners there power that effect.

profile.plan: A Beast-and-fairy dream deck that banishes its own Extra Deck face-down and turns the pile of face-down banished cards into removal and stat swings.

hooks.label: Level 10 Beast monsters
hooks.why: Reveil Special Summons itself by sending a Level 10 Beast, Louve summons one from Deck, and Repeter uses one on field to negate, so any outside Level 10 Beast is free material.

hooks.label: Banishes your Extra Deck face-down
hooks.why: Reveil and Repeter pay their costs by banishing Extra Deck cards face-down, so any outside card that does the same grows the face-down banished pile for Dreaming Nemleria and Louve.

hooks.label: Scales with face-down banished cards
hooks.why: Dreaming Nemleria banishes opponent's cards for every 3 of your face-down banished cards and Louve drops ATK per face-down banished card, so outside effects that count or use your face-down banished cards compound the payoff.

profile.plan: A Synchro deck whose Normal Traps turn themselves into Level 1 Tuner monsters and whose big monsters Summon themselves by bouncing your own face-down cards, so it wins by keeping lots of cards face-down and looping Traps out of the GY.

hooks.label: Normal Trap payoff
hooks.why: Mikumari the Banisher Ashtra and Ashtraya Mikumari-no-Mikoto Set any Normal Trap from the GY, and Ashtraja Susanoo banishes Traps from the GY as cost, so strong Normal Traps get reused here for free.

hooks.label: Traps that live in the GY
hooks.why: Akasuna the Battle Ashtra sends a Trap from your hand or face-down field to the GY as a cost and Ashtraja banishes Traps from the GY as a cost, so outside Traps with effects from the GY or banishment get those costs paid for them.

hooks.label: Sets more face-down cards
hooks.why: Kuzuha the Hex Ashtra destroys one card for every 2 face-down cards on the field, Ashtraya unlocks any Trap in the GY with 3 or more face-down cards, and every Ashtra monster self-Summons by revealing a face-down card you control, so outside cards that Set extra cards face-down power all of it.

hooks.label: Flips monsters face-down
hooks.why: Kuzuha the Hex Ashtra counts every face-down card on the field and Ashtraya Mikumari-no-Mikoto needs 3 or more of them, so outside cards that flip monsters face-down Defense Position turbo both effects.

profile.plan: Level 4 Warriors that discard cards as costs, float when destroyed or hit the GY, and revive or reward small Warriors, Spellcasters and Normal Monsters.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Dragodies and Dragonox both discard 1 card as a cost, so any outside card with an effect when it is discarded gets triggered for free.

hooks.label: Summon a Normal Monster
hooks.why: Terratiger Special Summons a Level 4 or lower Normal Monster from the hand and Ventdra recycles Dragon, Warrior and Spellcaster Normal Monsters, so outside cards that Summon or search Normal Monsters are engine pieces.

hooks.label: Small Spellcaster monsters
hooks.why: Arnis Special Summons a Spellcaster with 1500 or less ATK from the Deck and Dragodies searches Warriors or Spellcasters with 2000 or less ATK, so any small Spellcaster boss or floater is a target.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every Empowered Warrior is a Warrior, and Dragodies searches Warriors with 2000 or less ATK, so generic Warrior support covers the whole deck.

profile.plan: Level 2 'baby' monsters that Tribute themselves while 'Neo Space' is on the field to hatch into bigger Neo-Spacian monsters from the hand, Deck or Graveyard.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Every Chrysalis monster's Tribute effect only works while 'Neo Space' is on the field, so outside cards that put Field Spells onto the field from the Deck are the deck's engine starter.

hooks.label: Neo-Spacian support
hooks.why: Contact, Cocoon Party, Cocoon Rebirth and Cocoon Veil all Summon or count Neo-Spacian monsters, so any outside card that supports them pays off twice.

hooks.label: Effect when Tributed
hooks.why: The whole deck's monsters Tribute themselves as a cost, so outside monsters that trigger when they are Tributed get their effect for free alongside the hatch.

hooks.label: Sends to the Graveyard
hooks.why: Contact sends every Chrysalis monster you control to the Graveyard, so outside cards that send your own monsters there set up Cocoon Party and Cocoon Rebirth.

hooks.label: Level 2 spam
hooks.why: Cocoon Party Special Summons a Chrysalis from the Deck for each different Neo-Spacian in the Graveyard, so cheap Level 2 monsters keep Tribute and Xyz material on the board.

profile.plan: FIRE Warrior knights armed with Equip Spells that Special Summon and search each other, locking you into Warrior monsters while stacking up equips.

hooks.label: FIRE Warrior support
hooks.why: Noble Arms Museum boosts all FIRE Warriors and Angelica sends a FIRE Warrior from the Deck to the GY as a cost, so cards that search, revive or boost FIRE Warriors fit the whole deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Angelica sends 1 FIRE Warrior from the Deck to the GY as its cost, so outside monsters with an effect in the GY get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Equip Spell abuse
hooks.why: Camelot destroys an Equip Card you control instead of your Noble Knights and Cursed Copycat scales with every Equip Spell in your field and GY, so outside cards that equip themselves, recur equips or reward controlling Equip Spells pile on.

hooks.label: Equip fodder that wants destruction
hooks.why: Camelot destroys 1 Equip Card you control as a replacement effect every turn, so outside Equip Cards with an effect when destroyed get triggered on schedule.

hooks.label: Banish-and-return support
hooks.why: Angelica and Camelot banish themselves until a later phase and return, so outside cards that interact with or reward your own cards returning from banishment synergise.

hooks.label: Warrior Tribute bosses
hooks.why: Museum and Cursed Copycat lock you into Special Summoning Warrior monsters only, so outside Warrior monsters with an easy self-Special Summon or Tribute Summon keep the lock harmless.

profile.plan: Level 10 Beast dream monsters that pay costs by banishing face-down cards from their own Extra Deck, where their sleeping princess Pendulum Monster 'Dreaming Nemleria' must stay face-up.

hooks.label: Banishes your Extra Deck face-down
hooks.why: Oreiller, Couette and Dream Tower all pay their costs by banishing face-down cards from your own Extra Deck, so outside cards that do the same keep the deck's fuel engine going and shrink the Extra Deck no further.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished face-down
hooks.why: The deck banishes face-down Extra Deck cards as a cost every turn, so an outside card that triggers when it is banished (face-down) gets used for free.

hooks.label: Level 10 Beast monsters
hooks.why: Dream Tower of Princess Nemleria searches any two differently named Level 10 Beasts, and Oreiller and Couette summon themselves without Tributes, so outside Level 10 Beasts are free boss monsters for the deck.

hooks.label: Pendulum face-up in Extra Deck
hooks.why: Oreiller and Couette only work while a face-up Pendulum Monster sits in the Extra Deck, and Sweet Dreams puts 'Dreaming Nemleria' back face-up, so outside cards that add or place a Pendulum Monster face-up into the Extra Deck keep the deck's ignition on.

profile.plan: Normal Traps that punish the opponent's Summons by destroying or banishing their monsters, growing stronger when other 'Hole' Traps are already in the GY.

hooks.label: Normal Trap support
hooks.why: All three cards are Normal Traps and Terrifying Trap Hole Nightmare wants a 'Hole' Normal Trap in the GY, so outside cards that search, copy or set Normal Traps double the deck.

hooks.label: Loves banished face-down cards
hooks.why: Banishing Trap Hole banishes the opponent's monsters face-down, so outside cards that reward or exploit cards banished face-down turn that removal into a payoff.

hooks.label: Feeds off opponent Special Summons
hooks.why: All three Traps only work on a turn the opponent has Special Summoned, so outside cards that force or bait the opponent into Special Summoning keep the Traps live.

profile.plan: Pendulum Normal Monsters whose Pendulum Effects reward battle: searching when a Normal Monster destroys by battle, popping cards on battle damage, and summoning when anything dies in battle.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: All three Draconia cards are Normal Monsters in the Monster Zone, so outside cards that search, summon or protect Normal Monsters work on the whole deck.

hooks.label: Pendulum Scale support
hooks.why: The deck needs two complementary Scales to Pendulum Summon, with Scale 2 and Scale 7 already covered, so cards that fill or replace Pendulum Scales keep the engine online.

hooks.label: Big Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Dragoons of Draconia searches any Level 4+ Normal Monster when one destroys a monster by battle, so outside high-Level Normal Monsters with attack power are the payoff targets.

hooks.label: Fights harder for you
hooks.why: Every Pendulum Effect only fires when your Normal Monster destroys by battle or deals damage, so outside cards that grant extra attacks or piercing make each battle pay off twice.

profile.plan: Level 12 Synchro bosses built from stacks of Tuners and Synchro Monsters, that banish themselves for mass removal or to Summon the next Dragon.

hooks.label: Tuners it can Summon
hooks.why: Red Hypernova Dragon needs 4 Tuners and Burning Soul needs 2, so any outside card that Special Summons Tuners is Summoning material.

hooks.label: Extra Tuner bodies
hooks.why: The deck burns through several Tuners at once for Red Hypernova Dragon, so Tuner monsters that Summon themselves or dodge costs keep the materials coming.

hooks.label: Summons Synchro materials
hooks.why: Quasar and Hypernova demand non-Tuner Synchro Monsters as material, so outside cards that put Synchro Monsters on the field are stepping stones.

hooks.label: Banishes itself for value
hooks.why: Quasar and Hypernova banish themselves as a cost for their effects, so outside cards that do something when they are banished get it for free.

hooks.label: Banishes Tuners from the GY
hooks.why: Burning Soul Special Summons itself by banishing 2 Tuners and a Red Dragon Archfiend from the GY, so outside cards that banish your own GY cards set that up.

profile.plan: WIND Warrior Synchro support built around Junk Warrior: search Synchron Tuners and Synchro-support Spells, Tribute spare bodies to cheat out more Warriors, and pump everything in the Battle Phase.

hooks.label: Synchron Tuner monsters
hooks.why: Assault Sonic Warrior searches any "Synchron" monster and the deck's payoff is Synchro Summoning Junk Warrior, so Tuners with that name are the engine's fuel.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be Tributed
hooks.why: Swiftwind Panther Warrior Tributes another monster from your hand or field as a cost every turn, so outside monsters with effects when they are Tributed turn that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be discarded
hooks.why: Dragonic Warrior discards 1 card as a cost to Special Summon Dragons, so outside cards with an effect when they are discarded get that cost for free.

hooks.label: Small Dragon monsters
hooks.why: Dragonic Warrior Special Summons any Level 4 or lower Dragon from hand or Deck, so any low-Level Dragon is a free body and material for a Synchro Summon.

hooks.label: Assault Mode support
hooks.why: Assault Sonic Warrior searches and rewards "Assault Mode Activate", so the wider Assault Mode family slots straight into the deck.

hooks.label: Warrior Synchro bosses
hooks.why: Full-Speed Warrior pumps any Synchro Monster with "Warrior" in its original name, so every other Synchro Warrior is a payoff target the deck would not have thought of.

profile.plan: A LIGHT Spellcaster Ritual deck that wins by piling monsters of many different Attributes into the Graveyard, powering up Elemental Grace Doriado and freely Special Summoning whatever Attributes are missing.

hooks.label: Ritual searching support
hooks.why: Doriado's Blessing can only Ritual Summon Elemental Mistress Doriado, so outside cards that search or recover Ritual Monsters and Ritual Spells make the deck consistent.

hooks.label: Sends your monsters to the GY
hooks.why: Elemental Grace Doriado and Elemental Saga Doriado both count different Attributes among monsters in your GY, so any outside card that sends your own monsters there builds their power and revival fuel.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished from the GY
hooks.why: Elemental Grace Doriado's negation is paid by banishing 3 monsters from your GY, so outside monsters with effects that trigger when banished from the GY turn that cost into value.

hooks.label: Wants to be Tributed
hooks.why: Doriado's Blessing Tributes monsters from the field or hand for the Ritual Summon, so outside monsters with an effect when Tributed get it for free as Ritual fodder.

hooks.label: Off-Attribute boss monsters
hooks.why: Saga Doriado Special Summons any monster from the Deck with an Attribute you don't already have, and both Doriados scale with Attribute variety, so big outside monsters of unusual Attributes are free bosses and fuel.

profile.plan: Monsters that turn into Continuous Spells in the backrow when destroyed, as long as the Field Spell "Advanced Dark" stays up, then swarm back out of the Spell & Trap Zone.

hooks.label: Field Spell searchers
hooks.why: Every Advanced Crystal Beast sends itself to the GY unless "Advanced Dark" is in a Field Zone, so anything that fetches or plays that Field Spell keeps the whole deck alive.

hooks.label: Destroys your own monsters
hooks.why: Each monster destroyed in a Monster Zone goes to the Spell & Trap Zone as a Continuous Spell instead of the GY, so a card that destroys your monsters is a free way to build that backrow.

hooks.label: Continuous Spell payoffs
hooks.why: The deck stacks its own monsters face-up in the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells, and Ruby Carbuncle swarms them all back out, so cards that count or reward Continuous Spells scale with it.

hooks.label: Summons from backrow
hooks.why: Ruby Carbuncle Special Summons the Continuous Spell monsters out of the Spell & Trap Zones, so other cards that Summon monsters from there add more bodies on the same axis.

hooks.label: Beast support
hooks.why: Four of the seven monsters (Mammoth, Cat, Tiger, Pegasus) are Beasts, so generic Beast-Type search and revival reaches over half the deck.

profile.plan: WIND Insects that Special Summon themselves cheaply, raise each other's Levels and lock down enemy attackers by flipping them into Defense Position.

hooks.label: Insect support
hooks.why: Primitive Butterfly and Reed Butterfly are both Insect monsters, and Primitive Butterfly's Level-raising effect only hits Insects, so generic Insect support powers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Rank 5 Xyz plays
hooks.why: Primitive Butterfly Special Summons itself for free and every copy can sit at Level 5, so the deck fields two Level 5 monsters with almost no cost.

hooks.label: Piercing damage
hooks.why: Butterflyoke forces the attacking monster into Defense Position and keeps flipping it back, so the opponent's monsters are stuck in Defense where piercing damage punishes them.

hooks.label: Battle position manipulation
hooks.why: Butterflyoke and the deck's switching effects reward outside cards that also turn monsters to Defense Position or punish Defense Position monsters, compounding the lock.

profile.plan: LIGHT and EARTH Warriors that flood the field, feed each other to the GY, and Fusion Summon big Warrior Fusion Monsters mid-battle.

hooks.label: Fusion Summons Warrior Fusions
hooks.why: Todoroki Fusion Summons a Warrior Fusion Monster every Battle Phase using monsters from your hand or field, so outside cards that Fusion Summon Warrior Fusions stack on it.

hooks.label: Special Summons EARTH monsters
hooks.why: Senko Special Summons itself from hand whenever an EARTH monster is Normal or Special Summoned to your field, so outside cards that Summon EARTH monsters trigger it for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent from hand
hooks.why: Todoroki Special Summons itself by sending 1 other monster from your hand to the GY as a cost, so outside monsters with an effect when sent there get it for free.

hooks.label: Level 5+ LIGHT Warriors
hooks.why: Raijin's Fusion Summon needs a Level 5 or higher LIGHT Warrior as material, so outside monsters that fit and can Tribute Summon or Special Summon themselves are prime material.

hooks.label: Warrior support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is a Warrior, Todoroki only fuses Warrior Fusions, and Raijin revives Level 7 or lower Warriors from the GY, so generic Warrior support covers the whole engine.

profile.plan: A set of Trap Cards that equip to your Amazement monsters to power them up, or hitch a ride on the opponent's monsters and sabotage them with negation, position changes, stat loss and temporary banishment.

hooks.label: Battle position changers
hooks.why: Thrill Train and Rapid Racing change the equipped monster's battle position on demand, so any outside card that rewards or repeats position changes keeps the engine turning.

hooks.label: Flips opponent monsters face-down
hooks.why: Horror House and Thrill Train punish the opponent's equipped monster with a flip to face-down Defense or temporary banishment, so outside cards that also lock opponents down in face-down Defense stack with them.

hooks.label: Sets Traps from the GY
hooks.why: Thrill Train Sets Attraction Traps from your GY, and every Attraction card sends itself to the GY when used, so outside cards that Set Traps back out of the GY keep the ride going.

hooks.label: Equip card support
hooks.why: Every Attraction Trap is an Equip Card once activated, so outside cards that search, protect or recycle Equip Cards work across the whole archetype.

hooks.label: Equip-sabotage on opponent monsters
hooks.why: The Traps equip to the opponent's face-up monsters to sabotage them, so outside cards that also attach to or curse the opponent's monsters add more ways to hijack them.

profile.plan: Machine dynamo cards that feed on Gadget monsters, equipping them for ATK or sending them to the Graveyard to Summon big bodies, with a trap that wipes Attack Position monsters while you run all-Machine.

hooks.label: Gadget monsters
hooks.why: Destroyer Dynamo is Summoned by sending Gadget monsters to the GY and Corporal equips them to itself, so any outside Gadget monster is free fuel for the whole engine.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Gear Force only works when every monster you control is a face-up Machine, so the deck stays Machine-only and generic Machine support works across all of it.

hooks.label: Union monsters
hooks.why: Gear Charge Special Summons Monster Cards that are equipped to a monster back to the field, and Corporal equips monsters to itself for ATK, so Union monsters that live as equip cards recycle perfectly here.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Destroyer Dynamo's Summon sends Gadget monsters from the hand and field to the GY as material, so outside Machine monsters with an effect when they are sent there get it for free.

profile.plan: WIND Warrior Pendulum Spirits that Normal Summon themselves for a column-clearing effect, then return to the hand every End Phase so they can be Summoned again next turn.

hooks.label: Pendulum Summons monsters
hooks.why: All four cards are Pendulum monsters whose Pendulum Effects fire when a monster is Pendulum Summoned, returning the Scale to the hand so a new Spirit can be placed.

hooks.label: Spirit monsters
hooks.why: Every Martial Art Spirit is a Spirit monster that bounces itself back to the hand during the End Phase, so other Spirits and their support share that rhythm and need no setup.

hooks.label: WIND Warrior support
hooks.why: The whole archetype is WIND Warrior monsters, so generic WIND or Warrior searchers, boosters and revival work on all of them.

hooks.label: Likes being bounced
hooks.why: Han-Shi Kyudo Spirit and the Spirits' own End Phase effects constantly return your cards to the hand, so outside cards with an effect when they are returned to the hand get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Column-based cards
hooks.why: All four Spirits send cards in the same column as your Pendulum Zones to the GY, so outside cards that care about card columns stack with that removal.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: The Spirits only get their removal when Normal Summoned and leave each turn, so an extra Normal Summon each turn lets a Spirit be Summoned twice or alongside another monster.

profile.plan: DARK Zombies that banish themselves and each other for value, searching Ghost Fusion and recovering banished Zombies while banishment fuels their comebacks.

hooks.label: Banishes your own Zombies
hooks.why: Ghost Sleeper banishes itself to recover banished Zombies and Ghost Wyvern rewards being banished, so outside cards that banish your Zombies keep the engine running.

hooks.label: Rewards being banished
hooks.why: Ghost Wyvern triggers during the End Phase of the turn it is banished, so outside monsters with effects while banished stack more value on the deck's self-banishing.

hooks.label: Sends your Zombies to the GY
hooks.why: Ghost Sleeper adds Ghost Fusion when sent to the GY, so any outside card that sends your Zombies there is a free activator.

hooks.label: Level 2 or lower Zombie Tuners
hooks.why: Ghost Wyvern fetches a Level 2 or lower Zombie Tuner, so outside Tuners it can grab enable Synchro plays.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: Every Underworld monster is a DARK Zombie, so generic Zombie search, revival and boost cards work across the whole deck.

profile.plan: Trap-and-Spell engine for the lswarm/Steelswarm Insects, whose big bosses are Tribute Summoned and get recycled to the hand for draws and removal.

hooks.label: Self-Tribute Summoning monsters
hooks.why: First Step Towards Infestation and Infestation Wave only pay off while you control a face-up Tribute Summoned Steelswarm, so any outside monster that Tribute Summons itself cheaply is a partner boss.

hooks.label: Extra Tribute Summons
hooks.why: The Steelswarm bosses need full Tribute Summons, so outside cards that grant additional Normal or Tribute Summons let you Summon them without losing your whole turn.

hooks.label: Token generators
hooks.why: Steelswarm Tribute Summons need bodies, so outside cards that Summon Tokens give Tribute fodder turn after turn.

hooks.label: Insect support
hooks.why: Every lswarm and Steelswarm monster is an Insect, so generic Insect searchers, revival and boosts work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: DARK Insect graveyard revival
hooks.why: Infestation Ripples and Infestation Tool both want Steelswarm monsters in the Graveyard, so outside cards that mill or revive DARK Insect monsters feed and reuse the engine.

profile.plan: A pack of EARTH Machine robots that Normal Summon themselves into a board of Level 8 Machines and stack them into Rank 8 Xyz bosses, fuelled by Graveyard recycling.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Super Defense Robot monster is an EARTH Machine, so generic Machine searchers, boosters and revivals work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Rank 8 Xyz monsters
hooks.why: Elephan turns any Super Defense Robot or Orbital 7 into Level 8, so any Rank 8 Machine Xyz Monster — not just Googly-Eyes Drum Dragon — can be stacked on top of the board.

hooks.label: Recovers your Machines from the GY
hooks.why: Lio Special Summons a monster straight from the hand when exactly one is added from the Graveyard, so outside cards that return your own Machine monsters from the GY to your hand double as Summoning power.

hooks.label: Rewards being banished from the GY
hooks.why: Monki banishes a Machine from the Graveyard as a cost to recover robots, and Googly-Eyes Drum Dragon banishes Super Defense Robots to revive itself, so outside Machines that trigger when banished from the GY get used for free.

profile.plan: Extra Deck bosses that win battles — Gaia Blaze chains attacks and recovers FIRE monsters, Gaia Prominence negates hand/GY monster effects by discarding and revives FIRE monsters after battle, and Gaia Stream stacks Levels on a Rank 6 body.

hooks.label: FIRE monster support
hooks.why: Gaia Blaze adds FIRE monsters from the GY to the hand and Gaia Prominence Special Summons a FIRE monster from the GY after battle, so anything that stocks or supports FIRE monsters feeds both.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
hooks.why: Gaia Prominence discards 1 monster as the cost for its Quick Effect negation, so outside monsters with an effect when discarded get used for free.

hooks.label: Extra attack enablers
hooks.why: Gaia Blaze only makes its second attack after destroying a monster by battle and Gaia Prominence's revival also needs a battle destruction, so cards that give extra attacks or piercing turn battles into payoffs.

hooks.label: Rank 5 or 7 Xyz bases
hooks.why: Gaia Stream can be Xyz Summoned on top of any Rank 5 or 7 Xyz Monster you control, transferring its materials, so outside Rank 5/7 Xyz monsters are stepping stones.

profile.plan: Ritual Spells that Tribute monsters from your hand and field to Ritual Summon Nouvelles chefs, then recycle Recipes and punish the opponent's Defense Position monsters.

hooks.label: Monsters that want to be Tributed
hooks.why: Recette de Poisson and Recette de Viande Tribute monsters from your hand or field as Ritual material, so outside monsters with an effect when they are Tributed turn that cost into advantage.

hooks.label: Ritual Spell searchers
hooks.why: Fish Recipe rewards you by adding a Recipe Ritual Spell from Deck or GY, so outside cards that fetch or recycle Ritual Spells keep the engine running.

hooks.label: Generic Ritual Monsters
hooks.why: The whole engine Ritual Summons with any material whose total Levels equal the target's Level, so any outside Ritual Monster with its own easy Summon is extra ammunition for Recette de Personnel's exact-Level requirement.

hooks.label: Tribute fodder from the hand
hooks.why: Both Recipe Ritual Spells Tribute monsters from the hand as material, so outside monsters that Special Summon themselves or make tokens give you Tribute bodies without losing card presence.

profile.plan: Zero-ATK Spellcasters that Special Summon themselves the moment you draw them, then trigger a second effect off that Summon, so the deck wants to draw constantly.

hooks.label: Extra draw effects
hooks.why: Every Fortune Fairy Special Summons itself when you draw it, so any outside card that draws you extra cards becomes a free Special Summon plus its follow-up effect.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: All Fortune Fairies are Spellcasters, Lucky Loan summons Spellcasters from the Deck, and Lucky Loan and Miracle Stone only work while you have Spellcasters, so generic Spellcaster support covers the whole deck.

hooks.label: Banishes your Spellcasters
hooks.why: Hu adds a banished Spellcaster back to the hand, so outside cards that banish your own Spellcasters (as a cost or effect) set up that recovery while Ann can banish them from the Deck in the first place.

hooks.label: Level-flexible Spellcasters
hooks.why: Lucky Loan Special Summons any Spellcaster from your hand or Deck exactly one Level below a Fortune Fairy you control, so outside Spellcaster monsters at Levels 1 through 5 give the Deck bosses to fetch.

profile.plan: A chess-themed band of EARTH Warriors that swap low Levels for high ones from the Deck and GY, turning pawns into kings while bullying the opponent's searches.

hooks.label: EARTH Warrior support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is an EARTH Warrior, so generic EARTH or Warrior searchers and boosters hit the whole deck.

hooks.label: Level 6+ EARTH Warrior bosses
hooks.why: Puppet Queen summons a Level 7 EARTH Warrior straight from the hand or GY and Rook trades itself for a Level 6 or higher one from the GY, so any big EARTH Warrior fits.

hooks.label: Makes the opponent search
hooks.why: Puppet Queen Special Summons itself from the hand when the opponent adds a monster from their Main Deck to their hand, so outside cards that force an opponent search trigger it for free.

hooks.label: Reacts to being detached
hooks.why: Puppet Shark detaches a material from a monster on either field as its cost, so Xyz Monsters with effects that trigger when their material is detached get it for free.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Puppet Rook sends an EARTH Warrior from the Deck to the GY and Promotion sends a monster you control there, so outside EARTH Warriors with graveyard effects get milled for value.

profile.plan: Ritual Summons Egyptian sphinxes using Normal Monsters as Tribute material, then equips those Normal Monsters as Equip Spells to armor the Rituals while recycling the GY.

hooks.label: Revives Normal Monsters
hooks.why: Sphinx, Wadjet and the Field Spell all Special Summon Normal Monsters back from the GY, and Pere-Zenet Em Heru draws a card whenever you Special Summon a Normal Monster.

hooks.label: Ritual Monster searchers
hooks.why: The whole deck centers on Ritual Summoning Zenet Ritual Monsters, so outside cards that fetch Ritual Monsters or their support keep the engine running.

hooks.label: Equip Cards
hooks.why: Every Zenet Ritual gains protection while equipped, and Nefertari equips Normal Monsters to them as Equip Spells, so generic Equip Cards stack extra rewards on the Rituals.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: All Zenet monsters are Zombies, so cards that search, revive or boost Zombies work across the whole deck.

hooks.label: Wants to be sent to the GY
hooks.why: Sphinx, Wadjet, Pere-Zenet Em Heru and Am Duazenet all send your face-up Normal Monster Cards to the GY as material, so outside Normal Monsters and non-Effect monsters that trigger in the GY get used for free.

profile.plan: Gladiator Beasts battle, then shuffle themselves back into the Deck to 'tag out' and Summon a fresh Gladiator Beast from the Deck, chaining tag-outs through repeated battles and Battle Phases.

hooks.label: Extra attacks
hooks.why: Gistel and the other Gladiator Beasts only get their tag-out effect if they battled, so any outside card that lets a monster attack again or attack every monster gives more tag-outs per turn.

hooks.label: Forces opponent attacks
hooks.why: Flavian - Colosseum summons a Gladiator Beast straight from the Deck when the opponent declares an attack, so outside cards that force the opponent to attack keep that trigger firing.

hooks.label: Rewards being shuffled into the Deck
hooks.why: The tag-out and Gistel's Summon both shuffle Gladiator Beasts from the field or GY back into the Deck as a cost, so outside cards with an effect when they are returned to the Deck get that for free.

hooks.label: Battle Phase payoff cards
hooks.why: Claudius grants a second Battle Phase and the whole deck lives in the Battle Phase, so outside cards that give your monsters effects or protection that trigger 'during the Battle Phase' or when a monster battles stack on top of the tag-out engine.

profile.plan: A set of D/D-themed Spell and Trap contracts that pay you value over time while burning you for the privilege, ending with draw fuel and banishes when they are destroyed or sent to the GY.

hooks.label: D/D deck support
hooks.why: Patent License searches "D/D" monsters and only works while you control a "D/D/D" monster, so outside cards that support the D/D archetype slot straight in.

hooks.label: Triggers when you take damage
hooks.why: Dark Contract with the Different Dimension inflicts 1000 damage to you every Standby Phase, so outside cards with an effect when you take effect damage get a free recurring trigger.

hooks.label: Wants its Spells destroyed
hooks.why: Contract Laundering destroys every Dark Contract you control to draw, so outside Continuous Spells and Traps that trigger when destroyed by a card effect turn the mass destruction into extra advantage.

hooks.label: Floodgates matching Extra Deck types
hooks.why: Patent License locks the opponent out of Summoning the same Extra Deck card type as your D/D/D, so outside cards that restrict Special Summons from the Extra Deck stack with it.

profile.plan: Tribute Summons gigantic Machine bosses that need three Tributes apiece and then shrug off Spells, Traps and anything smaller than them on the field.

hooks.label: Counts as multiple Tributes
hooks.why: Apoqliphort Towers and Skybase each need 3 Tributes to Normal Summon, so any monster that is treated as 2 or more Tributes cuts that cost by a third or more.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: The deck needs a steady stream of bodies on the field to feed three-Tribute Tribute Summons, so extra Normal Summons each turn fill the Tribute slots.

hooks.label: Rewards when Tributed
hooks.why: The deck Tributes its own monsters three at a time for Apoqliphort bosses, so outside monsters that trigger or float when Tributed are paid for free.

hooks.label: Tribute Summon payoffs
hooks.why: Apoqliphort Towers and Skybase are only at full power once Tribute Summoned, so outside cards that reward Tribute Summoned or Level 10 monsters stack on top.

hooks.label: Machine support
hooks.why: Every Apoqliphort monster, and Qlife's End Summoned as a monster, is a Machine, so generic Machine searchers and boosts cover the whole deck.

hooks.label: EARTH support
hooks.why: All the deck's monsters are EARTH, so cards that search or revive EARTH monsters work across the archetype.

profile.plan: Level 8 monsters that banish themselves from the hand to search, then crawl back from banishment whenever you Summon from the Extra Deck, powering up their 'Power Patron' Link Monster bosses.

hooks.label: Extra Deck Summon enablers
hooks.why: Every Ars Magna monster Special Summons itself from banishment when a Fusion, Xyz, Synchro or Link Monster is Special Summoned, so any outside card that Summons from the Extra Deck pops them back out.

hooks.label: Banished-zone revival
hooks.why: Ars Magna the Division and the Union Special Summons from the banished zone and the monsters keep returning there themselves, so outside cards that retrieve monsters from banishment keep the cycle alive.

hooks.label: Link Monster support
hooks.why: The archetype's payoffs all key off 'Power Patron' Link Monsters — tripling their original ATK, granting extra attacks and destruction protection — so outside cards that Summon or strengthen Link Monsters fit.

hooks.label: Wants to be banished from the GY
hooks.why: Ars Magna the Division and the Union and Philosophorum banish 'Ars Magna' cards from the GY as costs, so outside cards with an effect when banished from the GY would not fit here but any deck engine that recycles banished Spell/Traps does.

profile.plan: A Zombie Xyz engine built around Level 6 monsters: Hubrow fills the GY, Officiating Reverie summons back from it, and they stack into Rank 6 Zombie Xyz Monsters that recycle the GY every turn.

hooks.label: Level 6+ Zombie bosses
hooks.why: Hubrow only sends and recovers Level 6 or higher Zombie monsters, and Officiator of Doom Samuel needs exactly two Level 6 monsters as material, so any big outside Zombie is both fuel and an Xyz body.

hooks.label: Revives Zombies from the GY
hooks.why: Hubrow Xyz Summons a Zombie Xyz Monster whenever any monster is Special Summoned from the GY, so every outside revival effect is also a combo starter.

hooks.label: Mills Zombie monsters
hooks.why: Officiator of Doom Samuel revives any Zombie from the GY and Officiating Reverie summons one, so outside cards that send Zombie monsters from the Deck to the GY stock both.

hooks.label: Gives Xyz Monsters material
hooks.why: Officiator of Doom Samuel detaches a material every turn for its revival effect, and Officiating Reverie reattaches itself from banishment, so outside cards that attach more material keep the engine running.

hooks.label: Rewards being detached
hooks.why: Officiator of Doom Samuel detaches a material as a cost each turn, so outside monsters with an effect when they are detached get it for free as material.

hooks.label: Zombie support
hooks.why: Every card in the archetype is a Zombie, and its engine lives in the Graveyard, so generic Zombie support slots straight in.

profile.plan: WIND Aqua Flip monsters that flip themselves and the opponent's cards up and down, reusing FLIP effects while punishing face-down cards.

hooks.label: WIND Flip monsters
hooks.why: Macchia Special Summons a Flip monster from the hand alongside itself and Kuro searches any WIND Flip monster, so the deck is built around that exact pool.

hooks.label: Flip monsters that want to be discarded
hooks.why: Earl discards 1 other Flip monster from the hand to Special Summon itself, giving any outside Flip monster a free trigger for its discard effect.

hooks.label: Flips monsters face-down
hooks.why: Kuro's FLIP effect turns an opponent's monster face-down and the deck's engine repeatedly flips cards back up, so outside cards that set monsters face-down restart FLIP effects and disrupt the opponent.

hooks.label: Sends face-down cards away
hooks.why: Macchia's End Phase effect sends a face-down card on the field to the GY, so outside cards that do the same clear opposing Sets and the deck's own spent cards.

profile.plan: Casino-styled Level 7 monsters that Special Summon themselves the moment you draw them, then stack into Rank 7 Xyz bosses while locking you out of everything except drawing.

hooks.label: Draw power
hooks.why: Every Raise Moon main deck monster Special Summons itself when drawn and the whole deck can only add cards from the Deck by drawing, so any outside card that draws is pure fuel.

hooks.label: Rank 7 LIGHT Xyz
hooks.why: Wings Rapi Xyz Summons a Rank 7 LIGHT monster on the opponent's turn and Elegance Carol locks you to LIGHT Xyz, so generic Rank 7 LIGHT bosses slot straight in.

hooks.label: Level 7 monsters
hooks.why: Hope Squeeze - Jackpot takes any 2+ Level 7 monsters as material and all the Main Deck monsters are Level 7, so outside Level 7s stack alongside them.

hooks.label: Spellcaster support
hooks.why: The City that Never Sleeps and The Stars of Raise Moon both draw only while you control a Spellcaster Xyz, and Cielo and her Xyz are Spellcasters, so Spellcaster support pulls double duty.

hooks.label: Mills the opponent's Deck
hooks.why: Hope Squeeze - Jackpot attaches the top card of the opponent's Deck every time they make a card leave their Deck, so any outside card that mills them feeds that trigger.

profile.plan: Monsters immune to their own punishing Field Spell "Clear World", which taxes the opponent while the deck searches its pieces and pushes for direct attacks.

hooks.label: Rewards being Tributed
hooks.why: Clear Vicious Knight Tribute Summons by Tributing 1 monster, so outside monsters that trigger when Tributed pay off for free.

hooks.label: Rewards being discarded
hooks.why: Clear Phantom's search costs discarding 2 cards, so outside cards with effects when discarded turn the cost into value.

hooks.label: Big Tribute Summon bosses
hooks.why: Clear Wall grants full "Clear World" pressure only while you control a Level 7+ monster, and Vicious Knight itself is a Tribute Summon payoff, so any Level 7+ Tribute Summon monster slots straight in.

hooks.label: Tribute fodder Tokens
hooks.why: Vicious Knight can be Tribute Summoned with any 1 monster, so outside cards that summon Tokens supply disposable Tribute material.

hooks.label: Extra Normal Summons
hooks.why: Clear Cube's own extra Normal Summon is once per turn, so more outside extra Normal Summons keep Tribute Summoning Vicious Knight without spending resources.
phrases: in addition to your Normal Summon

profile.plan: A loose band of EARTH Warriors and Level 8/10 bosses: Tyler burns for every monster he destroys by battle, Dark Creator floods the field with Tokens when monsters die by battle, and Demiurge Ema Special Summons itself by dumping big-ATK monsters from hand, Deck and field into the GY.

hooks.label: Normal Monster support
hooks.why: Doron, Genin and Dark Shade are vanilla monsters, so the classic Normal Monster support works on most of the archetype.

hooks.label: Fiend and Fairy Tribute fodder
hooks.why: Dark Creator Special Summons itself by Tributing 2 Fiend and/or Fairy monsters, so outside cards that put those Types on the field feed it.

hooks.label: Destroyed by battle payoffs
hooks.why: Dark Creator inflicts 700 damage every time any monster is destroyed by battle, so outside cards that force battles or destroy monsters by battle become burn.

hooks.label: Big monsters that want to be milled
hooks.why: Demiurge Ema sends monsters with 2400+ ATK from hand, Deck and field to the GY as its Summoning cost, so outside monsters with effects when sent to the GY get triggered for free.

hooks.label: Boosts ATK for battle burn
hooks.why: Tyler the Great Warrior burns for the destroyed monster's ATK and Dark Creator's Tokens are 3000 ATK beaters that cannot be destroyed by battle, so ATK boosts convert directly into damage.

archetype: Hunting Scout of the Deep Forest

profile.plan: EARTH Warrior Fusions that hunt in the Battle Phase: they Fusion Summon fast, dodge removal by tributing themselves, and Special Summon more EARTH Warriors from the GY as battles are won.

hooks.label: EARTH Warrior support
hooks.why: Every monster in the deck is an EARTH Warrior, including the Fusion materials, so generic EARTH Warrior searchers, revivers and boosters hit the whole deck.

hooks.label: Fusion Summons with Warriors
hooks.why: Hunting Horn wants Warrior monsters from the hand or field as material, so outside Fusion Summoning cards that use Warriors keep the deck going after the one-per-turn Horn.

hooks.label: Fills the GY with Warriors
hooks.why: Chevreuil and Faisan both Special Summon EARTH Warriors back from the GY, so any outside card that mills or self-sends EARTH Warriors loads the fuel.

hooks.label: Reacts to being Tributed
hooks.why: Faisan Tributes itself as a Quick Effect to dodge and rebuild, so an outside monster with an effect when it is Tributed gets that trigger for free if subbed in for a revival target.

hooks.label: Battle destruction payoffs
hooks.why: Chevreuil's revival only fires when another EARTH Warrior destroys a monster by battle, so outside EARTH Warriors that attack again or pierce multiply triggers.

profile.plan: DARK Fiends and Warriors that feed cards into the GY to Set and search their Spell/Traps, cap it with a Fusion that can be Summoned onto the opponent's field using their own monsters, and recover everything during the End Phase.

hooks.label: Sends opponent's monsters to GY
hooks.why: Viser Des Shock Special Summons itself from hand whenever a monster hits the opponent's GY while you control a Sun God card, so removal that sends or destroys their monsters is an extender.

hooks.label: Wants to be discarded
